No — citable listing records state Owner: No. Listings show Oakcrest units, built in 2022, as freehold strata. New doesn't mean fee simple; the Form B applies.
Market context: SnapStats recorded Sunsh: Market figures, September 2026: in Sunshine Hills Woods, 50 detached homes were listed and 3 sold (6%, the lowest share of North Delta's four areas that month), and 22 condos and townhomes were listed and 2 sold (9%). North Delta's detached median was $1,100,000. There are no separate figures for land.
Roads and transit: 72 Avenue and 64 Aven: Roads and transit: 72 Avenue and 64 Avenue run east–west, Kittson Parkway runs through the Watershed Park area, and Scott Road (120 Street) is the east side, with Highway 91 reached via 64 Avenue. Route 340 runs from Scottsdale Exchange to 22nd Street Station via Scott Road, 64 Avenue, Kittson Parkway, Highway 91 and the Alex Fraser Bridge; route 364 runs along the south edge, route 319 along the north edge, and the R6 RapidBus on Scott Road.
The Official Community Plan is Bylaw No. 8400 (2024), and zoning is Zoning Bylaw No. 7600, set lot by lot; check a specific lot's zone with the City.
Transit runs on the edges, not the inter: Transit runs along the edges, not through the middle: route 340 via Scott Road, 64 Avenue and Kittson Parkway; route 364 along the south edge; route 319 along 72 Avenue on the north edge; and the R6 RapidBus on Scott Road on the east side.
A townhouse complex just south of 72 Ave: A townhouse complex just south of 72 Avenue: a presale directory describes 40 wood-frame three- and four-bedroom townhomes by Bassi Properties, with strata fees to be set later. Listings show 2021 as the build year, though the presale marketing expected completion in late 2019.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates:: The townhouses are on the edges, not around the park: along 72 Avenue on the north edge (Chelsea Gate, 11188 72 Avenue, and Cyrus Hill, 7167 116 Street just south of 72nd), and around Nicholson Road in the southeast by Scott Road (Sunshine Woods, 6300 Cottonwood Street, and Nicholson Green, 6866 Nicholson Road). I don't know of any townhouse complexes in the detached streets around Watershed Park and Cougar Canyon.
Transit runs on the edges: route 340 run: Transit runs along the edges: route 340 from Scottsdale Exchange to 22nd Street Station via Scott Road, 64 Avenue, Kittson Parkway, Highway 91 and the Alex Fraser Bridge; route 364 from Langley Centre to Scottsdale Exchange via 64 Avenue and Scott Road, along the south edge; route 319 from Scott Road Station to Newton Exchange via 72 Avenue, along the north edge; and the R6 RapidBus on Scott Road on the east side. Highway 91 is reached via 64 Avenue.
Library and recreation: George Mackie Li: Library and recreation: George Mackie Library (8440 112th Street) is north of the area in Nordel, and there's no recreation centre in the area itself; North Delta Recreation Centre is at 11415 84 Avenue. The nearest hospital is Delta Hospital (5800 Mountain View Boulevard, Ladner), and the North Delta Public Health Unit is at 11245 84 Avenue.
Home type: townhouses / mixed residentia: Townhouses and other housing are planned under a City corridor pre-zoning report; I don't know of any individual project approved in Sunshine Hills Woods yet.
Why there is no condo stock — the city l: Why there are no condos: Delta's Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 8400, 2024) says Delta's industry is mainly along River Road East, in Tilbury Industrial Park, on Annacis Island and at Roberts Bank. Metro Vancouver's 2020 industrial lands inventory counted 1,527 hectares of industrial land in Delta, about 13% of the region's total.
Land use in one line: the Delta Official: Land use: Delta's Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 8400, 2024) says Delta's industry is mainly along River Road East, in Tilbury Industrial Park, on Annacis Island and at Roberts Bank, with pockets along River Road West and at Boundary Bay Airport. Metro Vancouver's 2020 inventory counted 1,527 hectares of industrial land in Delta, about 13% of the region's total.
Strata law still applies — to industrial: Strata rules apply to industrial stratas too: on a resale, the strata must provide a Form B (fees, amounts owing, approved levies, contingency reserve balance, insurance, rules, budget and latest depreciation report). Stratas with five or more lots need a depreciation report every five years, and at least 10% of the budget must go into the reserve. For an industrial unit, also get a Phase I environmental site assessment covering the unit's and the complex's past uses.
ALR and lease status on edge parcels: Ci: ALR and leases at the edges: City documents show farm leases on some Tilbury-area properties, and ALR status varies by property. A leased or ALR property doesn't sell like a clear freehold industrial lot, and ALR homes can't be stratified, so no strata townhouses can be built on that land.
Buyer frame (general BC layer, for buyer: If you're looking at homes elsewhere in Delta: the first-time buyers' GST rebate (law since March 13, 2026) covers all the GST on a new home up to $1 million (maximum $50,000), phasing out at $1.5 million, for agreements from March 20, 2025 to 2031; the GST New Housing Rebate is 36% up to $6,300 (phasing out between $350,000 and $450,000). First-time buyers pay no property transfer tax on the first $500,000 for homes up to $835,000 (partial up to $860,000), and the newly built home exemption is full up to $1,100,000 and partial up to $1,150,000. The Home Buyers' Plan allows $60,000, an FHSA $8,000 a year up to $40,000, and CMHC premiums run 0.6%–4.5%. Presales come with a 7-day right to cancel and deposits held in trust. A fee-simple townhouse has no strata, Form B or strata fees. There are no townhouses in Tilbury.
Land use, as the OCP states it: the Delt: Land use: Delta's Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 8400, 2024) says Delta's industry is mainly along River Road East, in Tilbury Industrial Park, on Annacis Island and at Roberts Bank, with pockets along River Road West and at Boundary Bay Airport. Metro Vancouver's 2020 inventory counted 1,527 hectares of industrial land in Delta, about 13% of the region's total.
Market figures: none cited, by design: T: There are no market figures for Tilbury: the board's Delta figures cover North Delta and its four residential areas only.
Search / alternate names: \"Tilbury Indu: Other names for the area: Tilbury Industrial Park, Tilbury Island, River Road industrial, and the South Fraser Perimeter Road corridor.
FTHB GST rebate / housing programs — not: The first-time buyers' GST rebate (law since March 13, 2026; up to $1 million, phasing out at $1.5 million, maximum $50,000, for agreements from March 20, 2025 to 2031) applies to new homes, not land, and not to industrial property. The same goes for the GST New Housing Rebate (36% up to $6,300), the Home Buyers' Plan ($60,000) and the FHSA ($8,000 a year up to $40,000): they're for homes, not a Tilbury industrial purchase.
The Delta OCP designates Tilbury as indu: Delta's Official Community Plan designates Tilbury as industrial land, and there are no homes there. Below: the two kinds of industrial ownership that sell, the industrial areas as the City names them, and the edge issues (the dike and farm leases) that affect a Tilbury property's price.
ALR: farm use leases on some Tilbury-are: ALR: City documents show farm leases on some Tilbury-area properties, so check a specific property's ALR status with the Agricultural Land Commission. On ALR land, subdividing needs Commission approval, homes can't be stratified, the main house can be up to 500 m² with a suite only inside it, and an additional home can be up to 90 m² (parcels of 40 ha or less) or 186 m² (larger). An ALR or farm-leased property doesn't sell like a clear freehold industrial lot. For farm tax status, you need farm income of $10,000 on under 0.8 ha, $2,500 on 0.8–4 ha, or $2,500 plus 5% of the land value over 4 ha, with applications due by October 31.
No. The Delta OCP treats Tilbury as indu: No. Delta's Official Community Plan treats Tilbury as industrial land, naming Tilbury Industrial Park with River Road East, Annacis Island and Roberts Bank as Delta's main industrial areas, and there are no homes in the industrial lands. Homes with the same postal area are on the farm and riverfront land around it in Ladner and East Delta.

No. Delta's Official Community Plan treats Tilbury as industrial land, naming Tilbury Industrial Park with River Road East, Annacis Island and Roberts Bank as Delta's main industrial areas, and there are no homes in the industrial lands.
Freehold strata, plan NWS2700, built 198: Freehold strata (plan NWS2700), built 1988, 38 units, self-managed, at 54A Street and 11 Avenue. Building sources describe an adult community with a 55+ age restriction, one pet but no dogs, and no rentals, with a workshop, storage lockers and a recreation room. Current listings say "Age restriction 55+, one occupant must be 55+," with a community room, bike room and workshop. Rental bans have been void since 2022, so check the current bylaws in the Form B and strata documents.
56 Street is the main north–south street: 56 Street is the main north–south street and 12 Avenue the main east–west street through the centre; most of the condos are on 54A Street and 55 Street.
Schools: South Park Elementary, K–7, Sch: Schools (SD37 Delta): South Park Elementary (K–7), 735 Gilchrist Drive; Cliff Drive Elementary (K–7), 5025 12 Avenue; and South Delta Secondary (8–12), 750 53 Street. Check the catchment for a specific address with the school district.
Where the townhouse stock actually sits:: Unlike the condos, which are on 56 Street and 54A and 55 Streets, the area's one townhouse complex, Sundial, is on 10 Avenue west of 56 Street, a short walk from the town centre, Winskill Park and the recreation centre.
Sundial is strata, so the strata documen: Sundial is strata, so the strata documents are the key: the Form B shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance after approved spending, and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page.
CRF minimum: since Nov 1, 2023, a strata: Since November 1, 2023, a strata must put at least 10% of its annual operating budget into the contingency reserve; compare Sundial's reserve balance on the Form B with that minimum and with the depreciation report's funding plans.
A fee-simple (non-strata) townhouse or r: A fee-simple (non-strata) townhouse or rowhouse has no strata corporation, Form B, strata fees or strata bylaws; you check the title, zoning and City records instead. Many buyers assume every townhouse is strata; here, the one complex is.
Fee-simple lots — the default and effect: Lots here are fee simple: houses and duplexes in the RS and RD zones, plus the strata condo buildings listed below. A fee-simple lot has no strata, Form B or strata fees.
Schools: Cliff Drive Elementary, K–7, Sc: Schools (SD37 Delta): Cliff Drive Elementary (K–7), 5025 12 Avenue; Pebble Hill Traditional Elementary (K–7), 246 52A Street; and South Delta Secondary (8–12), 750 53 Street. Check the catchment for a specific address with the school district.
Status (as of November 3, 2026): the ori: Status: the original rezoning application (October 2024) proposed about 1,433 homes; a smaller revised application (September 2025, about 600 homes) was rejected by Delta Council on October 6, 2025, according to the developer's project updates. The project isn't approved.
A seawall has its own rule here: Zoning: Seawalls have their own rule: Zoning Bylaw No. 7600 lets a seawall extend into the front setback on Boundary Bay lots along Beach Grove Road south of 16 Avenue. The bylaw doesn't set a flood construction level for Beach Grove, so ask the City about that.
10 homes, 3 storeys, by Century Group. T: Ten three-storey homes by Century Group. They're fee simple: the developer says the rowhomes are "non-strata, freehold" with no strata fees, so there's no strata corporation or Form B. These are the area's only known fee-simple townhouses.
Where the townhouse stock actually sits:: The townhouses are in two places, neither on the waterfront. The older condos are along 56 Street and 16 Avenue at the Beach Grove edge, and the townhouses are in the new Southlands community at the south end, around Market Avenue, Boundary Bay Road and the Market District, where Century Group is building townhomes, rowhomes and bare-land strata cottages.
Strata townhomes (The Granary): the Form: For The Granary's strata townhomes, the Form B is the key document on a resale: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance after approved spending, and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report, provided within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. On a presale, the developer's disclosure statement comes first.
ALR edges (Southlands farms): Southlands: Southlands is next to working farmland. ALR homes can't be stratified, which is why housing next to the farms is set up the way it is. Farm tax status needs farm income of $10,000 on under 0.8 ha, $2,500 on 0.8–4 ha, or $2,500 plus 5% of the land value over 4 ha.
High Street Rowhomes — Southlands Drive: High Street Rowhomes, Southlands Drive and Boundary Bay Road: 10 three-storey fee-simple homes by Century Group; the developer says they're "non-strata, freehold" with no strata fees. Each is a house on its own lot, with no strata corporation or Form B.
The Granary (townhome portion) — Market: The Granary, in the Market District at Red Barn Boulevard and Market Avenue, is strata: 19 walk-up townhomes, plus 16 garden flats counted with the condos; the strata fee in the presale marketing is the developer's estimate. Heirloom Townhomes in Southlands is a sold-out group of 33 townhouses and duplexes; sources don't say which are strata. Centennial Green is also in Southlands.
Beach Grove waterfront lots — fee-simple: Beach Grove waterfront lots are large fee-simple lots: 1728 Beach Grove Road, for example, is zoned RD2 (Duplex/Single Detached Residential 2), a zone the bylaw sets aside for Beach Grove waterfront lots, with a 4,000 m² minimum for new lots. RD2, RD3 and RS1–RS3 all have 4,000 m² minimums, so east-side lots, especially on the water, are much larger than in the town centre, where RS4 (610 m²) through RS7 (335 m²) apply. Check the zone for a specific lot.
Where land actually sits, in two systems: Land here falls into two groups: the large fee-simple waterfront and detached lots of Beach Grove and the Boundary Bay shore, and the Southlands community at the south end (Market Avenue and Boundary Bay Road), a former farm property being built in phases. The 56 Street and 16 Avenue corridor between them is built-out condos, not land.
Dyke / flood frame: the east side faces: Dikes and flooding: the east side faces Boundary Bay behind the Boundary Bay dike, and Delta maintains over 63 km of flood protection, 31 pump stations and about 538 km of drainage. The Province owns nearly all the saltwater foreshore and leases or licenses it through FrontCounter BC, and private moorage needs provincial permission, so a "private dock" isn't land the seller owns.
Bare-land strata rules (apply to Beachco: Strata rules apply to Beachcomber Cottages lots and any strata phase in Southlands: the Form B (fees, amounts owing, approved levies, contingency reserve balance, insurance, rules, budget and latest depreciation report) must be provided within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. Stratas with 5 or more lots need a depreciation report every 5 years (new stratas follow a first-report timeline), and at least 10% of the budget must go into the reserve. Rental bans are void (short-term rentals can still be limited), and only 55+ age bylaws are valid. None of this applies to the High Street homes, which have no strata, Form B or fees.
Presales (REDMA) — live in Southlands: a: Southlands has presales: the developer must give you a disclosure statement, you can cancel within 7 days of signing or receiving it (whichever is later), and deposits are held in trust.
GST — land and new homes, CRA level only: GST on land and new homes: most sales of vacant land by individuals for personal use are GST-exempt, but business sales and lots from a subdivision of more than two parts can be taxable, so developer lots generally are. A new Southlands home pays GST, with the first-time buyers' rebate (law since March 13, 2026; all the GST up to $1 million, maximum $50,000, phasing out at $1.5 million, for agreements from March 20, 2025 to 2031) for new homes, not bare land, and the GST New Housing Rebate (36%, up to $6,300, phasing out between $350,000 and $450,000). The Home Buyers' Plan allows $60,000, an FHSA $8,000 a year up to $40,000, and CMHC premiums run 0.6%–4.5%.
Landmarks and services: Boundary Bay Reg: Landmarks and services: Boundary Bay Regional Park and Centennial Beach (570 Boundary Bay Road), with the Dyke, Savannah and Raptor trails and Cammidge House; Tsawwassen Library (1321A 56 Street); South Delta Recreation Centre (1720 56 Street); Thrifty Foods at Tsawwassen Town Centre; and Delta Hospital (5800 Mountain View Boulevard, Ladner, 24/7 emergency). BC Ferries crossings take 1 hour 35 minutes to Swartz Bay and 2 hours to Duke Point. Bus 601's Boundary Bay trips run via 12 Avenue, Boundary Bay Road, 3 Avenue and 67 Street to 1A Avenue, then via South Delta Exchange and Ladner Exchange to Bridgeport Station.
Zoning / OCP / hazard frame: OCP Bylaw N: Zoning, plans and hazards: Delta's Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 8400, 2024) designates farmland "Agriculture (A)". 1728 Beach Grove Road is zoned RD2, the zone for Beach Grove waterfront lots, with a 4,000 m² minimum for new lots; on Boundary Bay lots along Beach Grove Road south of 16 Avenue, a seawall can extend into the front setback, and the bylaw sets no Beach Grove flood construction level. The Boundary Bay Foreshore and Southlands hazard permit area (SD3) requires living space at least 2.9 m above datum, ground around buildings at least 2.3 m, and no building within 7.5 m of the tidal boundary; check DeltaMap for whether a lot is inside it. The foreshore is provincial Crown land, so moorage is leased or licensed, never owned. The east side is behind the Boundary Bay dike, part of the City's 63 km of flood protection.
Directory records: Royal Oaks — pets all: From building directories: Royal Oaks and Heron Cove allow pets with restrictions; Windgrove's directory says pets with restrictions, but one listing calls it pet friendly with no size limit.
Off the Form B, not the listing: the cer: From the Form B, not the listing: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the budget and latest depreciation report. Since July 1, 2024, stratas with five or more lots must update that report every five years, which is what lets you compare an older building's fee fairly.
Tenure. The Granary is strata product (t: The difference is ownership. The Granary is strata (the presale marketing gives an estimated strata fee), so it has strata fees, bylaws, a Form B on resale and a depreciation report. The High Street Rowhomes are non-strata freehold, with no strata fees or documents. Same community, opposite paperwork.
Schools: Beach Grove Elementary, K–7, Sc: Schools: Beach Grove Elementary (K–7, SD37), 5955 17A Avenue; Southpointe Academy (K–12, independent), 1900 56 Street; and South Delta Secondary (8–12, SD37), 750 53 Street. Check the catchment for a specific address with the Delta School District.
Hobby acreage vs working-farm ground: no: Hobby acreage or working farm: to keep BC Assessment farm status, a property must keep meeting the minimum farm income, which goes up with the size of the farm, and that affects its value.
Subdivision of farm land (Delta zones):: Subdividing farmland: in Delta's A1 zone, subdivision is allowed only if it fits the Official Community Plan and is approved by the Agricultural Land Commission where the ALR applies, with an 8 ha minimum for new lots (except a home-site severance under the Commission's policy). A2 also has an 8 ha minimum, and A3 doesn't allow subdivision.
Water: the provincial GWELLS application: Water: wells and aquifers are listed in the provincial well database; well reports must be filed within 90 days of a well being built, changed or closed, and older wells may not be listed. Domestic groundwater use doesn't need a licence, but other uses, including irrigation, need a water licence.
The fringe is two different rulebooks st: The edge of Tsawwassen has two sets of rules: a drive toward Ladner crosses Delta properties designated Agriculture (A) under the Official Community Plan, and where a property is in the ALR, the Agricultural Land Commission's housing, subdivision and no-strata rules apply on top. Check a specific property on the Commission's map to see which rules apply; the area name won't tell you.
Services are south or on the corridor: S: Services are to the south or along Canoe Pass Way: South Delta Recreation Centre (1720 56 Street, at South Delta Exchange), Tsawwassen Library (1321A 56 Street), Thrifty Foods at Tsawwassen Town Centre, and Fraser Health's South Delta After-Hours Urgent and Primary Care Centre (1826–4949 Canoe Pass Way).
More City-side product is in the pipelin: More homes are coming on the City side of the same street: a townhouse project at 4800 Springs Boulevard (with part of 5133 Springs Boulevard) is on the City's housing projects map. Check it before paying extra for Tsawwassen First Nation leasehold on the basis that "nothing else is coming".
Boardwalk, including Boardwalk6 — Tsawwa: Boardwalk, including Boardwalk6, on Tsawwassen First Nation land, by Aquilini and TFSI Development: Boardwalk6 is 22 park-side townhomes sold as "Leasehold via a 99-year prepaid lease", with the First Nation leasing the land to the developer, who subleases to homeowners for 99 years. You buy a leasehold interest, not fee-simple title to the land.
Tsawwassen Landing — 4738 Hemlock Way, b: Tsawwassen Landing, 4738 Hemlock Way, by Onni Group: townhouses and single-family homes on Tsawwassen First Nation land (Tsawwassen Drive North and Hemlock Way), completed in 2022. It's under the First Nation's jurisdiction, not City of Delta zoning, and is leasehold, not fee simple; read the lease for a specific unit before relying on any details.
Tsawwassen Shores generally: the wider T: The wider Tsawwassen Shores development, over 1,500 homes including townhouses according to one neighbourhood source, is leasehold on treaty land. A property on Tsawwassen First Nation land isn't a freehold lot.
SSMUH (City side only): Bylaws 8394 and: Small-scale housing (City side only): Bylaws 8394 and 8395, adopted June 24, 2024, allow four units on all residential properties in Delta and six within 400 m of frequent transit on Scott Road in North Delta. Extra units don't create new lots, and these rules don't apply on Tsawwassen First Nation land. Subdivision and servicing on the City side follow Development and Subdivision Standards Bylaw No. 8288 (2024).
If a strata purchase is made on the City: If you buy a strata home on the City side (Springs Boulevard), BC strata rules apply: check the Form B and depreciation report (required every 5 years for stratas with 5 or more lots); at least 10% of the budget must go into the reserve; rental bans are void; and only 55+ age bylaws are valid, so a "45+" listing line isn't enforceable. None of this applies to a fee-simple lot.
Schools: Pebble Hill Traditional Element: Schools: Pebble Hill Traditional Elementary (K–7, SD37), 246 52A Street; South Delta Secondary (8–12, SD37), 750 53 Street; and Southpointe Academy (K–12, independent), 1900 56 Street. Check the catchment for a specific address with the Delta School District.
At Boardwalk, the developer states homes: At Boardwalk, the developer says homes are bought on a 99-year lease and cost much less than comparable freehold. The homes are on Tsawwassen Lands, where Tsawwassen First Nation governs land management, so rely on the lease documents, not a listing summary, for whether the lease is prepaid and for any ground rent and taxes.
Nearby areas: Ladner across Canoe Pass t: Nearby: Ladner across Canoe Pass to the east, Tsawwassen to the south, and Steveston (Richmond) across the Fraser River's south arm to the north. Port Guichon is in Ladner, not Tsawwassen or Westham Island.
Alaksen is four islands joined by dykes:: Alaksen National Wildlife Area, 349 ha on Westham Island, was set up in 1976 and is mainly four former delta islands joined by causeways and dikes. It's part of the Fraser River Delta Ramsar Site and an Important Bird Area, run by the Canadian Wildlife Service, and open 8 a.m. to 3 p.m., Monday to Friday except holidays. Part of it overlaps the George C. Reifel Migratory Bird Sanctuary; both are entered from Robertson Road (the wildlife area at 5421 and the sanctuary at 5191).
The usual duplex form: Delta's SSMUH zon: Duplexes: Delta's small-scale housing zoning allows up to 4 units on single-detached and duplex lots, and the City supports coach houses, garden suites and secondary suites, but on ALR land the Agricultural Land Commission's rules come first. The island is farmland: more than 700 hectares growing seed potatoes (over 25% of B.C.'s), vegetables, berries, forage and pasture, plus fruit, honey and livestock. For example, 2194 Westham Island Road (Reynelda Farms) is a 65.2 ha property zoned Agriculture (A1) and entirely in the ALR. Any duplex-style building on the island would be on a single farm property under those rules.
Thin and slow-turning in the most recent: Few sales lately: in September 2026, 28 detached homes were listed in Anmore and none sold, with no condos or townhomes listed. Across Port Moody that month, 15 detached homes and 29 condos and townhomes sold.
Belcarra sets its own tax rates: the 202: Belcarra sets its own tax rates: 2026 rates are in Village of Belcarra Tax Rates Bylaw No. 641-2026, and 2025 rates were in Bylaw No. 634. The Province's figures put Belcarra's total 2025 residential rate at 3.38873 per $1,000 of assessed value.
A total of 131 three- and four-bedroom T: 131 three- and four-bedroom Tudor-style row homes on the south-facing side of Burke Mountain, completed in spring 2020. A listing at 3552 Victoria Drive shows a freehold strata townhouse built in 2020; one other listing says 2018, because the project was built in phases. Check any rental or pet restrictions on the Form B.
YOU OWN YOUR LOT!\" and \"no strata fee!: Listings for these rowhomes say "YOU OWN YOUR LOT!" and "no strata fee!" (units at 3416 Roxton Avenue, built 2018, and 3406 Roxton Avenue, built 2020). Presale directories call them "Roxton at Leigh Park" and "Roxton Row". With no strata, there's no Form B or strata fees; check the title, City rules and any registered covenants.
Form B diligence (all 9 counted strata c: For the nine strata complexes, and the two presales once they're registered as stratas, read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. Rental and pet lines in listings aren't the bylaws; the Form B and registered bylaws are what count.
City zoning and plan: Zoning Bylaw No. 3: Zoning and plans: Coquitlam's Zoning Bylaw No. 3000 (1996) has small-scale residential zones R-1, R-2 and R-3, with minimum new lots of 650 m² and 18.5 m wide (R-1 and R-3) or 465 m² and 12.5 m wide (R-2). The Interim Official Community Plan (Bylaws 5511 and 5512, adopted April 27, 2026) replaced the old OCP, and the Burke Mountain neighbourhood plans (Hyde Creek, Smiling Creek and Partington Creek) and the Northwest Burke Vision sit under it.
Watercourse check — doubled reach on the: Creeks: in Northeast Coquitlam, a watercourse development permit can apply within 50 metres of the top of any creek bank (30 metres elsewhere in Coquitlam), and the zoning bylaw sets flood and streamside setbacks. Several complexes are between creeks (Kentwell between Burke Mountain Creek and Smiling Creek, Secret Ridge between two greenbelt creeks, and Rocklin on the Creek beside a protected creek), so check the setbacks for a specific property.
No. Rocklin on the Creek (1220 Rocklin S: No. Rocklin on the Creek (1220 Rocklin Street, by Woodbridge, built 2021, freehold strata) is finished; Rocklin (1295 Rocklin Street, by StreetSide) is under construction, expected late 2026. Different builders, addresses and paperwork (a Form B for one, a disclosure statement for the other).
Creek/slope position: the Watercourse Pr: Creeks and slopes: in Northeast Coquitlam, a watercourse development permit can apply within 50 metres of the top of any creek bank (30 metres elsewhere in Coquitlam), and the zoning bylaw sets flood and streamside setbacks.
Market context: SnapStats covers Coquitl: Market figures for Coquitlam as a whole (there are no separate figures for land or for this area): the detached median was $1,455,000 ($550 per sq ft, 97% of list price, 35 days on the market), and the condo and townhome median $625,000 ($687 per sq ft, 96% of list, 23 days).
Zoning — Zoning Bylaw No. 3000, 1996: sm: Zoning: Coquitlam's Zoning Bylaw No. 3000 (1996) has small-scale residential zones R-1, R-2 and R-3, with their minimum lot sizes, plus flood and streamside setbacks.
Subdivision + servicing — Subdivision an: Subdivision and servicing: minimum lot sizes come from the zone, and servicing follows Bylaw No. 3558 (2003), which requires the owner to provide rights-of-way for the services a subdivision or development needs and to pay for City-installed traffic and street-name signs before subdivision approval or a building permit. Check the requirements for a specific property with the City.
Schools: Coast Salish Elementary, grades: Schools (SD43 Coquitlam): Coast Salish Elementary (K–5), 3538 Sheffield Avenue; Smiling Creek Elementary (K–5), 3456 Princeton Avenue; and Minnekhada Middle (6–8), 1390 Laurier Avenue, Port Coquitlam. Check the catchment for a specific address with the school district.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates:: There are no townhouses in Canyon Heights. The District's townhouses and condos are in its centres, Lynn Valley Town Centre, Lions Gate Village and Edgemont Village, all outside Canyon Heights; Edgemont is right next door.
Main streets and transit: Highland Boule: Roads and transit: Highland Boulevard is the main road, with routes 246 and 232; Capilano Road on the west side has routes 232 and 236 to Grouse Mountain and south to Marine Drive and the Lions Gate Bridge; and the Upper Levels Highway is reached via Capilano Road or Edgemont Boulevard. Taxes/rebates/financing: PTT 1% on first: Taxes, rebates and financing: property transfer tax is 1% on the first $200,000, 2% up to $2 million and 3% above, plus another 2% on the residential part above $3 million. First-time buyers are exempt on the first $500,000 for homes up to $835,000, with a partial exemption up to $860,000; the newly built home exemption is full up to $1,100,000 and ends at $1,150,000. For example, at $715,000 (Port Moody's September 2026 condo and townhome median) with no exemption, the tax is $2,000 + $10,300 = $12,300. The first-time buyers' GST rebate (law since March 13, 2026) covers all the GST on a new home up to $1 million (maximum $50,000), phasing out at $1.5 million, for agreements from March 20, 2025 to 2031; the GST New Housing Rebate is 36% up to $6,300 (phasing out between $350,000 and $450,000). The Home Buyers' Plan allows $60,000, an FHSA $8,000 a year up to $40,000, and CMHC premiums run 0.6%–4.5%. GST applies to new homes, not resales, and Vancouver's Empty Homes Tax doesn't apply.

Property transfer tax — worked example (: Property transfer tax example: on a $1,000,000 house and lot with no exemption, the tax is 1% of the first $200,000 ($2,000) plus 2% of the rest ($16,000), or $18,000. The District's 32-lot waterfront assembl: The District has been buying Ambleside waterfront lots since 1975 for a continuous public waterfront. On March 31, 2025, it announced it had bought the last one, 1444 Argyle Avenue, the 32nd lot, for Brissenden Waterfront Park, which connects Ambleside Park to John Lawson Park. The Ambleside Waterfront Concept Plan (2016) links John Lawson Park, Millennium Park, Brissenden Waterfront Park and Ambleside Green, and the District's waterfront principles call public ownership from 13th to 18th Streets a community value. These lots are off the private market for good.
Civic core, inside the sub-area: West Va: Civic centre, in the area: West Vancouver Community Centre and Aquatic Centre (2121 Marine Drive), West Vancouver Memorial Library (1950 Marine Drive), Municipal Hall, the Seniors' Activity Centre (695 21st Street), and police and fire services, all in and around the town centre. The Official Community Plan makes Ambleside the District's town centre, with Marine Drive as West Vancouver's main street. Lions Gate Hospital (231 East 15th Street, North Vancouver) serves the North Shore.
No. Park Royal is the neighbouring sub-a: No. Park Royal is the neighbouring area east across Taylor Way; the four townhomes in the Executive on the Park presale are in Park Royal, and part of Park Royal is on Capilano Reserve No. 5 land, so check the ownership type before treating anything there as fee-simple.
District zoning and plan (not Burnaby's): Zoning and plans (West Vancouver, not Burnaby): Zoning Bylaw No. 4662 (2010) sets minimum site areas for the RS single-family zones of 8,094 m² in RS1, 1,625 m² in RS2, 975 m² in RS3 and RS10, 731 m² in RS4 and 488 m² in RS5. The Official Community Plan is Bylaw No. 4985 (2018), and Council adopted an amendment (Bylaw No. 5406, 2025) to match the Interim Housing Needs Report.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates:: There are no townhouses in Bayridge: homes are single-family houses in the RS zones on the slope above Marine Drive and on the waterfront streets, with secondary suites and detached secondary suites allowed.
There is no strata townhouse stock in Ba: There are no strata townhouses in Bayridge today; anything sold as "in Bayridge" is probably in another area. For any strata purchase, read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page.
District zoning and plan: Zoning Bylaw N: Zoning and plans: under Zoning Bylaw No. 4662 (2010), the RS single-family zones have minimum site areas of 8,094 m² in RS1, 1,625 m² in RS2, 975 m² in RS3 and RS10, 731 m² in RS4 and 488 m² in RS5, and allow secondary suites and detached secondary suites; lots can have up to 4 homes, or 6 within 400 metres of a designated bus stop. The Official Community Plan is Bylaw No. 4985 (2018), amended in 2025 (Bylaw No. 5406) to match the Interim Housing Needs Report.
No named bare-land development, assembly: I don't know of any development sites, land assemblies or rezoning proposals in Bayridge, and there's no Bayridge area plan. The only recent change is District-wide: the 2025 Official Community Plan amendment (Bylaw No. 5406) to match the Interim Housing Needs Report.
Parks: Benbow Park, 3151 Westmount Place: Parks: Benbow Park (3151 Westmount Place) and West Bay Park (3482 Marine Drive, on the waterfront) are in the area. Recreation is at West Vancouver Community Centre and Aquatic Centre (2121 Marine Drive, Ambleside), and the library is West Vancouver Memorial Library (1950 Marine Drive). Health care: Lions Gate Hospital (231 East 15th Street, North Vancouver) and West Vancouver Community Health Centre (2121 Marine Drive).
Zoning — Zoning Bylaw No. 4662, 2010: th: Zoning (Bylaw No. 4662, 2010): the RS single-family zones allow secondary suites and detached secondary suites, which must be registered with the District, and lots can have up to 4 homes, or 6 within 400 metres of a designated bus stop.
SSMUH / added units as the District stat: Extra units: RS lots can have a secondary suite and a detached secondary suite (registration required), and up to 4 homes, or 6 near a designated bus stop. Eligibility depends on the lot, so check with the District before paying for suite potential.
Hazard Development Permits (District fra: Hazard permits: a foreshore development permit for work in the foreshore area (waterfront property or other land at risk of coastal flooding), an environmental development permit for work within 15 metres of the top of any creek bank, and a wildfire development permit for work within about 100 metres of undisturbed forest. On Marine Drive waterfront lots, the foreshore permit is the one to check.
A 3-storey, 31-unit low-rise; the buildi: A three-storey, 31-unit low-rise with an elevator, in-suite laundry, storage and a hot tub. The directory says it was built in 1989, but current listings say 1992. One listing mentions freehold strata title, a clubhouse, exercise centre and recreation facilities. The directory lists age restrictions, pets allowed with restrictions and no rentals; one listing puts it as "no rentals except to immediate family", but rental bans have been void since November 24, 2022.
GEOGRAPHY / MLS-CLASSIFICATION FLAG: thi: This new Anthem community is at the area's south edge, and listings split it between Blueridge NV and Windsor Park NV. It's a 6.25-acre planned community by Anthem Properties; one project source says 119 condos, 133 townhomes and 89 rental apartments when finished, and another says 341 homes in total. Listings show the garden flats as wood-frame freehold strata condos built in 2026. Because homes are completing in 2026, early purchases may still be on developer contracts, with presale rules.
Anchors inside and beside the area: Blue: In and beside the area: Blueridge Elementary (2650 Bronte Drive) and Seymour Heights Elementary (2640 Carnation Street) are in the neighbourhood; Windsor Secondary (931 Broadview Drive) is just beside it; Parkgate Village, Parkgate Community Centre (3625 Banff Court) and the Parkgate library (3675 Banff Court) are to the northeast; and Mount Seymour Provincial Park rises behind.
Municipality, stated first because it de: Blueridge is in the District of North Vancouver, so the District's Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 7900) and Zoning Bylaw No. 3210 apply, not the City of North Vancouver's bylaws.
Where the stock sits: detached houses ac: Homes are mostly detached houses. The only condo building is Berkley Terraces on Berkley Road, and the only townhomes are part of Baden Park at the south edge on Lytton Street at Mount Seymour Parkway. Other condos and townhomes are near Parkgate Village and along Mount Seymour Parkway, outside the area.
Form B diligence (strata purchases — Ber: For Berkley Terraces or a Baden Park strata unit, read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. For a 2026 Baden Park unit, find out first whether it's a developer sale (disclosure statement) or a resale (Form B).
District plans and zoning — the DISTRICT: District plans and zoning: the District of North Vancouver's Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 7900) and Zoning Bylaw No. 3210, Section 525. R1 lots must be at least 4,000 m², 30 m wide and 34 m deep, and R2 lots 660 m², 18 m wide and 34 m deep, with variations R2(S1) at 335 m² and 10 m wide, R2(S2) at 1,100 m² and 24 m, and R2(S3) at 4,000 m² and 30 m. An R2 lot allows a house, a secondary suite and a coach house. The Seymour Local Plan keeps Blueridge mostly single-family.
SSMUH / suites as the District states th: Suites and extra units: since June 2024, the District allows a house, a secondary suite and a coach house (three units) on all single-family lots inside its urban boundary. The District's GEOweb map shows eligible lots allowing up to 3 units at 280 m² or less, up to 4 on larger lots, and up to 6 on larger lots within 400 m of a frequent bus stop. A suite or coach house is a second unit on a house lot, not a townhouse.
District taxes: District of North Vancou: District taxes: 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty after July 2 and another 5% after September 1. The 2026 residential municipal rate is 1.83419 and the total residential rate 3.28195 per $1,000 of assessed value. Single-family utilities total $2,571.20 in 2026 (water $932.80; sewer and drainage $1,255.60).
Lot character from the zone ladder, as s: Lot sizes (District Zoning Bylaw 3210, Section 525): R1 lots must be at least 4,000 m², 30 m wide and 34 m deep; R2 lots 660 m², 18 m wide and 34 m deep, with variations R2(S1) at 335 m² and 10 m wide, R2(S2) at 1,100 m² and 24 m, and R2(S3) at 4,000 m² and 30 m. These are minimums, not actual lot sizes; check a specific lot's zone on the District's GeoWeb.
Parks, recreation and services: Mount Se: Parks, recreation and services: Mount Seymour Provincial Park (established 1936) rises behind the Seymour area, with hiking and mountain-bike trails (Baden-Powell and Old Buck) and the Mt Seymour ski area (39 runs, 12 lit for night skiing). Parkgate Community Centre (3625 Banff Court) and the Parkgate library (3675 Banff Court) are to the northeast, and Ron Andrews Community Recreation Centre (931 Lytton Street) is beside Windsor Secondary to the south. Northlands Golf Course (3400 Anne Macdonald Way) is public and District-owned; Seymour Golf & Country Club (3723 Mount Seymour Parkway) is private. Health care: Lions Gate Hospital (231 East 15th Street) and the North Vancouver Urgent and Primary Care Centre (2nd floor, 221 West Esplanade). Parkgate Village is Seymour's shopping centre.
Zoning — District Zoning Bylaw No. 3210,: Zoning (District Zoning Bylaw No. 3210, Section 525): an R2 lot allows a house, a secondary suite and a coach house. Since June 2024, all single-family lots inside the District's urban boundary can have those three units.
Hazard Development Permits (District fra: Hazard permits: the District's plan has development permit areas for slopes, creeks, streamsides, wildfire and natural environment. On Berkley-side lots, check the Berkley escarpment first: a landslide on January 19, 2005 led to ongoing management, and the risk assessment was updated in 2026. Pull the hazard layers on GeoWeb and budget for a geotechnical report before pricing a renovation or rebuild.
Schools: Seymour Heights Elementary, K–7: Schools (SD44 North Vancouver): Seymour Heights Elementary (K–7), 2640 Carnation Street; Blueridge Elementary (K–7), 2650 Bronte Drive; and Seycove Secondary Community (8–12), 1204 Caledonia Avenue. Check the catchment for a specific address with the school district.
The building directory states 1989; curr: The building directory says 1989, and current listings say 1992. Check the year in the strata plan and Form B before relying on either for warranty, insurance or depreciation report timing.
City side — plans and zoning (south of H: City side (south of Highway 1): the City of North Vancouver's Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 8400, 2014, amended December 8, 2025) and Zoning Bylaw No. 6700 apply. The Ground Oriented Zone, adopted December 8, 2025, allows up to 3 units on lots of 280 m² or less, up to 4 on larger lots in Low Rise Neighbourhood 1, and up to 6 in Low Rise Neighbourhood 2 or Residential Level 4, raising the limit from 3 to 4 units on nearly 4,300 properties. Grand Boulevard is also a heritage character area, so frontage and character rules, not just zoning, shape what can be built facing the boulevard.
Why this section exists on a zero-stock: There are no strata complexes on the Boulevard itself. The strata rules below matter if you widen your search to a townhouse in Central Lonsdale or Lynn Valley; for a house on the Boulevard, the fee-simple rules and the City-or-District split that follow apply, and which side of Highway 1 the lot is on changes its minimum lot sizes, taxes and permit areas.
Form B diligence (any strata purchase of: For any strata purchase nearby, read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. It doesn't apply to Chesterfield Manor, where you buy shares, or to a house on the Boulevard.
SSMUH as each municipality states it: Ci: Extra units depend on the municipality: on the City side, the Ground Oriented Zone allows 3, 4 or 6 units by lot size and designation; on the District side, an R2 lot can have a house, a secondary suite and a coach house (three units) inside the urban boundary since June 2024.
Tax timing — both municipalities, differ: Taxes differ by municipality. District side: 2026 taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty after July 2 and another 5% after September 1; the residential municipal rate is 1.83419 and the total 3.28195 per $1,000, and single-family utilities total $2,571.20. Check the municipality on title before comparing.
Two rulebooks, one corridor — read the s: Two sets of rules on one street, so read the side that matches the title. City side: the City of North Vancouver's Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 8400, amended December 8, 2025) and Zoning Bylaw No. 6700. District side: the District of North Vancouver's Official Community Plan (Bylaw 7900) and Zoning Bylaw 3210. Neither applies on the other side of Highway 1.
Bare-land strata rules (the 1555 Grand B: If title shows 1555 Grand Boulevard is a bare-land strata, BC strata rules apply: check the Form B (fees, amounts owing, levies, contingency reserve balance and insurance; within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page). Stratas with 5 or more lots need a depreciation report every 5 years (check the lot count on the strata plan), and at least 10% of the budget must go into the reserve. Rental bans are void (short-term rentals can still be limited), and the only valid age bylaw is 55 and older, so a "45+" listing line isn't enforceable.
Property taxes — stated per side: City s: Property taxes by side. District side: 2026 taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty after July 2 and another 5% after September 1; the residential municipal rate is 1.83419 and the total 3.28195 per $1,000, and single-family utilities total $2,571.20.
The nearest known age-restricted strata: The nearest age-restricted strata building to Braemar, listed in Delbrook: built 1997, three storeys, described in listings as a boutique 22-unit "55+ community". Building sources list age restrictions, pets and rentals allowed; listings allow two pets, cats or dogs, and mention secure parking, storage, a clubhouse, workshop, exercise centre and bike room. Check the registered bylaw wording in the strata documents.
Nearest Kiwanis seniors rentals, outside: The nearest Kiwanis seniors rentals are outside the area, on Whiteley Court toward Capilano: the Kiwanis North Shore Housing Society's below-market independent-living apartments for adults 55 and older include Lynn Manor (2555 Whiteley Court, for applicants 65 and older) and Lynn Woods (2551 Whiteley Court, 60 and older for its deepest-subsidy units). Applicants must be able to live independently, be non-smokers and meet income and asset limits; North Shore residents get preference, and pets aren't allowed.
Housing form: detached houses on the Dis: Homes are detached houses in the District's R1 and R2 zones (Zoning Bylaw 3210). I don't know of any condo buildings, townhome complexes or seniors residences in Braemar.
If a strata townhouse is ever found in B: If a strata townhouse ever comes up in Braemar, read the Form B: it shows the fees, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page.
Fee-simple reality in Braemar: the stock: Braemar is fee-simple detached houses, with no strata, Form B or strata fees; District rules (Zoning Bylaw 3210) and any registered covenants apply. The R2 zone allows a house with a secondary suite plus a coach house; since December 2023, a suite can be up to 49% of the house with no minimum size, and coach houses can be two storeys.
Serviced vs unserviced: District single-: Services: Braemar is on District water and sewer; 2026 single-family utilities total $2,571.20 (water $932.80; sewer and drainage $1,255.60).
Roads and transit: Mahon Avenue and Delb: Roads and transit: Mahon Avenue and Delbrook Avenue are the main north–south roads, West Queens Road crosses the south side, and Lonsdale Avenue to the west leads south to Lonsdale Quay and the SeaBus and north to the Upper Levels Highway. Route 249 (Delbrook / Lonsdale Quay) runs through the area via Delbrook Avenue and West Queens Road; route 230 runs on Lonsdale Avenue; and route 241 runs via Lonsdale Avenue, Rockland Road, Prospect Avenue and Balmoral Avenue, then over the Lions Gate Bridge downtown. The SeaBus reaches Waterfront Station in 12 minutes, every 15 minutes during the day.
Strata block: Form B diligence (fees, am: Strata rules: check the Form B (fees, amounts owing, levies, contingency reserve balance and insurance; within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page). Stratas with 5 or more lots need a depreciation report every 5 years, at least 10% of the budget must go into the reserve, rental bans are void, and only 55+ age bylaws are valid, so a "45+" listing line isn't enforceable. Strata disputes can go to the Civil Resolution Tribunal.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates:: The townhouses are in two pockets: Whitby Estates (Garden Court and Highgrove Mews) in Chartwell, and the Hawksley podium on Uplands Way in the Rodgers Creek lands. The original subdivision below is detached houses, and the District's plan directs growth to the town and village centres, not into the Properties.
District plans and zoning: District of W: Plans and zoning: the District of West Vancouver's Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 4985, 2018) and Zoning Bylaw No. 4662 (2010). Houses in the original subdivision are in the RS single-family zones, and the Rodgers Creek lands have site-specific zoning (CD3). Lots can have up to 4 homes, or 6 within 400 metres of a designated bus stop.
Established-bench estate lots: detached: Estate lots: detached houses on large hillside lots in the RS single-family zones of Zoning Bylaw No. 4662. The original subdivision is mostly freehold detached; strata homes are in the Rodgers Creek and Uplands development above it and the small Whitby Estates pockets.
Zoning — Zoning Bylaw No. 4662, 2010: or: Zoning (Bylaw No. 4662, 2010): houses in the original subdivision are in the RS zones, and the Rodgers Creek lands above have site-specific zoning (CD3). Lots can have up to 4 homes, or 6 within 400 metres of a designated bus stop.
SSMUH / added units as the District stat: Extra units: the RS zones allow a secondary suite and a detached secondary suite, within the limit on homes per lot. Eligibility depends on the lot, so check with the District before paying for suite potential.
Strata block (for the Uplands/Whitby str: If you look at a strata in Uplands or Whitby Estates instead: the Form B must be provided within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page; stratas with 5 or more lots need a depreciation report every 5 years; at least 10% of the budget must go into the reserve; rental bans are void (short-term rentals can still be limited); and only 55+ age bylaws are valid, so a "45+" listing line isn't enforceable.
Schools: Chartwell Elementary, grades K-: Schools (SD45 West Vancouver): Chartwell Elementary (K–7), 1300 Chartwell Drive; Westcot Elementary (K–7), 760 Westcot Road; and Sentinel Secondary (8–12), 1250 Chartwell Drive. Check the catchment for a specific address with the school district.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates:: There are no townhouses in Canterbury. West Vancouver's condos and townhouses are downhill in Ambleside and the village centres, and so are the services: Park Royal and Ambleside on Marine Drive, West Vancouver Community Centre and Aquatic Centre (2121 Marine Drive) and West Vancouver Memorial Library (1950 Marine Drive).
District zoning and plan: houses sit in: Zoning and plans: houses are in the RS single-family zones of West Vancouver's Zoning Bylaw No. 4662 (2010), with minimum site areas of 8,094 m² in RS1, 1,625 m² in RS2, 975 m² in RS3, 731 m² in RS4 and 488 m² in RS5 (RS6 uses the existing lot size), and secondary suites and detached secondary suites allowed. The Official Community Plan is Bylaw No. 4985 (2018).
No condominium building or townhome comp: I don't know of any condo buildings or townhome complexes in Canterbury; homes are freehold detached houses.
Schools beside the corridor: Canyon Heig: Schools near the corridor: Canyon Heights Elementary (4501 Highland Boulevard), Highlands Elementary (3150 Colwood Drive), Cleveland Elementary (1255 Eldon Road) and Handsworth Secondary (1033 Handsworth Road). SD44 has no middle schools (K–7 and 8–12), and catchments are set by address, so check with the district. Capilano Elementary (1230 West 20th Street) shares the name but is in the City of North Vancouver, south of the corridor.
Nearby areas: Canyon Heights and Edgemon: Nearby: Canyon Heights and Edgemont Village to the east, Capilano Highlands and Grousewoods to the north, Norgate and Pemberton Heights below Highway 1 to the southeast, and, across the Capilano River, West Vancouver's Park Royal and Ambleside. Edgemont Village is the nearest shopping; I don't know of any shopping centre or grocery store on Capilano Road itself.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates:: There are no townhouses on the corridor: it's detached houses in the District's R1 and R2 zones, plus one condo building on Capilano Road near Edgemont Village. Edgemont Village, just east, is the nearest shopping.
Form B diligence (Canyon Park and any st: For Canyon Park or any strata you compare nearby, read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. Rental and pet lines in listings aren't the bylaws.
Lot character, as the bylaw states it: R: Lot sizes: R1 lots must be at least 4,000 m², 30 m wide and 34 m deep; R2 lots 660 m², 18 m wide and 34 m deep, with variations R2(S1) at 335 m² and 10 m wide, R2(S2) at 1,100 m² and 24 m, and R2(S3) at 4,000 m² and 30 m. Roads and transit: Capilano Road is the: Roads and transit: Capilano Road is the main road, south to Marine Drive and the Lions Gate Bridge and north to the Cleveland Dam and Grouse Mountain (6400 Nancy Greene Way; the only road up), with a Highway 1 interchange at Capilano Road. Route 236 runs the length of Capilano Road between Grouse Mountain and Lonsdale Quay; route 232 runs via Capilano Road on the east side; and route 246 runs via Capilano Road and Montroyal Boulevard, with downtown trips over the Lions Gate Bridge.
Anchors: Capilano River Regional Park (M: Landmarks: Capilano River Regional Park runs along the river through and above the corridor (Capilano Pacific Trail and Coho Loop Trail); the Cleveland Dam (1954, 91 m high) holds back Capilano Lake above it; and the Capilano River Hatchery (1971) gets about 250,000 visitors a year. Capilano Library (3045 Highland Boulevard) is in Edgemont Village to the east, and Delbrook Community Recreation Centre is at 851 West Queens Road. I don't know of any shopping centre or grocery store on the corridor itself. The nearest hospital is Lions Gate Hospital, 231 East 15th Street, North Vancouver.
Main streets: Marine Drive along the wat: Main streets: Marine Drive along the waterfront; Caulfeild Drive, Keith Road and Headland Drive inside the neighbourhood; and the Upper Levels Highway across the north side. Caulfeild Village Centre is the area's shopping centre.
Where the condo stock concentrates: nowh: There are no condo buildings in Caulfeild; West Vancouver's condos are in Ambleside and Dundarave, to the east. District zoning and plans: West Vancouve: Zoning and plans: West Vancouver's Zoning Bylaw No. 4662 (2010) and Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 4985, 2018). Nearby RS single-family zones have minimum site areas from 488 m² (RS5) to 8,094 m² (RS1).
Main streets: Marine Drive runs along th: Main streets: Marine Drive along the waterfront; Caulfeild Drive, Keith Road and Headland Drive inside the neighbourhood; and the Upper Levels Highway across the north side, east through North Vancouver and west to Horseshoe Bay and Highway 99. Caulfeild Village Centre is the area's shopping centre.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates:: The only townhouses are at Caulfeild Cove, on Marine Drive by the water. District zoning and plan: District of We: Zoning and plans: West Vancouver's Zoning Bylaw No. 4662 (2010) and Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 4985, 2018), which names the Caulfeild Village Centre. The former Caulfeild Land Use Contract area is now zoned CD86 (Caulfeild Zone, 2024), with two residential areas, a commercial area and parks. CD86 lots (the former Land Use Contract: CD86 lots (the former Land Use Contract area): this area is now zoned CD86 (Caulfeild Zone) under a 2024 amendment, with two residential areas, a commercial area and parks. Each lot's minimum size is simply its registered size (no new minimum applies), and Residential Area A allows up to three units per lot. A fee-simple lot has no strata, Form B or strata fees.

Roads and transit: Marine Drive runs alo: Roads and transit: Marine Drive along the waterfront, Caulfeild Drive, Keith Road and Headland Drive inside the neighbourhood, and the Upper Levels Highway across the north side. Zoning + OCP (District): Zoning Bylaw No: Zoning and plans: West Vancouver's Zoning Bylaw No. 4662 (2010), including CD86 (Caulfeild Zone, 2024) for the former Land Use Contract area and the RS zones nearby, and the Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 4985, 2018), which names the Caulfeild Village Centre.

ALR rules (no Caulfeild ALR parcel is co: I don't know of any ALR land in Caulfeild. On ALR land, homes can't be stratified, subdividing needs Agricultural Land Commission approval, the main house can be up to 500 m² with a suite only inside it, and an additional home can be up to 90 m² (40 ha or less) or 186 m² (larger). Farm tax status needs farm income of $10,000 on under 0.8 ha, $2,500 on 0.8–4 ha, or $2,500 plus 5% of the land value over 4 ha, with applications due by October 31.
Townhouse. Listings record Sub-Type Town: Townhouses: listings and the strata directory show 30 three-level wood-frame homes built in 1974, freehold strata, so the Form B and depreciation report matter as for any strata.
Townhouse, and strata: a full listing re: Townhouses, and strata: one listing shows Caulfeild Cove as freehold strata (plan VAS117), and the directory lists 30 three-level wood-frame homes. It's Caulfeild's only strata complex, so read the Form B and depreciation report.

Form B diligence (the 1 counted strata c: For the strata buildings, read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. Fee-simple homes (the side-street house: Fee-simple houses are on the side streets. Note that a home can look detached and still be part of a small strata (like the three-home strata on Bewicke Avenue); the title, not the look of the house, decides which rules apply.
City zoning and plan — the CITY pair onl: City zoning and plans: the City of North Vancouver's Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 8400, 2014, amended December 8, 2025) and Zoning Bylaw No. 6700 (1995). Side streets are in the Ground Oriented Zone, adopted December 8, 2025: lots of 280 m² or less can have up to 3 units, and larger lots up to 4 in Low Rise Neighbourhood 1, or up to 6 in Low Rise Neighbourhood 2 or Residential Level 4. That raised the limit from 3 to 4 units on nearly 4,300 properties and allows up to 6 on about 600. One secondary suite is allowed per single-family property (the owner must live there), and a suite can be combined with a coach house where the front lot line is at least 10 m, with a development permit and building permit.
The corridor's one counted townhouse com: The area's one townhouse complex, The Beeches, is known for a court case: its strata spent years and about $25,000 in legal fees fighting a townhouse used as a 16-bed hostel a block from City Hall. The Civil Resolution Tribunal ordered it shut down in September 2017, and the courts rejected the owner's appeals the next May. Ask about the strata's short-term rental enforcement and legal costs in the Form B and minutes.
Roads and transit: Lonsdale Avenue is th: Roads and transit: Lonsdale Avenue is the main street, south to Lonsdale Quay and the SeaBus and north to the Upper Levels Highway; Keith Road and the numbered streets run east–west. Route 230 runs the length of Lonsdale Avenue from Lonsdale Quay to Upper Lonsdale; the SeaBus reaches Waterfront Station in 12 minutes, every 15 minutes during the day; and the R2 RapidBus runs along 3rd Street and Marine Drive at the south edge, and since September 7, 2026 runs straight through from Park Royal via Lonsdale Quay and Phibbs Exchange to Metrotown Station.

Land status and neighbourhoods: the Nati: Land and neighbourhoods: the Nation has 10 reserves totalling about 2,930 ha, within a traditional territory of about 780,000 hectares. Its Community Housing Plan names four neighbourhoods: Mount Currie Village (IR 1 and IR 10), the centre with the administrative and civic buildings; Xet̓ólacw Village (IR 6), the Upper Community, the largest residential neighbourhood; Lillooet Lake Road (IR 3 and IR 8); and Kwetsa7 (IR 2), the last two more rural. The surrounding Pemberton Valley off reserve is in the Squamish-Lillooet Regional District's Area C. The 2021 Census counted 1,240 people living in Mount Currie, with a median age of 33.2.
How ownership actually works here (the o: How ownership works here, following the Nation's "Five Steps to Home Ownership on Reserve": (1) meet the Housing Manager; (2) get a land encumbrance check from the Lands Department confirming a serviced lot is available and registered to you; (3) get a Band Council Resolution, with the Council guaranteeing the loan; (4) check for housing subsidies from Indigenous Services Canada; and (5) get a Ministerial Loan Guarantee and bank financing. Because of those guarantees, regular mortgage and foreclosure rules don't work the way they do off reserve. The Nation estimates modest new homes at about $250–$300 per sq ft including water, sewer and hydro hookups, and modular homes (CSA Z-240) at about $160–$180 per sq ft installed, built to zone 6 standards with a roof snow load of 136 lb per sq ft.
Form B — does not exist here: Off reserv: There's no Form B here: there are no stratas and no resale market in Mount Currie. For a citizen, the equivalent check is the Lands Department's land encumbrance check in the five steps above.
Rental and age bylaws — provincial strat: Strata rental and age rules don't apply here: off reserve, rental bans are void and only 55+ age bylaws are allowed, but Mount Currie has no strata corporations, so there are no 55+ stratas, and rental housing is band housing run by the Nation.

No strata frame on this area: there is n: There are no strata corporations, Form Bs, strata fees, reserve funds or depreciation reports for any home in this community.
Taxes and rebates (off-reserve compariso: Taxes and rebates if you buy off reserve, such as in Pemberton: property transfer tax is 1% on the first $200,000, 2% up to $2 million and 3% above, plus another 2% on the residential part above $3 million. First-time buyers are exempt on the first $500,000 for homes up to $835,000, with a partial exemption up to $860,000; the newly built home exemption is full up to $1,100,000 and ends at $1,150,000. The first-time buyers' GST rebate (law since March 13, 2026) covers all the GST on a new home up to $1 million (maximum $50,000), phasing out at $1.5 million, for agreements from March 20, 2025 to 2031; the GST New Housing Rebate is 36% up to $6,300 (phasing out between $350,000 and $450,000). The Home Buyers' Plan allows $60,000, an FHSA $8,000 a year up to $40,000, and CMHC premiums run 0.6%–4.5%. GST applies to new homes, not resales.
What a \"lot\" means here — the Nation's: What a "lot" means here: a citizen gets a lot through the Nation's "Five Steps to Home Ownership on Reserve": (1) meet the Housing Manager; (2) get a land encumbrance check from the Lands Department confirming a serviced lot is available and registered to you; (3) get a Band Council Resolution, with the Council guaranteeing the loan; (4) check for Indigenous Services Canada housing subsidies; and (5) get a Ministerial Loan Guarantee and bank financing. Serviced lots are allocated and registered through that process; they're never listed, priced or sold on the open market.
Land use — no municipal zoning bylaw for: There's no municipal zoning on the reserve lands; land is allocated through the Nation's Lands Department and Band Council. The off-reserve valley is in the regional district's Area C, and the Village of Pemberton's bylaws cover Pemberton only; neither applies to reserve land.
Taxes and rebates (off-reserve compariso: Taxes and rebates if you buy off reserve, such as in Pemberton: property transfer tax is 1% to $200,000, 2% to $2 million and 3% above, plus another 2% on the residential part over $3 million. On a $900,000 home with no exemption, that's $2,000 + $14,000 = $16,000 (on $3.5 million, $93,000). The first-time buyers' GST rebate (law since March 13, 2026) covers new homes, not land: all the GST up to $1 million, phasing out at $1.5 million, maximum $50,000, for agreements from March 20, 2025 to 2031. The GST New Housing Rebate is 36% up to $6,300, the Home Buyers' Plan allows $60,000, and an FHSA $8,000 a year up to $40,000.
Strata block — stated for comparison, no: For comparison only: off reserve, a bare-land strata lot comes with a Form B (within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page), a depreciation report every 5 years for stratas with 5 or more lots, at least 10% of the budget into the reserve, no rental bans, and only 55+ age bylaws. None of this applies on reserve land, where there are no stratas.

Freehold strata apartment complex on the: Somerset Green: a freehold strata condo complex on the south side of West 29th Street, also fronting Chesterfield Avenue. A 2004 District report describes it as "the existing 143 unit 'Somerset Green' seniors' condominium apartment development in the City of North Vancouver," with suites averaging about 1,100 sq ft. Current listings market it as 55+: "Owner can be legal age, but one resident must be 55+." Amenities include an indoor pool, hot tub, workshop, gym, library, games room, lounge, courtyard gardens and 2 guest suites, and cats are allowed. Most listings say it was built in 1987 (one says 1989).
Freehold strata, plan BCS2494, built 200: Vista 29: freehold strata (plan BCS2494), built 2007, between West Queens Road and West 29th Street east of Chesterfield Avenue, with 50 units, zoned CD52. Current listings market it as a 55+ building: "One owner to be 55+." The District approved it in 2004 as 42 single-level condos in a four-storey building plus 8 three-bedroom townhouses, with a covenant limiting occupancy to households where one member is 55 or older. Listings mention a clubroom, guest suite (one says $35 a night; confirm with the strata), workshop, secure underground parking, 13 visitor stalls and storage lockers, and it's pet friendly.

Chartwell describes it as a boutique residence with both independent and assisted living under one roof (which it says is unique on the North Shore), with 24/7 staff, emergency response and pet-friendly suites from studios to two-bedrooms. It's at West 29th Street and Lonsdale Avenue, near Queens Road and Highway 1, five minutes from Lions Gate Hospital.
Somerset Green's build year is not consi: Sources disagree on Somerset Green's build year: most listings say 1987, at least one says 1989. A 2004 District report puts it at 143 units, which listings rarely mention.

Two known: Somerset Green, 121 West 29th: Two: Somerset Green (121 West 29th Street, 143 units, on the City side of 29th Street) and Vista 29 (188 West 29th Street, 50 units, built 2007, on the District side). Property transfer tax — worked example (: Property transfer tax example: on a $1,200,000 house and lot with no exemption, the tax is 1% of the first $200,000 ($2,000) plus 2% of the rest ($20,000), or $22,000. Other examples: $500,000 is $8,000; $800,000 is $14,000 ($6,000 for a first-time buyer who fully qualifies); $900,000 is $16,000; $1.0 million is $18,000; $1.5 million is $28,000; $2.0 million is $38,000; and $3.5 million is $93,000, including the extra 2% on the residential part over $3 million.
Municipal / reserve split first, because: The first thing to check here is whether a property is on reserve land. Part of the Park Royal shopping centre lands are on Capilano Indian Reserve No. 5 (X̱wemelch'stn), Squamish Nation land held under the 1974 Park Royal Lease, where the Squamish Nation controls land use and zoning; the rest is District of West Vancouver land under Zoning Bylaw No. 4662 (2010) and Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 4985 (2018). Check the ownership type on title for every property before pricing or financing.
The sub-area's best-known condo developm: The area's best-known condo development: two concrete towers at Taylor Way beside Park Royal, built in 1993, with an indoor pool, sauna, exercise centre, workshop and garden. Recreation and development-permit frame:: Recreation and permits: Ambleside Park and the east end of the Centennial Seawalk are just west along the waterfront, and Capilano River Regional Park runs up the canyon across the river, with the 91 m Cleveland Dam (1954) at its head and the Capilano River Hatchery (1971; normally about 250,000 visitors a year, reported closed to the public for construction from October 1, 2026). The Park Royal shopping centre lands are a design development permit area, and foreshore and environmental permits apply along the waterfront and creeks. The Lions Gate Bridge is right next door.
