⚠️ TWO MUNICIPALITIES — READ THIS FIRST:: Upper Lonsdale is split between two municipalities at 29th Street. Lonsdale Avenue from about 25th to 29th Street is in the City of North Vancouver, and 29th Street north to Rockland Avenue is in the District. The line runs right through the condo cluster: Somerset Green (121 West 29th Street) is taxed and zoned by the City, while Vista 29 (188 West 29th Street), across the street, is taxed and zoned by the District. Taxes, plans, zoning and permits follow the municipality, not the area name. Chartwell Churchill House, on the same block of 29th Street, is a private-pay rental retirement residence, not for sale.
Freehold strata apartments on the south: Somerset Green: freehold strata condos on the south side of West 29th Street. A 2004 District report describes it as "the existing 143 unit 'Somerset Green' seniors' condominium apartment development in the City of North Vancouver," with suites averaging about 1,100 sq ft. Current listings market it as 55+, with "one resident must be 55+"; the registered bylaws are what count. Amenities include an indoor pool, hot tub, workshop, gym, library, games room, lounge, courtyard gardens and 2 guest suites, and cats are allowed.
Freehold strata, plan BCS2494, built 200: Vista 29: freehold strata (plan BCS2494), built 2007, with 50 units, zoned CD52. The District approved it in 2004 as 42 condos plus 8 townhouses, with a covenant limiting occupancy to households where one member is 55 or older. That covenant is on top of the strata bylaws, so review both when buying. Current listings say "One owner to be 55+" and mention a clubroom, guest suite (one listing says $35 a night), workshop, secure underground parking, 13 visitor stalls and storage lockers; it's pet friendly.
Recreation: the new Harry Jerome Communi: Recreation: the new Harry Jerome Community Recreation Centre opened July 25, 2026 at 130 East 23rd Street, in the City just south of the area (the pools were expected to open for fall programs), and Delbrook Community Recreation Centre (851 West Queens Road), with a main pool and leisure pool, serves the District blocks.
CITY rules (south of 29th Street — the S: City rules (south of 29th Street, the Somerset Green side): the City's Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 8400, 2014, amended December 8, 2025) and Zoning Bylaw No. 6700 (1995). On December 8, 2025, the City adopted the Ground Oriented Zone, raising the limit from 3 to 4 units on nearly 4,300 properties and allowing up to 6 units on about 600. Secondary suites have been legal in City houses since 1993 (one per property, and the owner must live there), and a coach house needs a front lot line of at least 10 m, a development permit and a building permit. These City rules don't apply to District addresses.
Schools: School District 44 serves both: Schools: SD44 serves both municipalities. Elementary schools for the area include Westview Elementary and Larson Elementary (both K–7; École Larson Elementary, 2605 Larson Road, has both English and French Immersion); École André-Piolat (K–12, 380 West Kings Road), the francophone public school, is also in Upper Lonsdale; and the catchment secondary for most of the area is Carson Graham Secondary (Grades 8–12, 2145 Jones Avenue).
Recreation and elevation: the new Harry: Recreation and elevation: the new Harry Jerome Community Recreation Centre opened July 25, 2026 at 130 East 23rd Street, in the City just south of the area, with an NHL-sized arena, 25-metre pool and full gym (the pools were expected to open for fall programs); Delbrook Community Recreation Centre (851 West Queens Road), with a main pool and leisure pool, serves the District blocks. The top of Lonsdale at Rockland is often said to be about 850 feet above sea level. On the District side, slope is the main hazard; the District has natural hazard development permit areas and publishes property-level hazard reports on GeoWeb.
Age bylaws — and the Vista 29 covenant l: Age bylaws, and Vista 29's covenant: only 55+ age bylaws are valid, with exemptions for a younger spouse or partner, live-in caregivers, existing residents and some children (expanded May 1, 2023). A 45+ bylaw is void and doesn't become 55+. The bylaw limits who can live there, not who can own, so someone under 55 can own a unit but may not be able to live in it. Vista 29 also has a separate covenant from its 2004 approval limiting occupancy to households where one member is 55 or older.
CITY rules (south of 29th Street — the S: City rules (south of 29th Street, the Somerset Green side): the City of North Vancouver's Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 8400, 2014, amended December 8, 2025 for provincial housing rules) and Zoning Bylaw No. 6700 (1995). On December 8, 2025, the City adopted the Ground Oriented Zone, raising the limit from 3 to 4 units on nearly 4,300 properties and allowing up to 6 units on about 600. Secondary suites have been legal in City houses since 1993 (one per property, and the owner must live there), and a coach house is allowed where the front lot line is at least 10 m, with a development permit and building permit. The City planned its 2025 updates for 21,301 more homes over 20 years, on top of its existing 29,021. These City rules don't apply to District addresses.
The BC strata rules that applies to the: BC strata rules for the strata buildings: a depreciation report every five years for stratas with five or more units, at least 10% of the budget into the reserve, no rental bans, and only 55+ age bylaws.
Schools (SD44, same district on both sid: Schools (SD44, the same district on both sides of the municipal line): Westview Elementary and Larson Elementary (both K–7; École Larson Elementary, 2605 Larson Road, has English and French Immersion); École André-Piolat (francophone, K–12, 380 West Kings Road); and Carson Graham Secondary (2145 Jones Avenue) for most of the area, with an IB program. Catchments are set by address; check the easternmost addresses against the Argyle boundary with SD44.
Recreation: the new Harry Jerome Communi: Recreation: the new Harry Jerome Community Recreation Centre (130 East 23rd Street, in the City just south of the area) opened July 25, 2026 with an NHL-sized arena, 25-metre pool and full gym (the pools were expected to open for fall programs); Delbrook Community Recreation Centre (851 West Queens Road) serves the District blocks. Tempe Heights Park, at the east edge, is a 1.74-hectare City natural area with tennis courts, a playground and a pond.
DISTRICT SIDE — SSMUH position as the Di: District side, extra units: since June 2024, single-family lots inside the District's urban boundary can have a house, a secondary suite and a coach house, with suites up to 49% of the house and coach houses up to two storeys. The District's GeoWeb map shows potential for up to 3 units at 280 m² or less, 4 on larger lots, and 6 on larger lots within 400 m of a frequent bus stop. Provincial law (Bill 25) requires full density by June 30, 2026, and the District's changes were still being prepared in spring 2026, so these rules are still changing.
Schools: Larson Elementary, K–7; Braemar: Schools (SD44 North Vancouver): Larson Elementary (K–7), Braemar Elementary (K–7), Boundary Elementary (K–7) and Carson Graham Secondary (8–12), plus Holy Trinity School (K–7, independent). Check the catchment for a specific address with the school district.
Form B diligence (both counted pockets a: Both pockets are strata, so read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. With only 18 concrete terrace homes with private elevators at Highgrove, and 8 homes at Aerie II, the Form B and depreciation report show what the envelope, elevators and landscaping cost.
What and where: Whitby Estates is a smal: Whitby Estates is a small subdivision inside the Chartwell neighbourhood of the British Properties, District of West Vancouver, on the slope above Taylor Way, with streets including Whitby Road, Folkestone Way, Kadlec Court, Garden Court and Highgrove Mews. It's also the real estate board's name for the area, though some Whitby Road homes are listed under neighbouring Chartwell. Nearby: Chartwell around it, Chelsea Park to the south, Westhill and Canterbury to the west, and the Taylor Way corridor to the east. Other names for the area include Chartwell, the British Properties and the Lower British Properties.
Transit and access: no frequent transit: Transit and access: there's no frequent transit in the Estates; the nearest is Park Royal Exchange, down Taylor Way, with the R2 RapidBus (straight through to Lonsdale Quay, Phibbs Exchange and Metrotown since September 7, 2026) and Blue Bus routes, so plan on driving. Highway 1 at Taylor Way goes west to Horseshoe Bay and Highway 99 and east across the Second Narrows, and Taylor Way leads down to Marine Drive and the Lions Gate Bridge.
Strata diligence (BC strata rules apply: Strata rules apply to both strata pockets (and any bare-land strata lot): the Form B (fees, amounts owing, approved special levies, contingency reserve balance, insurance, rules, budget, rental disclosure and latest depreciation report) must be provided within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. With 18 concrete terrace homes with private elevators at Highgrove and 8 homes at Aerie II, the Form B and depreciation report show what the envelope, elevators and landscaping cost. Both need a depreciation report every 5 years, at least 10% of the budget must go into the reserve, and rental bans are void. Only 55+ age bylaws are valid, and neither strata has one; a 45+ bylaw is void and doesn't become 55+.
Plan and zoning (West Vancouver's OWN in: Plans and zoning (West Vancouver's own): the Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 4985, 2018) treats the British Properties as an established neighbourhood and directs growth to the town and village centres, not into the Properties; Zoning Bylaw No. 4662 (2010) sets land use, height, density, setbacks and lot coverage.
Where the homes sit: detached houses on: Homes are mostly detached houses on tree-lined streets (the City calls Arbutus Ridge a mature community with restored heritage houses and striking views of the North Shore mountains), with fewer strata homes than the busier streets around it. Arbutus Street, West Boulevard and the Arbutus Greenway run north–south along the east side, and West 16th Avenue, West King Edward Avenue, West 33rd Avenue and West 41st Avenue cross the area.
Ridge house lots: detached houses on tre: House lots: mostly detached houses on tree-lined streets (the City calls Arbutus Ridge a mature community with restored heritage houses and striking views of the North Shore mountains), with fewer strata homes than the busier streets around it. A fee-simple lot has no strata, Form B or strata fees.
Lot character: R1-1 minimum site areas r: Lot sizes (R1-1 zone): the minimum site is 306 m² with a 10.0 m frontage for a house, duplex or 3–4-unit multiplex, 464 m² (13.4 m) for 5 units, and 557 m² (15.1 m) for 6–8 units. A house can have a secondary suite and a laneway house, and a multiplex up to 6 units, or 8 if they're rentals. These are minimums, not actual lot sizes; check a specific lot.
Bare-land strata / strata rules (BC stra: Strata rules apply in full at Arbutus Village, and to any bare-land strata lot: check the Form B (fees, amounts owing, levies, contingency reserve balance and insurance; within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page). Stratas with 5 or more lots need a depreciation report every 5 years, which is the key document for a complex from around 1975, and at least 10% of the budget must go into the reserve. Rental bans are void (short-term rentals can still be limited), and the only valid age bylaw is 55 and older, with exemptions for a younger spouse or partner, caregivers, existing residents and some children, so a "45+" listing line isn't enforceable.
Schools: Shaughnessy Elementary, grades: Schools: Shaughnessy Elementary (K–7, SD39), 4250 Marguerite Street; York House School (K–12, independent), 4176 Alexandra Street; and Prince of Wales Secondary (8–12, SD39), 2250 Eddington Drive. Check the catchment for a specific address with the Vancouver School Board.
City plan and zoning: the Cambie Corrido: Plans and zoning: the Cambie Corridor Plan (approved 2011, with Phase 3 in 2018) guides growth along Cambie Street from 16th Avenue to the Fraser River around the Canada Line stations. Under the Zoning and Development By-law, side streets are R1-1 (306 m² minimum for a house or duplex; a multiplex can have up to 6 units, or 8 rentals), Cambie Street sites are C-2, and station-area sites usually have their own CD-1 zoning.
Concrete townhomes by Arno Matis design: Concrete townhomes designed by Arno Matis at the Oakridge–41st station area: a current listing describes a detached concrete townhome with no shared walls, freehold strata, built 2017, with pets allowed with restrictions; confirm on the Form B.
Schools located in the corridor's offici: Schools along the corridor (SD39 has no middle schools: K–7 and 8–12; catchments are set by address, so check the VSB School Locator): in South Cambie, Carr Elementary (4070 Oak Street) and Cavell Elementary (500 West 20th Avenue); in Riley Park, Livingstone Elementary (315 East 23rd Avenue) and Wolfe Elementary (4251 Ontario Street); and in Oakridge, Osler Elementary (5970 Selkirk Street) and Van Horne Elementary (5855 Ontario Street). Sir Winston Churchill Secondary is at 7055 Heather Street.
Form B diligence (both strata complexes: For both strata complexes, read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. Lines in listings, such as Aperture's pet line, aren't the bylaws.
Established side-street lots: single det: Side streets: houses, duplexes and multiplexes in the R1-1 zone, with townhouse and rowhouse areas under the Cambie Corridor Plan, and condo and mixed-use buildings at the Canada Line stations and on Cambie Street. Houses on the side streets are freehold, condos and townhouses on the corridor are strata, and many newer station buildings are purpose-built rentals.
Lot character, as the R1-1 schedule stat: Lot sizes (R1-1 zone): the minimum site is 306 m² with a 10.0 m frontage for a house, duplex or 3–4-unit multiplex, 464 m² (13.4 m) for 5 units, and 557 m² (15.1 m) for 6–8 units. A multiplex can have up to 6 units, or 8 if they're rentals, and a house can have a secondary suite and a laneway house. Station-area and Cambie Street sites follow the corridor plan and CD-1 or C-2 zoning instead; C-2 is meant for shops and homes along main streets.
Civic anchors: Queen Elizabeth Park, ato: Landmarks: Queen Elizabeth Park, on Little Mountain in Riley Park, 52 hectares at 125 metres above sea level, the highest point in Vancouver, with the Bloedel Conservatory, quarry gardens and an arboretum; Douglas Park Community Centre (801 West 22nd Avenue) at the north end and Hillcrest Centre (4575 Clancy Loranger Way) on the east side; and the Oakridge library branch at the south end. South Cambie is known for its hospitals, including BC Children's Hospital and BC Women's Hospital (4480 Oak Street).

Form B and strata records (strata purcha: For a strata resale, the strata must provide a Form B; the BC Real Estate Association recommends checking it for the latest depreciation report, the strata's financial statements, the contingency reserve balance and planned work, to spot future special levies.

Champlain Mall / Champlain Square ground: Champlain Mall (Champlain Square), 3200 East 54th Avenue: the shopping centre, with a public library inside, has its own zoning from 1970, older than the neighbourhood itself. It's built-out commercial land, not land for sale.
Subdivision — Subdivision By-law No. 520: Subdivision: Vancouver's Subdivision By-law (No. 5208) sets minimum lot widths and areas by zone and block type, administered by the City's Approving Officer; its fees were last updated for 2026. A fee-simple lot split has to meet both the zone and the subdivision rules for its block; don't assume it from a neighbour's history. Land leased from the City can't be split into fee-simple lots at all.
The leases were a deliberate 1970s plan,: The leases were planned in the 1970s, and renewals are happening now: Champlain Heights was planned in the early 1970s as a showcase community of curved roads and cul-de-sacs mixing housing types and incomes, and built mostly on City-owned land, which is why much of it is on prepaid 99-year City leases ending in the 2080s. From 1974 to 1986 the City leased sites to non-market housing groups instead of selling them, and new long-term leases are being approved for co-ops such as Cedar Mill (July 2025). If you buy a leasehold or co-op home here, lease renewal is still an open question.
Kiwanis Manor (independent suites) — 959: Kiwanis Manor (independent suites), 959 21st Street, Ambleside: the Kiwanis North Shore Housing Society lists it as 55+ independent living in West Vancouver, and says most of its seniors buildings are below-market rentals. The same address also has a registered assisted-living residence; see the care section.
Kiwanis Manor (assisted living) — 959 21: Kiwanis Manor (assisted living), 959 21st Street: BC's Assisted Living Registry lists it as a registered assisted-living residence, and Park Place Seniors Living has an assisted-living page for it, while the Kiwanis society describes the same address as 55+ independent living. Both appear to operate at this address.
Zoning: Zoning Bylaw No. 4662, 2010: Hou: Zoning (Bylaw No. 4662, 2010): houses are in the RS single-family zones; condos and care homes are in the Ambleside town centre.
West Vancouver zoning: houses sit in the: West Vancouver zoning: houses are in the RS single-family zones of Zoning Bylaw No. 4662 (2010), with minimum site areas of 8,094 m² in RS1, 1,625 m² in RS2, 975 m² in RS3, 731 m² in RS4 and 488 m² in RS5 (RS6 uses the existing lot size), and secondary suites and detached secondary suites allowed. Check a specific lot's zone on the District's Zoning Map.
Form B diligence (strata purchases gener: For any strata purchase, read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page.
Lot character, as the bylaw states it: S: Lot sizes: West Vancouver's RS zones have minimum site areas of 8,094 m² in RS1, 1,625 m² in RS2, 975 m² in RS3, 731 m² in RS4 and 488 m² in RS5 (RS6 uses the existing lot size); the larger RS1 and RS2 minimums are typical of the British Properties benches. These are minimums, not actual lot sizes; check a specific lot on the District's Zoning Map. Secondary suites and detached secondary suites are allowed in the single-family zones.
The enclave is named by its schools, not: The area takes its name from its school, not the District: Chartwell Elementary, in the British Properties overlooking Vancouver and Burrard Inlet, has two playgrounds, a gravel field, soccer and basketball courts and the Properties Family Hub. The school grounds are the area's main public open space; I don't know of a separate District park in Chartwell.
The District's Official Community Plan (: West Vancouver's Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 4985, 2018) names Ambleside as the town centre, Park Royal, and the village centres of Dundarave, Caulfeild Village and Horseshoe Bay; Chartwell isn't a named neighbourhood in the plan.
Where the housing stock concentrates: al: Homes here are almost all strata condos in towers along the waterfront and on West Cordova Street, West Hastings Street and the downtown grid as it extends into Coal Harbour, with some townhouse-style homes at the base of the towers. There are no detached houses.
Anchors: Coal Harbour Community Centre,: Landmarks: Coal Harbour Community Centre (480 Broughton Street), Harbour Green Park on the waterfront, and Devonian Harbour Park (1929 West Georgia Street), the gateway between Stanley Park and Coal Harbour. The waterfront walkway runs continuously along Coal Harbour.
Schools: SD39 catchments are address-bas: Schools: Vancouver School Board catchments are set by address (check the VSB School Locator), and there are no middle schools (K–7 and 8–12). The VSB has opened a new elementary school in Coal Harbour, the Seaside school. Elsie Roy Elementary (150 Drake Street) and Crosstown šxʷwəq̓ʷəθət Elementary (55 Expo Boulevard) are in Yaletown and Crosstown, not Coal Harbour.
There is no standalone townhouse complex: There are no standalone townhouse complexes here; a townhouse-style home in Coal Harbour is a strata lot in a tower, so read the building's Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. In towers with hotels (Fairmont Pacific Rim and Paradox), the Form B also shows how the homes are separated from the hotel.
Presales (REDMA), where a Coal Harbour p: If you buy a presale in Coal Harbour, the developer must give you a disclosure statement, you can cancel within 7 days of signing or receiving it (whichever is later), and deposits are held in trust. I don't know of any Coal Harbour presales right now.
Bare-land strata rules: Form B diligence: Bare-land strata rules: the Form B must be provided within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page; stratas with 5 or more lots need a depreciation report every 5 years; at least 10% of the budget must go into the reserve; rental bans are void (short-term rentals can still be limited by bylaw, and Vancouver licenses them separately); and only 55+ age bylaws are valid, so a "45+" listing line isn't enforceable.
Schools: New School at Coal Harbour, K-6: Schools (SD39 Vancouver): the new school at Coal Harbour (K–6), 482 Broughton Street; Lord Roberts Elementary (K–7), 1100 Bidwell Street; and King George Secondary (8–12), 1755 Barclay Street. Check the catchment for a specific address with the Vancouver School Board.
A three-tower condominium and townhouse: A three-tower community of condos and townhouses at Boundary Road and Kingsway, with 1,060 homes in total according to the developer (strata plan EPS3434). The tower at 5665 Boundary Road has 36 floors and was built in 2017; some listings at 5515 Boundary Road say 2016, as the towers finished at different times. The directory lists pets and rentals allowed. The townhouses are part of this community.
Where the townhouse stock actually sits:: The townhouses are in three places: the Chambers Street cluster in Norquay Village, south of Kingsway (two small complexes on one street); Rae Avenue and Wellington Avenue east of Joyce Station, toward Central Park and the Burnaby border; and the townhouse parts of the condo stratas near the stations (Wall Centre Central Park, Clive at Collingwood and 2300 Kingsway). The City says most of the wider area is single-family homes, with townhouses and mid-rise apartments around Joyce Station.
Form B diligence (all 4 counted strata c: For the four strata complexes, read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. Rental and pet lines in listings aren't the bylaws.
Civic anchors: Renfrew Park Community Ce: Nearby: Renfrew Park Community Centre (2929 East 22nd Avenue) and Renfrew Pool, the Central Valley Greenway running through the area, the Collingwood library branch (2985 Kingsway) and the Renfrew branch (2969 East 22nd Avenue), and Renfrew Ravine Park (3900 Renfrew Street), 5.89 hectares with part of Still Creek running through it. The Collingwood stretch of Kingsway is a shopping street.
Schools: Collingwood Neighbourhood Schoo: Schools: Collingwood Neighbourhood School (K–3, SD39), 3417 Euclid Avenue; St. Mary's (K–7, independent), 5239 Joyce Street; and Graham Bruce Community Elementary (K–7, SD39), 3633 Tanner Street. Transit: the R5 Hastings St RapidBus ter: Transit: the R5 Hastings Street RapidBus runs from Burrard Station to SFU Exchange; route 50 runs from Waterfront Station via Chinatown, Granville Island and the south shore of False Creek to Olympic Village Station; route 22 runs from Burrard Station via Pender, Gore, Prior, Venables, Clark and Knight; and Yaletown–Roundhouse Station on the Canada Line serves the south side.
Downtown has elementaries but no confirm: Downtown has elementary schools but no public secondary school: Elsie Roy and šxʷməqʷəθət Crosstown elementaries are downtown, and King George Secondary (1755 Barclay Street) is in the West End. If you have kids, check the catchment for a specific address.
Strata diligence — the operative regime: Strata rules downtown: read the Form B (fees, amounts owing, levies, contingency reserve balance and insurance; within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page) along with the depreciation report, reserve and any special levies before making an offer. Stratas with 5 or more lots need a depreciation report every 5 years, and at least 10% of the budget must go into the reserve. Rental bans are void (short-term rentals can still be limited by bylaw, and Vancouver licenses them), and the only valid age bylaw is 55 and older, with exemptions for a younger spouse or partner, caregivers, existing residents and some children, so a "45+" listing line isn't enforceable.
SkyTrain stations on downtown ground (Tr: SkyTrain stations downtown: Waterfront, Burrard and Granville on the Expo Line, and Vancouver City Centre on the Canada Line; Waterfront is on both.
The twisting Bjarke Ingels Group tower i: Bjarke Ingels Group's twisting tower in the Beach District at the Granville Street bridge: presale marketing gave 548 units in a 52-storey tower and 9-storey podium, though an earlier source said 502. Most sources, including current listings, say it was completed in 2020 (the directory says 2019).
There is no strata townhouse complex to: There are no townhouse complexes here; a ground-level home downtown is a strata lot in a tower, so read the building's Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page.
Presales (REDMA), where a Downtown presa: If you buy a presale downtown, the developer must give you a disclosure statement, you can cancel within 7 days of signing or receiving it (whichever is later), and deposits are held in trust.
No fee-simple house-lot stock exists to: There are no house lots downtown. The Downtown District zoning allows commercial, residential, institutional and light industrial uses, parks and public uses in what the City calls the main business district; homes are almost all strata condos, plus rental apartment buildings and hotel and office stratas. The lots are commercial and strata parcels.
Lot character — district minimums, as th: Downtown lots are zoned DD, CD-1 or C-3A, not house zones. CD-1 zones are site-specific, so each property's own bylaw sets what can be built.
Roads and transit: West Georgia Street,: Roads and transit: the main downtown streets include West Georgia, Granville, Burrard, Howe, Hastings, Pender and Cordova. Downtown is where the Expo, Millennium and Canada Lines meet, with Waterfront, Burrard, Granville and Stadium-Chinatown stations; the R5 Hastings Street RapidBus runs from Burrard Station to SFU Exchange, and route 22 runs from Burrard Station toward Knight Street and Richmond.
Schools: Elsie Roy Elementary, K-7, 150: Schools: Elsie Roy Elementary (K–7, SD39), 150 Drake Street; King George Secondary (8–12, SD39), 1755 Barclay Street; and Pattison High School (10–12, independent), 981 Nelson Street. Check the catchment for a specific address with the Vancouver School Board.
Tenure for a specific Downtown building:: For a specific downtown building, check the title shows freehold strata; the buildings listed above are all freehold strata.
No park, community centre or pool in the: The main civic landmark in the core is the Central Library (350 West Georgia Street). Coal Harbour Community Centre and the West End's facilities are in neighbouring areas.
Presales (REDMA), where a Downtown VW pr: If you buy a presale downtown, the developer must give you a disclosure statement, you can cancel within 7 days of signing or receiving it (whichever is later), and deposits are held in trust.
No fee-simple house-lot stock exists to: There are no house lots downtown: most of the core is Downtown District zoning, which allows commercial, residential, institutional and light industrial uses, parks and public uses, with development permits approved by the City; parts are CD-1 or C-3A. Homes are almost all strata condos, plus rental apartment buildings and hotel and office stratas.
Strata block (the operative tenure block: Strata rules (most homes here are strata): the Form B must be provided within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page; stratas with 5 or more lots need a depreciation report every 5 years; at least 10% of the budget must go into the reserve; rental bans are void (short-term rentals can still be limited); and only 55+ age bylaws are valid, so a "45+" listing line isn't enforceable. Review the depreciation report, reserve and any special levies before making an offer; strata disputes can go to the Civil Resolution Tribunal.
Where condo stock actually concentrates:: Dunbar is mostly detached houses. Its condos are three low-rise buildings, all on its two commercial strips: Dunbar Street itself (West Pointe at the south end and Fifty-Five 55 Dunbar in the middle of the village) and the corner of Dunbar and West 39th Avenue (3590 West 39th Avenue). There are no condos on the interior streets or on the Southlands country lots at the south edge.
Form B diligence (the 3349 Dunbar Street: For the strata at 3349 Dunbar Street, or any Dunbar strata, read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. Rental and pet lines in listings aren't the bylaws.
Established-street house lots: detached: House lots: mostly detached houses on tree-lined streets (the City calls Dunbar-Southlands a mature community of quiet residential streets lined with grand old trees), with low-rise strata buildings on Dunbar Street and West 41st Avenue. A fee-simple lot has no strata, Form B or strata fees.
The one age-restricted strata ownership: Fairview's only age-restricted strata building, and an unusual one: you buy a strata suite in a building that also runs as a boutique retirement community. A current listing says: "Welcome to the Terraces on 7th, a much sought after retirement community with a 55 plus age restriction." Building records show age-restriction bylaws, pets allowed, 52 units, an elevator, in-suite laundry, storage and wheelchair access. Building records say it was built in 2003; the listing says 2002.
Transit: Broadway-City Hall Station (Can: Transit: Broadway-City Hall and Olympic Village stations on the Canada Line serve the east and northeast edges; the 99 B-Line runs along West Broadway from Commercial-Broadway Station to UBC, route 9 along Broadway to Alma Street, and route 50 via Granville Island to Olympic Village Station. The Broadway Subway, a 5.7 km Millennium Line extension from VCC-Clark to Arbutus Street with six new stations, including South Granville and Broadway-City Hall, is on schedule to open in fall 2027, according to the Province.
Fairview Slopes zoning: FM-1 District Sc: Fairview Slopes zoning (FM-1): meant to keep the slopes' small-scale residential character by encouraging existing houses to stay and allowing new low-profile homes, FM-1 allows houses, duplexes, multiplexes and house conversions at a floor space ratio of up to 0.60. Southern Fairview lots are R1-1 (a multiplex of up to 6 units, or 8 rentals; a house can have a secondary suite and a laneway house), and the commercial streets are C-3A.
Where the condo stock concentrates: in t: The condos are in three pockets: the False Creek South waterfront (mostly on City ground leases, not freehold), the Fairview Slopes along West 7th and 8th Avenues above the shore (Terraces on 7th and Manhattan West), and the Oak Street and Marpole Avenue edge toward Shaughnessy (Hycroft Towers and The Oaks).
Where the townhouse stock concentrates:: The townhouses are on the Fairview Slopes side streets off West 7th Avenue and West 15th and 16th Avenues (Fairview Village and Marvista on West 7th, Tisdall Row on West 15th, and the Heritage project at 16th and Burrard), not on Broadway or Granville, which are condos and mixed-use buildings. The False Creek South waterfront homes are on City-owned leased land.

Fairview was named by the CPR's land com: Fairview was named by the CPR's land commissioner, L.A. Hamilton, whose survey set up the numbered east–west avenues and named the cross streets after trees; before that, False Creek and Fairview Slopes were fir forest.

Floodplain diligence — the north-edge it: Floodplain, on the north edge: the False Creek shoreline is in the City's floodplain, including False Creek South along the south shore of Fairview, and land there must meet the building bylaw's floodplain setbacks and flood construction levels. Vancouver Empty Homes Tax — 3%, vancouve: Vancouver's Empty Homes Tax applies here: properties declared, found or deemed vacant pay 3% of their assessed value each year. Most homes aren't affected, including principal residences and homes rented out for at least six months of the year, but every Vancouver owner must file an annual declaration. The 2025 tax was due April 16, 2026, with a 5% penalty after that. A Fairview lot or house left empty is exposed to this tax; New Westminster and Burnaby don't have it.

It is not one of the City of Vancouver's: False Creek isn't one of Vancouver's 22 official local areas; the City splits it into False Creek North (in Downtown), False Creek South (in Fairview) and the False Creek Flats (in Strathcona). The big thing to watch is leasehold: False Creek South is City-owned land on 60-year ground leases. The buildings listed below are the freehold strata buildings in Southeast False Creek, Olympic Village and on the north and east shores.

Tenure first, Form B second: On a freeho: Check the ownership type first, then the Form B. Rental-restriction bylaws are void — wit: Rental bans are void, but only for strata bylaws: since November 24, 2022, no strata can ban long-term rentals (short-term rentals can still be limited, and Vancouver licenses them separately). So the Lamey's Mill listing's "pets & rentals permitted w/ restrictions" line needs to be read against that building's lease.
Presales (REDMA), where a False Creek pr: If you buy a presale in False Creek, the developer must give you a disclosure statement, you can cancel within 7 days of signing or receiving it (whichever is later), and deposits are held in trust.

Form B diligence (E15, the one counted s: For E15, the one strata complex, read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. An undivided-interest building like the Lee Building has no Form B at all, so if there isn't one, that tells you something right away.
Historic fabric — built lots, not offeri: Heritage: the area high above False Creek was named "Mount Pleasant" in 1888, and the City highlights its heritage buildings, many from the early 1900s. Heritage status is something to check on side-street lots.
Schools: Mount Pleasant Elementary, K-7,: Schools (SD39 Vancouver): Mount Pleasant Elementary (K–7), 2300 Guelph Street; General Brock Elementary (K–7), 4860 Main Street; and Sir Charles Tupper Secondary (8–12), 419 East 24th Avenue. Check the catchment for a specific address with the Vancouver School Board.
Tenure warning specific to this corridor: Ownership differs along this corridor: OPAL's condos are freehold strata, but future homes on the Heather Lands will be leasehold. Don't assume one is like the other.
Property tax — UEL side: provincial rura: Property tax on the UEL side is provincial rural tax, not City tax: the University Endowment Lands are run directly by the Province, so taxes are billed each June by the Province's Surveyor of Taxes. City of Vancouver water isn't on the tax bill; it's billed separately, which catches some Vancouver buyers out.
Transit: UBC Exchange is the bus exchang: Transit: UBC Exchange is the bus exchange here; there's no SkyTrain. The R4 41st Avenue RapidBus runs from Joyce Station to UBC Exchange, at least every 10 minutes at peak times and every 15 minutes otherwise.
Schools: University Hill Elementary, K-7: Schools (SD39 Vancouver): University Hill Elementary (K–7); Norma Rose Point Elementary Junior (K–7), 5488 Ortona Road; and University Hill Secondary (8–12). Check the catchment for a specific address with the Vancouver School Board.
Tenure is checked per building and state: Check the ownership type for each building: Yaletown is on False Creek north-shore land that includes former Expo lands, some once City leasehold, so don't assume a building is freehold unless the title says freehold strata.
Where the condo stock concentrates: two: The condos are in two groups: the False Creek waterfront towers on Beach Crescent, Homer Mews and Marinaside Crescent (King's Landing, Crestmark I and II and Azura 2), facing David Lam Park, George Wainborn Park and the seawall; and the inland towers on Mainland, Homer, Cambie and Richards Streets (Yaletown Park 3, The Bentley, City Crest, Waterworks and Pacific Landmark II), plus the heritage warehouse lofts in the Homer Street core (The Murchies).
Empty Homes Tax (Vancouver): every Vanco: Empty Homes Tax (Vancouver): every Vancouver homeowner must file a property status declaration by the second business day of February each year. A property without a declaration is treated as vacant, the tax is 3% of assessed value, and unpaid tax gets a 5% penalty after the tenth business day of April. If you're buying as an investor, know the declaration dates before closing.
Airspace subdivision as the operative fo: Downtown, built projects are divided into separate airspace parcels for homes, shops and parking, not into ground lots. A Yaletown condo buyer owns a strata lot within that structure; there's no separate lot to check beyond the strata documents.
Downtown districts (DD / CD-1 frame): Ya: Yaletown properties are in the City's downtown zoning (DD and CD-1). CD-1 zones are site-specific, so each property's own bylaw, not a general density figure, sets what can be built; check it before pricing any redevelopment.
Subdivision — Subdivision By-law No. 520: Subdivision: Vancouver's Subdivision By-law (No. 5208) applies, with fees under By-law No. 14538; downtown, properties are divided by airspace, confirmed property by property with the City.
Strata block (the operative diligence fo: Strata rules (most Yaletown homes are strata): the Form B must be provided within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page; stratas with 5 or more lots need a depreciation report every 5 years; at least 10% of the budget must go into the reserve; rental bans are void (short-term rentals can still be limited); and only 55+ age bylaws are valid, so a "45+" listing line isn't enforceable. Read the depreciation report, reserve fund and any lease or rental bylaws in the strata documents.
Housing shape: predominantly detached si: Homes: mostly detached houses on tree-lined streets, from early-1900s character homes to post-war bungalows, some "Vancouver Specials" and large new rebuilds, on typical west-side lots, with bigger estate lots north toward Shaughnessy; almost all are freehold. Condos and townhouses are along West 41st Avenue and the edges of the village, including some seniors-oriented buildings.
Schools (SD39 Vancouver): public element: Schools (SD39 Vancouver): public elementaries in Kerrisdale include Kerrisdale Elementary (5555 Carnarvon Street), Kerrisdale Annex (3250 West 43rd Avenue), Maple Grove Elementary (1924 West 45th Avenue) and Dr. R.E. McKechnie Elementary (7455 Maple Street), and Magee Secondary (6360 Maple Street, Grades 8–12) is in Kerrisdale. Secondary catchments are split between Point Grey and Magee by address: for example, 5555 Carnarvon Street is in the catchment for Kerrisdale Elementary and Point Grey Secondary, and 7455 Maple Street for McKechnie Elementary and Magee Secondary. Crofton House School (3200 West 41st Avenue), an independent girls' school from junior kindergarten to Grade 12 founded in 1898, is on a 10-acre campus at Kerrisdale's west edge.
Form B diligence (any strata, including: For any strata, including the Sterling and McKinnon townhouses, read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. A townhouse in a condo development is part of the same strata as the condos, with the same Form B.
Fee-simple lots: almost all detached sto: Lots: almost all detached homes are freehold; a fee-simple lot has no strata corporation, Form B or strata fees.
Housing and lot shape: predominantly det: Homes and lots: mostly detached houses on tree-lined streets, from early-1900s character homes to post-war bungalows, some "Vancouver Specials" and large new rebuilds, on typical west-side lots, with bigger estate lots north toward Shaughnessy; almost all are freehold. Condos and townhouses are along West 41st Avenue and the edges of the village.
Schools (SD39 Vancouver): Kerrisdale Ele: Schools (SD39 Vancouver): Kerrisdale Elementary (5555 Carnarvon Street), Kerrisdale Annex (3250 West 43rd Avenue), Maple Grove Elementary (1924 West 45th Avenue) and Dr. R.E. McKechnie Elementary (7455 Maple Street) are in Kerrisdale, as is Magee Secondary (6360 Maple Street, Grades 8–12). Secondary catchments are split between Point Grey and Magee by address: for example, 5555 Carnarvon Street is in the catchment for Kerrisdale Elementary and Point Grey Secondary, and 7455 Maple Street for McKechnie Elementary and Magee Secondary.
Strata block (applies to the neighbourho: Strata rules (for the strata homes here and any bare-land strata lot): the Form B within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page; a depreciation report every 5 years for stratas with 5 or more lots (smaller ones, like many of Kerrisdale's new multiplex stratas, are exempt); at least 10% of the budget into the reserve; no rental bans; and only 55+ age bylaws. None of this applies to a fee-simple lot.
Three: Sterling by Cressey (6400 West Bo: Three: Sterling by Cressey (6400 West Boulevard, 37 homes, completed 2018), McKinnon by Cressey (6300 West Boulevard, 40 homes, completed 2019) and Boulevard Private Residences (5325 West Boulevard, 38 units, built 2017). Otherwise Kerrisdale is mostly detached homes, with only a few condos at the edges of the village.
SD39 catchments are address-based and sp: SD39 catchments are set by address and split here: for example, 5555 Carnarvon Street is in the catchment for Kerrisdale Elementary and Point Grey Secondary, and 7455 Maple Street for McKechnie Elementary and Magee Secondary. Magee Secondary (6360 Maple Street) is in Kerrisdale. Check the exact address with the VSB School Locator.
A presale condominium project in Mount P: A presale project in Mount Pleasant by Jim Pattison Developments: a six-storey mixed-use building with 73 condos and 3 townhomes, expected to finish in 2027. Every sale here is a developer contract, with GST and presale rules.
Terraces on 7th is Fairview stock and OP: Terraces on 7th is in Fairview, and OPAL by Element (438 West King Edward Avenue) is in South Cambie. Both often show up in "Mount Pleasant condo" searches, but neither is in Mount Pleasant.
Fee-simple lots: the side-street stock i: Lots: the side streets are fee-simple detached character houses on their own lots, with no strata corporation, Form B or strata fees; City zoning, heritage register status and any registered covenants apply.
Older rental buildings as land: the King: Older rental buildings: the walk-up rentals along Kingsway are the area's most affordable homes and its most contested. They're purpose-built rentals, not strata or house lots, and they're exactly what the Broadway Plan's renter protections and tenant relocation rules were written for, so redeveloping them works very differently from a strata or house site.
City frame: Vancouver's Zoning and Devel: Plans and zoning: Vancouver's Zoning and Development By-law applies, with site-specific CD-1 zoning along the main streets. The Broadway Plan (approved June 22, 2022; updated December 12, 2024) is the area plan, but it's policy, not zoning, and most higher-density buildings still need a rezoning. City-wide direction now comes from the Vancouver Official Development Plan, which replaced the Vancouver Plan on March 31, 2026.
Two sample addresses were actually run i: For example, 5970 Selkirk Street is in the catchment for Sir William Osler Elementary and Eric Hamber Secondary, and 5855 Ontario Street for Sir William Van Horne Elementary and Eric Hamber Secondary. So the elementary school depends on the address, and both feed Eric Hamber.
Form B diligence (the counted strata com: For the strata complex, read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. Oakhaus was built in 2025, so for a unit still sold by the developer, the disclosure statement applies instead; for a resale, the Form B.
Schools (SD39): the VSB lists two elemen: Schools (SD39): the VSB lists two elementary schools in Oakridge itself, Sir William Osler Elementary (5970 Selkirk Street) and Van Horne Elementary (5855 Ontario Street), with Sir Wilfrid Laurier Elementary (7350 Laurel Street) serving the south side and Eric Hamber Secondary (960 West 33rd Avenue) on the north side. For example, 5970 Selkirk Street is in the catchment for Osler Elementary and Eric Hamber Secondary, and 5855 Ontario Street for Van Horne Elementary and Eric Hamber, so the elementary school depends on the address (Sir Winston Churchill Secondary is the French Immersion option for the Selkirk Street address).
Anchors: Queen Elizabeth Park — 52 hecta: Landmarks: Queen Elizabeth Park, 52 hectares at 125 metres above sea level and the highest point in Vancouver, is just northeast of the town centre; Langara Golf Course (6706 Alberta Street, the City's 18-hole course), Winona Park and Langara College (at West 49th Avenue) are just south; and Montgomery Park serves the Osler Elementary streets on the west side.
Property transfer tax — worked example (: Property transfer tax example: on a $2,000,000 house and lot with no exemption, the tax is 1% of the first $200,000 ($2,000) plus 2% of the rest ($36,000), or $38,000. Other examples: $500,000 is $8,000; $800,000 is $14,000 ($6,000 for a first-time buyer who fully qualifies); $1.0 million is $18,000; $1.2 million is $22,000; $1.5 million is $28,000; and $3.5 million is $93,000, including the extra 2% on the residential part over $3 million.
Presales (REDMA) — the live frame at Oak: Oakridge Park and Mayfair West are presales: the developer must give you a disclosure statement, deposits are held in trust, and you can cancel within 7 days of signing or receiving it (whichever is later). Check completion timing, strata setup and what the developer still owes, phase by phase; the developer expects the first homes at Oakridge Park to be ready in early 2027, with other phases following over several years.
Where the condo stock sits: there is ess: There's essentially one condo address: Shaughnessy Place, 4900 Cartier Street, beside VanDusen Botanical Garden at the southeast edge, plus strata townhouses at the Oak Street and West 37th Avenue edge. The rest of the area is freehold estate houses; the First Shaughnessy zoning is meant to protect its estate character, and there's no shopping street in Shaughnessy.
Form B diligence (the counted strata com: For the strata buildings, including the Shaughnessy Place townhouses, read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. Whitford was built in 2026, so for a unit still sold by the developer, the disclosure statement applies instead. A Shaughnessy Place II townhouse is part of the whole mixed complex, so review the whole complex's documents.
Heritage and zoning (the rules that defi: Heritage and zoning: First Shaughnessy (north of King Edward Avenue, within the heritage conservation area) has its own heritage plan (adopted 2015) and zoning. Protected pre-1940 homes can only come off the protected list through Council, after a heritage assessment, and owners of protected homes can add a coach house, convert the house into multiple units or build infill as incentives to keep the heritage house. House size is capped (0.45 floor space ratio with a conserved heritage house; otherwise 0.25 plus 139 m², to a maximum of 911 m²), and new lots must be at least 100 ft wide and 13,000 sq ft. South of King Edward (Second and Third Shaughnessy), the regular city-wide rules apply, including the R1-1 multiplex rules for detached lots outside the heritage area (up to 6 strata units or 8 rentals); check how the two sets of rules interact for a specific property.
Lot character, as the City states it: Fi: Lot sizes: in First Shaughnessy, new lots must be at least 100 ft (30.48 m) wide and 13,000 sq ft (1,207.7 m²), which is why its estate lots are among the largest in the city. Homes are large estates, from Edwardian and interwar mansions in First Shaughnessy to mid-century and modern homes further south, many on 100 ft-plus lots with mature landscaping. It's almost all freehold detached, with a few strata homes at the edges.
Strata frame: Form B under SPA s. 59; de: Strata rules: the Form B; a depreciation report every 5 years for stratas with 5 or more lots; at least 10% of the budget into the reserve; no rental bans; and only 55+ age bylaws, so a "45+" listing line isn't enforceable.
Schools: Eric Hamber Secondary, grades 8: Schools (SD39 Vancouver): Shaughnessy Elementary (K–7), 4250 Marguerite Street; Eric Hamber Secondary (8–12); and Prince of Wales Secondary (8–12). Check the catchment for a specific address with the Vancouver School Board.
Schools (SD39): Edith Cavell Elementary: Schools (SD39): Edith Cavell Elementary (500 West 20th Avenue) is the corridor's public elementary, and Sir Winston Churchill Secondary (7055 Heather Street) is the public secondary in the corridor. But location isn't catchment: for 500 West 20th Avenue, the catchment is Cavell Elementary and Eric Hamber Secondary, not Churchill.
Heather Lands — a documented rezoned dev: The Heather Lands are a rezoned development site, not lots for sale: 8.5 hectares (21.1 acres) between West 33rd and West 37th Avenues, owned by the Musqueam, Squamish and Tsleil-Waututh Nations with Canada Lands Company. Council approved a rezoning in 2022 (about 2,600 homes and 4.4 acres of park), replaced on March 31, 2026 by a new rezoning under the provincial Attainable Housing Initiative: 16 buildings of 4 to 46 storeys with about 4,200 homes, including about 2,940 discounted leasehold strata homes, 700 market leasehold strata homes and 610 social housing homes, plus a 125-space child care centre, a cultural centre, a one-acre school site and over four acres of park. Most homes there will be leasehold strata.
Landmarks and anchors: Queen Elizabeth P: Landmarks: Queen Elizabeth Park (52 hectares at 125 metres above sea level, the highest point in Vancouver) on the east side; Douglas Park Community Centre (801 West 22nd Avenue); BC Children's Hospital and BC Women's Hospital on the west side (4500 Oak Street); VanDusen Botanical Garden (5251 Oak Street, 22 hectares) at the northwest edge; and Langara College at the south end at West 49th Avenue.
Schools: public schools are run by the V: Schools are run by the Vancouver School Board (SD39). Edith Cavell Elementary (500 West 20th Avenue) is the corridor's public elementary, and Sir Winston Churchill Secondary (7055 Heather Street) is the public secondary in the corridor, but being nearby doesn't make it the catchment school; check the address with the VSB School Locator.
Schools: Edith Cavell Elementary, K-7, S: Schools (SD39 Vancouver): Edith Cavell Elementary (K–7), Eric Hamber Secondary (8–12) and Sir Winston Churchill Secondary (8–12). Check the catchment for a specific address with the Vancouver School Board.
Where the condo stock concentrates: on t: The condos are on the residential side streets on either side of Granville (West 6th, West 8th and West 14th Avenues between Burrard or Fir and Oak), not on Granville Street's shopping strip. Those streets also have many purpose-built rental buildings, so a lot of the "apartment buildings" here aren't condos.
Development-site frame — documented in t: Development here is driven by plans: the Broadway Plan allows buildings of 30–40 storeys near the future South Granville Station, and Vancouver General Hospital's campus is being redeveloped over 30-plus years in 10 phases with buildings up to 24 storeys; a July 14, 2026 approval allows an 11-storey emergency and inpatient building at 818–990 West 10th Avenue and 803–899 West 12th Avenue. These are policies and institutional sites, not lots for sale.
Same development and strata family, diff: Pintura is one development with two parts: condos at 1530 West 8th Avenue and townhouses at 1576 West 8th Avenue, both concrete, built by Intracorp in 2005. Check the address and type on any "Pintura" listing before comparing, and don't assume the condos' "rental and pet friendly" description applies to the townhouses; read the Form B.
Zoning frame: Southlands is governed by: Zoning: Southlands is zoned RA-1 (Limited Agriculture), created in 1955 for Southlands "to maintain and encourage the semi-rural, equestrian and limited agricultural nature of this District," allowing single-family homes and, in some cases, infill homes. The Agricultural Land Reserve has covered the area since 1973, and the City's 1988 Southlands Plan still applies under the Vancouver Official Development Plan. Standard detached lots elsewhere in the area are R1-1; RA-1 lots have their own rules.
Recreation anchors: McCleery Golf Course: Recreation: McCleery Golf Course (7188 Macdonald Street), a City golf course at the southwest edge, and Deering Island Park (3530 Deering Island Place), a natural park on the Fraser River, plus the Fraser River dike trails. There are no shops in the area; the nearest shopping streets are Kerrisdale Village (West 41st Avenue) to the north and Marpole (Granville Street) to the east.
Flood, transit and anchors: the City's F: Flooding, transit and landmarks: the City's floodplain standards (in force since 2015, amended 2023) set flood construction levels and setbacks in the floodplain, including the Fraser River floodplain, with a section specifically for the RA-1 zone; the City publishes the floodplain map online. Transit is by bus: the 49 (Metrotown Station–UBC), a frequent route, runs along West 49th Avenue and, west of Dunbar Street, along Southwest Marine Drive; the nearest Canada Line station is Marine Drive Station in Marpole. McCleery Golf Course (7188 Macdonald Street) and Deering Island Park (3530 Deering Island Place), a natural park on the Fraser, are the main recreation spots. There are no shops in the area; the nearest are in Kerrisdale Village and Marpole.
Form B diligence (any strata, including: For any strata, including Gulf View Court, read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page.
No bare-land strata plan in S.W. Marine: I don't know of any bare-land stratas here, and in Southlands itself there are almost no strata homes, because RA-1 allows one home per lot with only limited infill. If one came up, stratas with 5 or more lots need a depreciation report every 5 years, at least 10% of the budget must go into the reserve, rental bans are void, and only 55+ age bylaws are valid.
Zoning — RA-1 (Southlands) vs R1-1 (else: Zoning differs between Southlands and the rest of the area. Southlands lots are RA-1 (Limited Agriculture, 1955; single-family homes, with limited infill in some cases), under the 1988 Southlands Plan. Standard detached lots elsewhere are R1-1, where Vancouver's multiplex rules allow up to 6 strata units or 8 rentals. RA-1 lots aren't R1-1, so the multiplex rules don't apply to a Southlands lot unless the City confirms otherwise.
Jurisdiction trap — three tenures within: Three kinds of ownership within a few blocks: City of Vancouver freehold (RA-1 or R1-1), University Endowment Lands to the west, and leases on Musqueam reserve land. They finance, insure and resell differently, so check the jurisdiction on any listing near the Musqueam boundary, and make the ownership type clear up front.
Empty Homes Tax — 3%, Vancouver only, an: Vancouver's Empty Homes Tax applies here: it charges 3% of assessed value on homes declared or deemed empty, with the annual declaration due February 3, 2026 and payment due April 16, 2026. This area is in the City of Vancouver, so the tax applies.
Transit: Nearest rapid-transit station:: Transit: the nearest SkyTrain is Marine Drive Station on the Canada Line, to the east, where route 10 ends. Route 49 (Metrotown Station–UBC) runs via Langara Station, Southwest Marine Drive and Dunbar, along SW Marine Drive through the area.
Schools: Southlands Elementary, K-7, SD3: Schools (SD39 Vancouver): Southlands Elementary (K–7), Point Grey Secondary (8–12) and Magee Secondary (8–12). Check the catchment for a specific address with the Vancouver School Board.
Zoning: the RA-1 district (in place sinc: Zoning: the RA-1 zone (since 1955) allows single detached houses and only limited infill houses, so there are almost no strata homes, rental apartments or townhouses in Southlands itself; the condos and townhouses are on the regular streets at the Kerrisdale and Marpole edges.
\"University VW\" is not in the City of: "University VW" isn't in the City of Vancouver: the board's area covers the University Endowment Lands (unincorporated, run by the Province, in Metro Vancouver's Electoral Area A) plus UBC's campus neighbourhoods (Wesbrook Village, Hampton Place, Chancellor Place, Hawthorn Place and East Campus). Addresses say "Vancouver", which is what confuses people, but no City of Vancouver bylaws apply, and neither does the Empty Homes Tax. Ownership differs: the older UEL streets are mostly freehold, while every UBC neighbourhood home is on a prepaid 99-year lease of UBC land, never sold outright. At the seniors rental building, BC's Assisted Living Registry names Seasons as the operator, but Chartwell also has a page for the same address.
Tenure: leasehold strata on UBC land — U: Ownership: leasehold strata on UBC land. UBC never sells its land; it's leased on prepaid 99-year leases, so the time left runs from the project's original lease date, not your purchase date. The 55+ restriction is only from listings, which say the community is "restricted to 55+ years", allow pets and rentals, and describe a mandatory service package (dining credit, weekly housekeeping and a 24-hour emergency system). Check the Form B and registered bylaws before relying on the age rule, the package or its cost. 3338 Wesbrook Mall is Building 1 (the rental side) and 3382 Wesbrook Mall is Building 2 (the condos).
Where condo stock concentrates: Wesbrook: The condos are in Wesbrook Village, the village centre south of West 16th Avenue on Wesbrook Mall and around Birney Avenue and Webber Lane; Hampton Place (from the 1990s, UBC's first campus neighbourhood) and the other campus neighbourhoods have more leasehold strata condos and townhouses.
Two jurisdictions share this one board s: Two jurisdictions share this one board area: the University Endowment Lands, an unincorporated community between Vancouver and UBC on the Point Grey peninsula, the only urban area in BC where the Province provides local services directly, with no elected council (it's governed by the Minister of Municipal Affairs), in Metro Vancouver's Electoral Area A; and UBC's own neighbourhoods on campus land (Wesbrook Village, Hampton Place, Chancellor Place, Hawthorn Place and East Campus). Addresses say "Vancouver, BC", which causes most of the confusion. The UEL Administration runs day-to-day services under the UEL's community plan and land use bylaw.
Schools (SD39 Vancouver): University Hil: Schools (SD39 Vancouver): University Hill Elementary (5395 Chancellor Boulevard, K–7, about 385 students), University Hill Secondary (3228 Ross Drive, since 2013) and Norma Rose Point School (5488 Ortona Road, K–7, over 770 students, serving Wesbrook Place). For example, 5395 Chancellor Boulevard is in the catchment for University Hill Elementary and University Hill Secondary, and 5488 Ortona Road for Norma Rose Point and University Hill Secondary.
Head-lease diligence (the leasehold town: Leases on the townhouses: the land is never sold, and the time left on the lease runs from the project's original lease date, which matters to lenders and price, especially in Hampton Place, the oldest neighbourhood, with the shortest time left.
Form B diligence (leasehold strata is st: Leasehold strata is still strata, so read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. Also check the UNA services levy and any neighbourhood charges in the strata budget; the University Neighbourhoods Association, not a city, provides local services in the UBC neighbourhoods.
The BC strata rules that applies to the: BC strata rules apply to the leasehold stratas: a depreciation report every five years for stratas with five or more units, at least 10% of the budget into the reserve, no rental bans, and only 55+ age bylaws. That's why Tapestry's 55+ status, which comes from listings, needs checking on the Form B.
Anchors: UBC Hospital, 2211 Wesbrook Mal: Landmarks: UBC Hospital (2211 Wesbrook Mall), with an urgent care centre; the Museum of Anthropology (6393 NW Marine Drive); UBC Botanical Garden (6804 SW Marine Drive); and Wesbrook Village's centre on Birney Avenue and Webber Lane, with a Save-On-Foods at 5945 Berton Avenue. UBC has 60,309 students on its Vancouver campus.
River employment lands: the wider Big Be: Industrial land by the river: the wider Big Bend and south Burnaby river lands also have industrial uses. The City says industrial space makes up nearly half of Burnaby's employment space, with much of it in what the City's study calls Big Bend; that study area isn't the same as the real estate board's Big Bend.
Market context: Burnaby is a SnapStats-c: Burnaby's medians were $1,825,000 for detached homes and $686,000 for condos and townhomes. There are no separate figures for land.
ALR block — the governing rules for Big: ALR rules for Big Bend farmland: subdividing needs Agricultural Land Commission approval, homes can't be stratified, the main house can be up to 500 m² with a suite only inside it, and an additional home can be up to 90 m² (186 m² on parcels over 40 ha). For farm tax status, BC Assessment looks for farm income of $10,000 a year on under 0.8 ha, $2,500 on 0.8 to 4 ha, and $2,500 plus 5% of the value of land over 4 ha; applications are due by October 31. Check a property's ALR status and allowed uses on the Commission's map first, before paying for any development or non-farm value.
Floodplain diligence — the second defini: Flooding is the other big factor: the City says Burnaby's south edge runs along nearly 7 km of the Fraser River's North Arm, and the nearly 800 hectares of low land between the south slope and the river is floodplain. The river is a real flood risk from snowmelt in late spring and early summer, and from heavy rain combined with winter storm surges. The City protects the lowlands with dikes, pump stations and flood boxes and has a flood response plan. Check a property's flood construction requirements, dike position and insurance before removing subjects.
\"Nearly half the city's employment spac: "Nearly half the city's employment space" refers to a City study area, not the board's Big Bend area. The City says industrial space is nearly half of Burnaby's employment space, with much of it in its Big Bend study area; a seller quoting that figure for the board area is using the wrong boundary.
Brentwood Park is the residential sub-ar: Brentwood Park is the residential area in northwest Burnaby around Brentwood Park Elementary, south and east of Brentwood Town Centre. It's the real estate board's name for the area and the school's name; for planning, the City treats it as part of Brentwood Town Centre, one of Burnaby's four town centres.
Where the condo stock concentrates: in t: The condos are in two clusters. Towers ring the town centre and its two SkyTrain stations: the Amazing Brentwood towers at Willingdon and Lougheed, the SOLO District towers on Rosser Avenue and Skyline Drive, Concord Brentwood along the south side of Lougheed Highway, Gilmore Place and Triomphe / Escala at Gilmore Avenue, and Affinity on Douglas Road. An older group of mid- and high-rises (Vantage Point and Anola Place) is on Bellwood Avenue above the residential streets, with low-rises (Memento on Beta Avenue) toward the houses.
Two current listings at consecutive stre: Two listings on the same block of Springer Avenue show townhouses: 2082 Springer Avenue, a 2,205 sq ft four-level split built in 1976, freehold strata, backing onto a greenbelt, and 2078 Springer Avenue, a 2,175 sq ft townhome that one listing calls "Springdale Manor". This complex isn't the Slate tower at 2135 Springer Avenue: same street, different strata.
Form B diligence (the 1 strata complex a: For the strata complex and the tower stratas, read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page.
SSMUH (R1): Burnaby's R1 district (conso: Small-scale housing (R1): Burnaby's R1 zone (since June 2024) allows 3 units on lots up to 280 m², 4 on larger lots, and 6 on lots of 281 m² or more within 400 m of a frequent bus stop, with a minimum lot of 10 m wide and 281 m². Form B diligence (Oakwood's strata, and: For the Oakwood strata and each small strata project, read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. In a four-unit strata the package is short, so read all of it, including who the other owners are and how much is actually in the reserve.
Depreciation reports — the small-strata: Depreciation reports in small stratas: since July 1, 2024, stratas with five or more lots must get a depreciation report every five years and can't vote to skip it. Oakwood is well over that; a four-unit strata on Buxton or Elgin isn't, so no report is required and you'll need your own building inspection instead. At least 10% of the budget must go into the reserve each year, which in a four-unit strata adds up to very little.
Taxes and rebates (any new-build purchas: Taxes and rebates on a new home, such as the 2026 Buxton, Elgin and Dufferin multiplexes: property transfer tax is 1% on the first $200,000, 2% up to $2 million and 3% above, plus another 2% on the residential part above $3 million. First-time buyers are exempt on the first $500,000 for homes up to $835,000 (partial up to $860,000), and the newly built home exemption is full up to $1,100,000 and ends at $1,150,000. The first-time buyers' GST rebate (law since March 13, 2026) covers all the GST up to $1 million (maximum $50,000), phasing out at $1.5 million, for agreements from March 20, 2025 to 2031; the GST New Housing Rebate is 36% up to $6,300 (phasing out between $350,000 and $450,000). The Home Buyers' Plan allows $60,000, an FHSA $8,000 a year up to $40,000, and CMHC premiums run 0.6%–4.5%. 5% GST applies to new homes like these multiplexes, not resales, and the new-home warranty on a four-unit strata is worth checking separately.
The new ground-oriented form — SSMUH str: The new small multiplexes are stratified units on former house lots under the R1 zone. Check each project's strata plan and Form B; none of them is vacant land.

A stratified multiplex unit in Garden Village is a strata lot, so the Form B, depreciation report and reserve fund rules apply.
Market frame: Burnaby community-level Co: Burnaby's condo and townhome figures in September 2026: a median of $686,000, $763 per sq ft, 98% of list price and 36 days on the market.
The only lot-size figures a source state: The only lot-size figures are the R1 zone's thresholds (280 m² and 281 m²). The interior streets were built as one planned post-war subdivision, which is why two similar 1950s houses can be worth quite different amounts once you check, lot by lot, whether they're within 400 m of a frequent bus stop.
Market context: Burnaby is a SnapStats-c: Market figures, September 2026 (homes, not land): in Garden Village, 9 detached homes were listed and 1 sold (11%), with no condos or townhomes. Burnaby's medians were $1,825,000 for detached homes and $686,000 for condos and townhomes.
Garden Village is a City of Burnaby sub-: Garden Village is in southwest Burnaby, west of Metrotown toward Boundary Road, around Central Park and Patterson Station; Heritage Burnaby places the original Garden Village subdivision in the historic Central Park neighbourhood. It's also the real estate board's name for the area. The City doesn't publish a boundary; the original subdivision was a 140-acre site built from 1953, and today's area is roughly the streets between Central Park and Boundary Road to the west, Kingsway to the north and the Metrotown side to the east.
Main roads and transit: Kingsway runs ea: Roads and transit: Kingsway runs east–west along the north edge, Boundary Road runs along the Vancouver border on the west, and Patterson Avenue and Imperial Street run through toward Metrotown. Patterson Station on the Expo Line, at Patterson Avenue and Central Park, serves the north side; Metrotown Station, the next stop east, is the main bus exchange, and route 116 runs from Metrotown Station south through Sussex and Imperial toward Edmonds Station.
Parks and services: Central Park, immedi: Parks and services: Central Park, just northeast, is the big park (with 12 lit tennis courts and a practice wall); the Rumble Street Urban Trail runs south of the area, part of Burnaby's 70-plus kilometres of urban trails. The Bob Prittie Metrotown library and Bonsor Recreation Complex are on the Metrotown side, the Metrotown Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at 102-4555 Kingsway, and Burnaby Hospital (3935 Kincaid Street) is to the northeast.
Age-of-stock diligence: the housing stoc: Age of homes: the area was subdivided in 1953, so many houses are post-war, with later infill and rebuilds.
The sample-address school run is a trap: Be careful with school catchment examples here: the one School Locator check used 5455 Rumble Street, Burnaby South Secondary's own address, which is in the catchment for Nelson Elementary. That shows catchments go by address, not which school a Rumble Street house is in; check the specific address.
Burnaby-wide (SnapStats publishes commun: For all of Burnaby in September 2026, condos and townhomes had a median of $686,000, $763 per sq ft, and 36 days on the market. There's no median for Garden Village itself.
Serviced position, as the City states it: Services: Burnaby's 2026 utility bill covers water, sewer use, a cross-connection device charge where needed and a garbage fee; water for a detached house is $652.33, with a 5% discount if paid on time, and sewer for houses is a parcel tax on the property tax notice. Existing lots are on City services; check servicing for a specific lot, and any upgrades a subdivision would trigger, with the City.
SSMUH / subdivision potential as the Cit: Small-scale housing (for the fee-simple house lots around Greentree, not the strata townhouses): R1 lots can have 3 units on lots up to 280 m², 4 on larger lots, and 6 on lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent bus stop, with a minimum lot of 10 m wide and 281 m². Lots with two or more main units can be stratified, and the zone allows houses, duplexes, multiplexes, rowhouses and secondary suites.
Strata block: Form B diligence (provided: Strata rules: the Form B must be provided within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page; each Greentree phase is its own strata with its own Form B, reserve fund and depreciation report. Stratas with 5 or more lots need a depreciation report every 5 years, at least 10% of the budget must go into the reserve, rental bans are void (short-term rentals can still be limited), and only 55+ age bylaws are valid, so a "45+" listing line isn't enforceable.
Where the condo stock concentrates: nowh: There are no condos here; the buildings are industrial and business-centre buildings.
Market volume: no SnapStats sub-area row: There are no market figures for Lake City: it has no homes, so the board doesn't report it.
Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B s: The Form B shows a strata lot's monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page.
What actually governs here — zoning: the: Zoning: Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026 (No. 14815) has applied since July 1, 2026, replacing the 1965 bylaw. It has a townhouse zone (R2) elsewhere in the city, but the plan for this area doesn't use it.
PTT (1% on the first $200,000, 2% to $2M: For homebuyers: property transfer tax is 1% on the first $200,000, 2% up to $2 million and 3% above, plus another 2% on the residential part above $3 million; first-time buyers are exempt on the first $500,000 for homes up to $835,000 (partial up to $860,000), and the newly built home exemption is full up to $1,100,000 and ends at $1,150,000. The first-time buyers' GST rebate (law since March 13, 2026) covers all the GST up to $1 million (maximum $50,000), phasing out at $1.5 million, for agreements from March 20, 2025 to 2031; the GST New Housing Rebate is 36% up to $6,300; the Home Buyers' Plan allows $60,000, an FHSA $8,000 a year up to $40,000, and CMHC premiums run 0.6%–4.5%. None of these apply to buying industrial property, which has its own GST rules, so get tax advice on any commercial deal. Vancouver's Empty Homes Tax doesn't apply in Burnaby.
Designated ground, as the plan states it: The Lake City Community Plan (2000) designates the area for mixed commercial, office, industrial and business-centre uses, with commercial, business centre, institutional, and park and public use designations; there's no residential land in it.
Strata block: Form B diligence (provided: Strata rules: the Form B must be provided within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page; stratas with 5 or more lots need a depreciation report every 5 years; at least 10% of the budget must go into the reserve; rental bans are void (short-term rentals can still be limited); and only 55+ age bylaws are valid. For an industrial strata unit, review the strata documents early; strata disputes can go to the Civil Resolution Tribunal.
FTHB GST rebate / programs — land angle: The first-time buyers' GST rebate (law since March 13, 2026; all the GST up to $1 million, maximum $50,000, phasing out at $1.5 million, for agreements from March 20, 2025 to 2031) applies to new homes, not land, and not to industrial property. The same goes for the GST New Housing Rebate (36% up to $6,300), the Home Buyers' Plan ($60,000) and the FHSA ($8,000 a year up to $40,000).
Because SnapStats publishes no Lake City: Because the board doesn't report Lake City separately, there are no listing or sales figures for it. Any Burnaby figures shown are for the whole city's homes, not Lake City.

Subdivision + servicing — confirmed inst: Subdivision and servicing: Burnaby's Subdivision Control and Development Servicing Bylaw (updated in 2024) requires new lots to meet the zoning, and lets the City require roads, lanes, water, sewer and drainage connected to City systems. The City's Servicing Improvements Guide applies it to developments of four or more main units on a residential lot, including cash contributions for curbs, sidewalks, lanes, boulevards, street trees, streetlights and road widening. Check the requirements for a specific lot with the City's Engineering Department before pricing a lot split.
Where the condo stock concentrates: nowh: There are no condos in Oakdale; the nearest condo buildings are west, at Lougheed Town Centre.
Established house lots off the Lougheed: House lots off the Lougheed corridor: only detached houses are for sale here; condos are west at Lougheed Town Centre. A fee-simple lot has no strata, Form B or strata fees.

Established-street house lots: freehold: House lots: freehold detached houses on the streets around Kensington Avenue and Halifax Street.
