In trust, as REDMA s.18 requires — verif: In trust, as the law requires. Check who holds the trust account, as named in the disclosure statement, before paying any instalment.
The City of Langley share of the band is: In the City of Langley, condos at this price are the downtown apartments around 200 Street, 56 Avenue and Fraser Highway, the same area where the City's May 2026 development report lists its current apartment applications.
The under-$399K band is mostly older low: Condos under $399,000 are mostly older low-rise buildings in the City of Langley, plus newer low- and mid-rise buildings in the Township. Age matters because of one deadline: stratas in Metro Vancouver and the Fraser Valley with no depreciation report, or one from before December 31, 2020, had to get a current one by July 1, 2026.
In the City of Langley, land designated: In the City of Langley, land designated Mid Rise Residential needs a development permit for the building's form and character, which shapes the new apartment buildings going up here. On that basis, the City's Bylaw 3303 (2025) rezoned 20239–20249 54A Avenue from low-density multi-family (RM1) to a comprehensive development zone (CD105).
Most City households live in attached ho: Most City households live in attached homes: about 80% are apartments and townhouses, with the detached houses mainly in the Uplands and on the streets north of Grade Crescent and south of the Nicomekl floodplain.
The Official Community Plan (OCP) sorts: The Official Community Plan sorts homes by type: high-density mixed-use in the "Core" around the planned SkyTrain stations near 196 Street and 203 Street, mid-rises up to 12 storeys, low-rises up to 6 storeys, townhouses along future frequent bus routes, and compact lots with secondary or garden suites north of Grade Crescent.
No — separate municipalities, separate b: No. They're separate municipalities with separate bylaws. In the City: Zoning Bylaw 3300 (2025) and small-scale housing Bylaw 3284 apply, and a suite can be 100 m² or 40% of the home, whichever is less, with the owner living there. The Township's small-scale housing bylaw and 120 m² suite limit don't apply here.
A park's 55+ rule has its own legal foot: A park's 55+ rule has its own legal basis: BC's manufactured home park rules recognize parks where every pad is reserved for someone 55 or older (or two or more people, at least one of them 55 or older), and the park owner can refuse a sale where no buyer meets that age. That's how the 55+ rules at the three Newton and Fleetwood parks work; I don't know of any pad-rental park in South Surrey.
Assignment consent has a clock: Under MH: Consent has a deadline: a seller can assign the pad tenancy only with the landlord's written consent first (or deemed consent), an arbitrator's order, or where the tenancy agreement allows it. The park owner must answer within 10 days of the written request (RTB Form 10), silence counts as consent, and no fee can be charged. Before asking, the seller must give the buyer written copies of the park rules and the relevant parts of the tenancy agreement.
Park closure / conversion (MHPTA s. 42,: Park closure or conversion: if a landlord plans to convert all or much of a park to another use, they must have all the government permits and approvals first, give 12 months' notice, and pay each tenant $20,000 by the date the notice takes effect. The tenant can move out early with at least 10 days' written notice, can dispute the notice within 15 days, and in some cases can apply for more compensation (the home's assessed value minus the $20,000). Surrey's Tenant Protection Bylaw (2025) doesn't apply to manufactured home parks.
City zoning: A specific park's zone is c: Zoning: check a specific park's zone on the City's COSMOS map.
Surrey's tenant-protection bylaw does no: Surrey's Tenant Protection Bylaw (2025) doesn't cover any park on this page, because it doesn't apply to manufactured home parks. Park residents' protection if a park is redeveloped comes from the provincial rules: permits first, 12 months' notice and $20,000 compensation.
Sea Ridge Bays still carried Land Use Co: When the City reported on Sea Ridge Bays, the property still had a 1977 land use contract (No. 283) on top of its manufactured home zoning. Have a lawyer explain how the old contract and the current zoning work together.
In a park, the manufactured home only —: In a park, only the manufactured home: you rent the pad under a Manufactured Home Site Tenancy Agreement, and buying means taking over that tenancy, which needs the park owner's written consent first and registration with the Manufactured Home Registry. At Sea Ridge Bays you own the strata lot too, pay a strata fee instead of pad rent, and review strata documents.
The framework is known, not open-ended:: The rules are set out: the landlord must have all permits and approvals first, then give 12 months' notice and pay $20,000 compensation by the date the notice takes effect, with more owed in some cases. Surrey's 2025 Tenant Protection Bylaw doesn't cover park residents.
The page is about the board sub-area \"B: This page covers Brookswood in the Township of Langley, in the Brookswood-Fernridge community area (the Booth, Fernridge and Rinn neighbourhood plans), with a focus on development potential after the Township's 2024 small-scale housing rezoning.
ALR / second dwellings: the Agricultural: ALR and second homes: on ALR land, the Agricultural Land Commission allows one main house and, if conditions are met, one additional home of up to 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less, or 186 m² on larger ones. Homes on ALR land can't be stratified, so ALR land doesn't become condos.
An assembly framing is not a subdivision: A land assembly isn't a subdivision, serviced lots or homes for sale.
Brookswood is a board sub-area in the To: Brookswood is in the Township of Langley, in the Brookswood-Fernridge community area (the Booth, Fernridge and Rinn neighbourhood plans). It's also a real estate board area.
Zoning: City of Langley Zoning Bylaw, 20: Zoning: City of Langley Zoning Bylaw 3300 (2025), which replaced the 1996 zoning bylaw.
Township rules: R-CL s. 403 allows lot a: Township rules: the compact lot zone (R-CL) allows lots of 220 to 464.5 m². Sources differ on suites in townhouses, so confirm with the Township.
Planning frame: the City's Official Comm: Plans: the City's Official Community Plan was adopted on November 22, 2021, built on the "Nexus of Community" vision adopted on July 23, 2018, to guide how the city grows over the next 25-plus years.
Zoning — City of Langley Zoning Bylaw, 2: Zoning: City of Langley Zoning Bylaw 3300 (2025), which replaced the 1996 zoning bylaw.
City — zoning: City of Langley Zoning By: Zoning: City of Langley Zoning Bylaw 3300 (2025), which replaced the 1996 zoning bylaw. The Township of Langley's zoning doesn't apply to any City property.
The rental line does not — rental-restri: The rental line doesn't: strata rental bans have been void since November 24, 2022. The 55+ line can: a 55-and-older bylaw is the one age bylaw still allowed, with exemptions for existing residents, live-in caregivers and (since May 1, 2023) younger spouses or partners and some children. A building directory lists both Parkway buildings as age restricted, with no pets and no rentals; only the age and pet lines may still apply, so confirm both in the registered bylaws.
A transfer does not trigger a market re-: A sale doesn't reset the pad rent to market. Unlike a strata, where fees follow the current budget, an assignment passes the current pad rent and the date of the next increase to the buyer. The rent history is in the tenancy agreement, which the seller must share before asking the park for consent.
\"55+\" in a Langley park and \"55+\" in: "55+" in a Langley park and "55+" in a Langley strata are legally different. A park's rule is in the tenancy regulation and park rules and can be a reason to refuse a sale; a strata's rule is a registered bylaw with set exemptions. A couple who can live in a Parkway Estates strata unit on a spouse exemption don't automatically have the same right in a Brookswood park.
Under MHPTA s. 42: the landlord must fir: If a park is being closed or converted, the landlord must have all the permits and approvals first, then give 12 months' notice and pay each tenant $20,000 by the date the notice takes effect. The tenant can leave early with 10 days' written notice, can dispute the notice within 15 days, and in some cases can claim more (the home's assessed value minus the $20,000). If the landlord doesn't go ahead within a reasonable time, they owe a further $5,000 or 12 months' rent, whichever is more.
Tenure frame the whole page turns on: in: How ownership works in a park: many residents own their manufactured home and rent the site it sits on under a Manufactured Home Site Tenancy Agreement, under BC's Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act. Where both the home and the site are rented, a Residential Tenancy Agreement applies instead.
Where condo stock concentrates: there is: Where the condos are: there are none on this page. Compare park by park, not area by area, because pad rent, what it includes and the park rules are set by each park in its written site tenancy agreement.
Assignment on a sale (MHPTA s. 28): assi: Assignment on a sale: assigning the site tenancy transfers the pad tenancy to the buyer for good. A tenant can assign only with the landlord's written consent first (or deemed consent), an order from the Residential Tenancy Branch, or where the tenancy agreement allows it. The landlord can't charge a fee for consent, and the pad rent and the date of the next increase stay the same for the buyer.
Assignment on a sale (MHPTA s. 28): Assi: Assignment on a sale: assigning the site tenancy transfers the pad tenancy to the buyer for good. A tenant can assign only with the landlord's written consent first (or deemed consent), an order from the Residential Tenancy Branch, or where the tenancy agreement allows it. The landlord can't charge a fee for consent, and the pad rent and the date of the next increase stay the same for the buyer.

Where both the home and the site are rented, a Residential Tenancy Agreement applies instead.
In a strata, 55+ is a registered bylaw u: In a strata, 55+ is a registered bylaw with exemptions set by law. In a park, 55+ is a rule in the park's written rules; the strata exemptions don't apply, and the park's wording decides. Get the park rules in writing before you remove subjects.
In a strata, 55+ is a registered bylaw with exemptions set by law. In a park, 55+ is a rule in the park's written rules; the strata exemptions don't apply, and the park's wording decides.
No: you own the home (a chattel) and ren: No. You own the home and rent the pad; your right to the site is the pad tenancy assigned to you. Pioneer Park in Aldergrove is the exception: it's a co-op.
There is therefore no in-area condo stoc: There are no condos to list on this page. Note that some of the plan pages linked below say their plans were "repealed by the Township of Langley on June 15, 2026" and replaced by Bylaw 6202 or 6203, but the Township's own Willoughby Community Plan Update page shows only first and second reading of Bylaws 6201, 6202 and 6203 on May 25, 2026, with a public hearing set for June 15, 2026. Check the current status with the Township.
On MLS®: there is no board sub-area for: On MLS®, there's no single area for this topic; this page covers the whole Township.
Where condo stock concentrates under the: Where condos are planned: the Township's Willoughby update treats Willoughby as its urban growth area, expected to take a large share of future population growth, with TransLink's proposed bus rapid transit on 200 Street as a key driver and a new transit-oriented development permit area proposed. That's plan policy, not buildings.
What the page actually is: plan tiles on: This page lists the Township's community plans (Aldergrove, Brookswood-Fernridge, Murrayville, Walnut Grove and Willoughby) and the Willoughby neighbourhood plans (Carvolth, Central Gordon Estate, Jericho, Latimer, North East Gordon Estate, Routley, Smith, Williams and Yorkson), each linking to the Township's website.
Transit frame named by the Township: Tra: Transit: TransLink's proposed bus rapid transit on 200 Street is a key driver of the Township's Willoughby Transit Corridor Plan.
Condo stock concentrates in four pockets: Most condos are in four places: Gladwin Road beside Mill Lake, Simon Avenue in Clearbrook, South Fraser Way downtown, and Montrose Avenue in Historic Downtown.
Start with the depreciation report on an: Start with the depreciation report for any building from before 2000: on Gladwin Road and Simon Avenue, the first required reports arrive just as roofs, pipes and parkades come due.
Abbotsford's tallest condo stock is one: Abbotsford's tallest condo building is Mahogany at Mill Lake, 2180 Gladwin Road: a 27-storey concrete tower with 152 suites above three storeys of commercial space and a two-level underground parkade, developed by Quantum Properties Mahogany LP and built by Ventana Construction.
Part of that tower is not strata resale: Part of that tower isn't for sale: floors five to ten of Mahogany are run by Aging in Place at Mahogany as private rental suites for independent seniors, with six floor plans from 674 to 1,661 sq ft. So the same address has both strata condos and rental suites.
The low-rise end of the stock is planned: The low-rise buildings are planned at six storeys and under: in the Historic Downtown plan, the Urban 1 – Midrise designation allows up to 6 storeys, and Urban 2 – Ground Oriented allows rowhouses, townhouses, multiplexes and duplexes.
Mill Lake Park, the green edge of the ce: Mill Lake Park, beside the central condo buildings, is reached from Bevan Avenue and Emerson Street.
Clearbrook Library is at 32320 George Fe: Clearbrook Library is at 32320 George Ferguson Way and the Abbotsford library branch is at 33355 Bevan Avenue, both in the central area where most of the condos are.
The cap sits above the middle of the com: The $800,000 cap is above the middle of the market: Abbotsford's median for condos and townhomes combined was $497,500 in September 2026, $302,500 below the cap. That median mixes townhomes with condos, so it shows where the cap sits, not what a typical condo costs.
Where does Abbotsford's attached stock a: Where are Abbotsford's condos and townhomes?
By September 2026 inventory, Central Abb: In September 2026, Central Abbotsford had 256 condos and townhomes for sale and Abbotsford West 210, out of 572 across Abbotsford; the rural areas (Bradner, Matsqui, Sumas Mountain and Sumas Prairie) had none. Those numbers are condos and townhomes combined, not just condos under $800,000.
That housing mix is exactly why the 55+: That mix of homes is why there are no 55+ homes to buy here.
The one 55+ address in the sub-area, Cas: The one 55+ address in the area, Cascade Court, is on Delair Road on the McMillan-side flats at the west edge, the part of Abbotsford East closest to Clearbrook and Mill Lake, where most of the city's 55+ homes are.
Why there is no \"45+\" anything anymore: Why there are no "45+" buildings anymore: since November 24, 2022, 55+ is the only age a BC strata bylaw can set, and every 19+, 40+ or 45+ bylaw became invalid that day. So an old east-side ad describing a 45+ complex proves nothing today, and the same rule applies to any 55+ home an east-side seller buys across town in Abbotsford West.
The empty 55+ shelf is a housing-mix fac: There are no 55+ homes here because of the mix of housing, not because the search missed them. Age-restricted complexes get built where condos and townhomes already are, in Clearbrook and around Mill Lake, which is why Abbotsford's 55+ homes are on the west side.
The bylaw route most owners use is a sec: What most owners do is add a secondary suite: one is allowed in every single detached house, if the lot meets the City's criteria (at least 400 m² with 12 m of frontage, on a collector or local road, and not on a cul-de-sac bulb). Strata age rules don't apply to a freehold house; there's no age bylaw on a detached lot.
The Assisted Living Registry and the Sen: The Assisted Living Registry and the Seniors Directory show the city's care and subsidized seniors housing in Central Abbotsford and Abbotsford West (Menno Place, Tabor Village and the Marshall Road group).
Presales and assignments (REDMA): Sage i: Presales and assignments: Sage is sold under BC's presale rules, which give you 7 days to cancel from the later of signing and receiving the disclosure statement, and require deposits to be held in trust.
Where the townhouse stock actually sits:: Where the townhouses are: not on the hillside. The complexes are on the McMillan and Old Yale flats at the west edge (Yale Court, Immel Ridge and East Ridge), at Whatcom Road and Old Yale Road by Highway 1 (Vantage at Whatcom), and on the Eagle Mountain and Old Yale east side (The Falls and Mountain View Village).
Is there any condo stock in the hillside: Are there any condos in the hillside neighbourhoods (McKee, Auguston and Sandy Hill)?
Fee-simple lots are the default land for: Fee-simple lots are the norm: the detached homes are freehold, in the City's RS3, RS5 and RS6 residential zones, "from established streets along Old Yale Road to newer subdivisions on the McKee and Eagle Mountain slopes." A bare lot in one of those subdivisions is fee simple, with no strata, Form B or strata fees. Zoning, the Official Community Plan and any covenants or building scheme on title apply instead.
What slope or flood diligence applies to: What slope or flood checks apply to a hillside or low-lying lot?
You would own the land; the open diligen: You'd own the land. The question to check is the home's status in the Manufactured Home Registry: still registered as a movable home, or de-registered and attached to the land.
On the edges, yes: Low lots toward the S: On the edges, yes. Low lots toward the Sumas River and Whatcom Road are in the floodplain, and McKee-area slope lots are in the Steep Slope Development Permit Area, with geotechnical conditions. Check the property on the City's WebMap and on title before making an offer.
Zoning Bylaw s.140.3.8 permits one secon: The zoning bylaw allows one secondary suite in every single detached house; City council reports give criteria including a lot of at least 400 m² with at least 12 m of frontage on a collector or local road, not on a cul-de-sac bulb.
The detached stock is freehold and attac: The detached homes are freehold, and the condos and townhomes are strata.
No Fraser Valley Regional Library branch: There's no library branch in the area; Clearbrook Library, 32320 George Ferguson Way, is to the west.
Under Zoning Bylaw 2014 No. 2400, a seco: Under Abbotsford's zoning bylaw, a secondary suite must be less than half the size of the main home, and garden suites and coach houses can cover up to 15% of the lot, to a maximum of 100 m². The small-scale multi-unit housing amendment (adopted June 25, 2024) sets the rules for eligible lots.
The farm stock here is working farms, no: The farms here are working farms, not houses on lots. The City calls Abbotsford one of the most intensively and diversely farmed areas in Canada, with many kinds of crops and livestock.
Farm dwellings sit inside that working f: Farm homes are part of those working farms. The Agricultural Land Commission generally allows one main house per ALR parcel, plus one additional home only where the parcel qualifies.
City zoning still applies on top of the: City zoning applies on top of the ALR rules. The City tells buyers to check current zoning, future land use and development permit areas through its property information search or WebMap.
Check ALR status and residence limits on: Check ALR status and the limits on homes with the Agricultural Land Commission. Local governments can add their own limits on homes in the ALR, so read both the City's zoning and the Commission's rules for the same parcel.
The City publishes its communities as de: The City publishes its communities as demographic profile areas, including Bradner – Mt. Lehman (area 1), Aberdeen (area 6) and West Abbotsford (area 7). The real estate board's area names and the City's overlap but aren't the same list.
The city-wide stock is governed by Abbot: Across the city, Abbotsford's Zoning Bylaw (2014, No. 2400) applies, with zones running from agricultural (A1 and A2) through urban residential zones such as RS3 and the infill RS7 zone to apartment and mixed-use zones.
Under the ALC frame, generally one princ: On ALR land, the Agricultural Land Commission generally allows one main house of 500 m² or less, with no more than 1,000 m² of fill for building it; a secondary suite only inside that house; and one additional detached home of up to 90 m² (properties of 40 ha or less) or 186 m² (over 40 ha). City zoning must also allow the home, and anything larger or more needs the Commission's approval.
The stock is working poultry operations: These are working poultry farms on large ALR parcels, which the City splits into upland and lowland areas. Its AgRefresh process divided the Agriculture designation into Agriculture 1 – Uplands and Agriculture 2 – Lowlands to reflect existing lots, keeping a minimum new lot size of 8 hectares in the A1 zone and 16 hectares in the A2 zone.
The City also adopted a new Official Com: The City also adopted a new Official Community Plan in December 2025. After more than two years of planning, the update focused on housing supply and variety and allows for 37,185 homes over 20 years. That growth is planned inside the urban area, so poultry land stays governed by the ALR boundary, not urban rezoning.
Because the main production prairie floo: Because the main farming prairie flooded in 2021 and again in 2025. The City says the November 2021 flood forced the evacuation of over 1,100 properties and caused major livestock and poultry losses, and the December 2025 flood put 485 properties under evacuation order and 1,069 under alert. Allow for checks on dikes, pumps and flood construction rules, and their cost, in any Sumas Prairie purchase.
In the listings we checked: Abbotsford E: Current listings are in Abbotsford East (Marble Hill Drive in McMillan, and Marshall Road) and Abbotsford West (Simon Avenue). Across the city, Central Abbotsford and Abbotsford West had the most condos and townhomes for sale in September 2026 (256 and 210).
Where the 55+ stock actually is: it clus: Where the 55+ homes are: in Clearbrook and around Mill Lake. Almost every age-restricted building I know of in this area is on Old Yale Road, Tims Avenue, Gladwin Road, Peardonville Road or Simon Avenue.
55+ is the only age bylaw a BC strata ma: 55+ is the only age bylaw a BC strata can have: since November 24, 2022, a strata can limit residents to 55 or older, and any older 19+, 40+ or 45+ bylaw stopped being enforceable that day. That's why an older description of Trethewey Tower as 45+ can't be relied on.
Almost all of Abbotsford's 55+ strata st: Almost all of Abbotsford's 55+ strata homes are in this one corridor. If you want another part of Abbotsford, you're mostly choosing between detached houses, life leases and rentals.
The frame roads are Highway 1 across the: The main roads are Highway 1 across the north-centre (with interchanges at Mt. Lehman Road, Clearbrook Road and McCallum Road), South Fraser Way running east–west, and Clearbrook Road and Mt. Lehman Road running north–south, with the Agricultural Land Reserve and Abbotsford International Airport (YXX) to the southwest.
Two supportive-housing projects frame th: Two supportive housing projects are on the Gladys and South Fraser edge: the City has BC Housing lease agreements for 61 supportive units being built on Riverside Road and 48 units on Gladys Avenue going through approvals (City update, October 2026). That's useful to know if you're comparing buildings in the Clearbrook and Simon Avenue corridor.
55+ is the only legal age bylaw: a strata can only require residents to be 55 or older, with exemptions for existing residents, live-in caregivers and (since May 1, 2023) younger spouses or partners and some children. Carriage Lane, Fircrest Estates and The Wedgewood are the 55+ townhouse complexes here; confirm the registered bylaw on the Form B.
Rural and agricultural parcels (Mt. Lehm: Rural and farm properties (Mt. Lehman Road and the airport edge): there are acreages with houses on the rural west and southwest edges. Servicing is the big difference: lots outside the urban boundary in rural residential zones may not be on City water or sewer, and use wells and septic systems instead. Serviced and rural land on the west side are different purchases with different things to check.
Schools physically in or serving the wes: Schools on the west side (SD34 Abbotsford): École Clearbrook Elementary (3614 Clearbrook Road), John MacLure Community School (2990 Oriole Crescent), Colleen and Gordie Howe Middle, Eugene Reimer Middle (3433 Firhill Drive) and W.J. Mouat Secondary. Check the catchment for a specific address with the school district.
SSMUH / added units on a lot: Small Scal: Small-scale housing and extra units: Abbotsford's zoning bylaw allows one secondary suite in every single detached house, with City criteria including a lot of at least 400 m² with 12 m of frontage, on a collector or local road and not on a cul-de-sac bulb. A suite must be under 50% of the main home, and a coach house or garden suite can cover up to 15% of the lot, to a maximum of 100 m². These are Abbotsford's rules only, and they don't override the A1 and A2 minimum lot sizes or the ALR on the rural edge.
Well and septic diligence (rural edge):: Wells and septic on the rural edge: a price that assumes city services is too high for a rural lot without them.
The plan citation on most west-side page: Many west-side descriptions still quote the old 2016 plan. The current one is the 2050 plan, with its transit corridor around Highstreet.
ALR frame (rural west/southwest edges):: ALR rules (rural west and southwest edges): on ALR land, the main house can be up to 500 m² with up to 1,000 m² of fill, a suite only inside it, and one additional home of up to 90 m² (40 ha or less) or 186 m² (over 40 ha). Registering a strata plan counts as subdividing in the ALR and needs the Agricultural Land Commission's permission.
Strata tenure applied to land: you own a: How strata ownership of land works: you own a strata lot (here, a lot with a rancher on it) and a share of the common property, you pay a bare-land strata fee, and the strata's bylaws apply to your lot. It isn't fee simple: "Freehold Strata" on title means strata, so you need a Form B as well as a title search.
The west side mixes older Clearbrook det: The west side mixes older detached houses in Clearbrook with City Centre apartments and townhouses around Mill Lake and South Fraser Way.
\"Aberdeen\" is both the Fraser Valley R: "Aberdeen" is both the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board's name for the area and an official City of Abbotsford name: profile area 6 in the City's 2020 Demographic Profiles, separate from Bradner–Mt. Lehman (area 1) and West Abbotsford (area 7).
Where condo stock concentrates: nowhere: Where the condos are: there aren't any in Aberdeen.
In BC the only legal strata age bylaw is: In BC, the only legal strata age bylaw is 55+.
\"Aberdeen\" is both the board sub-area: "Aberdeen" is both the real estate board's name for the area and an official City name: profile area 6 in the City's 2020 Demographic Profiles, separate from Bradner – Mt. Lehman (area 1) and West Abbotsford (area 7).
The acreage is the parcel stock itself,: Acreages here sell whole, as fee-simple properties.
The stock is single-detached houses on r: The homes are detached houses on rural and agricultural lots; the area is rural, with working farms, under Abbotsford's zoning bylaw.
Homes are effectively all freehold farm: Homes are almost all freehold farm and rural residential lots. The only strata housing I know of in the wider area is the Lantern Park townhome complex at 27640 Lantern Avenue, at the western edge by the Aldergrove border.
Neither. It is a City of Abbotsford comm: Neither. It's a City of Abbotsford community: the rural land around Bradner Road, south of Fraser Highway, west of Clearbrook and north of the airport. The City treats it as its own area (profile area 6), separate from Bradner – Mt. Lehman and West Abbotsford. Aldergrove (Langley) is further west along Fraser Highway.
Price from the rural default: lots outsi: Assume rural services when you price: lots outside the urban boundary may use wells and septic systems instead of City water and sewer. Look up the well record in the provincial GWELLS registry, and confirm the septic system was filed with Fraser Health by an authorized professional.
Pull the well record in GWELLS and confi: For any rural lot, look up the well record in GWELLS and confirm the septic system's filing with Fraser Health.
Aberdeen Elementary at 2975 Bradner Road: Aberdeen Elementary, 2975 Bradner Road, is the public elementary school in the area. That address is in the Aberdeen Elementary catchment, followed by Eugene Reimer Middle and Rick Hansen Secondary. Check the catchment for a specific address with the Abbotsford School District.
Board position: Agassiz is a CADREB boar: Agassiz is covered by the Chilliwack and District Real Estate Board (Harrison Mills is listed under it), which publishes statistics only for its whole area, so there are no separate market figures for Agassiz.
Where condo stock concentrates: the town: Where the strata homes are: they're townhouses, grouped on Mackay Crescent, Heath Road and Morrow Road around the core: Village Gate and The Langtry on Mackay Crescent, Gallagher Landing and Town Centre Gable on Heath Road, Fraser Green on the Agassiz-Rosedale Highway and the Morrow Road complexes to the south.
Renting a unit out (landlord frame): RTB: Renting a unit out: rent increases are capped at 2.3% for 2026 and 2.2% for 2027 for ordinary tenancies.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates:: Where the townhouses are: in the townsite core, on Mackay Crescent (Village Gate and The Langtry), Heath Road, the Agassiz-Rosedale Highway (Fraser Green and MountView) and Morrow Road (Huckleberry Lane). The District's Official Community Plan describes recent development the same way: mostly single-family houses and townhouses in the townsite, with some semi-detached and low-rise multi-family homes. Townhouses are the main strata homes, and most homes overall are freehold.
Flood frame: the townsite sits on the Fr: Flooding: the townsite is on the Fraser River floodplain, behind dikes. The local system includes Maria Slough and the Hammersley, Kilby and Bateson pump stations, and the District has a floodplain bylaw with flood construction levels for each area.
They are built townhouse stock. They are: They're built townhouses, not lots for sale.

Lot sizes/zones: under Zoning Bylaw 2020: Lot sizes and zoning: in the Agricultural Lowland (AL) zone, the minimum lot is 7.5 ha for land excluded or exempted from the ALR or approved for subdivision within it, 1 ha for a boundary adjustment, and 0.2 ha for a homesite severance or boundary adjustment approved by the Agricultural Land Commission; the minimum width is 25 m. There are smaller residential lots near the school and along Chilliwack Central Road; check their zoning with the City.
The City states nearly 70% of land in Ch: The City says nearly 70% of Chilliwack's land is in the ALR and not available for development, which is why East Chilliwack stays low-density.
Because the ground is ALR farm land plan: Because it's ALR farmland planned through the City's Agricultural Area Plan, with mostly dairy and poultry farms, nurseries and greenhouses, and homes on ALR land can't be stratified. So the housing stays freehold houses on larger lots.

What matters for a purchase is the dike: What matters when buying here is the dikes and the floodplain. The neighbourhood is in the Fraser River floodplain, which the City regulates under its floodplain bylaw: new buildings must be at the flood construction level plus 0.6 metres, setbacks apply from the Fraser River, and a covenant can be registered on title where that extra height is waived.

Rundle Middle (45660 Hocking Avenue) and Chilliwack Secondary (46363 Yale Road).

Only inside the Agricultural Land Reserv: Only within the Agricultural Land Reserve's limits on homes. Anything more needs an application to the Agricultural Land Commission, and City bylaws can be stricter, not looser.
The scale of the farm frame is city-wide: For scale: Chilliwack has 41,862 acres in the ALR, about two-thirds of the city's land, most of it farmland on the Fraser River valley bottom.

Pad rentals follow the same rules across BC: pad rent can go up once every 12 months with three full months' notice, by up to 2.3% plus a proportional amount for 2026 (2.2% for 2027), and a sale needs the landlord's consent to assign the tenancy. Mission Mobile Home Park's 55+ rule is a park rule, not a strata bylaw; listings at Green Acres say park approval is required and mention no age rule.
The valley has a documented history — th: The valley has flooded before: the 1948 dike break put Hatzic Prairie largely under water.

Three Edelweiss Drive addresses are thre: Addresses on Edelweiss Drive are owned in different ways. 20649 Edelweiss Drive looks like a townhouse, with no ownership type given in its listing; 20668 Edelweiss Drive is a freehold fourplex, expressly "no strata". Check each address on its own.
Detached cabins and chalets are the hous: The houses here are detached cabins and chalets, in a small resort village of about 200 homes. The regional district's evacuation guide describes them as mainly vacation homes and short-term rentals, with the resort at the upper end of the village.
Hemlock Valley OCP, FVRD Bylaw No. 1626,: Hemlock Valley Official Community Plan (Fraser Valley Regional District Bylaw 1626, 2021, Electoral Area C): adopted March 17, 2022, replacing the plan from 2000 (as of November 3, 2026). It's the plan that applies to every Hemlock lot.
Evacuation is a real due-diligence item,: Take evacuation seriously: the regional district publishes an evacuation guide for the valley, and there's only one road out, past Harrison Mills.
Existing accommodation base, per the OCP: Existing accommodation, according to the Official Community Plan: 226 resort residential units at Hemlock (1,072 bed units), about 60% of them ski-in/ski-out or a comfortable walk from the base area. Those are built homes, not vacant land.
Property taxes — RURAL regime (the only: Property taxes follow the rural rules: a property outside any city, town, district or village is in a rural area, and its tax notice comes from the Province's Surveyor of Taxes; you pay the Province, not the regional district. Rural taxes are due July 2, with a 5% penalty on anything unpaid then and another 5% on anything unpaid on October 31. No city's tax dates apply to a Hemlock Valley lot.
Park Street Manor turned 50 in 2025. The: Park Street Manor turned 50 in 2025. The Hope Standard reported its 50th anniversary on July 18, 2025 (it was founded in 1975 as a partnership between a society and the provincial and federal governments). It has been the core of the town's seniors housing for decades.
Housing shape: predominantly freehold de: Homes: mostly freehold detached houses, with post-war and 1970s–90s houses on the townsite grid, ranchers in Silver Creek and recreational properties around Kawkawa Lake. A smaller number of strata homes are near the core, and there are manufactured homes in parks on the District's edges. The District's Interim Housing Needs Report (November 2024) shows permits from 2021 to October 2024 were mostly for single-family homes (70) plus suites (22), and estimates a 20-year need of 2,123 homes.
Flood — the District's first diligence i: Check flooding first: the Province's design flood for the Fraser River is measured at the Hope gauge (based on the 1894 flood, now treated as roughly a 500-year event), and new provincial floodplain maps for the Coquihalla and Fraser rivers from Yale to Mission came out in June 2026. The District looks after two regulated Coquihalla River dikes, River Parade (0.93 km) and Glenhalla Subdivision (1.01 km), and building in hazard areas needs a Flood and Erosion Hazards Development Permit with a qualified professional's report (as Council required on January 13, 2025 at 62180 Delair Road). Check a property's flood status before pricing or making an offer; a nearby dike doesn't remove the permit step.
The town's largest apartment building ca: The town's largest apartment building isn't for sale. The Riverstone's 37 apartments and eight townhouses are all rent-geared-to-income homes (opened July 2, 2021), so there are fewer apartments to buy in Hope than a count of buildings suggests.

The nearest recreation and library are o: The nearest recreation centre and library are outside the area: Matsqui Recreation Centre, 3106 Clearbrook Road, and Clearbrook Library, 32320 George Ferguson Way. Services are south of the prairie, not on it, which is also why there are no condos here.

ALR vs non-ALR split: The prairie's agri: ALR or not: the prairie is in the Agricultural Land Reserve, and the City updated its farm policies through its AgRefresh review, which led to plan and zoning amendments in 2022.

One non-profit runs most of Mission's se: One non-profit runs most of Mission's seniors housing. The Mission Association for Seniors Housing operates The Cedars (7380 Hurd Street), Welton Towers (33214 2nd Avenue) and, through its life lease society, Cedar Valley Manor (8358 Cedar Street), and says all of its housing is for people 55 and older. The Waterfront itself is described by th: The City describes the Waterfront as the largest undeveloped river frontage in the Lower Mainland, so most waterfront housing is still planned, not built.
Confirmed apartment-form. 33 units in th: Apartments: 33 units, Strata Plan LMS1049, 3 storeys, wood frame with brick and vinyl siding. Listings say gas and hot water are included in the strata fees and parking is secured under the building. The zoning is MA1.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates:: Where the townhouses are: in the urban core and Mission West. Cherry Lane and Luther Place are on or near Seventh Avenue, Briskham Hill is on Briskham Street west of downtown, and Archer Green is on Nelson Street in Mission West.

First-page cards are labelled with the b: Current listings are in the core Mission area (McRae Avenue, 4th Avenue, Egglestone Avenue and Hillcrest Avenue, for example) and Mission West (Alexandra Street and Mitchell Avenue), and include detached houses, condos, townhouses, half duplexes and a manufactured home.
SSMUH / added units (Mission frame): the: Small-scale housing and extra units in Mission: the City added the provincial small-scale multi-unit housing rules to its zoning bylaw on July 17, 2024, and merged the Urban Residential 930 Secondary Dwelling zone (R930s) into R930. Being allowed extra units doesn't mean you can subdivide.
Floodplain / hazard diligence: Parcel-le: Floodplain and hazards: the City looks at hazards, creek setbacks and geotechnical issues for each property through its site assessment for development applications, which asks about septic systems, ditches and ponds, and vegetation, among other things.
It spans 1975 (Glenkirk Court) to 2026 c: From 1975 (Glenkirk Court) to buildings finishing in 2026 (Montgomery and Silver & Cedar). In September 2026, Mission recorded 231: In September 2026, Mission had 231 detached homes for sale and 28 sold, at a median of $814,000 (29 days on the market), and 122 condos and townhomes for sale and 10 sold, at a median of $430,000 (61 days). Those figures are for all of Mission.
Mission's condo stock is small and centr: Mission has few condos, and they're central: almost every apartment building is in the urban core around 1st Avenue, 2nd Avenue, Horne Street and Stave Lake Street, below the hillside neighbourhoods.

Only a 55-or-older residency bylaw is le: Only a 55-and-older bylaw is legal in a BC strata, with exemptions for existing residents, live-in caregivers and, since May 1, 2023, younger spouses or partners and some children. That's the basis for the 55+ rules at Briskham Manor and Luther Place; confirm them on the Form B.
Every Mission strata of five or more lot: Every Mission strata with five or more lots must now get a depreciation report every five years and can't vote to skip it (since July 1, 2024), and must put at least 10% of its operating budget into the contingency reserve. Those two rules are behind special levies in the 1975–1993 buildings.
Preston on Fourteenth, 32690 14th Avenue: Preston on Fourteenth, 32690 14th Avenue, by Redekop Faye: a four-storey building with 103 condos plus 11 affordable rental homes, finished in 2023 and now selling as resales.
For the 1975–1993 resale stock, the Form: For the 1975–1993 resale buildings, the Form B and the current depreciation report are the key documents: they show the contingency reserve balance and the planned work that decide future special levies.
Very little, and it is concentrated. The: Very few, and they're close together. The condos are three resale low-rises from 1975 to 1993 (Glenkirk Court, Mission Manor and Briskham Manor), plus the Redekop Faye buildings Preston on Fourteenth (2023), Montgomery and Silver & Cedar. By September 2026 inventory, the urban \: In September 2026, the urban Mission area had 104 condos and townhomes for sale, Mission West 8 and Hemlock 9, out of 122 across Mission; the rural areas had almost none. Those numbers are condos and townhomes combined, not just condos under $800,000.

Only with the licence position confirmed: Only with the water licence checked. Groundwater used for anything other than household use, such as irrigation, needs a provincial water licence, with fees, before it can legally be used; household use doesn't need one. For any farm that relies on irrigation, ask for the licence, or proof one isn't needed.
The City's Rural Mission Strategy covers: The City's Rural Mission Strategy covers the rural communities inside the city.
Mission's 55+ map is two geographies, no: Mission's 55+ homes are in two very different places. Almost all the strata, life lease and co-op homes are within a few blocks on the 7th Avenue and Cedar Street bench (Cherry Lane, Luther Place, Cedar Valley Manor and St. Andrew's Place, plus the Briskham Street pocket west of downtown), while the only rural 55+ homes are in the manufactured home parks on Lougheed Highway. One listing's \"First Nations Lease\" li: If a listing mentions a "First Nations Lease", it changes what you need to check: where a park sits on leased First Nations land, that lease's term, consent rules and registration sit under every pad tenancy in the park. Confirm it from the park's documents, not the listing, before making an offer.
It is the top tail: the September 2026 c: It's the very top of the market: Mission's September 2026 medians were $814,000 for detached homes and $430,000 for condos and townhomes, so $1.8 million is more than double the typical detached sale price.
The ALC frame permits one principal resi: On ALR land, the Agricultural Land Commission allows one main house of up to 500 m², a secondary suite only if it's entirely inside that house and local bylaws allow suites, and at most one additional detached home of 90 m² (parcels of 40 ha or less) or 186 m² (over 40 ha). Local governments can restrict homes further through zoning.
Manufactured-home parks run on tenancy l: Manufactured home parks follow tenancy law, not strata law: under BC's Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act, the resident owns the home and rents the pad. A park's age rule is a park rule, not a strata bylaw. That's why strata 55+ rules don't settle the question of Oasis's "adult side", and why Mission Mobile Home Park's 55+ status comes from its park documents and listings, not a strata Form B.
Park closure / conversion (MHPTA s.42):: Park closure or conversion: if a landlord plans to convert all or much of a park to something other than a manufactured home park, they must have all the government permits and approvals first, give a full 12 months' notice, and pay each tenant $20,000 by the date the notice takes effect. The tenant can move out early with at least 10 days' written notice and can dispute the notice within 15 days. In some cases (the home can't be moved, there's no site within a reasonable distance, and no tax is owing on the home), the tenant can apply for more: the home's assessed value minus the $20,000. If the landlord doesn't go ahead within a reasonable time, they owe $5,000 or 12 months' rent, whichever is more.
No manufactured-home statistic exists in: There are no separate market figures for manufactured homes
Assignment consent is the hidden closing: The park's consent is a closing step people forget. A house sale closes on title; a home in a park also needs the landlord's consent to assign the site tenancy, and the buyer must get the park rules before consent is even requested. Build that timing into the contract, or you could own the home before the pad is yours.
The sale works by assigning your site te: You sell by assigning your site tenancy, which needs the landlord's written consent first (or deemed consent, an order from the Residential Tenancy Branch, or permission in the agreement itself). The landlord can't charge a fee for consent, you must give the buyer the park rules and written tenancy terms before asking for consent, the pad rent carries over unchanged, and an unreasonable refusal can be taken to Residential Tenancy Branch dispute resolution.
Under MHPTA s.42 the landlord needs all: The landlord needs all permits first, then must give 12 months' notice and pay $20,000 per tenancy, with more owed where the home can't be moved or there's no site within a reasonable distance, and a further payment ($5,000 or 12 months' rent, whichever is more) if the landlord doesn't go ahead with the conversion within a reasonable time. Check who owns the park and whether there are any signs of redevelopment.
Check the dike and flood frame on south-: Check dikes and flooding for south-side complexes: the Fraser River floodplain runs along the city's south edge, low areas such as Hatzic Prairie are protected by the Dewdney dikes, and the City charges a diking levy on top of the usual City, school, regional district and BC Assessment charges.
Geography: Mission West is inside the Ci: Mission West is inside the City of Mission, on its western side, covering Silverdale and the rural edge toward Stave Falls and Ruskin. City of Mission planning, zoning and the flat 10% tax penalty apply; the rural 5% plus 5% rules don't. Sources describe Archer Green differently: a presale directory calls its ownership "Condominium" and its building type "Townhouse", and MLS® listings show freehold strata townhouses. The Wilson Street parks are listed as "Mission-West" in some listings and "Stave Falls" in others, for the same addresses; either way, how the parks are owned and the City's tax rules are the same.
Listings here carry the board sub-area \: Listings here show the "Mission-West" area with a Mission mailing address, on streets including Wilson Street, Hayward Street, Olson Avenue, Haffner Terrace, Silverdale Avenue, Keystone Avenue, Gunn Avenue, Nelson Street and Townshipline Avenue.
Secondary suites (City frame): all secon: Secondary suites in the City: every suite in Mission must be registered with the City. A suite must be a self-contained living space in a single-family home, suites aren't allowed in townhouses or rowhomes, a new suite needs a building permit, and a yearly suite fee of $63 plus utility fees goes on the property tax notice.
Mission West's \"highest ratio in Missio: Mission West's "highest sales ratio in Mission" comes from a single sale. With so few homes for sale, don't base pricing on it.
A detached second home on a rural Missio: A detached second home on a rural Mission West lot is first a zoning question. A suite inside the house must be registered with the City (with a building permit for a new one, a $63 yearly fee plus utility fees, and no suites in townhouses), while a detached coach home or garden cottage depends on the property's zoning. On ALR land, a second home is limited to 90 m² or 186 m², depending on the parcel's size.
Geography, stated up front: Mission West: Mission West is inside the City of Mission, on its western side, covering Silverdale and the rural edge toward Stave Falls and Ruskin. So City of Mission planning, zoning and the flat 10% tax penalty apply, and the rural 5% plus 5% rules don't.
Nearby areas and alternate names: Stave: Nearby: Stave Falls and Steelhead to the north, Silverdale in the southwest of the area itself, central Mission to the east, and Ruskin and Maple Ridge across the Stave River to the west.
