Sumas Mountain detached stock splits int: Detached homes on Sumas Mountain are of two kinds: serviced subdivision houses on the lower McKee and Auguston benches, and rural acreage houses higher up and in Straiton. The McKee Neighbourhood Plan covers about 842 hectares on Sumas Mountain, with steep forested slopes and creek headwaters.
Eagle Mountain catchment review, Abbotsf: Eagle Mountain catchment review, Abbotsford School District (SD34): the district is reviewing catchments on the Eagle Mountain side of the mountain; details are on its engagement site.
A zero-listing month is a thin-market fa: A month with nothing for sale means few homes come up here, not that there are no homes.
Where the townhouse stock actually conce: Where the townhouses are: at the foot of the mountain and on its lower slopes, in the built Auguston and McKee neighbourhoods and on Lower Sumas Mountain Road. The upper mountain and the regional district side are rural homes on large lots.
The next townhouses on the mountain are: The next townhouses on the mountain are planned at its foot, in one proposal. It's only a proposal: not built and not a presale.
City-side servicing contrast: the built: Servicing: the built City neighbourhoods are the serviced side of the mountain; on the regional district side, homes rely on wells and septic systems, as noted above.
Semá:th First Nation states the Lightnin: Semá:th First Nation says the Lightning Rock site on the mountain is a culturally significant area in its traditional territory, and ownership was transferred to Semá:th First Nation under an agreement with the Province. Keep that history in mind when looking at land on the mountain. The Province, Semá:th First Nation and the City also agreed to a study of an alternate route to the quarry.
The park-form stock that does exist here: The one community of this kind here is a bare-land strata of detached houses, where you own your lot. It isn't a pad-rental park.
The care and 55+ stock is down the mount: Care and 55+ homes are down the mountain, not on it: every 55+ complex to buy in Abbotsford that I know of is in Abbotsford West or Central Abbotsford, with a few on the Abbotsford East side. On the mountain itself, a downsizer's choices are Straiton (no age restriction) and fee-simple houses.
What diligence does a slope acreage need: What should I check on a sloped acreage that I wouldn't on a flat lot?
City side or FVRD side — does it change: City side or regional district side: does it change what I should check?
Sumas Prairie is an FVREB board sub-area: Sumas Prairie is in the City of Abbotsford, and is a real estate board area.
The zero is structural, not a slow month: There are no condos or townhomes here for a reason, not because of a slow month: Sumas Prairie is farmland in the ALR, where homes can't be stratified. Don't wait for a condo project on the prairie; the rules don't allow one.
The flood-mitigation money is real, and: The flood protection money is real, but the plan isn't finished. About $220 million in provincial funding since 2021, and $76.6 million for the Barrowtown Pump Station, sound like a done deal. But the Province says the initiative's hydraulic model, risk assessment, ecological assessment and pump station studies are at various stages, and that flooding in December again showed how exposed the area is. Treat the prairie as flood land first, and count on the protection work second.
Flood sorts every parcel on the floor: t: Flooding matters for every property on the prairie floor. The Sumas River Watershed Flood Mitigation Planning Initiative was signed in April 2023, after the widespread flooding on Sumas Prairie from heavy rain in November 2021. The Province is providing $3.3 million for design and assessment work and has provided about $220 million for recovery, preparedness and flood protection in Abbotsford and Sumas Prairie since 2021, including $76.6 million for upgrades to the Barrowtown Pump Station. It also says flooding in December again showed the area is highly prone to water surges, and that the hydraulic model, risk assessment, ecological assessment and pump station studies are at various stages, so flood protection is still being planned. Confirm a property's flood status (elevation, flood construction level, and where it sits relative to dikes and pumps) with the City.
The board does not publish sub-area medi: There are no published medians for individual areas like this one.
The zero attached row is structural, not: There are no condos or townhomes here for a reason, not because of a slow month: Sumas Prairie is farmland in the ALR, where homes can't be stratified and new lots must be at least 8 ha or 16 ha. Don't wait for a strata or townhouse project on the prairie; the rules don't allow one.
Abbotsford's attached stock is in the ur: Abbotsford's condos and townhomes are in its urban areas.
Because ALR residences cannot be stratif: Because homes on ALR land can't be stratified. On ALR land you can have one main house up to 500 m², a suite only inside it, and at most one additional home of 90 m² (40 ha or less) or 186 m² (over 40 ha): a house on land, never condo lots.
Real Canadian Superstore, 2855 Gladwin R: Real Canadian Superstore, 2855 Gladwin Road, Abbotsford, is the main grocery store for this area; I don't know of a supermarket on the prairie itself.
The housing stock is farmhouses and rura: The homes are farmhouses and rural homes on working farms, not subdivisions: the prairie is designated Agricultural in Abbotsford's Official Community Plan and zoned mainly Agricultural One (A1) and Agricultural Two (A2).
Where the parcel is in the ALR, the ALC: On ALR land, the Agricultural Land Commission allows one main house of up to 500 m², a secondary suite only inside it, and at most one additional detached home of 90 m² (parcels of 40 ha or less) or 186 m² (over 40 ha). The City's limits also apply (a suite under 50% of the main home; a coach house or garden suite of up to 15% of the lot, to 100 m²). Confirm the parcel's ALR status and zoning first.
The housing is planned, newer stock rath: The homes here are newer and planned, not on an old townsite grid: Garrison Crossing is a residential subdivision on the former military base, and Canada Education Park takes up 200 acres of the 400-acre former base for institutional, commercial and residential development.
South Vedder Neighbourhood Plan implemen: South Vedder Neighbourhood Plan, east of Vedder Road below Promontory: a City of Chilliwack plan under the Official Community Plan, which expects infill redevelopment along Vedder Road with buildings of 3 to 6 storeys. The plan was adopted in April 2022 and kept in the 2050 Official Community Plan update in 2025 (as of November 3, 2026).
The lease clock is the real due-diligenc: The lease is the main thing to check at Cottonwood. Listings give a 2076 lease expiry with an option to extend, on leased First Nations land. Lenders, insurers and future buyers will all ask about the remaining term and how the extension works, so get the head-lease summary and park rules before removing subjects.
West Chilliwack is a board sub-area name: West Chilliwack is a real estate board area name, not a City of Chilliwack plan area. The City doesn't publish a boundary for it; it covers the western rural and farming part of the city, planned through the Agricultural Area Plan in the City's Official Community Plan.
In a 55+ park, yes, in effect: assignmen: In a 55+ park, yes, in effect: taking over a pad tenancy needs the park owner's consent, and the provincial rules let the owner refuse where no buyer meets the park's 55+ age requirement. Get the park rules in writing before making an offer; the seller must provide them.
This large Evans Road neighbour is a man: This large community on Evans Road is a manufactured home community (listings describe manufactured homes in a 55+ community in central Sardis, on leased land), not a strata condo building.
Where condo stock actually concentrates:: Where the condos are: there's just one condo building in the area, on Evans Road.
Chilliwack's new OCP is recent: the Chil: Chilliwack's Official Community Plan is recent: the Chilliwack 2050 plan (Bylaw 5500, 2025) is the current city-wide plan and includes the Agricultural Area Plan, so keeping the west side for farming is current policy.
Cottonwood Village is a pad-rental park: Cottonwood Village is a pad-rental park, not townhouses, even though some listings say "Townhouse". Listings place it in either West Chilliwack or Sardis West Vedder.
Cottonwood Village (Cottonwood Mobile Ho: Cottonwood Village (also called Cottonwood Mobile Home Park or Cottonwood Retirement Village), 7610 Evans Road: not townhouses.
Listings for homes in the park carry for: Listings for homes in the park say "Townhouse" or "Row / Townhouse", and describe "duplex-style townhouse" and "rancher-style townhome" units, but these aren't townhouses you own with the land: you buy a manufactured home and rent the pad, on leased land, with no strata and a monthly pad fee.
Where townhouse stock actually concentra: Where the townhouses are: there aren't any in this area.
Search names: \"West Chilliwack\" and th: Other names for the area: "West Chilliwack", and "Evans" for the Evans Road corridor (as in BC Transit route 52 Evans and Evans Elementary).
Pet rule — conflict carried open: the pa: Pets: a park specialist's list says one pet is allowed at Cottonwood Village; confirm with the park.
The lease clock is the real due-diligenc: The lease is the main thing to check at Cottonwood. Listings give three different lease terms (to 2076 with an option to extend; to November 30, 2039; and about 16 years), disagree on whether the land is leased First Nations land, and one says "cash purchase only". Get the head-lease summary and park rules before removing subjects; lenders, insurers and the next buyer will all care about the remaining term.
Its sub-area placement (West Chilliwack: Listings place it in either West Chilliwack or Sardis West Vedder, and disagree on its lease terms, so search both area names and check the lease itself.
On ALR parcels around the village, the A: On ALR land around the village, the Agricultural Land Commission allows one main house of 500 m² or less, a suite only inside it, and at most one additional home of 90 m² (parcels of 40 ha or less) or 186 m² (over 40 ha).
On MLS®: the containing board sub-area i: On MLS®, the complex is in Grandview, in South Surrey and White Rock.
Servicing position: the complex is compl: Servicing: the complex was finished in 2011, on an urban site in Grandview Heights, and homes there are resales.
Fee-simple lots — the default and only d: Fee-simple lots are the only kind of property sold on non-reserve land here: a fee-simple farm parcel has no strata, Form B or strata fees.
A principal residence with a suite withi: A main house with a suite inside it, or an additional small home, on a farm parcel under the ALR rules. That's a farm with the homes it's allowed, not a duplex or two halves that can be sold separately.
No — none in any form. No strata product: No, not of any kind. There are no strata homes on the island: what sells is freehold farm parcels (the Katzie reserve land isn't on the market), and homes on ALR land can't be stratified.
The Province, under the rural system — r: The Province, under the rural system: rural owners get their notice from the Surveyor of Taxes and pay the Province, by July 2, with a 5% penalty on July 3 and another 5% on November 1. Metro Vancouver and school charges are on the same bill.
The one documented change at the sub-are: The one change at the area's edge is transit: Green Timbers Station on the Surrey Langley SkyTrain, expected to open in 2029. It's a station, not a development site or land for sale.
The board name and the City's map disagr: The real estate board's name and the City's map don't match. "Bear Creek Green Timbers" is only a board area name; the City treats the same area as parts of Whalley, Newton, Fleetwood and Guildford, and puts Bear Creek Park in Whalley, beside the Surrey Arts Centre. Searching City plans under the board's name finds nothing, so search by property on the City's COSMOS map.
The usual duplex form: The current frame: The usual duplex form: under Surrey's zoning bylaw and its small-scale housing rules (in force July 8, 2024), a lot can have up to 3 units if it's smaller than 280 m², 4 if it's larger, and up to 6 on eligible lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent bus stop. A duplex is the basic two-unit form, and it may be a semi-detached building, two strata halves (a two-lot strata plan) or two fee-simple halves on subdivided lots; check the title.
The City does not use the name as a comm: The City doesn't use the name: it lists seven communities (City Centre, Cloverdale, Fleetwood, Guildford, Newton, South Surrey and Whalley) and puts Bear Creek Park in Whalley. So this real estate board area covers parts of what the City calls Whalley, Newton, Fleetwood and Guildford.
The stock is detached-led: established h: Most homes are detached: established houses on larger, treed lots around the two parks, with a group of condos on 81A Avenue and townhouse complexes toward the Fleetwood and Guildford edges.
The forest is called British Columbia's: The forest is called British Columbia's "Birthplace of Reforestation": the land was completely logged by 1929, then replanted and run as a forestry school and nursery before becoming a park in 1974. A glacial erratic, a boulder left behind by glacial ice, sits on its northwestern trails.
What creek or park diligence applies to: What should I check for a lot near a creek or Bear Creek Park?
Neither is duplex stock. Read the addres: Neither is a duplex. Go by the address and the MLS® property type, not just the name.
Schools confirmed by address in and arou: Schools in and around this area include Bear Creek Elementary (13780 80 Avenue), Green Timbers Elementary (8824 144 Street), Frank Hurt Secondary (13940 77 Avenue) and Enver Creek Secondary (14505 84 Avenue), all in the Surrey School District (SD36). Catchments go by address, so check the exact address with the district's School Locator.
An Apartment/Condo building by Dawson +: A condo building by Dawson + Sawyer, south of Bear Creek Park: listings show condos built in 2020, with a clubhouse and bike room, and a building directory describes a wood-frame development with pets allowed. The directory's "251 Unit Development" figure is for the whole development, not this building alone.
The rest of the named attached stock ver: The other attached homes here are townhouses.
Bear Creek Park sits in the City's Whall: The City puts Bear Creek Park in Whalley (with the Surrey Arts Centre nearby), and Green Timbers Urban Forest is in the north-centre. City documents are under those names, so a search for "Bear Creek Green Timbers" alone misses them.
The townhouse stock is materially older: The townhouses are much older than the condos. Carlingwood was built around 2000, two decades before the Kings Landing apartment buildings, so depreciation report and building envelope questions matter far more there than in the 2020 and 2021 buildings.
Year conflict stated: listings checked r: Listings give both 1994 and 1995 for units at this address, so the year depends on the unit.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates:: Where the townhouses are: in three pockets. They're on 81A Avenue and 136A Street south of Bear Creek Park (the Kings Landing townhomes), on 84 Avenue facing Bear Creek Park (the townhouses at Trails), and at 151 Street on the Fleetwood edge (Carlingwood).
One real estate board area with a double name. The City doesn't use the name: it puts Bear Creek Park in Whalley and treats Green Timbers as the urban forest in the north-centre. So City documents for this area are under Whalley, Newton, Fleetwood and Guildford, not the board's name.
Surrey–Langley SkyTrain, as it touches t: Surrey–Langley SkyTrain near this area: Green Timbers Station (140 Street and Fraser Highway, beside Green Timbers Urban Forest and the Jim Pattison Outpatient Care and Surgery Centre, near the RCMP's BC headquarters) and 152 Street Station (152 Street and Fraser Highway) are on the south edge. The line is under construction and expected to open in late 2029 (July 2026 status report; as of November 3, 2026).
The City places both parks in Whalley an: The City puts both parks in Whalley and City Centre; the park names are older than the real estate board's name for the area around them.
A glacial erratic, a large rock carried: A glacial erratic, a large rock left behind by glacial ice, sits on the trails in the northwestern part of Green Timbers park.
The legal frame the City itself uses is: The property is the lot at 15988 32 Avenue, under Comprehensive Development By-law No. 16608, with Development Permit No. 7907-0105-00 allowing the townhouse project.
The planned stock change is written into: Change is written into the City Centre Plan: the July 11, 2022 land use changes for Bolivar Heights allow a range from single-family homes and multiplexes to townhouses and low-rise apartments, plus a new mixed-use village with shops and services.
Part of the existing detached stock is a: Some of the detached homes are in a protected pocket: the Bolivar Park neighbourhood and Extension Area was downzoned at residents' request (adopted April 18, 2016) to limit house size and height, one of five such areas in Surrey.
The recreation stock shapes the lots aro: Bolivar Park has several baseball fields, a field house, a playground and a two-acre fenced off-leash dog area east of the main parking lot.
Inside the Bolivar Park enclave, the 201: Inside the Bolivar Park pocket, the 2016 downzoning still limits rebuilds: the zones created by the residents' petitions generally cap the size and height of houses, and Bolivar Park's was adopted on April 18, 2016.
City Centre Plan update — Bolivar Height: City Centre Plan update, Bolivar Heights district: the update is under way, with a mixed-use neighbourhood centre and more parks and amenities planned for Bolivar Heights, and Council endorsed an Entertainment District and updated plan maps in October 2025 (as of November 3, 2026).
The existing attached stock is small, bu: There are few condos or townhomes here now, but the plan allows many more: on July 11, 2022, Council approved City Centre Plan changes adding townhouses, low-rise apartments and multiplexes to a district that was single-family houses.
The residential stock is an older lowlan: Bridgeview is an older lowland neighbourhood beside industrial land, not a planned new subdivision. The City says it's zoned mainly for residential and industrial uses, with a mix of light industrial, commercial and residential zones.
Bridgeview Park at 12560 115 Avenue carr: Bridgeview Park, 12560 115 Avenue, has a playground, water park, picnic shelters, two softball diamonds, a multi-use field, and tennis, pickleball and basketball courts.
It has no plan of its own. A buyer's lot: It has no plan of its own. A lot here can fall under either of two plans, so check which one covers the address.
Heavy trucks on soft local roads are a d: Heavy trucks on soft local roads are a real issue: the City's 2025 truck-park report describes trucks damaging ditches and roads and shaking nearby homes on 124 Street.
Why is there so little condo or townhome: Why are there so few condos and townhomes to choose from here?
Detached houses here are the older, smal: Detached houses here are the older homes on smaller lots typical of north Surrey, not a new subdivision. Lots in the nearby South Westminster Heights infill area, beside Bridgeview, range from 700 square metres to 4.12 acres across about 182 properties, which shows how mixed the old lots are. Check each Bridgeview lot on the City's COSMOS map; don't assume a standard size.
Yes, on some streets it is documented, n: Yes, on some streets, and it's on record. A 2025 City planning report for 124 Street in Bridgeview describes truck drivers ticketed for driving through the residential neighbourhood, heavy loads damaging ditches and roads built on soft ground, and neighbours' concerns about vibration.
Cedar Hills stock is detached houses on: Cedar Hills is detached houses on standard urban lots that are being split into smaller ones: a February 24, 2025 planning report for 12248 97 Avenue (a 0.2-hectare site) proposed rezoning from Urban Residential (R3) to Small Lot Residential (R4), with lot widths reduced from 12 metres to 11.76 metres, to create four small lots with side-by-side garages and access from a future 96A Avenue.
The house stock is an established north-: The houses are established north Surrey detached homes around a long-standing elementary school, not a named new subdivision.
Apartment/Condo, freehold strata, wood f: Freehold strata condos, wood frame, built in phases: listings show the 6420 and 6440 buildings as built in 2010 and the Esplanade building in 2015. A building directory describes a 274-unit development at the 6440 address, with a clubhouse of about 15,000 sq ft with an indoor 60-foot pool, hot tub, steam room and sauna, fitness facilities and a guest suite.
Listings classify 18755 68 Avenue as Apa: Listings show 18755 68 Avenue as condos and 18777 68A Avenue as townhouses. A project source describes two four-level wood-frame buildings built in 2008, with 57 suites in the condo buildings and 104 homes in the whole complex, including the townhouses.
Clayton is a Surrey board sub-area in th: Clayton is a real estate board area in Cloverdale. The City of Surrey plans the same area as Clayton Heights, a plan area of about 809 hectares (2,000 acres) running north from Fraser Highway, with the Agricultural Land Reserve to the north and west and the Township of Langley on the east.
The apartment-condo stock clusters along: The condos are mostly along 68 Avenue, 194 Street and 195A Street in the older East Clayton core; the newest building, Harlo, is in East Clayton near 65B Avenue and 195A Street.
The Form B Information Certificate is th: The Form B is the key document for any Clayton strata: the strata must provide it within 7 days of a request, for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. It has the real numbers: strata fees, the contingency reserve balance, the parking and storage that come with the unit, and the bylaws that apply to it.
Age bylaws: the only age-restriction byl: Age bylaws: the only age bylaw a BC strata can enforce is 55+, with exemptions added on May 1, 2023 (including for caregivers and spouses or partners).
ALR edge: Clayton's north and west edges: ALR edge: Clayton's north and west edges meet the Agricultural Land Reserve. On ALR land, the main house can be up to 500 m², with one additional home of 90 m² (lots of 40 ha or less) or 186 m² (over 40 ha). That matters for acreage buyers on the edge, not for strata homes.
Presales: REDMA gives a 7-day rescission: Presales: BC's presale rules give you 7 days to cancel and require deposits to be held in trust. They apply to contracts at Steelix on 188th and to any unit bought from the developer at Harlo.
The area has three names for the same ar: The area has three names, depending on who's using them: Clayton (the real estate board), Clayton Heights (the City's plan name) and East, West and North Clayton (the neighbourhood plans). Search all of them, or you'll miss some listings.
Clayton is a board sub-area of the Frase: On MLS®, Clayton is one of three areas in Cloverdale (Clayton, Cloverdale and Serpentine). It's a neighbourhood in the City of Surrey's Cloverdale community, one of the City's seven communities.
ALR edge: Clayton Heights runs to the AL: ALR edge: Clayton Heights runs up to the ALR in the north and west. On ALR land, the Agricultural Land Commission allows one main house up to 500 m² plus at most one additional home of 90 m² (parcels of 40 ha or less) or 186 m² (over 40 ha), and homes on ALR land can't be stratified.
\"Clayton\" has three names for the same: Clayton has three names: Clayton (the real estate board), Clayton Heights (the City's planning name) and East, West and North Clayton (the neighbourhood plans). Search all of them, or you'll miss listings and City documents.
Clayton was the Cloverdale community's f: Clayton had the fastest sales in Cloverdale in September 2026: 29% of detached homes for sale sold, and 21% of condos and townhomes, ahead of the Cloverdale area itself (13% and 17%). Medians are published only for Cloverdale as a whole.
Planning frame: the Clayton General Land: Plans: the Clayton General Land Use Plan (approved January 25, 1999) set up the neighbourhood plans; East Clayton's was endorsed in 2003 and West Clayton's final plan was approved in July 2015, planned for over 12,000 residents with a mixed-use centre at 184 Street and Fraser Highway. The City says those plan designations have been replaced by the Surrey 2050 Official Community Plan update, so check a lot's current designation instead of relying on the older plan.
Confirm the current OCP designation, not: Check the current Official Community Plan designation, not the older neighbourhood plan, and check whether a lot is in a Transit-Oriented Area around the future 184 Street or 190 Street stations, which allows more density.
The City describes Cloverdale's borders: The City describes Cloverdale as bordered by 160 Street on the west and 48 Avenue on the south, with Langley to the east. The acreages are in the southern and western lowlands, not in Clayton's subdivisions.
Where the 55+ stock actually sits: both: Where the 55+ homes are: both complexes you can buy in are in the town centre and east side, not in Clayton: Carriage House at 17695 58 Avenue in downtown Cloverdale, and The Estates at Manor Ridge at 6140 192 Street. The seniors rental residence, Bethshan Gardens, is at 17528 59 Avenue, a block from Carriage House.
ALR edge: Cloverdale includes ALR farm p: ALR edge: Cloverdale includes ALR farmland on its lowland side. On ALR land, the Agricultural Land Commission allows one main house up to 500 m² plus at most one additional home of 90 m² (parcels of 40 ha or less) or 186 m² (over 40 ha).
An apartment-condo complex in Clayton: c: A condo complex in Clayton: listings show freehold strata condos built in 2010, around a 15,000 sq ft clubhouse with an indoor 60-foot pool, hot tub, steam room, sauna, fitness centre and guest suite. A building directory lists a 274-unit wood-frame development; that's the total for the whole complex. A current listing says pets are allowed.
Clayton was the community's fastest shel: Clayton had the fastest sales in Cloverdale in September 2026: 29% of detached homes for sale sold, and 21% of condos and townhomes, ahead of the Cloverdale area itself (13% and 17%). So a Clayton condo and a town-centre condo were in different markets. Medians are published only for Cloverdale as a whole.
Clayton moved faster than the rest of Cl: Clayton sold faster than the rest of Cloverdale in September 2026, and Serpentine had no residential listings or sales at all.
No counted complex is published as age-r: None of the complexes here is described as age restricted, but check the registered bylaws on the Form B before assuming either way.
The Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) edge: The Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) runs along the community's lowland side. On ALR land, the Agricultural Land Commission allows one main house of up to 500 square metres plus at most one additional home.
Cloverdale Town Centre is the historic h: Cloverdale Town Centre is the historic heart of Surrey, at Highway 10 and Highway 15 (Pacific Highway), and the City is updating its town centre plan, which covers the condos in the town centre.
Compass at 18755 68 Avenue in Clayton is: Compass at 18755 68 Avenue in Clayton is the condo part of a complex that shares the name: two four-storey wood-frame buildings from 2008. The Compass homes at 18777 68A Avenue are townhouses.
The diligence document for every buildin: For every building on this page, read the Form B: it shows the unit's strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget and latest depreciation report.
Highway 10 and Highway 15 (Pacific Highw: Highway 10 and Highway 15 (Pacific Highway) cross at the town centre, and Highway 15 runs south to the Pacific border crossing, so both condo areas are easy to drive from.
No. SnapStats splits Cloverdale only as: No. The market report covers Cloverdale only as detached homes and as condos and townhomes combined, with medians for the whole community. The combined median in September 2026 was $740,000 ($503 per sq ft, 96% of list price, 32 days on the market).
Suites / coach houses: Surrey's urban ru: Suites and coach houses: in urban Surrey, each single-family, semi-detached or duplex home can have one secondary suite, up to 40% of the home's living area, never inside a coach house or garden suite and never a separate strata lot. Coach houses and garden suites can be 35 to 75 m² (up to 120 m² on some lots that are under their maximum floor area), with one extra parking space. On ALR land, the stricter ALR rule above applies (a suite only inside the main house). Surrey's small-scale housing rules (3, 4 or up to 6 units, depending on the lot; July 8, 2024) are for urban lots and don't allow extra homes on ALR farmland.
On Serpentine lowland ground those are p: On the Serpentine lowlands, check those with the City and on title for each property, and budget for the checks.
Detached houses are an explicit plan cat: Detached houses are a planned part of the area. The Cloverdale Town Centre Plan includes Detached Residential and Semi-detached Residential along with townhouses and low-rises, with the detached homes in the residential areas on either side of the historic core.
Heritage houses are part of the stock, n: Some houses here are heritage buildings: Surrey's Heritage Register for Cloverdale lists the 1881 Town Hall at 17635 60 Avenue and the 1912 Municipal Hall at 17671 56 Avenue under heritage designation bylaws, and the Clova Theatre at 5732 176 Street and Cloverdale United Church at 17575 58A Avenue under heritage revitalization agreements. Check any house on the City's Heritage Register before assuming it can be altered or demolished.
The ALR edge is the southern due-diligen: Check the ALR on the south side: the plan area runs south to the Agricultural Land Reserve, so for a house lot near that edge, check the Agricultural Land Commission's map; farm-use and subdivision rules change at the boundary.
The stock splits by pocket, which is why: The homes differ from pocket to pocket, so each has its own guide.
The local pocket name inside East Newton: The local name for part of East Newton is Chimney Hill, as in Chimney Hill Elementary and Chimney Heights Park.
Fee-simple is the default and only lot f: Fee simple is the norm: where there's a two-unit building, it can be one fee-simple property or a two-lot strata, so check each property's title.
The East Newton Business Park plan area: The East Newton Business Park plan area (128 Street to 144 Street, from 80 Avenue to the south side of 88 Avenue) is at the north end. It's industrial and business park land, not residential, so if you're buying at the north edge, check what's allowed next door.
No in-area ALR or floodplain designation: I don't know of any ALR or floodplain designation in the area; the uplands are east of the Serpentine lowlands. Check the property on the Agricultural Land Commission's maps and the City's flood mapping before removing subjects.
The area's newest and largest condo comm: The area's newest and largest condo community: three 4-storey wood-frame buildings with 261 condos, by Wanson Group, at 75A Avenue and 138 Street, opposite Frank Hurt Secondary.
A low-rise condo building by Wanson Grou: A low-rise condo building by Wanson Group, built in 2011, wood frame, steps from Newton Exchange; listings describe a central courtyard and underground parking.
Where the condo stock actually concentra: Where the condos are: there are no towers in East Newton. The condos are low-rise, in two pockets: on 70 Avenue west of 140 Street (Chelsea Gardens), and on 75A and 76 Avenues just east of King George Boulevard around 137 and 138 Streets (Silva, Mirra and Earl's Court), a walk from Newton Exchange.
The rest of East Newton is single-family: The rest of East Newton is single-family subdivision streets built under the East Newton neighbourhood plans, plus the Chimney Hill pocket around Chimney Hill Elementary and Chimney Heights Park.
Age bylaws: 55+ is the only legal form:: Age bylaws: 55+ is the only legal kind. A strata can limit residents to 55 or older, and any bylaw set below 55 has been invalid since November 24, 2022. The bylaw covers who can live in the unit, not who can own it, with exemptions for existing residents, live-in caregivers, a younger spouse or partner, and some children.
A very large King George corridor projec: A very large project is proposed on King George Boulevard, just north of the area. The 55+ stock here is a full community,: The 55+ homes here are a whole community, not one building. Chelsea Gardens covers four addresses (13860–13888 70 Avenue) on 23 acres, with its own clubhouse, guest suites and RV parking, so its fees, amenities and social life don't compare directly with an ordinary low-rise like Earl's Court a few blocks away.
72 carriage-style townhouses, built 1984: 72 carriage-style townhouses built in 1984, the area's oldest.
Where the townhouse stock actually conce: Where the townhouses are: in the Chimney Hill pocket in the southeast (Chimney Ridge and The Summit), on 72 Avenue in the middle of the area (Newton Park I), on 138 Street south of 66 Avenue (Charleston Green), and in the Chelsea Gardens community on 70 Avenue (its townhouses are at 13888). The rest of East Newton is single-family subdivision streets built under the East Newton neighbourhood plans.
No. Every known apartment-condo building: No. Every condo building I know of in the area is low-rise: Silva is three 4-storey wood-frame buildings, and Chelsea Gardens, Mirra and Earl's Court are low-rise too.
Two creeks frame the area — Bear Creek t: Two creeks mark the area's edges, Bear Creek to the north and Hyland Creek to the south.
The Surrey Langley SkyTrain extension ru: The Surrey Langley SkyTrain extension runs along Fraser Highway, north and east of East Newton, with no station in this area.
Fleetwood Tynehead is a single board sub: Fleetwood Tynehead is one real estate board area in Surrey's Fleetwood community, not two separate neighbourhoods, and one of 15 board areas in Surrey.
The City's frame for the same area is th: The City plans the same area through the Fleetwood Plan, which guides growth over the next 30-plus years as SkyTrain extends along Fraser Highway. The plan area runs from Green Timbers Urban Forest in the west toward the Agricultural Land Reserve in the east; Anniedale-Tynehead, at the east end, has its own City plan.
ALR edge: the Fleetwood plan area runs t: ALR edge: the Fleetwood plan area runs toward the Agricultural Land Reserve in the east. On ALR land, the Agricultural Land Commission allows one main house up to 500 m² plus at most one additional home of 90 m² (parcels of 40 ha or less) or 186 m² (over 40 ha).
Fleetwood's care campus is bigger than i: Fleetwood has far more care housing than 55+ homes to buy. Elim Village alone reports over 500 units and over 600 residents in independent living, assisted living and full care on one Fleetwood site, compared with 46 strata homes at Fleetwood Gardens plus the pads at Westwood Court. Seniors move to Fleetwood for the range of care; the 55+ homes you can buy are a small part of it.
The Fleetwood Plan itself (Stage 1 endor: The Fleetwood Plan (Stage 1 endorsed March 7, 2022 and updated October 16, 2023, with further changes for Transit Oriented Areas since, and Council to consider the updated plan in 2026) is a planning process, not a development site or land for sale. Until the updated plan is considered, a lot's future designation near the town centre and stations isn't final.
That count is a snapshot, not a market s: That number is a snapshot from September 2026, not a market statistic.
Small plan wording, real consequence: th: A small point that matters: the Fleetwood Plan area "stretches towards" the ALR. That doesn't make a Fleetwood lot ALR land, and it doesn't exempt a lot on the ALR edge from ALR rules. Check each property's status.
Planning frame: the Fleetwood Plan will: Plans: the Fleetwood Plan will guide growth over the next 30-plus years as SkyTrain extends along Fraser Highway. The Stage 1 Plan was endorsed on March 7, 2022 and updated on October 16, 2023, with further changes for Transit Oriented Areas since, and Council is to consider the updated plan in 2026. Until then, a lot's future designation could still change.

One board sub-area; the City plans the g: It's one real estate board area. The City plans it under the Fleetwood Plan (from Green Timbers in the west toward the ALR in the east), with Tynehead, or Anniedale-Tynehead, at the east end under its own plan.

The building record's bylaw summary says: The building's bylaw summary says "Age restrictions" without giving an age, and since November 24, 2022 only a 55+ bylaw can be enforced. Fleetwood's detached stock is mostly sin: Fleetwood's detached homes are mostly single-family houses, in a neighbourhood the City describes as home to many families, with a growing number of businesses. Family houses define the area, unlike the towers of central Whalley.
Its east end has a precise official fram: Its east end is well defined: Abbey Ridge, the neighbourhood in East Fraser Heights, is about 175 hectares (430 acres) north of Highway 1, between 172 Street in the west and the Port Kells Industrial Area and the Golden Ears Connector in the east.
The east end's stock story is acreage lo: At the east end, acreage lots are being converted to urban housing: the City says Abbey Ridge was originally suburban acreage lots and is now designated for urban development, mostly residential, with industrial land along the Golden Ears Connector and a small neighbourhood commercial area on Barnston Drive.
TransLink's own South of Fraser engageme: In TransLink's South of Fraser engagement, riders asked for more frequent peak service on the 337 and 338 and for the 337 to be extended to Pacific Academy, Fraser Heights Secondary and the Fraser Heights Recreation Centre at 10588 160 Street, so crowding at school times is a known issue.
Mostly townhomes and detached houses — n: Mostly townhomes and detached houses; I don't know of any condo building here. Fraser Heights is planned as a low-density area of Guildford, and the one pocket planned for more density is Abbey Ridge in the east, under its 2017 Local Area Plan. If you want an apartment, compare Guildford Town Centre instead of waiting for a Fraser Heights tower.
Development in Guildford has predominant: Development in Guildford has centred on 152 Street and 104 Avenue around Guildford Town Centre mall, so the condos and townhomes are at the town centre and the detached subdivisions are on the blocks behind it.
Fraser Heights, in the community's north: Fraser Heights, in the north of the community, has the newer subdivisions, on streets sloping toward the Fraser River, with views of the Port Mann Bridge along the northern edge.
Guildford's detached stock is mostly mat: Guildford's detached homes are mostly in mature neighbourhoods that grew up around Guildford Town Centre mall, plus the newer Fraser Heights subdivision: two visibly different kinds of houses in one community.
The Guildford Plan is a complete land-us: The Guildford Plan, a land-use plan for parts of North Surrey including Guildford, was approved by Council on October 30, 2023, so the mature neighbourhoods around the town centre are now in a plan that allows more density along 104 Avenue.
Fraser Heights is a subdivision inside G: Fraser Heights is a subdivision in Guildford, not a separate community. The City describes Guildford as mature urban neighbourhoods around the town centre mall plus the newer Fraser Heights subdivision, which slopes down toward the Fraser River. Listings may show Fraser Heights as its own area, so search both "Guildford" and "Fraser Heights" to see all the houses.
By area, new detached listings met the s: By area, new detached listings sold fastest in Cedar Hills (27%), Sullivan Station (20%) and East Newton (15%). The areas with the most homes for sale compared with sales were Queen Mary Park (3%), Bolivar Heights (4%) and Whalley (5%), so a new listing there is likely to have competition.
The detached stock changes character acr: Detached homes differ across the three communities: Fleetwood is mostly single-family houses, Guildford is mature urban neighbourhoods plus the newer Fraser Heights subdivision, and Whalley's houses surround a high-rise core.
Fraser Heights, inside Guildford, is the: Fraser Heights, in Guildford, has North Surrey's newer subdivisions, sloping down toward the Fraser River, while the neighbourhoods around Guildford Town Centre mall are older.
It covers the Whalley, Guildford and Fle: It covers the Whalley, Guildford and Fleetwood communities in the northern half of the city, not one real estate board area. Fleetwood is in the middle, with Whalley to the west and Guildford to the east and north, and each has its own land-use plan and its own kinds of houses. When comparing two "North Surrey" houses, first work out which community each is in, because transit, plans and flood checks all differ.
The 55+ stock is not spread across the r: The 55+ homes aren't spread across the ridge: they're on West Boundary Drive at Boundary Park, at the area's west edge, in the Lakewood Place and Lakewood Heights townhouse complexes.
All of Panorama Ridge's known 55+ owners: All of Panorama Ridge's 55+ homes to buy are on one short street: Lakewood Place (6061) and Lakewood Heights (6211) on West Boundary Drive. There's no 55+ condo tower, rental building or care residence in the area if neither complex has a home for sale.
The same drive is split between two MLS: The same street is split between two MLS® areas. Lakeview Estates, at 6090 West Boundary Drive, is listed in West Newton, while its two neighbours are listed in Panorama Ridge, so search both or you'll miss a third of the Boundary Park 55+ complexes.
The newest townhouse stock here is famil: The newest townhouses here are family homes, not seniors' homes.
Riparian / creek diligence (the Panorama: Creeks: the headwaters of Archibald Creek, Sullivan Heights Creek and tributaries of Hyland Creek run through the plan area. Setbacks from creeks and any development permit areas can limit where you can build on creek-side lots, so check the City's mapping and the lot's permit areas before valuing an addition, rebuild or subdivision.
Slope / south-edge diligence: the area i: Slope and the south edge: the area is a ridge, with Highway 10 along the south edge and lowlands beyond it. Check for highway noise, and confirm the lot is on the upland side of the floodplain, before removing subjects.
Where the condo stock actually concentra: Where the condos are: there's just one project, Amson Bloc, at 5937 144 Street near 60 Avenue, on the Sullivan Heights side of the ridge. The townhouse complexes are on 62 Avenue (Nora at 12830 62 Avenue on the Colebrook, or west, side, and The Uplands at 15152 62A Avenue by 152 Street) and at Highway 10 and 132 Street (Steller Panorama).
42 townhouses, built 2022, by Valour Dev: 42 townhouses built in 2022 by Valour Development and JB Group, on the Colebrook side of the area; a listing describes a 42-unit wood-frame townhouse development with pets allowed. Long-term rentals can't be banned in any case.
Where the townhouse stock actually conce: Where the townhouses are: on 62 Avenue at both ends of the ridge (Nora at 12830 62 Avenue on the Colebrook, or west, side, and The Uplands at 15152 62A Avenue by 152 Street); at Highway 10 and 132 Street (Steller Panorama); on 129 Street south of 60 Avenue (Panorama Mews); and on West Boundary Drive at Boundary Park, at the west edge (the two 55+ Lakewood complexes).
Where a presale does apply, the develope: For a presale, the developer must give you a disclosure statement, you have 7 days from the later of signing or receiving it to cancel and get your deposit back, and deposits must be held in trust. Whether you can assign the contract depends on the contract.
All of the sub-area's 55+ townhouse stoc: All of the area's 55+ townhouses are on one short street, and that street is split between two MLS® areas. Lakewood Place (6061) and Lakewood Heights (6211) on West Boundary Drive are listed in Panorama Ridge, while Lakeview Estates, at 6090 on the same street, is listed in West Newton. Search both.
On the record, no. The only apartment-co: No, as far as I know. The only condo project in the area is Amson Bloc, a new presale at 5937 144 Street with 121 condos; the established attached homes are townhouses (Nora, Steller Panorama and The Uplands).
No library or recreation centre inside t: There's no library or recreation centre in the area; Newton Athletic Park, 7395 128 Street, to the west, is the main sports park nearby.
Catchments are address-based in SD36. Th: Catchments go by address in the Surrey School District (SD36). For example, 13220 64 Avenue is in the North Ridge Elementary and École Panorama Ridge Secondary catchments. Check any other address with the district's School Locator.
Surrey Zoning By-law No. 12000 zone name: Zoning for these homes includes One-Acre Residential (RA), Half-Acre Residential (RH) and General Agriculture (A-1).
North of Highway 1 the stock changes com: North of Highway 1 it's completely different: the Port Kells industrial area covers 781 acres, zoned mainly for light industry.
No, only detached houses are counted her: No, this page covers detached houses only; condos and townhomes have their own page.
The residential stock is single-detached: The homes are detached houses on suburban and larger rural lots, plus the cluster housing shown in the South Port Kells Land Use Plan, mostly freehold. North of Highway 1, the land is industrial, not housing.
Tenure: The old village core around Port: The old village core around Port Kells Elementary (the school dates from 1907) has a mix of older homes, with newer suburban houses at the edges.
Anniedale-Tynehead, immediately south: a: Anniedale-Tynehead, just to the south: a neighbourhood plan is being prepared for a mix of industrial, commercial and residential growth, which the City expects will open up more land next to Port Kells. None that I know of. A buyer set on stra: None that I know of. If you want a strata home, look in Guildford, Fleetwood or Walnut Grove, not Port Kells.

No. Barnston Island is Metro Vancouver E: No. Barnston Island is in Metro Vancouver Electoral Area A, along with Katzie reserve land. It's grouped with Port Kells on MLS® only because the free ferry to it leaves from the foot of 104 Avenue in Port Kells. An island property isn't in Surrey.

Where stock is building up faster than i: Where homes are piling up faster than they sell, sellers tend to cut prices first. Queen Mary Park Surrey is a board sub-ar: Queen Mary Park is a real estate board area in central Surrey, west of King George Boulevard and south of 96 Avenue, named after the City park. The City of Surrey doesn't plan it as a named neighbourhood, so it has no City boundary.
In the 1990s southern cluster this repor: For the 1990s buildings in the south, this report is the key document: it's where a claim like Sterling Court's "completely rainscreened, new building envelope" is either backed up or not.
Presales and new completions: REDMA give: Presales and newly finished buildings: BC's presale rules give you 7 days to cancel and require deposits to be held in trust. They apply to developer contracts at Gabriel and to any units still sold by the developer at Galilea and Quinn.
Quinn's own directory presence contains: Be careful with one figure for Quinn: a building directory shows a "22-unit development" at its 9456 134 Street address, but the project has 174 units.

Where the townhouse stock concentrates:: Where the townhouses are: in two pockets. No City plan area stands behind the name: There's no City plan area by this name. "Queen Mary Park" is a real estate board area and a park, not a City planning district; City documents for this area are under Whalley / City Centre and Newton, so search those names too.
Detached barely moved here in September: Few detached homes sold here in September 2026; most sales were condos and townhomes.
\"Queen Mary Park\" is a Fraser Valley b: "Queen Mary Park" is a Fraser Valley Real Estate Board area in central Surrey, west of King George Boulevard and south of 96 Avenue, named after Queen Mary Park, the City park at 8972 Queen Mary Boulevard.
Where the mobile-home stock sits: the on: Where the mobile homes are: the one park, Westwood Estates, is on 134 Street at the area's southeast edge, just south of 88 Avenue and, according to its listings, a short walk from Bear Creek Park.
Queen Mary Park is a Fraser Valley board: Queen Mary Park is a Fraser Valley Real Estate Board area in central Surrey, west of King George Boulevard and south of 96 Avenue, named after the City park at its centre. It's a board and local name, not a City of Surrey plan area.
The stock is detached houses — older bas: The homes are detached houses (older basement-entry homes, half duplexes and newer custom builds), with low-rise condos and townhomes at the edges and at least one manufactured home park, on 134 Street.
Suite use is a defining feature of the d: Suites are a big part of the detached homes here: houses are often described with basement suites, side suites and multi-suite half duplexes, used for extended family and rental income. That's why whether a suite is legal matters more here than in most of Surrey.
Suite legality is the financial due-dili: Whether a suite is legal is the key financial check here: an unauthorized suite can cause problems with financing and insurance. Test the property against the City's rules: one suite per home, up to 40% of its size.
No boundary was confirmed: the name is a: There's no official boundary: the name belongs to a City park and a Fraser Valley Real Estate Board area, and there's no City plan area by this name.
Two RapidBus corridors frame the sub-are: Two RapidBus routes run along the area's edges: the R1 on King George Boulevard on the east side and the R6 on Scott Road (120 Street) on the west side, both connecting to Expo Line stations. The area's detached stock sits between t: The area's detached homes sit between two RapidBus routes, King George Boulevard to the east and Scott Road to the west; there's no single village centre.
Outside the enclave the guide area is st: Outside the downzoned pocket, the area is typical northwest Surrey detached housing, designated Urban in the Official Community Plan, with the park at its centre: over 2.2 hectares, forest on the west and an open field on the east, with the streets curving around it.
The 2025 owner survey is a due-diligence: The 2025 owner survey is worth reading: 93 percent of properties in the downzoned pocket responded, 86 percent knew the area had been downzoned, and support for larger houses was highest among owners who bought after the 2008 downzoning. Royal Heights has no City boundary for t: The City has no boundary for Royal Heights as the real estate board uses the name, but a City report describes a Royal Heights pocket of 127 lots, bounded by Royal Heights Park to the north, 116 Street to the east, properties on 96A Avenue to the south and Princess Drive to the west.
Small and defined at its core. A City co: Small and well defined at its core. Parcel by parcel: if the parcel is in th: It depends on the parcel. King George Corridor's 10 known condos a: The King George Corridor's 10 condo buildings are low-rise apartments in South Surrey, not townhouses and not in Serpentine.

Not while the parcel is in the ALR — ALR: Not while the land is in the ALR: homes on ALR land can't be stratified, and subdividing needs the Agricultural Land Commission's permission.
It is a board sub-area name only — not a: It's only a real estate board area name. It isn't a City of Surrey planning name, and the City has no boundary for it.
The stock here is acreage-led, not strat: Homes here are mostly acreages, not stratas: estate houses on multi-acre properties, working blueberry farms and vacant land, not condo or townhome complexes.
No, not in city planning terms. Serpenti: No, not in city planning terms. Serpentine is a Fraser Valley Real Estate Board area name within Cloverdale, alongside Clayton and Cloverdale. Only within the ALC frame if the parcel: Only within the ALR's limits, if the property is in the Agricultural Land Reserve: one main house up to 500 square metres with any suite inside it, plus at most one additional home of 90 square metres, or 186 square metres on parcels over 40 hectares.
The oldest part of the stock is the 1950: The oldest homes are in the 1950s subdivision east of Stoney Creek Park; the condos and townhomes are mainly in the multi-family buildings west of the park, built after 1974.
The house stock is a 1950s single-family: The houses are in a 1950s single-family subdivision. Heritage Burnaby dates the Sullivan Heights subdivision east of Stoney Creek Park to the 1950s, separate from the multi-family buildings west of the park, built after 1974.
West of Stoney Creek Park the stock chan: West of Stoney Creek Park it's different: Heritage Burnaby describes a higher-density residential area of multi-family buildings built after 1974.
The newest stock is The City of Lougheed: The newest homes are at The City of Lougheed: the developer, SHAPE, says Neighbourhood One is finished, with 1,500 homes, an amenity facility of over 22,000 square feet and shops anchored by PriceSmart Foods, on the 37-acre site at 9855 Austin Avenue.
Municipality and community: City of Surr: City of Surrey, in the Newton community. \"Sullivan Station\" is the SnapStats /: "Sullivan Station" is the real estate board's name for the area; the City doesn't publish a separate Sullivan Station plan boundary.
Sullivan Station is ringed by 55+ stock: Sullivan Station is surrounded by 55+ homes but has none of its own. Chelsea Gardens and Charleston Green in East Newton, to the northwest, and the two Lakewood complexes in Panorama Ridge, to the south, are the nearest. A "Sullivan Station 55+" search on a listing site will show all of them, under three different area names.
Sullivan Station is a board sub-area nam: Sullivan Station is a real estate board area name in South Newton, in the Newton community of Surrey. The City doesn't publish a separate Sullivan Station boundary; its own names for the area are Sullivan, Sullivan Heights and South Newton.
The nearest known 55+ ownership stock is: The nearest 55+ homes to buy are north, in East Newton: Chelsea Gardens at 13870 and 13888 70 Avenue, a gated freehold strata (plan LMS1416) built in 1995–1996, with apartment-style condos at 13870 and ground-level townhouse-style homes at 13888; and Charleston Green at 6537 138 Street, a gated 55+ townhouse complex built in 1988.
Highway 10 forms the south edge of the S: Highway 10 is the south edge of the South Newton plan area and 152 Street its east edge, with King George Boulevard to the west. There's no rapid transit station in the area.
The main due-diligence risk on this page: The main thing to watch here is labelling: a complex with "Sullivan" in its name, or one that shows up in a Sullivan Station search, may be in East Newton or Panorama Ridge, and may be a membership instead of a strata. Check the address, the area and the type of ownership separately.
An Apartment/Condo building in Sullivan: A condo building in Sullivan Station, built in 2013: listings show 4 storeys, wood frame with brick and fibre-cement siding, freehold strata, with a clubhouse, gym, guest suite and landscaped courtyard. One listing names Porte Communities as the builder.

Three bus routes frame the area, per Tra: Three bus routes serve the area (TransLink timetables from January 5, 2026): route 342 (Newton Exchange / Langley Centre) runs through it on Highway 10, 152 Street, 60 Avenue, 142 Street, 57 Avenue, 144 Street and 72 Avenue; route 345 runs along 152 Street on the east edge; and route 364 runs along 64 Avenue on the north edge.
Secondary suites (settled position): und: Secondary suites: under Surrey's zoning bylaw, each single-family, semi-detached or duplex home can have one secondary suite, a suite isn't allowed inside a coach house or garden suite, and a suite's living area can't be more than 40% of the main home's.
Most of Surrey's 55+ strata complexes we: Most of Surrey's 55+ strata complexes were built between 1986 and 2000. Fleetwood Gardens (2005) and The Greens at Douglas (2012–2013) are the newer exceptions, so if you only search the older South Surrey and Newton areas, you'll miss the city's newest 55+ homes.
Your search has to be filed under \"Whal: Search under "Whalley". On MLS®, downtown Surrey is listed as Whalley; a search for a "City Centre" area finds nothing, because the real estate board has no such area, even though the City officially calls the downtown "City Centre (Whalley)".

It depends on the unit, not the building: It depends on the unit, not the building. Plaza One, Plaza Two, The Grand on King George and Park George were all finished in 2025. Per exact address — the one documented r: It depends on the exact address. For example, 13367 97 Avenue is in the A.H.P. Matthew Elementary and Queen Elizabeth Secondary catchments; École Kwantlen Park Secondary is nearby but isn't that address's catchment school.
Towers cluster in Whalley at City Parkwa: The towers are in Whalley, at City Parkway, 104 Avenue and King George Boulevard; low-rise condos line King George Boulevard in South Surrey, and are also found in Guildford and Newton.
Towers stand in Whalley, around City Par: The towers are in Whalley, around City Parkway, 104 Avenue and Surrey Central Station, where the City describes new residential high-rises at a transit hub. Elsewhere, condos are low-rise and wood frame; King + Crescent in South Surrey, for example, is four six-storey buildings. The City divides Surrey into six communi: The City divides Surrey into six communities (Cloverdale, Fleetwood, Guildford, Newton, South Surrey and Whalley), and there are condos at this price in all six, with the towers mostly in Whalley / City Centre.
In this band the stock is strata apartme: At this price, you're buying a strata condo, not a detached house: you own a strata lot and share the common property through the strata corporation.

There are no condo towers in West Newton: There are no condo towers in West Newton; the condos are 1990s low-rises, and the Highway 99 part of the plan area is industrial, not housing.
The south end drops into floodplain coun: The south end drops toward the floodplain: the southern part of West Newton slopes down to the Serpentine and Nicomekl lowlands, the diked floodplain south of Newton. Where the townhouse stock actually conce: Where the townhouses are: in three pockets. There are no townhouse towers and no kno: I don't know of any fee-simple townhouse complex in West Newton; the townhouses are stratas built from 1986 to 2004, and the Highway 99 part of the plan area is industrial, not housing.

Creek corridor is not buildable lot area: You can't build on the creek corridor: Kanaka Creek Regional Park follows the creek through this part of Maple Ridge, with the Canyon Trail from the fish hatchery to Cliff Falls (1.2 km one way) and the Riverfront Trails (3 km one way) where the creek meets the Fraser River. Metro Vancouver warns of steep, slippery cliffs along the creek, especially at Cliff Falls, and the Bell-Irving Hatchery supports chum and coho salmon and cutthroat trout. Lots backing onto the creek have setbacks and slopes to check, so value the area you can build on, not the whole lot.
The creek through the subdivision is a s: The creek through the neighbourhood is a salmon stream with a hatchery: Kanaka Creek Regional Park protects the creek corridor, and the Bell-Irving Hatchery supports chum and coho salmon and cutthroat trout. The Canyon Trail runs 1.2 km one way from the hatchery to Cliff Falls, and the Riverfront Trails run 3 km one way where the creek meets the Fraser River. Lots beside the creek get the trails, along with setback and slope rules to check.

Fee-simple lots are the default form: si: Fee-simple lots are the norm: single detached houses are on fee-simple lots on the residential streets east and north of downtown, zoned RS-1, with a minimum lot of 668 m², 18 m wide and 27 m deep, and up to 40% lot coverage. Density policy is the land story here, n: Here the value in land comes from density policy, not vacant lots. Pricing a teardown as just a single house misses that direction, but pricing it as if rezoning were certain means paying for a designation, not an approval.
RS-1 house lots (residential streets eas: RS-1 house lots (the residential streets east and north of downtown): single detached houses on fee-simple lots, with a minimum lot of 668 m², 18 m wide and 27 m deep, and up to 40% lot coverage. A bare-land strata lot is strata tenure: A bare-land strata lot is strata ownership: you own a strata lot, pay strata fees, follow the strata bylaws and review the Form B, as with any strata. The difference is that the lot is bare land or a detached-house lot, not a unit in a shared building.
The RS-1 minimums are 668 m² in area, 18 m wide and 27 m deep, and both the original lot and any new lot must meet them.
You own a strata lot, pay strata fees, f: You own a strata lot, pay strata fees, follow the bylaws and review the Form B, but the lot is a detached-house lot, not a unit in a shared building.
Yes — flood construction level 6.7 m geo: Yes: a flood construction level of 6.7 m, no living space below it on affected lots, a covenant on title, and no suites on floodplain properties. Confirm the covenant and level on title before valuing any lower-level space.

In the Town Centre and along the Loughee: In the Town Centre and along Lougheed Highway, as planned. Southwest Maple Ridge is a board sub-are: Southwest Maple Ridge is only a real estate board area name; the City's name for this corner is Hammond, with Pitt Meadows and the Katzie First Nation to the west, the Fraser River to the south, and the Lougheed Highway and Dewdney Trunk Road commercial areas to the north.
All of the attached stock sits at the so: All the attached homes are on 248 Street at the area's southwest edge (The Terraces, Terraces II and Rydge); the rest of the area is freehold acreages.
The strata stock does not spread across: The strata homes aren't spread across the hill: they're all on 248 Street at the area's southwest edge, below the forested acreages that run east toward 264 Street.
Tenure frame, cross-referenced: fee-simp: Ownership: fee-simple lots are the norm, with rural minimum lot sizes of 2.0 ha (A-1), 4.0 ha (A-2), 8.0 ha (A-3), 0.4 ha (RS-2) and 0.8 or 2.0 ha (RS-3). ALR status depends on the parcel.
Thornhill's stock is mainly residential: Thornhill is mainly residential and rural: the City describes it as heavily forested and mainly residential, with farms and nurseries. It isn't a condo or townhome area.
One secondary suite per lot inside the b: One secondary suite per lot, inside the house, in zones including A-1, A-2 and A-3 (up to 40% of its floor area, and not in the floodplain). On ALR land, the ALR rules also apply, and a separate additional home is allowed only if their conditions are met.
One half of a two-unit building sold sep: One half of a two-unit building, sold on its own: either a strata lot in a two-lot strata plan (so you read the Form B) or a fee-simple lot created by subdividing. If a duplex was never stratified or subdivided, only the whole building can be sold.
The City publishes no street-by-street b: The City publishes no street-by-street boundary for Thornhill as an MLS® area; the City plan that applies is the Official Community Plan's Thornhill Urban Reserve, not a neighbourhood plan.
The existing stock is large rural-reside: The homes are on large rural lots, with farms and nurseries in a heavily forested setting, as the City describes it, not in built-out subdivisions.
Groundwater is a documented Thornhill is: Groundwater is a known issue in Thornhill: the Official Community Plan requires an aquifer groundwater management study before any urban development. So check the well and septic system lot by lot, and don't assume City services.
The stock is rural-residential: detached: The homes are rural: detached houses on large lots, farms and nurseries, not urban subdivisions.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates:: Where the townhouses are: there aren't any. I don't know of a townhouse complex or condo building anywhere in this area.
The name itself is spelled two ways, and: The name is spelled two ways. The City and the school district write "Webster's Corners", with an apostrophe; the real estate board writes "Websters Corners", without one. Search both spellings.
Identity: \"Websters Corners\" is both a: "Websters Corners" is both a City of Maple Ridge neighbourhood name and the real estate board's name for the area.
Aquifer No. 38 underlies the western sid: Aquifer No. 38 lies under the western side of that northern study area and is fed by the Alouette River, so groundwater is a feature of the wider Websters Corners and 256 Street area.
Groundwater and springs are a documented: Groundwater and springs are a known risk north of Websters Corners: where the ground drops sharply to the Alouette River floodplain, springs feeding small creeks are common, according to the same assessment.
Why is there no townhouse stock here at: Why are there no townhouses here at all?
The City spells the name Webster's Corne: The City spells the name Webster's Corners, with an apostrophe; the real estate board drops the apostrophe.
Built 2007, 58 units, by Falcon Homes (c: Built in 2007, 58 units, by Falcon Homes, according to listings: wood frame with glass, stone and vinyl siding, 9-foot ceilings, underground parking and a courtyard set back from Dewdney Trunk Road. A current listing says cats are OK.
The first phase of the Era master-planne: The first phase of the Era master-planned community, by Johnston Meier Insurance and SwissReal Developments, on Dewdney Trunk Road between Plaza and 224 Streets. Listings show units at 22265 Dewdney Trunk Road as built in 2022, with a fitness centre, rooftop deck and garden, party room and EV charging. Sources differ on size: a building directory describes the 22226 Brown Avenue building as a 143-unit concrete development, while the project's presale pages describe Phase 1 as either 143 market condos and townhomes plus 49 rental apartments, or 192 condos plus 49 rental apartments, in four buildings of 3 to 6 storeys. The 49 rental apartments in Phase 1 are non-market rentals, not strata condos, so confirm which building a unit is in and how it's owned.
Where the condo stock concentrates: the: Where the condos are: around Dewdney Trunk Road and 222 to 224 Streets on the west side of downtown (Falcon Manor, Era, The 222 and Canuck Plaza), on 122 Avenue to the north (Emerson, Magnolia Gate and Inspire), and in low-rises along Lougheed Highway (223 North).

The escarpment policy area's east boundary is 224 Street, and a geotechnical report is required within 300 m of the top of the escarpment.
The biggest \"townhome\" complex at the: The biggest "townhome" complex at the west edge isn't a strata. Brookside Gardens (20834 Dewdney Trunk Road; 44 units, built in 1978) is a rental complex held as an investment property, so its units are never sold individually.
The board's 12 Maple Ridge sub-areas are: On MLS®, Maple Ridge's 12 areas are Albion, Cottonwood, East Central, North, Northeast, Northwest, Silver Valley, Southwest, Thornhill, Websters Corners, West Central and Whonnock. "West Central" is one of them; "Town Centre", the City's planning name, isn't.

The Fraser River Escarpment policy area's east boundary is 224 Street, and lots within 300 m of the top of the escarpment need a geotechnical report, registered as a covenant.

Where the townhouse stock concentrates:: Where the townhouses are: on Dewdney Trunk Road in the 21700 and 21800 blocks, where both complexes are, west of the downtown condos. No — it is a board sub-area name. The Ci: No, it's a real estate board area name. The City publishes no boundary for it and doesn't list it as a neighbourhood. Listings in West Central include addresses on 222 and 223 Streets at its east edge.

Rail noise is a West Central due-diligen: Check for rail noise in West Central: the Town Centre is beside the CPKC railway, and the City's capital plan funds crossing upgrades at Port Haney and at 203 Street and Maple Crescent.
The Town Centre Area Plan (first adopted: The Town Centre Area Plan (first adopted in November 2008 and updated on November 25, 2025) covers the downtown core at the area's east edge, the City's Transit-Oriented Area bylaw covers the areas around Haney Transit Exchange and Port Haney Station, and TransLink's Langley–Haney Place bus rapid transit line is in detailed planning.
The slowest detached shelf in the city s: Detached homes sell more slowly here than anywhere else in the city. If you're pricing a teardown, compare it with sales here, not the city median.

No. No residential housing mix was confi: No. There are no homes on the island; Delta's Official Community Plan treats it as industrial land, home to the Annacis Business Park, the Port of Vancouver auto terminal and Metro Vancouver's wastewater treatment plant.
Established fee-simple stock: an establi: Established fee-simple homes: an established residential area of mostly single detached houses, on freehold detached and duplex lots. The park beside the school is a live Cit: The park beside the school is being planned: Annieville Lions Park, 9150 112 Street, is beside Annieville Elementary, and the City is preparing a master plan for it. George Mackie Library, 8440 112 Street, is just east in Nordel. There's no recreation centre in Annieville; the North Delta Recreation Centre, 11415 84 Avenue in Nordel, serves North Delta.
By rezoning plus subdivision — the City': By rezoning and then subdividing. The City's example is 10604 River Road, proposed to go from RD3 to RS6 for a two-lot subdivision. Find out what rezoning and servicing would involve, and cost, before you price the property; don't just price the house.
Built 1973, 96 units. The directory reco: Built in 1973, 96 units. Where the condo stock concentrates: the: Where the condos are: on the Scott Road (120 Street) east edge, in just two buildings: Delta Cedars at 8635 120 Street and Muse North Delta at 9015 120 Street.

The corridor's oldest strata stock: the: The oldest strata building along here: a building directory shows 3 levels, finished in 1977, freehold strata, in Beach Grove.

Municipality and plan: Tsawwassen, City: Tsawwassen, City of Delta, planned under the Delta Official Community Plan (Bylaw 8400, adopted July 8, 2024), a single plan for the whole city. It designates farmland as "Agriculture (A)".
Its \"What to look at in a Beach Grove h: The page's "What to look at in a Beach Grove home" cards cover three kinds of home: detached houses in general; homes near the golf club (with easements or covenants and stray golf balls to consider); and shoreline homes on Boundary Bay and low-lying lots (elevation, drainage, covenants on title and insurance).
The stock is mainly detached houses on l: The homes are mainly detached houses on low, flat lots behind the Boundary Bay dike, some on the bay shoreline and some on the interior streets around 17A Avenue. Delta's Official Community Plan (Bylaw 8400, 2024) applies.
Hazard DPA SD3 sets a 2.9 m GSC datum mi: For the Boundary Bay foreshore, the City's hazard development permit area sets a minimum floor level of 2.9 m, a minimum ground elevation of 2.3 m and a 7.5 m setback from the tidal boundary, and the shore is behind the Boundary Bay dike, which the City of Delta maintains. Where the townhouse stock actually sits:: Where the townhouses are: not on the beachfront.
None that I know of. The apartment-condo: None that I know of. The condo projects (The Granary's 16 garden flats and District Flats' 34 homes) are in Southlands, on the Market Avenue side. One 3-storey woodframe Century Group pro: A 3-storey wood-frame project by Century Group at Red Barn Boulevard and Market Avenue in Southlands: 16 single-level garden flats and 19 walk-up townhomes around a garden courtyard, with underground parking and the Four Winds brewery and restaurant at the north end of the courtyard. Monterra is a strata community, not a 2-: Monterra is a strata community, not a two-lot duplex: a unit there is a strata lot (plan LMS469), bought with a Form B like any strata. "Half duplex" is how one listing labelled it, not a different kind of title.
At Tsawwassen’s south end on Boundary Ba: Boundary Beach is the beachfront strip at Tsawwassen's south end on Boundary Bay, next to Boundary Bay Regional Park and running toward the border. South Delta (Ladner / Tsawwassen) is not: The monthly market report I use covers North Delta only, not Ladner or Tsawwassen, so there are no figures for Cliff Drive, and North Delta's numbers don't apply here.
The escarpment permit area starts at the: The escarpment permit area starts at the area's western edge. English Bluff (the Tsawwassen Escarpment) is a hazard development permit area under the Official Community Plan, which matters on the English Bluff Road side and isn't something listings mention.
None of Delta's five known 55+ complexes: None of Delta's five 55+ complexes is townhouses.

No condo or townhome complex with a stre: I don't know of any condo or townhome complex with a Cliff Drive address.

Lot character: the zoning minimums frame: Lot sizes: the zoning minimums are 550 m² in RS5 (or 460 m² in some areas), 390 m² in RS6 and 335 m² in RS7, 836 m² in the RD1 duplex zone and 504 m² in RD4, with 4,000 m² in RS1 in lower-density pockets. Check a property's zone on the City's zoning maps.
The Evergreen Lane names are a trap of a: The Evergreen Lane names are easy to mix up. Since 2023 the Form B must include a sum: Since 2023, the Form B must include a summary of the strata's insurance. The water-damage deductible is the number that matters most in a wood-frame low-rise: owners are often charged the deductible after a leak from their unit.

Check the property's OCP designation in: Check three things, in order: the property's designation in the Official Community Plan's Land Use Plan, its zone on the zoning maps (Zoning Bylaw 7600), and whether a development permit area applies. All three count.

It is a detached Ladner house with a gol: A detached Ladner house with "golf course" ticked under Site Influences on MLS®. The listing agent decides whether to tick it, so the true number of golf-course homes is likely higher than the 54 shown here.
The usual duplex form: Individual duplex: The usual duplex form: individual duplex buildings on single lots on Ladner's residential streets. Delta's small-scale housing zoning (adopted June 24, 2024) allows combinations of single detached homes, duplexes, secondary suites, coach houses and garden suites where it applies, and up to four units on single-detached and duplex lots. A duplex like this sells whole (building and lot, on one title) unless the property was divided into a two-lot strata or subdivided. Being allowed extra units doesn't mean you can subdivide or create new lots.
Delta's Official Community Plan, Bylaw N: Delta's Official Community Plan (Bylaw 8400, 2024) is a single plan for the whole city; it designates farmland "Agriculture (A)".

Nearby areas: Ladner village and its sub: Nearby: Ladner village and its areas (Hawthorne, Holly, Delta Manor and Neilsen Grove) to the east, East Delta beyond them, Westham Island to the west, and Tsawwassen to the south. Ladner's condos are in the village areas; there are none in rural Ladner.

Float homes — documented as a tenure que: Float homes: the West River Road listings are float homes in a marina, with boat slips that come with, or are rented through, the complex, and listing wording that sounds like a strata (garage, reserved parking, slips). Check exactly what you'd own.

More than a typical wood-frame building': More than a typical wood-frame building's, going by listings: a listing at 5011 Springs shows caretaker, garbage, heat, hot water and sewer included in the fee, which fits the buildings' geothermal heating and cooling. Where condo stock concentrates: nowhere: Where the condos are: there are none on the island.
No. Zero known apartment-condo buildings: No. I don't know of any apartment condo buildings, and the rules explain why: the island is ALR farmland (more than 700 hectares), and homes on ALR land can't be stratified. The homes are farmhouses, acreages and float homes at marinas.

Only inside the ALC frame: Principal res: Only within the Agricultural Land Commission's limits: the Agricultural Land Commission allows one main house up to 500 m² plus at most one additional home of 90 m² (parcels of 40 ha or less) or 186 m² (over 40 ha), and a suite only inside the main house. Barber Street is a board sub-area name i: Barber Street is a real estate board area name inside the City of Port Moody's Pleasantside neighbourhood, not a City neighbourhood name. The City plans the area under its Official Community Plan Bylaw, 2026, No. 3522.
The stock is primarily single-detached h: The homes are mostly single detached houses, with a small number of townhouse developments along Ioco Road. That's how the Official Community Plan describes the Pleasantside and April Road area this page covers.

The stock is almost entirely detached ho: The homes are almost all detached houses: the Village's tax base is almost all residential, and most lots are zoned One-Family Residential (RS-1) under Zoning Bylaw No. 510, 2018.
Wildfire interface is a named planning i: Wildfire is part of the Village's planning: the Official Community Plan draws on a Wildfire Protection Plan, and the earlier plan had wildfire protection policies for the forested peninsula.

The mountain has been a planned growth a: The mountain has been a planned growth area for three decades. That's why the homes are all newer townhouses and detached houses.
Unit listings record built 2013 and 2014: Listings give build years of 2013 and 2014 for different homes; a strata directory shows 2014. The 3451 address ("Secret Ridge 1", also built in 2014, with the same published restrictions) is the same complex's second phase.

Plan frame for the remaining land: the N: The plan for the remaining land: the Northwest Burke Vision covers about 400 hectares (980 acres), which the City describes as the last large undeveloped area in Coquitlam, and guides growth over 30 years or more.
