The Burke Mountain Community Centre and: The Burke Mountain Community Centre and Burke Village Park broke ground in May 2026, with design finished and full building construction following in 2026, beside a village centre planned at about 120,000 square feet of retail including a grocery store. They'll serve the whole mountain. I don't know of anything under construction inside the subdivision itself.
Downtown is bounded in practice by the C: Downtown runs from the Coquitlam River on the west to the Mary Hill slope on the east, with Gates Park at 2300 Reeve Street at its north end.
A 55-plus bylaw is the only age bylaw a: A 55+ bylaw is the only age bylaw a strata can enforce. That's the rule behind Mayfair Terrace's registered bylaw at 2266 Atkins Avenue.
The Port Coquitlam Community Centre at 2: The Port Coquitlam Community Centre at 2150 Wilson Avenue (three arenas, a leisure pool, a fitness centre and the Terry Fox Library) fully opened on October 2, 2021, among the downtown condos.
The plan frame is the Official Community: The City's Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 3838) identifies Downtown as a mixed-use neighbourhood and sets the development permit areas, including watercourse protection, that apply to the city's lots.
Townhouse stock sits in four pockets: Ci: The townhouses are in four places: Citadel (Citadel Drive), Riverwood (Fremont Street), Glenwood (Prairie Avenue) and Central (Atkins Avenue).
Shaughnessy Park, 3655 Shaughnessy Stree: Shaughnessy Park, 3655 Shaughnessy Street, is a 32-home townhouse complex with its own zone in the Zoning Bylaw, Comprehensive Development Zone CD3.
For 1990s strata stock (Citadel Pointe,: For 1990s stratas (Citadel Pointe, 1999), compare the depreciation report's 30-year projection with the contingency reserve fund balance on the Form B.
One wood-frame development across two ad: One wood-frame development at two addresses in Polygon's Klahanie master plan, with residents' access to the Canoe Club amenity building. A building directory lists 700 Klahanie as built in 2007 and 600 Klahanie in 2008, with 150 homes at the 700 address, and bylaws of "pets allowed w/rest., rentals allowed w/restrictions". Rental restrictions have been void since November 24, 2022.
An industrial-inspired strata developmen: An industrial-style strata development at Moody and Clarke by Aragon Properties, which lists Platform as its Port Moody project. A building directory shows its bylaws as "pets allowed w/rest., rentals allowed". The development also has townhouses at the same address (see below).
The attached median fell while the detac: The attached median price fell while the detached median held.
Heritage rules touch the cheapest detach: Heritage rules affect the lowest-priced detached houses, not the condos. The older houses around St. Johns, Clarke and Murray Streets are in the Moody Centre heritage conservation area, where a heritage alteration permit can be required to build or rebuild. That adds cost and time, and listings don't mention it.
The Newport Drive catchment crosses into: The catchment for Newport Drive crosses into Coquitlam: School District 43's locator puts 100 Newport Dr in the Gleneagle Secondary catchment in Coquitlam.
Klahanie is the master-planned condo and: Klahanie is the master-planned group of condos and townhouses east of the centre: 50 Electronic at 55 Klahanie Drive, and Boardwalk at Klahanie by Polygon at 600 and 700 Klahanie Drive. Confirm addresses on title.
Suter Brook and Newport Village, around: Suter Brook and Newport Village, around Inlet Centre Station, are the centre's condos and townhouses over shops, and The Grande by Onni at 300 Morrissey Road is the Suter Brook tower.
Coronation Park has its own height secti: Coronation Park has its own height limits: Area A, mixed use up to 31 storeys, and Area B, residential up to 26 storeys, under the vision the City brought into Port Moody 2050, with a third Area C designated multi-residential up to 8 storeys, subject to a master plan.
Platform is one mixed development at 83: Platform is one development at 83 Moody St with both condos and townhouses, so it's listed once, under condos.
Platform has townhouses — why aren't the: Platform has townhouses. Why aren't they listed separately here?
Quote neither as settled; the strata pla: Don't rely on either year; the strata plan or Form B settles it.
It replaces a house neighbourhood with a: Over time, it replaces a neighbourhood of houses with a district built around transit. It doesn't rezone existing townhouses nearby, but look into construction and land assembly around a home you're considering.
Moody Centre is a heritage conservation: Moody Centre is a heritage conservation area, so the older houses here come with heritage rules the newer suburbs don't have.
Serviced position: city stock is on muni: Services: homes here are on municipal water and sewer, with utilities (water, sewer, waste) billed separately from property taxes. The 2026 utility bill was due February 27, 2026.
Heritage and history: Port Moody was cho: Heritage and history: Port Moody was chosen as the western end of the transcontinental railway, and the former CPR station on Murray Street is now the Port Moody Station Museum. Moody Centre is a heritage conservation area (as is the Ioco townsite), so a heritage alteration permit can be required to build or rebuild on properties in it. Check that for any lot in the old townsite.
On the developer source, six towers and: According to the developer: six towers and three low-rise buildings with about 2,500 homes, a supermarket, a drug store, daycares and a park, with the first residents expected around 2029. It's new housing beside Inlet Centre Station, not duplexes.
Port Moody's condo stock sits in two sta: Port Moody's condos are in two station areas, not spread across the city: Suter Brook and Newport Village by Inlet Centre Station on Ioco Road, with Klahanie along Klahanie Drive, and St. Johns Street by Moody Centre Station.
The two SkyTrain stations that organise: The condos are around two SkyTrain stations: Moody Centre Station at 65 Williams Street and Inlet Centre Station on Ioco Road, with St. Johns Street and Clarke Street as the east–west streets below them.
The newest tower stock is at Suter Brook: The newest tower is at Suter Brook Village: The Grande, by the Onni Group, at 300 Morrissey Road (some homes use 305 and 308 Morrissey Road), which the developer describes as the final offering in Suter Brook Village, with 1-, 2- and 3-bedroom homes.
The Moody Centre shelf's named strata is: The named strata near Moody Centre Station is Platform by Aragon at 83 Moody Street, at Moody Street and Clarke Street. Aragon lists Platform as its Port Moody project, and the development has both apartments and townhouses at one address.
Inlet Centre Station, on Ioco Road, is t: Inlet Centre Station, on Ioco Road, is the SkyTrain station for the Suter Brook, Newport Village and Klahanie condos. It has no West Coast Express service.

Inlet Centre Station, on Ioco Road, is the SkyTrain station for Suter Brook and Newport Village. Moody Centre Station, at Williams Street, is the station for St. Johns Street and is also a West Coast Express stop. Both are Millennium Line stations.
Port Moody Centre, by a wide margin on t: Port Moody Centre, by a wide margin for condos and townhomes: 120 of Port Moody's 192 condos and townhomes for sale in September 2026, plus 15 detached houses. North Shore is next for condos and townhomes (43), and the most detached houses for sale are in Anmore (28) and Heritage Woods (18) (Source: SnapStats FVR/GVR September 2026 report).
City lots are on municipal water and sew: City lots are on municipal water and sewer; there are no well-and-septic lots in Port Moody's built-up area.
Townhome stock concentrates in Klahanie: The townhouses are mostly in Klahanie (Klahanie Drive, off Barnet Highway), Suter Brook (Morrissey Road) and along St. Johns Street.
Suter Brook's anchor is The Grande, 300: Suter Brook's landmark is The Grande, 300 Morrissey Road, a 26-storey condo tower by Onni. The townhouses are in the low-rise buildings around it.
Suter Brook Village and Newport Village,: Suter Brook Village and Newport Village, on either side of Ioco Road, are the two planned shopping villages for these homes.
Ranch Park is the house pocket around Sp: Ranch Park is the area of houses around Spuraway Avenue and the north side of Mariner Way in central Coquitlam, with Mundy Park's forest on its south edge. The City publishes no boundary for this real estate board area, so go by street names, not a line on a map.
The slope is the defining physical fact: The slope defines the area: BC Hydro says the elevation drops 170 metres between the top of the slope at Spuraway Avenue and Pinnacle Street and the Como Lake Substation at Como Lake Avenue and Lougheed Highway, so lots step down the hillside instead of being flat.
Slope is the first check on any Spuraway: Check the slope first on any Spuraway Avenue lot: the City asks owners of lots with a steep slope on or beside them to contact Development Services early, before any small-scale building, and BC Hydro puts the elevation change here at 170 metres.
The documented age in this pocket is in: What's on record about this area's age is in its street names: the City says several River Springs streets were named after 1930s Hollywood visitors to the river, when the Oxbow Ranch on the Coquitlam River was renamed Steelhead Lodge, a fishing lodge visited by film stars of the day.
The City treats it as an existing river: The City treats it as an existing riverside area on Shaughnessy Street under the Northeast Coquitlam Area Plan, with a history going back to the 1930s: the Oxbow Ranch became Steelhead Lodge, a fishing lodge visited by Hollywood stars, and several streets here were named after those visitors. The newer Burke Mountain neighbourhood plans (Lower Hyde Creek, Upper Hyde Creek and Smiling Creek) cover separate areas to the north.
Riverwood's attached market is mostly to: Riverwood's attached homes are mostly townhouses, plus one condo building at the Fremont edge. Port Coquitlam's other condo buildings are in other areas: Central Port Coquitlam (Montrose Square, Symphony at Gates Park, Lumiere, The POCO, The Shaughnessy, Mayfair Terrace, Shaughnessy Square and Luxora) and Glenwood (The Arden, The Sapphire, Portica West and Lexford by Polygon).
By Mosaic Homes. MLS listing data for un: By Mosaic Homes. MLS® listings for homes in the building show apartment condos, freehold strata, built in 2014, in Riverwood, with a clubhouse and gym at The River Club.
\"Riverwood\" is also the board (GVR) su: "Riverwood" is also the real estate board's name for the area, so the City's name and the board's name match.
Riverwood's attached market outran its d: Riverwood's condos and townhomes sold faster than its detached houses in September 2026: 38% of the condos and townhomes for sale sold, against 20% of detached houses (SnapStats GVR September 2026). Townhouses are what sells here.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates:: Where the townhouses are: along Riverwood Gate (Mountain View Estates), around Avon Place and Nile Gate at the Fremont edge (Dominion, beside the Fremont Green condo building), and on Skeena Street (the complex named Riverwood).
No — Riverwood is a City of Port Coquitl: No. Riverwood is a City of Port Coquitlam neighbourhood and a real estate board area in north-east Port Coquitlam, by the Pitt River. Port Coquitlam's Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 3838) and Zoning Bylaw No. 3630 apply, not Surrey's.
The stock is detached houses on the Rive: The homes are detached houses on the streets around Riverwood Gate and Coast Meridian Road, in the City's RS zones under Zoning Bylaw No. 3630. The minimum lot width is 15 metres in RS1, 12 metres in RS2, 30 metres in RS3 and 9.5 metres in RS4.
Minnekhada Middle is the middle school i: The school locator gives Minnekhada Middle as the middle school for the Riverwood Gate address I checked, so the schools there are Blakeburn, Minnekhada and Terry Fox.
Serviced position: city stock is on muni: Services: homes here are on municipal water and sewer, charged as flat annual fees, billed separately from property taxes and due March 31, 2026.
ALR vs non-ALR: no ALR land was confirme: ALR: I don't know of any ALR land in Riverwood, which is an urban part of north-east Port Coquitlam. Check a specific property on the Agricultural Land Commission's map.
3 to 6 small-scale multi-unit housing un: 3 to 6 small-scale multi-unit homes without rezoning, depending on lot size, location and distance to transit, according to the City. The RS zones' minimum lot widths (9.5 m in RS4 up to 30 m in RS3) also limit any lot split.
Address-based in SD43 — the settled samp: By address, in School District 43. The address I checked (1260 Riverwood Gate: Blakeburn Elementary, Minnekhada Middle, Terry Fox Secondary) doesn't tell you the schools for other addresses, though Terry Fox Secondary is in the neighbourhood. Run the locator for the exact lot.
The duplex form here is individual two-u: Duplexes here are individual two-unit homes on RS lots, under the City's rule allowing 3 to 6 homes on a lot. The area's known attached housing is 3 townhouse complexes plus one condo building.
Houses here are the low-density stock ar: The houses here are low-density homes around the Lansdowne Drive and Falcon Drive school campus, not apartments or townhouses: the City Centre Area Plan designates this part of the plan area "One Family Residential" and "Compact One Family Residential", with apartment designations closer to City Centre.
The strata stock for this slope sits on: The strata homes for this slope are on Lansdowne Drive at the bottom of the area, below the detached streets. The one complex that appears in City records is at 1170 Lansdowne Drive, on the same street as the Eagle Ridge Park campus and near Eagle Ridge Elementary at 1215 Falcon Drive.
Lansdowne Drive addresses are not all fi: Lansdowne Drive addresses aren't all listed under one area name, so search for condos by street address and strata plan, not by "Upper Eagle Ridge" alone.
That conversion history is the stock's d: The conversion is what matters most about this complex: it was built as a rental building and its strata corporation was formed afterwards. The depreciation report, the Form B and the conversion disclosure describe it; there's no developer's sales material to rely on.
The City's own archives are a working du: The City's archives are useful for checking strata homes on this slope: the 1980 Subdivision Committee minutes for 1170 Lansdowne Drive can be searched in the Coquitlam archives, along with the neighbourhood's storm drain and creek records.
Houses here are the one-family stock on: The houses here are single-family homes on the slope around Falcon Drive, Charter Hill Drive and upper Lansdowne Drive. The City Centre Area Plan shows "One Family Residential" and "Compact One Family Residential" designations in this part of the plan area, with apartments and townhouses closer to City Centre.
The slope is the stock's defining physic: The slope defines the area: the City's Crunch Trail page gives 242 metres of elevation gain from the Lansdowne Drive and Eagle Ridge Park side to the top of Westwood Plateau, which this area climbs toward.
Northwest Coquitlam Area Plan, carried i: Northwest Coquitlam Area Plan, part of the Interim Official Community Plan
The plateau's stock is a master-planned: The plateau is a master-planned mix: streets of detached houses higher up, and townhouse and condo complexes on Plateau Boulevard, Parkway Boulevard, Paddock Drive and Dayanee Springs Boulevard below, all within the one 2,309-hectare community the City's profile describes.
Apartments sit in the RA1 and RA2 zones: Apartments are in the RA1 and RA2 zones and townhouses in the RTh1 to RTh3 zones under the same bylaw, so the detached houses are the ones in the RS zones.
The Traboulay PoCo Trail is the city's r: The Traboulay PoCo Trail is the city's riverfront trail system, for walking and cycling along the river.
The City's Official Community Plan (OCP): The City's Official Community Plan doesn't name Woodland Acres as a neighbourhood the way it names Lincoln Park and Mary Hill.
Rail noise is a Moody Centre shelf item:: Rail noise matters near Moody Centre Station: the Canadian Pacific Railway tracks run through Moody Centre.
Rail noise matters near Moody Centre Sta: Rail noise matters near Moody Centre Station: the Canadian Pacific Railway tracks run through Moody Centre.
Farm stock character: working farms and: The farms: working farms and nurseries in the A1 agricultural district, including the historic Chinese Canadian small farms the City has documented.
Big Bend is in the City of Burnaby, BC —: Big Bend is in the City of Burnaby, BC. It's the City's main agricultural area, in south Burnaby on the flat land along the Fraser River below the city's steep south slope. "Big Bend" is both the real estate board's name for the area and the name the City uses.
A building profile gives Hillside East T: A building profile gives Hillside East Tower D at 4890 Lougheed Hwy, built in 2024, 45 storeys, by Concord Pacific. Another source lists "Concord Brentwood Phase One" at 4890 Lougheed Hwy and "Concord Brentwood Phase Two - Hillside East" at 4880 Lougheed Hwy. Sources disagree on which phase is at which address, so take a specific tower's address from its strata plan.
The old stock is one street, not scatter: The older buildings are on one street. Vantage Point I and II and Anola Place are all on Bellwood Avenue (2020, 2060 and 2041 Bellwood). They're the area's high-rises from before the town centre was built, and listings say strata fees at Vantage Point I include heat and hot water, which the new towers' fees don't.
\"Brentwood Park\" is the GVR board sub-: "Brentwood Park" is a Greater Vancouver REALTORS® area name: the residential area around Brentwood Park Elementary, south and east of Brentwood Town Centre, one of Burnaby's four town centres.
Presale protection (Oasis, Brentwood Blo: Presale protection (Oasis, Brentwood Block, Étoile Gold): a presale buyer can cancel within 7 days of the later of signing the purchase agreement or receiving the disclosure statement, and all deposits must be held in trust by a brokerage, lawyer, notary or other approved trustee.
Two complexes share the Springer Avenue: Two complexes use the Springer Avenue name in listings: the 1976 strata at 2078–2082 Springer and the 2026 Slate tower at 2135 Springer. A search that doesn't separate them mixes a small wood-frame strata with a 45-storey concrete tower.
Two \"Tower One\" buildings, one word ap: Two "Tower One" buildings: the strata Tower 1 (4510 Halifax Way) and SHAPE's rental Tower ONE (1820 Willingdon Ave) are in the same town centre with nearly the same name. A careless search can mistake the rental building for condos you can buy.
What do strata fees cover in the older s: What do strata fees cover in the older buildings?
Buckingham Heights is the detached-house: Buckingham Heights is the slope of detached houses east and south-east of Deer Lake in south-central Burnaby, around Buckingham Elementary School (6066 Buckingham Ave), between Deer Lake Park and Royal Oak Avenue. The real estate board treats it as a separate area from Deer Lake, Deer Lake Place and Upper Deer Lake.
Where the condo stock concentrates: nowh: Where the condos are: there are none. The area is almost entirely freehold detached houses.
\"Buckingham Heights\" is the GVR board: "Buckingham Heights" is a Greater Vancouver REALTORS® area name, separate from Deer Lake, Deer Lake Place and Upper Deer Lake, which border it. The area surrounds Buckingham Elementary (6066 Buckingham Ave), between Deer Lake to the north-west and Royal Oak Avenue to the west and south-west, on and around Buckingham Drive and Buckingham Avenue.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates:: Where the townhouses are: there are none. The area is almost entirely freehold detached houses.
ALR vs non-ALR: no ALR parcel in Bucking: ALR: I don't know of any ALR land in Buckingham Heights.
Heritage diligence: Sperling Avenue fron: Heritage: Sperling Avenue facing Deer Lake Park is in the Deer Lake Park Heritage Precinct, and houses on the heritage register go through heritage review. Check the register and the precinct before planning a rebuild or subdivision on a lot facing the park.
The usual duplex form: A specific proper: Duplexes: if a property on this slope is marketed as a duplex, check its title to see whether it's one lot, a strata or a subdivided pair.
It is a separate board sub-area from Dee: It's a separate real estate board area from Deer Lake, Deer Lake Place and Upper Deer Lake, which border it, even though all four are around the same lake.
No — there is no known condo or townhome: No. I don't know of any condos or townhomes in the area.
A property marketed as a duplex here is: If a property here is marketed as a duplex, check its title first.
The detached-house slope east and south-: The slope of detached houses east and south-east of Deer Lake in south-central Burnaby, around Buckingham Elementary School (6066 Buckingham Ave), between Deer Lake Park and Royal Oak Avenue. It's a separate MLS® area from Deer Lake, Deer Lake Place and Upper Deer Lake.
Whether a specific lot qualifies is a pa: Whether a specific lot qualifies depends on Zoning Bylaw 2026 No. 14815, not the repealed Bylaw 4742.
ALR vs non-ALR: no ALR parcel in this su: ALR: I don't know of any ALR land in this area.
If a bare-land strata lot is ever market: If a bare-land strata lot is ever for sale here, remember that it's strata ownership: you own a strata lot, pay strata fees, follow the bylaws and review the Form B.
Schools: SD41 (Burnaby) runs 41 elementa: Schools: School District 41 (Burnaby) runs 41 elementary and 8 secondary schools across the city, with no middle schools: elementary is K–7 and secondary is 8–12. Schools in or beside this area include Douglas Road Elementary (K–7), 4861 Canada Way; Cascade Heights Elementary (K–7), 4343 Smith Ave, on the south side; and Burnaby Central Secondary (8–12), 6011 Deer Lake Parkway, on the east side. As one example, the district's School Locator gives Douglas Road Elementary and Burnaby Central Secondary for 4861 Canada Way.
\"Burnaby Hospital\" is a board sub-area: "Burnaby Hospital" is a real estate board area name taken from the hospital, not a City of Burnaby community plan name. The City publishes no boundary for it.
ALR vs non-ALR: no ALR parcel in Burnaby: ALR: I don't know of any ALR land in Burnaby Lake. Check a specific property with the Agricultural Land Commission.
Burnaby Lake is a City of Burnaby GVR bo: Burnaby Lake is a real estate board area around Burnaby Lake Regional Park in central-east Burnaby: residential streets on the edges of the lake (Sperling and Kensington to the west and north-west, Government Road and Beaverbrook to the east) around a large Metro Vancouver regional park. The park and lake aren't residential land; the area is the housing around them.
Lake-edge diligence: the lake shore is l: Near the lake: the shore is low, marshy wildlife habitat. For lots beside the lake or a creek, check flood, habitat and watercourse setback rules early, because setbacks tend to come up late in a deal.
Two lakes' names are used interchangeabl: Two lakes' names get used for the same homes on Canada Way: Savile Row is listed in Burnaby Lake and marketed as the "heart of Deer Lake". If you search only one lake's name, you can miss homes along the south edge.
Flood, habitat and watercourse-setback c: Check flood, habitat and watercourse setback rules early. The shoreline is protected wildlife habitat, and I don't know of a floodplain designation for the residential streets, so it depends on the specific property.
Built 2015 (building directory, secondar: Built in 2015, according to a building directory and current listings. Listings describe a boutique building in the Heights near Confederation Park, with an elevator and garage parking; a top-floor listing mentions 11-foot vaulted ceilings.
The biggest \"condo\" complex on the hil: The biggest "condo" complex on the hill isn't a condo. Kensington Gardens has 125 homes that a search site would count as Capitol Hill condos, but it's co-ownership (undivided interest) from the mid-1960s. Without it, the area's strata apartments are five small buildings on Hastings Street plus one presale.
Listings describe \"a boutique collectio: Listings describe "a boutique collection of 32 luxurious townhomes" in Capitol Hill: a current listing shows a 2-storey townhouse built in 2009, wood frame with fibre-cement siding, in a managed strata complex with a bike room and with hot water, sewer, grounds maintenance and snow removal covered. The 32 homes is the listings' number. Confirm rental, pet and age rules with the Form B.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates:: Where the townhouses are: not on the hilltop, which is detached houses on sloping streets with views, but at the bottom and east edge of the hill. They're on Ellesmere Avenue just south of Hastings (Hilltop Greene and the strata at 388 Ellesmere) and at the end of Hastings Street at the foot of Burnaby Mountain (Cassia).
The biggest attached complex on the hill: The biggest attached complex on the hill isn't a strata. Kensington Gardens has 125 homes that a search site would count as Capitol Hill attached homes, but it's co-ownership (undivided interest) from the mid-1960s. Without it, the area's townhouses are two small stratas on Ellesmere Avenue plus Cassia at the foot of the mountain.
The only lot-size figures an official so: The only lot sizes an official source gives are the R1 small-scale housing thresholds: 280 m² and 281 m². What matters more about lots here is the slope, which you check lot by lot.
ALR vs non-ALR: no ALR parcel on Capitol: ALR: I don't know of any ALR land on Capitol Hill. Check a specific property with the Agricultural Land Commission.
The hill's biggest \"condo\" complex hol: The hill's biggest "condo" complex has no strata lots: Kensington Gardens' 125 homes are co-ownership (undivided interest) from the mid-1960s, and listings say its maintenance fee includes property tax, which is typical of co-ownership, not strata. Without it, the hill's attached homes are a handful of small Hastings Street buildings plus Cassia at the foot of the mountain.
So what is Capitol Hill's actual strata: So what strata apartments does Capitol Hill actually have?
The presale record describes 20 condomin: A presale directory describes 20 condos plus 11 live-work homes (31 in total) in a 4-storey wood-frame low-rise finished in 2023; a building directory says 36 homes and built in 2024. The strata plan and Form B settle the number of homes, so don't rely on either figure.
A comp search run under only one sub-are: If you search for comparable sales under only one area name, you'll miss homes listed under the other.
Wood-frame, built 1982. A current listin: Wood frame, built in 1982. A current listing describes the 9880 building as a "99 Unit Development, Wood Frame". Published restrictions: one cat allowed, no dogs (from a current listing). Published major work: rainscreening and re-piping in 2025, windows in 2019, elevator in 2017. Amenities: fitness centre and sauna.
Three concrete high-rises, built 1994 —: Three concrete high-rises, built in 1994. They're the area's only towers and its newest buildings. Published restrictions: pets allowed, rentals allowed. Amenities: outdoor pool, hot tub, sauna, gym, tennis courts and concierge.
The condo stock concentrates in one pock: The condos are in one place: Manchester Drive, south of Lougheed Highway, where four wood-frame and concrete complexes are together. MLS® lists them in Cariboo.
The secondary school is a heritage recor: The secondary school is an older campus. The City's heritage record says Cariboo Hill Secondary (8580 16th Avenue) was built in 1961, with additions in 1969, 1971 and 1974.
Two of the four complexes have already b: Two of the four complexes have already done their most expensive repairs. Brookside Court's rainscreening and re-piping were done in 2025 and Barclay Woods' roof in 2018. Here, ask what work remains and what the depreciation report schedules next.
Fresh listings for the townhouse complex: Recent listings for the townhouse complex below, however, show its MLS® area as "Sullivan Heights" (Burnaby North).
\"Cariboo\" is the GVR board sub-area na: "Cariboo" is a Greater Vancouver REALTORS® area name.
ALR vs non-ALR: no ALR parcel in Cariboo: ALR: I don't know of any ALR land in Cariboo. Check a specific property with the Agricultural Land Commission.
Creek-side diligence: Stoney Creek and t: Near the creek: Stoney Creek and the Brunette River conservation lands run along the area's north side and are dedicated as park by bylaw. Check hazards and watercourse setbacks for the specific property.
Cariboo is a City of Burnaby GVR board s: Cariboo is a real estate board area in east Burnaby around Cariboo Road and Cariboo Hill, between Lougheed Highway and the Edmonds side, with Cariboo Hill Secondary and Armstrong Elementary. The City's heritage record for the secondary school places it in the "Cariboo-Armstrong" planning study area and the East Burnaby historic neighbourhood.
Watercourse diligence: the Cariboo and B: Creeks: the Cariboo and Brunette River Conservation Lands and the Stoney Creek Park and Trail System are dedicated as park by City bylaw on the area's north side. For creek-side lots, check watercourse setbacks early; they're measured from the creek, not the lot line.
The distinction matters because the Manc: That matters because the Manchester Drive buildings are low-rises and towers from 1981–1994, not new town-centre towers.
Which buildings are wood-frame and which: Which buildings are wood frame and which are concrete?
Main streets: Canada Way is the main roa: Main streets: Canada Way is the main road through the area, with Willingdon Avenue to the west and Sperling Avenue to the east; Highway 1 runs to the north. The townhouses in Cascade Heights are on Norfolk Street and Smith Avenue.
A self-managed 7-unit strata from 1983 s: A self-managed 7-home strata from 1983 is here. The complex at 3058 Smith Avenue is a 7-home, self-managed townhouse strata built in 1983. With a small strata, look closely at how it's run: there's no professional manager, a depreciation report is required at 5 or more lots, and the contingency reserve fund has a 10% minimum contribution.
Any page presenting Central as a North B: Central isn't a North Burnaby neighbourhood.
\"Central\" is the GVR board sub-area na: "Central" is a Greater Vancouver REALTORS® area name: Burnaby's civic centre along Canada Way between Willingdon Avenue and Deer Lake, around City Hall and Burnaby Central Secondary.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates:: Where the townhouses are: around Norfolk Street and Smith Avenue, east of Canada Way, facing and near Broadview Park. All four complexes are there.
Established side-street lots: detached s: Side-street lots: detached single-family houses on the side streets off Canada Way, with civic and institutional land around City Hall and Deer Lake and a small number of apartment buildings along Canada Way and toward Metrotown.
No named bare-land development, assembly: I don't know of any bare-land development, land assembly, development site or rezoning proposal in Central
What condo stock actually exists in Cent: What condos are there in Central?
A concrete building by Bosa in the heart: A concrete building by Bosa in the heart of Metrotown, according to current listings, with an exercise centre, steam room and bike room. Listings give 1994 as the year built, while a building directory and another listing say 1995.
A listing for a unit at this address int: A listing for a home at this address calls it "Central Park Place", a concrete building, with 2 parking stalls and 1 locker for that home, and gives 1981 as the year built. A rental website's building profile gives the same name and address as 408 units, 21 storeys, built in 1992.
Where the condo stock concentrates: east: Where the condos are: east of the park, on Wilson Avenue, Barker Avenue and Patterson Avenue between the park and Metrotown. There's a group of 1990s Bosa concrete buildings (Paramount, Paramount II, Place Meridian), a 1970s–1990s group around Patterson and Sardis (Central Park Place at two addresses, Grand Central Park Place, Wimbledon Club), one 2017 tower (Aldynne on the Park), and the area's newest tower, Central Park House (2025), at the Patterson Station end of Wilson Avenue. In northeast Burnaby, south-west of Burn: In northeast Burnaby, south-west of Burnaby Mountain, between Kensington Avenue and the Greystone side, above Lougheed Highway and Burnaby Lake. The City also calls the area "Sperling-Broadway" for planning purposes; Montecito is the MLS® area name.
Oakdale (Burnaby) is the small residenti: Oakdale (Burnaby) is the small residential area in north-east Burnaby along Lougheed Highway, east of Lougheed Town Centre toward the Coquitlam border. "Oakdale" is a Greater Vancouver REALTORS® area name.

Where the condo stock concentrates: it b: Where the condos are: there are very few here. Burnaby's towers and low-rise condos are in its town centres (Metrotown, to the south-west, is this area's main shopping and condo centre), not around the hospital.

Where condo stock concentrates: nowhere: Where the condos are: none that I know of. The residential streets, both around the park and in the southern strip that MLS® lists as Burnaby Lake, are streets of detached houses.

The green space around the lake is a long-term arrangement, not land waiting to be developed.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates:: Where the townhouses are: around the park, none that I know of. The residential streets are streets of detached houses.
The park has been regionally run for alm: The region has run the park for almost five decades. Metro Vancouver has managed Burnaby Lake Regional Park since 1978, and the City and Metro Vancouver have signed a 25-year lease that secures that, with a Park Management Plan to be developed with the City within five years. The green space around the lake is a long-term arrangement, not land waiting to be developed.
A buyer set on strata living here is loo: If you want a strata home here, you're looking at townhouses, or at the neighbouring areas.
One documented townhome complex: Savile: One townhouse complex that I know of: Savile Row at 5122–5152 Canada Way (built in 2018, GBL Architects, freehold strata, 3 storeys). MLS® lists it in Burnaby Lake even though its own marketing calls the location the "heart of Deer Lake".
The plan frame is new: the Burnaby 2050: The main plan is new: the Burnaby 2050 Official Community Plan was adopted on December 9, 2025, replacing the 1998 plan, and the City reviews it every five years as the Province requires.
The current zoning bylaw is Burnaby Zoni: The current zoning bylaw is Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026, No. 14815, adopted June 9, 2026 and in effect July 1, 2026. The former Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 1965, No. 4742, was repealed, so don't check a lot against it.
If a lot is ever offered in bare-land st: If a lot is ever offered as a bare-land strata lot, review it the way you would any strata: request a Form B Information Certificate from the strata corporation, which sets out the lot's fees, amounts owing, special levies and insurance.
80 of the 1,656 Burnaby condo sales carr: 80 of the 1,656 Burnaby condos that sold had "Penthouse" entered as the style, most of them in Metrotown (22). The listing agent enters that, so some top-floor homes aren't marked and a marked one isn't always on the very top floor.
Capitol Hill's condo and townhome stock: Capitol Hill's condos and townhouses are on and below Hastings Street, not on the hilltop house streets. The City's major projects list shows the area's one current strata project at 4472 Hastings Street, at Willingdon Avenue.
The attached stock here is small and gro: The condos and townhouses here are small and low compared with Burnaby's town centres. The only strata project on the City's current major projects list for this area is a five-storey mixed-use building at 4472 Hastings Street, with 34 strata homes over ground-floor shops (3 studios, 4 one-bedrooms, 12 one-bedroom-plus-den homes and 15 two-bedroom homes, including adaptable units, by the City's count).
The current zoning frame is the Burnaby: Current zoning is the Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026, which replaced the 1965 bylaw. R1 is the Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing District.
One Hastings-fronting lot shows the tran: One lot on Hastings shows how the street is changing: 4472 Hastings Street, a former service station site, was planned for about 5,760 square feet of retail plus 34 strata homes under a Comprehensive Development (CD) zone.
Start with building age and construction: Start with the building's age and construction: Brookside Park is wood frame from 1982, so what matters is the depreciation report's timelines for the building envelope, roof and plumbing, more than the finishes in the unit.
Central Burnaby's strata stock is a Norf: Central Burnaby's strata homes are on Norfolk Street, not in a town centre: the named complexes line Norfolk Street between Canada Way and Deer Lake Parkway, with one complex on Canada Way, Savile Row.
Savile Row at 5122–5152 Canada Way is th: Savile Row at 5122–5152 Canada Way is the townhouse strata facing Canada Way, the only named complex on the main road itself.
A seven-unit self-managed strata, like t: A seven-home self-managed strata, like the complex at 3058 Smith Avenue, has the same duty to get a depreciation report: the Province makes no exception for self-managed stratas of five or more lots.
Burnaby City Hall and the Deer Lake civi: Burnaby City Hall and the Deer Lake civic buildings are at the east end of this area, beside Deer Lake Park, not in a shopping district.
Royal Oak Station on the Expo Line is th: Royal Oak Station on the Expo Line, between Metrotown and Edmonds, is the SkyTrain station for this area.
The house stock is detached houses on th: The houses are detached homes on the streets around Canada Way and Deer Lake Parkway, while the strata buildings are on Norfolk Street between Canada Way and Deer Lake Parkway, including two buildings named Winchelsea at 3738 and 3733 Norfolk Street.
Canada Way and Deer Lake Parkway frame t: Canada Way and Deer Lake Parkway border the area, and Sperling Avenue runs north from Deer Lake Park to Lougheed Highway and Sperling–Burnaby Lake SkyTrain station.
The strata stock sits east of Central Pa: The strata homes are east of Central Park, because the park fills the west side between Boundary Road and Patterson Avenue. Heritage Burnaby gives the park's boundaries as 49th Avenue to the south, Kingsway to the north, Boundary Road to the west and Patterson Avenue to the east.
Wilson Avenue holds the newest and talle: Wilson Avenue has the newest and tallest buildings: Central Park House at 5987 Wilson Avenue, a 41-storey Bosa Properties tower finished in 2025 with townhouses at its base, beside Paramount at 5833 Wilson Avenue, Paramount II at 5899 Wilson Avenue and Place Meridian at 5967 Wilson Avenue.
Two buildings share one name: Central Pa: Two buildings share one name: Central Park Place at 5652 Patterson Avenue and Central Park Place at 4160 Sardis Street. There are also Grand Central Park Place at 6128 Patterson Avenue, Wimbledon Club at 6188 Patterson Avenue and Aldynne on the Park at 5883 Barker Avenue. Confirm the street address, not just the name.
The house stock here is defined by what: The houses here are on the streets along the park's east and south edges, on Patterson Avenue and Imperial Street. The park itself is City park land.
The built landmark stock is institutiona: The landmark buildings are public, not strata: Burnaby Village Museum at 6501 Deer Lake Avenue and the Shadbolt Centre at 6450 Deer Lake Avenue are on the north shore.
The Edmonds, Cariboo and The Crest board: The Edmonds, Cariboo and The Crest real estate board areas are all part of what buyers call east Burnaby.
Planning frame: the Edmonds Community Pl: Planning: the Edmonds Community Plan was adopted in March 2025. It's the current plan for the town-centre part of east Burnaby.
Where condo stock concentrates: the apar: Where the condos are: the apartments listed in the "East Burnaby" area are scattered, not grouped in one place.
Route 116 runs Metrotown–Edmonds via 18t: Route 116 runs between Metrotown and Edmonds via 18th Avenue and Griffiths Drive, linking the two stations.
Edmonds, one of Burnaby's four town cent: Edmonds, one of Burnaby's four town centres, is on the west side, and the New Westminster border is on the east. Smaller real estate board areas, including Edmonds, Cariboo and The Crest, are part of what a buyer would call east Burnaby, so name the street and the nearest school, not just "east Burnaby".
Detached houses on the interior east-sid: This page covers the detached houses on the interior east-side streets. The condos and townhouses are mostly toward Edmonds and Highgate, which are reported as their own areas, while the house lots are on Second Street, Twelfth Avenue and the Cariboo Hill streets.
The plan's three nodes are where the con: The condos are at the plan's three centres: mid- and high-rises along Kingsway at the Town Centre, towers at the Station, and the Southgate City master plan to the south.
Zoning for the corridor stock is in the: Zoning for these buildings is in the Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026 (Bylaw No. 14815): Low-Rise Apartment (R3, R4), Mid-Rise Apartment (R5, R6) and High-Rise Apartment (R7, R8) districts, with a Townhouse District (R2) for townhouses.
The name buyers see on listings, \"Fores: The name on listings, "Forest Glen BS", is the real estate board's label (BS means Burnaby South). The park, schools and streets use Forest Glen on its own.
The towers and the low-rise stock fall i: The towers and the low-rises are in different districts of the Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026 (Bylaw No. 14815), which run from Townhouse District (R2) and Low-Rise Apartment (R3, R4) to High-Rise Apartment 2 District (R8). So the Hazel Street towers and a Denbigh Avenue low-rise aren't under the same rules.
Form and character of any new multi-fami: The look and layout of any new multi-family project here come under the Zoning Bylaw 2026's Form and Character Development Permit Area guidelines. They say a development permit isn't needed for permitted uses in the R1 Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing District, or for R1 uses proposed in an R2 Townhouse district, except supportive housing. That matters for small infill projects beside the low-rises.
No separate community plan; filed under: No separate community plan; the City includes it in the Metrotown plan area
Detached houses on the Bond, Nelson and: This page covers the detached houses on Bond, Nelson and the streets toward Sussex, not the towers. Kingsway through Forest Glen has taller buildings that are part of the town centre, while the interior streets are freehold house lots.
The City-facing name for the pocket is F: The City calls the area Forest Grove (Forest Grove Drive, Forest Grove Elementary at 8525 Forest Grove Drive and Forest Grove Park at 8505 Forest Grove Drive), while "Forest Hills" is the real estate board's name.
Wembley Estates, 8187 Forest Grove Drive: Wembley Estates, 8187 Forest Grove Drive at Underhill Avenue, is a 28-home townhouse complex, freehold strata. Its own strata council told the Trans Mountain hearing that it's roughly 50 metres from the entrance to the Burnaby Terminal.
Stratas with five or more lots here must: Since July 1, 2024, stratas with five or more lots must have a depreciation report, renewed every five years. For 1980s townhouses, that report is where building envelope, roofing and road work is scheduled.
The pocket's buyable attached stock is t: The attached homes you can buy here are townhouse complexes on Forest Grove Drive: Wembley Estates at 8187 Forest Grove Drive and Henley Estate at 8210 Forest Grove Drive are the two named in federal hearing records. The large sites a search turns up on Forest Grove Drive and Ash Grove Crescent are housing co-operatives, not condos for sale.
About 50 metres from the terminal entran: About 50 metres from the terminal entrance, according to the strata council: its submission to the Trans Mountain Expansion Project hearing describes the 28-home townhouse complex at the corner of Underhill Avenue and Forest Grove Drive as roughly 50 metres from the entrance to the Burnaby Terminal, with more tanks proposed uphill of the complex in that application. Read that submission before you offer on a Wembley home.
Polygon's wood-frame low-rise, built 200: Polygon's wood-frame low-rise, built in 2007. It's the newest condo building in the area.
It is counted once. Confirm name, year a: Confirm the name, year built and pet rules from the strata plan and Form B for the specific home.
Where the condo stock concentrates: that: Where the condos are: in that one area, in seven complexes built from 1974 to 2007, from 1970s low-rises and towers to a 2007 Polygon low-rise at the west end.
Planning frame: the Lochdale Urban Villa: Planning: the Lochdale Urban Village Plan was adopted on July 25, 2022. It covers the land north of Lougheed Highway, not this south side, but it's changing the area's northern edge.
\"Government Road\" is the GVR board sub: "Government Road" is a Greater Vancouver REALTORS® area name.
No. The City of Lougheed towers stand no: No. The City of Lougheed towers are north of Lougheed Highway; every complex here is south of the highway and MLS® lists it in Government Road. The buildings are also older: low-rises and mid-rises from 1974–2007, not new town-centre towers.
Polygon's 2007 pair at the west end: the: Polygon's 2007 pair at the west end: the Sandlewood condo low-rise (9233 and 9283 Government Street, wood frame, with Sandlewood Club amenities) and the Terramor townhouses next door at 9133 Government Street.
What is the newest stock in the corridor: What's the newest building in the area?
It is one building, counted once in; ord: It's one building. Order documents by the strata plan number, not the marketing name.
How old is the oldest stock, and what ha: How old is the oldest building, and what work has been done on it?
Yes, one complex counted once: the direc: Yes, it's one complex: a building directory lists it at 9088 Halston Court, built in 2006, while listings at 9133 Government Street say built in 2007.
Burnaby's zoning bylaw changed under thi: Burnaby's zoning bylaw changed in mid-2026. Zoning Bylaw 2026 (No. 14815) was adopted June 9, 2026 and took effect July 1, 2026, replacing the repealed 1965 Bylaw No. 4742, and the Burnaby 2050 Official Community Plan (adopted December 9, 2025) replaced the 1998 plan. A Greentree document or listing that cites the old bylaw numbers is out of date.
\"Greentree Village\" is the GVR board s: "Greentree Village" is both a Greater Vancouver REALTORS® area name and the name of the planned community in the City's Greentree Village Community Plan (dated November 6, 1972): a site of about 50 acres south of Canada Way and Highway 1, behind BCIT and west of Deer Lake, bounded by Wayburne Drive (west), Woodsworth Street (north), Forest Lawn Cemetery (east) and Moscrop Street (south), planned for about 450 homes at 12 per acre. The village streets are Garden Grove Drive, Fernglen Drive and Place, Cedarglen Place, Laurelwood Place, Elmgrove Drive, Driftwood Place and Village Drive.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates:: Where the townhouses are: throughout the village. It's a townhouse village built as a series of stratas, surrounded by streets of detached houses.
Greentree Village is older than the SkyT: Greentree Village is older than SkyTrain and older than most of Burnaby's townhouses: it was planned in one City report dated November 6, 1972, at about 450 homes on roughly 50 acres. It was a complete townhouse village approved before townhouses were common in Burnaby.
A \"100% sales ratio\" for this sub-area: A "100% sales ratio" for this area in September 2026 means two homes were for sale and both sold. With so few homes, statistics for the area describe individual sales, not a market.
The stock here is high-rise-led around H: Most homes here are in high-rises around Highgate Village. The plan records existing buildings ranging from 2- and 3-storey houses and townhouses up to taller apartment buildings.
Hall Avenue, Salisbury Avenue and Edmond: Hall Avenue, Salisbury Avenue and Edmonds Street border the residential blocks behind Kingsway, with the Tommy Douglas Library and Edmonds Community Centre beside Kingsway.
Tower strata are the stock here: the Cit: Homes here are strata units in towers. The City's current applications for the Metrotown plan area are high-rises: a 72-storey proposal at 4940 Kingsway, a 40-storey proposal at 5978 Wilson Avenue, and two towers of 32 and 28 storeys at 6470 and 6508 Silver Avenue, plus townhouses at the base of some towers.
The Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026 (Bylaw No. 14815) sets the districts for these buildings: Low-Rise Apartment (R3, R4), Mid-Rise Apartment (R5, R6) and High-Rise Apartment 1 and 2 (R7, R8), with a separate Townhouse District (R2).
No separate plan; filed under Metrotown: No separate plan; part of the Metrotown plan area
The Maywood stock a house buyer actually: What a house buyer sees in Maywood is mostly older low-rise rental and strata buildings, not detached houses on large lots. At 6450, 6486, 6488 and 6508 Telford Avenue, the City lists a three-storey, 33-unit strata apartment building at 6450 Telford (RM3), a two-storey, eight-unit rental building at 6486 Telford (R5), a three-storey, five-unit strata apartment building at 6488 Telford (RM3), and a vacant R5 lot at 6508 Telford.
The Willingdon Avenue stock is 1960s wal: The buildings on Willingdon Avenue are 1960s walk-up rentals: the City says the site at 6622 and 6688 Willingdon Avenue has two three-storey rental apartment buildings with 72 units in total, built in the 1960s. The City's report places the site in the Maywood neighbourhood of the Metrotown Downtown Plan.
Sussex Avenue carries the same era of st: Sussex Avenue has buildings from the same years: the City says 6620 Sussex Avenue has a 53-unit, two- to three-storey rental apartment building built in 1965, on five legal lots under one street address. It was zoned RM3 Multiple Family Residential when the City reported on it.
Silver Avenue's current buildings are al: Silver Avenue's current buildings are also low-rise rentals: the City's 2026 report for 6470 and 6508 Silver Avenue says the two lots have low-rise rental buildings with 83 rental units. The site is designated High-Rise Apartment 1 in the Official Community Plan.
Metropolis at Metrotown is listed by the: The City lists Metropolis at Metrotown as a Metrotown landmark, along with the Hilton Vancouver Metrotown, Holiday Inn Express Metrotown, Element by Westin and head or corporate offices including Interfor, TELUS and Sun Life Financial. The downtown's offices and hotels are in the same town centre as the Maywood residential streets.
For any tenanted walk-up on Telford, Sus: For any tenanted walk-up on Telford, Sussex, Silver or Willingdon, read the City's Rental Use Zoning Policy and Tenant Assistance Policy before you value it for redevelopment. City reports for these streets say proposals must follow both. The same reports give the existing rental counts: 72 units at 6622 and 6688 Willingdon Avenue and 83 units at 6470 and 6508 Silver Avenue.
Where the condo stock concentrates: a sm: Where the condos are: a small group of apartments and condos around Halifax Street at Phillips Avenue, on the north-west side of the area. The rest is detached houses on the sloping streets below Burnaby Mountain, with a few townhouses.
The City does not call this area Monteci: The City doesn't call this area Montecito. For planning and administration it's "Sperling-Broadway". If you look in City documents, community plan maps or facility pages under "Montecito", you'll miss what's under the planning name.
One strata apartment building — The Amba: One strata apartment building, The Ambassador at 7321 Halifax Street (1987), plus the rental-only Montecito Towers next door, which can't be bought. There were 12 condos and townhomes for sale in September 2026 and none sold that month (SnapStats, September 2026)
The SD41 School Locator check for 2176 D: For 2176 Duthie Ave, the School District 41 School Locator gives Montecito Elementary (K–7) and Burnaby North Secondary (8–12); Sperling comes up for that address only for Early French Immersion. So the catchment school there is Montecito, not Sperling. Catchments go by address, so check the building's exact address.
Detached houses on sloping streets below: This page covers the detached houses on the sloping streets below the mountain. There's a small group of low-rise apartments around Halifax Street at Phillips Avenue, but the house streets on Duthie Avenue, Halifax Street and Greystone Drive are freehold detached lots.
The stock contrast with Highgate is the: The difference from Highgate is the point: away from Kingsway and Edmonds, the Edmonds plan records existing buildings as 2- and 3-storey houses and townhouses and up, not a group of towers.
The district context for the stock is a: The homes are on a hillside below Burnaby Mountain Secondary at 8800 Eastlake Drive, a School District 41 secondary school.
The stock here is ground-oriented homes: The homes here are houses and townhouses on Forest Grove Drive, Beaverbrook Crescent and the courts off them, below the treeline of the Burnaby Mountain Conservation Area. The City lists Simon Fraser Hills Park as a neighbourhood park for these streets.
Check the lease first: the due-diligence: Check the lease first: for any UniverCity home, read the 99-year ground lease and the strata's leasehold terms, because SFU keeps ownership of the land. A freehold title search alone doesn't describe what you're buying.
Treat a UniverCity purchase as a strata: Treat a UniverCity purchase as a strata purchase: read the strata documents, bylaws and fee schedule, because the homes on the mountaintop are strata homes, not detached houses.
SFU student residences and campus housin: SFU student residences and campus housing aren't market housing and can't be bought.
The board sub-area name is printed in fu: The real estate board's full name for the area is "Simon Fraser University SFU". The neighbouring area, "Simon Fraser Hills", covers the Forest Grove side of the mountain and is a different area.
A buyer owns the strata lot and a lease: A buyer owns the strata lot and an interest in the lease, not the land. None of these homes is a duplex.
South Slope condo and townhome stock clu: South Slope's condos and townhouses are on the slope south of Rumble Street, along Marine Drive, Nelson Avenue, Patterson Avenue and Sussex Avenue.
The strata stock here is low-rise and mi: The strata homes here are low-rise and mid-rise apartment buildings and townhouse complexes along Nelson Avenue, Patterson Avenue, Sussex Avenue and Station Hill Drive, all freehold strata. Most Burnaby apartment and townhouse complexes are freehold strata, where each home is a strata lot on a registered strata plan.
The stock is detached houses on the slop: The homes are detached houses on the sloping streets between Rumble Street and Marine Drive. The Royal Oak Station area is on the northern half of the slope, outside the blocks of houses.
Rumble Street runs the top of the hill a: Rumble Street runs along the top of the hill and Marine Drive along the bottom, with Royal Oak Avenue and Gilley Avenue on the sides. The Royal Oak Station area is on the northern half of the slope.
South Slope is the house pocket on the h: South Slope is the area of houses on the hill between Rumble Street at the top and Marine Drive at the bottom. The City's Royal Oak Community Plan map shows the slope between Rumble Street, Royal Oak Avenue, Marine Drive and Gilley Avenue.
Schools (SD41): École Sperling Elementar: Schools (School District 41): École Sperling Elementary (2200 Sperling Avenue) is the elementary school on Sperling Avenue itself, and Burnaby Central Secondary (6011 Deer Lake Parkway) is the secondary school in the Deer Lake and Central Burnaby area. As one example, the School Locator gives Sperling Elementary (K–7) and Burnaby North Secondary (8–12) for 2200 Sperling Avenue, so the nearest secondary (Burnaby Central) isn't the catchment secondary for that address.
SSMUH on house lots: under the R1 SSMUH: Small-scale housing on house lots: in the R1 district, standard lots here can have 3–4 homes and larger lots within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop up to 6, and lots with two or more main homes can be stratified. That's where the new duplexes come from, and it affects prices for the area's biggest lots in Buckingham Heights and near Canada Way. Check the Burnaby 2050 Official Community Plan land use map (adopted December 9, 2025) before assuming density or subdivision potential on a large lot, because the new plan overrides older community plan maps.
The stock is almost entirely detached ho: The homes are almost all detached houses: post-war bungalows on the west side, and large custom and estate homes in Buckingham Heights on the slope east of Deer Lake.
Heritage fabric on the lots: Sperling Av: Heritage: Sperling Avenue facing Deer Lake Park is in the Deer Lake Park Heritage Precinct, where the City's heritage register lists early-1900s houses such as the Woodward House at 5195 Sperling Avenue (built in 1912). On that street, heritage review is part of checking a lot.
ALR vs non-ALR: no ALR parcel in Sperlin: ALR: I don't know of any ALR land in Sperling-Duthie. Check a specific property on the Agricultural Land Commission's map.
Hazard note, as documented: the Burnaby: Flooding: the Burnaby Lake Park Association warns that Sperling Avenue and Sprott Street along the park have no proper sidewalks and that the road floods after heavy rain.
Zoning: Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026, No. 14815, adopted June 9, 2026 and in effect July 1, 2026 (not the former 1965 Bylaw No. 4742). In June 2024, Burnaby combined its former single- and two-family districts into one R1 Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing District. R1 lots can have 3 homes on lots up to 280 m², 4 on larger lots, and 6 on lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop, and lots with two or more main homes can be stratified.
The stock is almost entirely detached ho: The homes are almost all detached houses, from post-war bungalows on the flatter western streets to large custom homes in Buckingham Heights on the slope above Deer Lake.
The Sperling Avenue lakefront holds Burn: Sperling Avenue on the lake has some of Burnaby's earliest houses: the City's heritage register lists the Woodward Cottage at 5141 Sperling Avenue, built in 1904 and described as the oldest house in the Deer Lake neighbourhood.
The stock is all detached houses, which: The homes are all detached houses, which sets Suncrest apart from Metrotown's towers immediately to the north and from the mix of homes around Royal Oak Station to the east.
Marine Drive is the slope's bottom stree: Marine Drive is the street at the bottom of the slope to the south, and Rumble Street is the street at the top of the South Slope hill, which Suncrest shares.
No. Suncrest is the all-detached pocket: No. Suncrest is the area of detached houses below Metrotown, and Metrotown's towers are to the north. Suncrest's own main street is Rumble Street, not the town-centre streets.
The stock is detached houses on the Rumb: The homes are detached houses on the streets off Rumble Street (Patterson Avenue, Joffre Avenue, Greenall Avenue and Clinton Street), with no strata complex in the area. The nearest multi-unit buildings are outside it: Metrotown's towers, one bus ride north on Patterson Avenue.
The Edmonds towers are not Crest stock,: The Edmonds towers aren't in The Crest, whatever a listing says. Kings Crossing and its neighbouring towers are west of the area at Edmonds Station, and current listings put them in Edmonds. A Crest search that brings in their prices, ages or amenities is comparing station-area towers with an area of houses and townhouses.
\"The Crest\" is the GVR board sub-area: "The Crest" is a Greater Vancouver REALTORS® area name. It matches The Crest Centre, the neighbourhood shopping plaza around 10th Avenue and Canada Way.
Two of the three complexes carry an unre: For two of the three complexes, sources disagree on the year built, and for one I couldn't confirm the number of homes (checked Nov 1–2, 2026). Start by confirming the strata plan.
Detached houses on side streets are the: Most homes in The Crest are detached houses on side streets. Two School District 41 elementary schools, Second Street Community and Morley, are inside the area of houses, which is typical of an established single-family district, not a tower district.
The oldest stock is the park-side herita: The oldest homes are the heritage houses beside the park: the Moore House at 5145 Sperling Avenue, built in 1941, is in the Deer Lake Park Heritage Precinct.
The stock here reads against the lake an: The area is next to the lake and City Hall, not a shopping street: the 144 bus passes the houses on Burris Street and Buckingham Avenue after leaving the City Hall loop and Deer Lake Avenue.
A 22-unit strata building: the building: A 22-home strata building: a building directory lists it as built in 1998, with bylaws of "pets allowed w/rest., rentals allowed w/restrictions" and air conditioning, a garden and private yards. Rental restrictions have been void since November 24, 2022. Current listings call it "The Sienna", an apartment condo building in Vancouver Heights built in 1998, which matches the directory.
The building directory records Heritage: A building directory lists Heritage Green as built in 1994 with 28 homes, in-suite laundry, and bylaws of "pets allowed w/rest., rentals allowed w/restrictions". Rental restrictions have been void since November 24, 2022. A home at 3978 Albert Street is listed in Vancouver Heights on MLS®.
The building directory records Evergreen: A building directory lists Evergreen Place as built in 1989, with in-suite laundry and bylaws of "pets allowed w/rest., rentals allowed w/restrictions". Rental restrictions have been void since November 24, 2022. The directory shows listings and sales at this address, most recently in October 2025; nothing was for sale when I checked.
The building called \"The Heights\" is n: The building called "The Heights" isn't listed in Vancouver Heights. The Heights (3768 Hastings St, 1998, 37 homes) has this neighbourhood's name, but its MLS® listing puts it in Willingdon Heights. It's on the south side of Hastings at the west edge.
Detached sold briskly while attached bar: Detached houses sold quickly while condos and townhomes barely sold. Price a condo or townhome against other condo and townhome sales, not the detached numbers.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates:: Where the townhouses are: there are no townhouse complexes here.
SnapStats publishes no Vancouver Heights: No median price is published for Vancouver Heights alone.
No. Seton Villa (3755 McGill St) is a 19: No. Seton Villa (3755 McGill St) is a 19-storey non-profit retirement centre run by Action Line Housing Society and registered in BC's Assisted Living Registry. It has independent and supportive suites and assisted living that you rent or are placed into; there's nothing to buy. It's the area's only seniors' building, and I don't know of any 55+ homes to buy here.

The attached stock is apartment condos a: The attached homes are apartment condos along Hastings Street and Willingdon Avenue and townhouse complexes on the side streets between them, all freehold strata. Older low-rise strata buildings, not tow: In Willingdon Heights itself, the established strata buildings are older low-rises, not towers.
Gilmore Avenue is the interior school st: Gilmore Avenue is the street with the schools: Kitchener Elementary is at 1351 South Gilmore Avenue and Gilmore Community School at 50 South Gilmore Avenue, both between Boundary Road and Willingdon Avenue.
The stock is detached houses on the Carl: The homes are detached houses on the streets around Carleton Avenue, Gilmore Avenue and Parker Street, with the Brentwood towers rising at the Lougheed Highway edge. Where the condo stock concentrates: at t: Where the condos are: at the Canada Line stations (King Edward, in Cambie Village; Oakridge–41st Avenue, the centre of the Oakridge Municipal Town Centre; and Langara–49th Avenue) and at the Marine Drive and West 59th Avenue end (Cambie Gardens, Belpark), plus the rise beside Queen Elizabeth Park around West 29th–35th Avenues (Chelsea, Livingstone, 35 Park West, Lina, The Charlotte). Aperture's townhomes share no walls (che: Aperture's townhouses share no walls (checked Nov 2, 2026). Empty Homes Tax — vancouver only, applie: Empty Homes Tax (City of Vancouver only; it applies here): Vancouver's Empty Homes Tax is 3% of assessed taxable value. Owners must submit a property status declaration every year, and the 2025 tax was due April 16, 2026, with a 5% penalty on any unpaid balance after that date. On any purchase here, confirm the seller has made the declaration.
Where multi-family stock actually concen: Where the multi-family homes are: there's no group of apartment condos. Multi-family housing here is townhouse complexes and co-ops around Kerr Street and East 54th Avenue, on the curved roads and cul-de-sacs of the original planned community, with detached houses alongside.

The Co-operative Housing Federation of BC records that the City developed Champlain Heights from 1974 to 1986 by leasing sites to non-market housing sponsors instead of selling them, and its 2026 update lists new long-term leases approved for co-ops including Cedar Mill (July 2025). Where the townhouse stock concentrates:: Where the townhouses are: there's no group of apartment buildings. The leases were a deliberate 1970s plan,: The leases were a deliberate 1970s plan, and they're being renewed now. Champlain Heights was planned in the early 1970s as a showcase community of curved roads and cul-de-sacs with a mix of housing types and incomes, and built in the early 1980s on a large piece of City-owned land. That's why so much of it is on prepaid 99-year City leases that expire in the 2080s. The Co-operative Housing Federation of BC records that the City developed the area from 1974 to 1986 by leasing sites to non-market housing sponsors instead of selling them, and its update lists new long-term leases approved for co-ops including Cedar Mill (July 2025). The mall's zoning is older than the neig: The mall's zoning is older than the neighbourhood. The Champlain Mall CD-1 zoning (By-law No. 4550) was approved at a public hearing on April 20, 1970, before the planned community was built. The mall site at East 54th Avenue and Kerr Street (3200 East 54th Avenue) had a public library in it from early on, and the Champlain Heights Branch library is now in its own building at 7110 Kerr Street.
Detached-house lots: freehold detached h: Detached house lots: freehold detached houses are alongside the townhouses and co-ops. A fee-simple lot has no strata, no Form B and no strata fees.

The multi-family stock is townhouse comp: Multi-family housing here is townhouse complexes and co-ops. The apartment towers sometimes linked with this corner of Vancouver are in the River District (East Fraser Lands), which is in Killarney, not Champlain Heights.
Three: Marine Woods (Millstone / Fieldst: Three: Marine Woods (Millstone, Fieldstone and Cobblestone; strata plan LMS1354; freehold, according to listings), Bordeaux at Champlain Gardens (3265 Clermont Mews, freehold strata, built in 2004) and Highgate. All three are on the Ambleside flat near: All three are on the flat part of Ambleside near Marine Drive, not in Chartwell or on the hillside. Confirm each building's registered age bylaw with its Form B.
Where the condo stock concentrates: nowh: Where the condos are: there are none. The homes are detached houses on hillside lots in the RS single-family zones.

Any British Properties building scheme o: Any British Properties building scheme or covenant is registered on the individual title, on top of District zoning. I haven't confirmed the terms of any covenant, so check the title.
No known condo or townhome stock exists: I don't know of any condos or townhomes here. The homes are detached houses in the RS single-family zones, and the only named buildings in the area are its two public schools.
Secondary suites and a detached secondar: Secondary suites and a detached secondary suite (coach house) are among the uses allowed in the single-family zones. They're rental suites on a detached property, not strata units you can buy separately, and not townhouses.
It is not one of the City of Vancouver's: It isn't one of the City of Vancouver's 22 official local areas. The City treats Coal Harbour as a neighbourhood inside the Downtown local area. On the City's areas page, the Coal Harbour link goes to the West End page, even though the West End is a separate official local area.
Where the condo stock concentrates: almo: Where the condos are: almost all are strata apartment towers along the waterfront and on West Cordova Street, West Hastings Street and the downtown streets that extend into Coal Harbour under the Coal Harbour Official Development Plan. There are no single detached houses in Coal Harbour. The Aspac-built Waterfront Place buildings (Avila, Bauhinia, Cascina, Denia, Escala) are on Nicola, Cardero, Broughton and Jervis Streets, and the Harbour Green and Fairmont towers are along West Cordova Street.
Five of the waterfront towers are one de: Five of the waterfront towers are one developer's set. Aspac's Waterfront Place is five buildings on Nicola, Cardero, Broughton and Jervis Streets, finished as a collection in 2003, with towers named after cities in Italy and Spain: Avila (built 1995–1998), Bauhinia, Cascina and Denia (the last two won a 2004 CHBA Gold Georgie for Best Multi-Family Development of the Year) and Escala. Buildings in Coal Harbour are easy to compare with each other because so many share one builder and one group of architects.
Coal Harbour's townhouses include a rent: Some of Coal Harbour's townhouses are rentals that never come up for sale. The 2003 affordable housing development on City land leased for 60 years included 31 townhouses among its 284 rental units. They explain some of the townhouses you see in the area, but none can be bought.
On the developer's own figures: Cascina: By the developer's own figures: Cascina (117 suites and 30 townhouses), Denia (86 suites and 4 townhouses) and Escala (98 suites and 7 townhouses), plus townhouses at 1 and 2 Harbour Green and 17 townhouses next door at Carina. The townhouses are strata too, but they aren't apartment condos.
Where the condo stock concentrates: in t: Where the condos are: in two groups. The area's official name is not the boar: The area's official name isn't the real estate board's name. City plans, the station area work and the community vision all say Renfrew-Collingwood; "Collingwood VE" is the board's short form. Search under both names.

Properties in the floodplain must meet the Building By-law's setbacks and flood construction levels.

The West End is its own separate officia: The West End is a separate official local area and isn't covered here. Downtown has the densest concentration of condos in the region; the list below covers major named towers, not every building.

Listing copy names the building \"Fifty-: Listings call the building "Fifty-Five 55 Dunbar" and show it as an apartment condo building built in 2015, wood frame, 4 storeys, strata plan EPS3033.
The whole Dunbar condo market is two str: All of Dunbar's condos are on one street. All three apartment buildings are on Dunbar Street or at its corner with West 39th Avenue. I don't know of any strata homes on the interior residential streets.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates:: Where the townhouses are: almost nowhere. Dunbar is overwhelmingly detached houses on tree-lined streets, with the country-style Southlands lots at the south edge.
Dunbar's townhouse supply is one documen: Dunbar's townhouses come down to one address that I know of. If you're waiting for a Dunbar townhouse complex to come up, there's very little to wait for.
Strata diligence (the frontage strata st: Strata note: no Dunbar building is published as 55+. The "55" in Fifty-Five 55 Dunbar is its street number, not an age bylaw.
Because those units are selling as new c: Because those homes are being sold as new construction through a receivership, with a disclosure statement and 2-5-10 warranty. You're buying from the developer's side, not from a homeowner. That changes the paperwork (a disclosure statement instead of a Form B), the tax (5% GST, partly offset by the Newly Built Home Exemption and the federal first-time buyers' GST rebate where you qualify), and what to check (confirm the receiver's authority and the warranty enrolment).
The one documented townhouse address is: The one townhouse address I know of is 3349 Dunbar Street: a strata without a name (the listing shows strata fees), built in 1995. A current listing describes a 2-level, 3-bedroom home with a 624 sq ft rooftop deck and pets "Yes With Restrictions". Everything else in Dunbar is detached houses, three apartment condo buildings, or Southlands country lots.
By the strata-fee record and title, not: By whether it charges strata fees and by the title, not by the word "townhome" in the marketing. The 3349 Dunbar Street listing shows strata fees, so it's a strata. A Dunbar multiplex, duplex or house with a laneway house that shows no strata fees is fee-simple: no strata and no Form B, and you check the title and City rules.
Heather Place is two different projects: Heather Place is two different projects with one name. The existing Heather Place at 774 West 13th Avenue is listed in directories as a seniors' development, while the Heather Place redevelopment at 725–799 West 14th Avenue is a 230-home mixed project for families, seniors and people with disabilities that replaces 86 aging units. Counting all of the redevelopment's homes as seniors' housing overstates it.
The West 7th Avenue pocket predates the: The seniors' buildings on West 7th Avenue are two decades older than the Broadway Subway: Glynn Manor (520 West 7th) and Terraces on 7th (1570 West 7th) are both on the avenue the Broadway Plan covers and the subway will serve from fall 2027. The area's seniors' housing is on the street now being rebuilt around it, with South Granville station at the west end.
Both halves are documented: suites in th: Both are true: suites in the building are listed for sale on MLS® as strata units, and the operator markets the same address as a retirement community for independent living with private suites. You own a strata unit; ask what the retirement community adds on top of strata fees, including services, meals and any mandatory charge.
Most False Creek leases expire in 2036 p: Most False Creek leases expire in 2036, according to one guide. That's within a standard 25-year mortgage, which is why lenders and buyers discount these homes, and why the first number to check is the remaining lease term.
South Granville's Gallery Row is in Fair: South Granville's Gallery Row is in Fairview. The South Granville shopping district and its art galleries are inside the local area north of 16th Avenue, and are the main shopping for the Fairview Slopes and Oak Street homes.
Firehall Library is the branch. Vancouve: The library is the Firehall Branch. Vancouver Public Library's Firehall Branch is at 1455 West 10th Avenue, and Charleson Park (999 Charleson Street) is on the south shore of False Creek.
The hospital is inside the area, not acr: The hospital is in the area, not across a bridge. Vancouver General Hospital, 899 West 12th Avenue, is near West Broadway in the Fairview local area. That's part of why condos near the Broadway medical district draw buyers who work there.
The published terms are a 55-plus age re: The published terms are a 55+ age restriction, 1 cat or 1 dog, and a mandatory service agreement with 10 meals a month, weekly housekeeping and a 24-hour concierge. The 55+ bylaw is legal (it's the only kind of age bylaw allowed, with exemptions for existing residents, caregivers and, since May 1, 2023, younger spouses or partners). The service agreement is a separate contract, so get its current monthly cost in writing.
SD39 catchments are address-based. The t: School catchments go by address.
