The False Creek South waterfront between: The False Creek South waterfront between the Cambie and Burrard bridges is leasehold. There are no detached houses on the False Creek shoreline, though there are houses in the FM-1 zone on the Fairview Slopes above the south shore.
The lands around False Creek are inside: The lands around False Creek are in the City's designated floodplain. The City's False Creek Coastal Adaptation Plan covers False Creek North, False Creek South, Granville Island and the Flats, and properties in the floodplain must meet the Vancouver Building By-law's floodplain standards for shoreline setbacks and flood construction levels. The Northeast False Creek Plan requires new developments to protect homes and critical infrastructure from flooding and rising sea levels, with a continuous line of flood protection across that site. On both shores, check the flood construction level for the specific building.
False Creek was an industrial centre fir: False Creek was industrial first. The City's Coastal Adaptation Plan says False Creek was historically one of Vancouver's major industrial centres and has become an area of higher-density housing, shops and parks. That's why the homes on the shoreline are almost all strata, built in planned phases (1970s–80s leasehold on the south side, the 2010 Olympic Village to the south-east, towers on the north side), with no detached houses.
One south-shore townhouse listing carrie: One south-shore townhouse listing needed court approval. The listing for a townhouse at 1201 Lamey's Mill Road says "ALL OFFERS SUBJECT TO APPROVAL OF THE SUPREME COURT OF B.C." along with its lease to 2040. In False Creek South, read the listing itself for unusual conditions, and allow for them in your price and timing.
No named presale project around False Cr: I don't know of any presale project around False Creek.
Plans as the OCP-equivalent frame here:: Plans that apply here: the Northeast False Creek Plan, the Southeast False Creek development, the False Creek Flats Plan and the False Creek South planning that Council directed in March 2024. Each covers only its own part of the area.
No new housing in False Creek South sinc: Nothing new has been built in False Creek South since the 1980s: the City says the neighbourhood was built in the 1970s and 1980s on its 80 acres. Every False Creek South purchase is a purchase of the remaining lease term on a 1970s–80s home.
It is the Olympic Village development: a: It's the Olympic Village: a mixed-use development of 7 city blocks and 16 residential buildings, built for the 2010 Winter Games. The market strata buildings known by name are Kayak (185 homes), Brook (129), Bridge (119), Sails (114), Compass (63) and Shoreline (35), all built in 2010. About 250 of the development's roughly 1,000 homes are affordable housing, which isn't for sale.
Crosstown šxʷwəq̓ʷəθət Elementary, 55 Ex: Crosstown šxʷwəq̓ʷəθət Elementary, 55 Expo Boulevard, and Elsie Roy Elementary, 150 Drake Street, on the north shore, and False Creek Elementary, 900 School Green, on the south shore. I don't know of a secondary school on the shoreline. Catchments go by address and differ by shore, so check the exact address in the school board's locator.
Strata plan BCS3081; a 4-storey, 50-unit: Strata plan BCS3081: a 4-storey, 50-home wood-frame low-rise built in 2008 by Thind Properties Ltd. Current listings describe 9-foot ceilings, penthouses with skylights and in-suite laundry.

The first settlement here predates the s: Settlement here is decades older than the streets. The first non-Indigenous families settled the Victoria-Fraserview area in the 1860s, drawn to the forests on the north bank of the Fraser River, near the south ends of Main and Fraser Streets. The Avalon Dairy farmhouse (restored inside Avalon Mews) survives from that farming period.

Because they are purpose-built rentals h: Because they're purpose-built rentals owned as whole buildings: The Leeward is a 48-suite rental tower (1968) and Santa Monica a 13-suite rental building (1929), and the district from West 11th to 16th and Fir to Birch is an intact pre-war rental apartment neighbourhood. Killarney was forest and farms until aft: Killarney was forest and farms until after the Second World War. The City's history says the area stayed second-growth forest and farms until after the war, and that the first non-Indigenous settler, William Rowling (1868), came to own 3.5 kilometres of Fraser River shoreline, including all of Killarney's riverfront. That's why the houses are post-war and the waterfront is all new.

UEL tax due date and penalties: because: Property tax due date and penalties in the University Endowment Lands: because the area is taxed as a rural area, annual taxes are paid to the Province's Surveyor of Taxes and are due July 2. A 5% penalty is added to anything unpaid after July 2, and another 5% to anything still unpaid after October 31. Rural tax notices are mailed by May 31, and payment must be received by the due date to be on time.

Municipal frame: Yaletown is inside the: Municipality: Yaletown is in the City of Vancouver, within the City's "Downtown" local area, and the City regulates its historic core separately as the Yaletown Historic Area (HA-3). The City describes that area as bordered by Homer and Nelson streets to the north and east, and Cambie, Mainland and Drake streets to the south and west.
City plans, zoning and heritage: Yaletow: City plans, zoning and heritage: Yaletown comes under the City of Vancouver's Zoning and Development By-law, and its historic core is the Yaletown Historic Area (HA-3). The City has regulations and design guidelines to preserve its protected historic areas (Chinatown, Gastown, Shaughnessy and Yaletown), and the HA-3 zoning encourages converting and renovating Yaletown's heavy-timber, brick and concrete buildings, and compatible new buildings, for a mix of commercial, industrial and residential uses. If you plan to renovate a loft in a converted warehouse (such as The Murchies), the heritage rules apply as well as the strata bylaws.
The two sources for Yaletown's biggest i: Two sources disagree about Yaletown's biggest inland complex. Yaletown's character is a planning rule,: Yaletown's character is written into the planning rules. The City's description (heavy timber, brick and concrete buildings, narrow streets, and covered loading docks used as public space) is part of the HA-3 heritage zoning that governs conversions and new buildings. That's why the Homer Street lofts (The Murchies, 1912, converted in 1997) look and sell differently from the Marinaside towers.

Where condo stock concentrates: along We: Where the condos are: along West 41st Avenue and the edges of the village. There are low-rise condos and townhouses on West Boulevard and East Boulevard, plus seniors' buildings near the village. Otherwise, the homes are mostly detached single-family houses on tree-lined streets, almost all freehold. The Kerrisdale Business Association promotes more than 250 businesses in the village, mostly on West 41st Avenue between Maple and Larch streets and along West and East Boulevards.
Kerrisdale is a southwest Vancouver neig: Kerrisdale is a south-west Vancouver neighbourhood centred on the village on West 41st Avenue, between roughly Larch Street and Blenheim Street, extending north toward West 33rd and south toward West 49th. "Kerrisdale" is also the real estate board's name for the area. Nearby areas: Arbutus Ridge, Shaughnessy, Oakridge, Marpole, Dunbar-Southlands and Quilchena.
The community centre predates most of th: The community centre is older than most of the village around it. The Kerrisdale Community Centre has been run jointly with the Vancouver Park Board since 1943, making it one of Vancouver's first community centres. It includes the Cyclone Taylor Arena (5670 East Boulevard), where the Kerrisdale Play Palace runs in summer.
The newest \"townhouse\" supply here is: The newest "townhouses" here are multiplex homes, not complexes. Recent listings are pairs of half duplexes (some advertised with "no strata fees") and small stratas on R1-1 lots, like The Kerrisdale Collection (2535 West 39th Avenue, built in 2026, half duplexes with strata fees). The zoning change, not new townhouse complexes, is what's adding attached homes in Kerrisdale.
The secondary-school split runs through: The line between secondary school catchments runs through the middle of the neighbourhood. Magee Secondary is in Kerrisdale, but the School Locator gives Point Grey Secondary for Kerrisdale Elementary's own address (5555 Carnarvon Street). Being in Kerrisdale doesn't mean being in the Magee catchment, so check the address in the School Locator.

Planning frame: Mount Pleasant is one of: Planning: Mount Pleasant is one of the three neighbourhoods in the Broadway Plan, approved June 22, 2022 as a 30-year plan (Clark Drive to Vine Street, 1st to 16th Avenues), with buildings up to 20–30 storeys planned near the future Mount Pleasant Station at Main Street and Broadway.
The Broadway Plan's renter protections w: The Broadway Plan's renter protections were written with this area's buildings in mind. The plan's tenant relocation requirements apply to the walk-up rental buildings on Kingsway, which makes redeveloping those sites cost more than strata or house sites.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates:: Where the townhouses are: there are few, and many aren't labelled as townhouses. This is a mixed inner-city neighbourhood that's getting denser: heritage and character houses on the side streets (early 1900s to mid-century, many converted or with suites), older walk-up rental apartments along Kingsway, Broadway and the other main streets, and a growing number of newer low-rise and mid-rise strata condos and purpose-built rentals near Main Street and Kingsway.
The Broadway Plan frame: Mount Pleasant: The Broadway Plan: Mount Pleasant is one of the three neighbourhoods in the Broadway Plan, approved by Council on June 22, 2022. It's a 30-year plan (Clark Drive to Vine Street, 1st to 16th Avenues) that ties housing, jobs and amenities to the Broadway Subway, with buildings up to 20–30 storeys planned around Mount Pleasant station and over $1 billion of public benefits committed across Mount Pleasant, Fairview and Kitsilano in the first 10 years (including $96 million for parks and the renewal and expansion of the Mount Pleasant Neighbourhood House). Council approved updates to the Plan on December 12, 2024. Citywide land-use direction now comes from the Vancouver Official Development Plan, which replaced the Vancouver Plan on March 31, 2026.
The board splits the neighbourhood at Ma: The real estate board splits the neighbourhood at Main Street; the City doesn't. "Mount Pleasant VE" and "Mount Pleasant VW" are the board's two areas; the City's Mount Pleasant is one local area.
Land shape: a mixed, densifying inner-ci: The land: a mixed inner-city neighbourhood that's getting denser, with heritage and character houses on the side streets, older walk-up rental apartments along Kingsway, Broadway and the other main streets, and a growing number of newer low-rise and mid-rise strata condos and purpose-built rentals near Main Street and Kingsway. Check the specific address in the school board's locator before relying on a catchment.
Heritage frame: First Shaughnessy was de: Heritage: First Shaughnessy was designated a Heritage Conservation Area on September 29, 2015 (By-law No. 11349). Protected heritage properties (built before 1940) can only be removed from the protected list by Council, after an assessment of their heritage character and value.
Heritage frame: First Shaughnessy is a d: Heritage: First Shaughnessy is a designated Heritage Conservation Area; Council adopted the Heritage Conservation Area Official Development Plan (By-law No. 11349) on September 29, 2015. The City defines First Shaughnessy as bounded by West 16th, Marpole, Wolfe and Richelieu Avenues to the north, Arbutus Street to the west, West King Edward Avenue to the south, and the west lane of Oak Street to the east. Protected heritage properties (built before 1940) can only be removed from the protected list by Council, after an assessment of their heritage character and value.
One apartment-condo address: Shaughnessy: One address with apartment condos: Shaughnessy Place (4900 Cartier Street), a gated 1970s strata community beside VanDusen Garden that also has townhouses. Everything else in the area is estate houses, plus strata townhouses at the edges.
Resale supply in all three is thin — \"S: Few homes come up for resale in any of the three. If you want a Shaughnessy townhouse, set up a search and wait.
Is Whitford a presale or completed stock: Is Whitford a presale or already built?
The townhouse form changes the floor pla: Being a townhouse changes the floor plan, not what you review: there's one Form B package for the whole complex.
What the district actually offers in two: What the area does offer with two homes is a protected heritage house with a conversion into several units, an infill building or a coach house under the Heritage Conservation Area's incentives. That's a different kind of purchase, and you start with the heritage rules.
South Cambie is the City of Vancouver's: South Cambie is the part of Vancouver along Cambie Street between roughly West 16th Avenue and the Fraser River (Marine Drive), including Cambie Village and the north edges of the areas around King Edward and Oakridge–41st stations. "South Cambie" is the real estate board's name for the area. Nearby areas: Oakridge, Riley Park, Shaughnessy, Douglas Park, Marpole and Langara.
Where the condo stock concentrates: at t: Where the condos are: at King Edward station on the Canada Line (OPAL, 528 West King Edward Avenue) and on the rise beside Queen Elizabeth Park at Cambie and West 31st–35th (Parc Elise, Chelsea). The side streets between stations are mainly houses in the R1-1 multiplex zone.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates:: Where the townhouses are: at the stations, not on the side streets, and almost always as part of larger developments.
Side-street house lots: the stock is old: Side-street house lots: older detached houses on the side streets, mostly mid-century and earlier character homes on standard lots, freehold. Townhouses and 4–6 storey strata and rental buildings are on Cambie Street and around King Edward and Oakridge–41st stations under the Cambie Corridor Plan. A fee-simple lot has no strata, no Form B and no strata fees.
ALR vs non-ALR: no ALR parcel in South C: ALR: I don't know of any ALR land in South Cambie. Check a specific property on the Agricultural Land Commission's map.
Both, in different senses: the unit is t: Both, in different senses: the home is laid out like a townhouse (2 storeys plus basement, with parkade access), and the building is a six-storey concrete apartment building. It's a condo. Go by the strata plan, not the listing headline.
The board's \"South Granville\" label re: The real estate board's "South Granville" area reaches Kerrisdale. Listings in the area appear as far south as Adera Street and 6160 Granville Street, well outside South Granville itself, so a search by area mixes in a second market to the south.
Gallery Row is the BIA's own name for th: Gallery Row is the business association's name for the strip. The South Granville Business Improvement Association represents the district from the Granville Bridge to 16th Avenue and names Bau-Xi Gallery and Uno Langmann Gallery on Gallery Row, along with the Meinhardt Fine Foods grocery. These are the shops for the homes on the side streets.
South Granville is the City of Vancouver: South Granville is the part of Vancouver along Granville Street roughly between West 5th and West 16th Avenues, in the Fairview and Shaughnessy local areas. "South Granville" is also the real estate board's name for the area. Nearby areas: Fairview, Shaughnessy, Kitsilano, Arbutus Ridge, Douglas Park, and downtown Vancouver across False Creek. Other names: "South Granville Rise", "Gallery Row" (the stretch of art galleries) and "Fairview Slopes" (the residential slopes east of Granville).
Heritage fabric on the corridor: the cor: Heritage on Granville: the South Granville apartment district has heritage apartment buildings on the City of Vancouver Heritage Register at the Granville Street corners: Douglas Lodge (1507–1509 West 12th Avenue, also listed as 2799 Granville Street) and Crescent Court (1504–1512 West 14th Avenue, also listed as 3003–3007 Granville Street). Canterbury (1390 West 14th Avenue), a block east of Granville, is also on the register. Check register status for any property facing Granville.
Renter-protection frame for rental-land: Renter protections, if you're buying a rental building: purpose-built rental buildings here come under the Broadway Plan's renter protections, including tenant relocation. Check the current tenancies and the plan's protections before buying a rental building as an investment.
Because they are purpose-built rentals h: Because they're purpose-built rentals owned as whole buildings: The Leeward is a 48-suite rental tower (1968) and Santa Monica a 13-suite rental building (1929), and the district from West 11th to 16th and Fir to Birch is an intact pre-war rental apartment neighbourhood. A building being on the Heritage Register (Douglas Lodge, Crescent Court, Canterbury) doesn't mean it's a strata.
Where the condo stock concentrates: at t: Where the condos are: only at the area's eastern edge, at Granville Street and SW Marine Drive, where low-rise strata buildings are on the conventional streets at the edge of Kerrisdale and Marpole. In Southlands itself there are almost no strata homes, rental apartments or townhouses, because the RA-1 zone allows one home per lot, with only limited exceptions for infill.
The semi-rural character is locked in by: The semi-rural character is protected by bylaw. Southlands' RA-1 zone dates from 1955 and its area plan from 1988. That's also why nothing for downsizers will be built in Southlands under the current rules.
The sub-area's attached stock is confine: The area's townhouses and condos are only on the conventional streets at its Kerrisdale and Marpole edges.
The townhouse zero here is written into: There are no townhouses because of a 1955 zone. Southlands' RA-1 zone has allowed one home per lot since 1955, and its area plan dates from 1988. The area's protected character is on the record, and it's why there are no townhouse complexes.
The one counted building cannot agree on: Sources disagree on when the one building was built. For a 1980s building, the strata plan and depreciation report settle its age, not a listing.
There are no SnapStats numbers for Vanco: I don't have market figures for S.W. Marine: the monthly market report I use doesn't cover Vancouver.
Conventional streets at the Kerrisdale/M: Conventional streets at the Kerrisdale and Marpole edges: more conventional detached homes on the streets climbing toward Kerrisdale, which is also where the area's few attached and rental homes are. Almost everything in the City of Vancouver part is freehold.
Musqueam reserve lands — not City land,: Musqueam reserve lands: Musqueam Indian Reserve 2 is beside the area along the Fraser. Land in the reserve is under federal and First Nation jurisdiction, not the City of Vancouver's, and homes there are leasehold.
S.W. Marine is the Greater Vancouver REA: S.W. Marine is the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® area name for the south-west corner of the City of Vancouver along Southwest Marine Drive and the north arm of the Fraser River. It takes in Southlands and the streets between roughly Granville Street and the Musqueam lands and Camosun Street.
A zoning district from 1955 is what keep: A 1955 zone is what keeps these lots big: RA-1 was created in 1955 specifically for Southlands, and the Southlands Plan dates from 1988. The area's protected character is on the record, and it also limits what a buyer can do with a lot.
The flood rules have a Southlands-only c: The flood rules have a section just for Southlands: Section 6.0 of the City's Flood Plain Standards and Requirements covers the RA-1 zone. So the rules for riverfront lots here are more specific than the citywide floodplain rule, and you can check a lot's designation on the City's floodplain map.
Two places called Southlands, two munici: Two places called Southlands, in two municipalities: a search for "Southlands" also brings up Delta's Southlands master plan (Boundary Beach). It's a different city, with different rules and different homes, and has nothing to do with values in S.W. Marine.
Inside Southlands itself there is no con: There are no condos in Southlands itself.
Why is there no condo or townhouse stock: Why are there no condos or townhouses to downsize into in Southlands?
Is flooding a real diligence item on the: Is flooding something to check on the riverfront streets?
Two jurisdictions share this one board s: Two jurisdictions share this one real estate board area: (1) the University Endowment Lands (UEL), an unincorporated community between the City of Vancouver and UBC on the Point Grey Peninsula, administered directly by the Province under the University Endowment Land Act, with no elected municipal council, in Metro Vancouver Electoral Area A; and (2) UBC's own residential neighbourhoods on campus land. Day-to-day UEL services are delivered by the UEL Administration under the UEL Official Community Plan and the Land Use, Building and Community Administration Bylaw.
Head-lease diligence — unique to this ar: The head lease, which is unique to this area: on every purchase in a UBC neighbourhood, order and read the head lease for the property. Look for the start date, whether it's prepaid, the remaining term, UBC's rights under the lease, and any faculty or staff resale restrictions on the specific home. The remaining term runs from the project's original lease date, not your purchase date, and it's the term a lender lends against.
Property tax — provincial rural regime,: Property tax is provincial rural tax, not city tax: taxes here are paid to the Province's Surveyor of Taxes and are due July 2, with a 5% penalty on anything unpaid after July 2 and another 5% on anything still unpaid after October 31. Water isn't on the tax bill; it's billed separately.
If a presale is offered here, REDMA s. 2: If a presale is offered here, you have seven days to cancel a contract with the developer, and deposits are held in trust.
Even the rental residence's operator nam: Sources don't agree on who operates the rental residence. BC's Assisted Living Registry names Seasons Retirement Communities (Wesbrook Village) GP Inc. as the legal operator of the residence at 3338 Wesbrook Mall, while Chartwell publishes a full page for the same address.
Where townhouse-form stock concentrates:: Where the townhouses are: in the leasehold neighbourhoods. They're in Hampton Place (1990s, UBC's first campus neighbourhood) and Wesbrook Village (the largest and newest), and Hawthorn Place also has townhouses as well as condos. The freehold UEL streets have detached houses only.
UEL property taxes (the rural regime — n: UEL property taxes (rural tax, not City of Vancouver tax): UEL properties don't pay City of Vancouver property tax. Because the UEL is taxed as a rural area, annual property taxes are paid to the Province's Surveyor of Taxes and are due July 2. A 5% penalty is added to anything unpaid after July 2, and another 5% to anything still unpaid after October 31. Rural tax notices are mailed by May 31, and payment must be received by the due date to be on time.
The postal address is the trap. Every ho: Don't go by the postal address. Every home in this area has a "Vancouver, BC" mailing address, but none of the UEL or UBC land is in the City of Vancouver, so city taxes (including the Empty Homes Tax), city bylaws and city permits don't apply. Find out which jurisdiction a home is in before you look at price.
What the leasehold stock is: Named Wesbr: The leasehold homes: named Wesbrook Village buildings include Eton by Polygon and Wesbrook Properties' rental buildings (Georgia Point, Vista Point, Granite Terrace, Mews). These are built homes, not lots.
Municipality: none — the key identity fa: Municipality: none, and that's the main thing to know. The UEL is an unincorporated community between the City of Vancouver and UBC on the Point Grey Peninsula. It's the only part of BC where the provincial government provides local services directly to an urban area. It has no elected municipal council, and the Minister of Municipal Affairs governs it under the University Endowment Land Act. UBC's campus lands are governed by the university. "University VW" is the real estate board's name for the area (VW means Vancouver West).
Governing frame — UEL (provincial), not: Who governs the UEL: the Province, not a city. The UEL is governed under the University Endowment Land Act by the Minister of Municipal Affairs and administered by the UEL Administration under the UEL Official Community Plan and the Land Use, Building and Community Administration Bylaw. There's no municipal council, city zoning bylaw or city subdivision bylaw for UEL land.
UEL property taxes — the rural regime, s: UEL property taxes (rural tax): UEL properties don't pay City of Vancouver property tax. Because the UEL is taxed as a rural area, annual property taxes are paid to the Province's Surveyor of Taxes and are due July 2. A 5% penalty is added to anything unpaid after July 2, and another 5% to anything still unpaid after October 31. Rural tax notices are mailed by May 31, and payment must be received by the due date to be on time. UEL water is billed separately from the tax notice.
The tax bill comes from the Province, on: The tax bill comes from the Province, on the rural schedule. Don't budget on Vancouver's dates: taxes go to the Surveyor of Taxes and are due July 2, with a 5% penalty after July 2 and another 5% after October 31. Notices are mailed by May 31, and water is billed separately.
\"Vancouver, BC\" on the envelope proves: "Vancouver, BC" on the envelope proves nothing: the UEL Administration's own sheet for realtors stresses that the UEL isn't part of the City of Vancouver or UBC and has different bylaws. For every address here, first find out the jurisdiction (UEL, UBC lands or, east of Blanca, the City itself), because permits, bylaws and tax bills differ in each.
On the documented case (Sandringham), a: In the one case I've looked at (Sandringham), it's a townhouse-style home in a leasehold strata complex. The wording is a listing description, not a legal form of ownership. Review the Form B and the head lease; there's no party wall agreement.
254 of the 3,595 Vancouver condo sales c: 254 of the 3,595 Vancouver condos that sold had "Penthouse" entered as the style, most of them in Kitsilano (28). The listing agent enters that, so some top-floor homes aren't marked and a marked one isn't always on the very top floor.
Victoria-Fraserview has more ground-orie: Victoria-Fraserview has more houses, duplexes and townhouses than the city average; apartments were about 25% of homes, all under five storeys (2016 census).
It reported about 44,500 residents in 20: It had about 44,500 residents in 2011, with 81% of households renting and about one-third of the city's purpose-built rental homes.
Where condo stock would concentrate in W: West Vancouver's condos are on the Ambleside waterfront, in the Ambleside town centre and at the edge of Dundarave village, all outside Altamont.
What replaces the Form B diligence for a: What do I review instead of a Form B when buying an Altamont house?
West Vancouver Schools (SD45) directs fa: West Vancouver Schools (SD45) directs families to the school locator on its admissions page. Catchments go by address, and I haven't confirmed a catchment for Altamont, so check the exact address in the locator. SD45 has no middle schools: elementary is K–7 and secondary is 8–12.
The streets that frame the area are Mari: The main streets are Marine Drive along the waterfront below, Queens Avenue climbing the hillside, and the avenues above them, below the edge of the British Properties. Nearby areas are Dundarave (east), Caulfeild (west), the British Properties (north, uphill), Ambleside (south-east) and Chelsea Park (north-west, uphill).
Schools: School District 45 (West Vancou: Schools: School District 45 (West Vancouver Schools) catchments go by address, and I haven't confirmed a catchment for Altamont; SD45 directs families to the school locator on its admissions page. SD45 has no middle schools: elementary is K–7 and secondary is 8–12. Nearby schools are Irwin Park Elementary (K–7), 2455 Haywood Avenue in Dundarave, and Westcot Elementary (K–7) at the foot of the British Properties.
The demand side is documented by the Dis: The District's own figures show the demand: seniors went from about one in five West Vancouver residents in 2001 to nearly one in three in 2021, and the median age reached 51 in 2021, a decade older than the regional median. The Official Community Plan still describes the District as mostly detached, single-family housing with few other kinds of homes.
Condo stock actually concentrates in two: The condos are in two strips: the waterfront avenues (Bellevue Avenue and the Marine Drive and Esquimalt Avenue blocks at the east end of the town centre) and the numbered-street blocks just north of Marine Drive between 13th and 18th Streets. Every building I know of here is in one of those. Apartments and mixed-use buildings are in the town-centre blocks under the Official Community Plan and the Ambleside Centre Local Area Plan, while houses north of Marine Drive are in the RS single-family zones.
The seawalk predates most of the condo s: The seawalk is older than most of the condos. The Centennial Seawalk was built in 1967 for Canada's centennial and runs about 1.7 km from Ambleside Park west to Dundarave Park. The waterfront buildings (1964–1977) were built along a shoreline that was already public.
Where the attached stock actually sits:: Where the attached homes are: low-rise and mid-rise strata apartment buildings in the town-centre blocks and along Marine Drive and Bellevue Avenue, with detached houses in the RS zones on the streets north of Marine Drive. There's no group of townhouses.
The Centennial Seawalk predates most of: The Centennial Seawalk is older than most of the buildings: built in 1967 for Canada's centennial, it runs about 1.7 km from Dundarave Park east to Ambleside, and links the apartment buildings along the water into one neighbourhood.
Where the condo stock concentrates: it d: Where the condos are: there are none.
The OCP was amended for housing needs in: The Official Community Plan was amended for housing needs in 2025. Council adopted Amendment Bylaw No. 5406, 2025, bringing the Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 4985, 2018) into line with the Interim Housing Needs Report. Any future multi-unit proposal on this slope would be judged against it.
The T2 assembly records West Vancouver's: The townhouses I know of in West Vancouver are in Whitby Estates and Caulfeild, plus a few within two projects in Dundarave and the British Properties and Uplands. I don't know of any in Ambleside, Altamont, Chartwell outside Whitby Estates, Chelsea Park or Bayridge. If you're told a townhouse is "in Bayridge", it's in another area.
Villa Maris (Dundarave) is purpose-built: Villa Maris (Dundarave) is a purpose-built rental; nothing in it is for sale.
Fee-simple houses (the actual Bayridge s: Fee-simple houses (what Bayridge has): secondary suites must be registered with the District.
No named presale project in Bayridge was: I don't know of any presale project in Bayridge.
The school programme is real, the neighb: The school program is official; the neighbourhood name isn't. West Bay Elementary's IB Primary Years Programme is a School District 45 program at a school in the area, while "Bayridge" doesn't appear in any District plan. You can verify a listing's claim about the program, but not a claim that Bayridge is an official neighbourhood.
The District-wide housing alignment touc: The District aligned its Official Community Plan with housing needs in 2025: Amendment Bylaw No. 5406, 2025 brought the plan into line with the Interim Housing Needs Report. That's the current plan for every Bayridge lot, though there's no local area plan for Bayridge.
No official District neighbourhood or pl: I haven't found "Bayridge" as an official District neighbourhood or planning area name. It's a local name for the West Bay and Westmount slope in the District of West Vancouver, which is covered by the District-wide Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 4985, 2018).
Where the condo stock actually concentra: Where the condos are: there are almost none. They're in two places: one older low-rise on Berkley Road in the middle of the area (Berkley Terraces), and one brand-new master-planned community at the south edge, on Lytton Street at Mount Seymour Parkway. Everything else is detached houses.
One new community is filed under two dif: One new community is listed in two different neighbourhoods. Baden Park's Lytton Street homes appear on MLS® in both Blueridge and Windsor Park. A search, alert or set of comparable sales using only one name misses half the community.
The 2005 slide still shapes diligence on: The 2005 landslide still matters on the west side of the area. The Berkley Escarpment landslide of January 19, 2005 is why the District manages landslide risk actively and updated its Landslide Risk Assessment in 2026. For Berkley Road addresses, check the District's hazard maps, which you wouldn't need to do for most North Shore condos.
One new community is filed under two dif: One new community is listed in two different neighbourhoods (checked Nov 1, 2026). Baden Park's Lytton Street homes appear on MLS® in both Blueridge and Windsor Park: recent listings for its Cove townhouses use Windsor Park, while a Seymour townhouse listing at 954 Lytton Street uses Blueridge. A search, alert or set of comparable sales using only one name misses part of the community.
The 2005 slide still shapes diligence on: The 2005 landslide still matters on the west side of the area. The Berkley Escarpment landslide of January 19, 2005 is why the District manages landslide risk actively and updated its Landslide Risk Assessment in 2026. For Berkley Road addresses, check the District's hazard maps, which you wouldn't need to do in most North Shore neighbourhoods.
Baden Park (Lytton Street at Mount Seymo: Baden Park (Lytton Street at Mount Seymour Parkway) isn't included here.
No other named bare-land development, as: I don't know of any other bare-land development, land assembly, development site or rezoning proposal in Blueridge. The plan points the other way: the Seymour Local Plan manages slow, limited growth to protect the area's forested character and keeps established neighbourhoods such as Blueridge mainly single-family.
No named presale lot project in Blueridg: I don't know of any presale lots in Blueridge.
Only a 55-or-older bylaw is valid under: Only a 55+ bylaw is legal, and the directory doesn't give the age or the terms of the bylaw.
Where the condo stock concentrates: nowh: Where the condos are: there are none on Grand Boulevard. The street is known for its wide, park-like boulevard with detached houses facing it, under City rules on the City side and District rules on the District side. Listings describe Grand Boulevard as mainly detached homes on larger lots, unlike Central Lonsdale's condos and townhouses.
Heritage frame: Grand Boulevard is a Cit: Heritage: Grand Boulevard is a City heritage character area and part of the system of boulevards and parks known as North Vancouver's Green Necklace, which also includes Victoria Park, Ottawa Gardens and Mahon Park. The Canadian Register of Historic Places describes a central garden boulevard 105 metres wide and 1.6 kilometres long, planned from 1906 by the North Vancouver Land and Improvement Company, with wide lots facing it.
Where the housing stock is: predominantl: Where the homes are: mostly freehold detached houses facing Grand Boulevard and on the side streets. There's no group of townhouses. Grand Boulevard Park is the central park, Grand Boulevard is a City heritage character area, and the boulevard is part of the system of boulevards and parks known as North Vancouver's Green Necklace, which also includes Victoria Park, Ottawa Gardens and Mahon Park.
Rental-restriction bylaws are void / age: Rental and age bylaws: since November 24, 2022, strata rental bans have been void in BC (short-term rentals can still be restricted by bylaw), and only 55+ age bylaws are legal (with exemptions expanded May 1, 2023).
Fee-simple houses (the corridor's actual: Fee-simple houses (what Grand Boulevard has): on the City side, Grand Boulevard is also a heritage character area, so rules about frontage and character, not just zoning, affect what can be built facing the boulevard.
1555 Grand Boulevard — a single detached: 1555 Grand Boulevard: a single detached house with a strata plan (VAP1904), according to a building directory
No major project specific to the Bouleva: I don't know of any major project on Grand Boulevard
Heritage / covenant diligence (City side: Heritage and covenants (City side): Grand Boulevard is a City heritage character area in the Green Necklace. A rebuild facing the boulevard is expected to fit that character, which a side-street lot isn't. Check the title and the City's heritage record for the specific lot before you price a teardown.
No known condo or townhome stock exists: I don't know of any condos or townhomes on Grand Boulevard. The homes are detached houses facing the boulevard and its park, on both the City and District sides.
Nearest new affordable rental, outside t: Nearest new affordable rental, outside the area: Hollyburn Delbrook, 600 West Queens Road. A BC Government release (March 1, 2024) said construction was under way on 86 affordable rental homes at the former Delbrook Lands: a four-storey wood-frame building with 47 one-bedroom, 27 two-bedroom and 12 three-bedroom homes, owned and operated by Hollyburn Community Housing Society and funded through BC Housing's Community Housing Fund, for independent seniors, individuals and families with low to moderate incomes. It's affordable rental for a mix of people, including independent seniors, not a seniors' building.
Braemar is a North Vancouver pocket file: Buyers tend to think of Braemar as part of Delbrook. The District plans it within the North Lonsdale–Delbrook area with Delbrook, Norwood/Queens, Upper Delbrook and Carisbrooke, and the area's only 55+ building, Queensbrook, is in Delbrook on West Queens Road. A search for 55+ homes in Braemar alone finds nothing; the one building is a few streets over.
French Immersion is the pocket's real am: French Immersion is the area's main draw, and that cuts both ways for seniors. École Braemar's English, Early and Late French Immersion programs bring family buyers to these streets, which supports the resale value of a detached house. It also means the area stays family housing, with nothing built for seniors.
Where the District's condo stock concent: The District's condos are in Lynn Valley Town Centre, Lions Gate Village and Edgemont Village, all outside Braemar.
R1/R2 lot fabric (Zoning Bylaw 3210, Sec: Lot sizes in the R1 and R2 zones (Zoning Bylaw 3210): the R1 Rural and Suburban Detached Residential Zone has minimums of 4,000 m², 30 m width and 34 m depth. The R2 Urban Detached Residential Zone has minimums of 660 m², 18 m width and 34 m depth, with variations of 335 m² and 10 m (R2(S1)), 1,100 m² and 24 m (R2(S2)) and 4,000 m² and 30 m (R2(S3)). So minimum lot sizes range from 335 to 4,000 m²; confirm a lot's zone on the District's GeoWeb map. A fee-simple lot has no strata, no Form B and no strata fees.
The hazard frame that does apply is the: The hazard rules that apply here are the District's Development Permit Areas, not ALR rules.
Delbrook Lands — 600 West Queens Road, s: Delbrook Lands, 600 West Queens Road, south-west of the area (not in Braemar): the District divided the former Delbrook school and centre lands into a new neighbourhood park on the north part and, on the south part, a four-storey building with rental housing for low to moderate incomes and a seniors' care facility (approved in 2019). It's a District project at the edge of the area, with rental housing and a park, not lots for sale. It's mentioned because it changes the look of the streets closest to Braemar.
The area is detached houses on R1/R2 lot: The area is detached houses on R1 and R2 lots. If a search shows a "townhouse" in Braemar, check whether it's really a suite or coach house on a detached-house lot, or a home in a neighbouring centre.
Where the condo stock actually concentra: Where the condos are: only at the top of the area, on the Rodgers Creek and Uplands lands on and around Uplands Way and Cypress Bowl Road, under site-specific Comprehensive Development (CD3) zoning, plus two small groups of townhouses in Whitby Estates in Chartwell. The original subdivision below is detached houses in the RS zones. The Official Community Plan directs growth to the town and village centres, not into the British Properties.
A buyer who means \"a townhouse in the o: If you want a townhouse in the original British Properties subdivision, you won't find one.
Hawksley townhomes — 3963 Uplands Way (U: Hawksley townhouses, 3963 Uplands Way (Uplands / Rodgers Creek). Strata townhouses that are part of a larger project with condos
The Whitby Estates townhouses are estate: The Whitby Estates townhouses are very large, not entry-level (checked Nov 1, 2026). Highgrove's 18 terrace homes are roughly 3,282–3,569 sq ft, built in concrete with private garages and private elevators, and were finished in December 2013. They're strata homes the size of detached houses, so their fees and reserve fund look more like a small luxury building's than a row of townhouses'.
Hazard frame: creeks cross this hillside: Hazards: creeks cross this hillside and forest borders it. An Environmental Development Permit is required for work within 15 metres of the top of any watercourse bank, and a Wildfire Hazard Development Permit for work within the Wildfire Hazard Development Permit Area (within 100 metres of undisturbed forest).
Hazard Development Permits (District fra: Hazard development permits (District rules): an Environmental Development Permit for work within 15 metres of the top of any watercourse bank, and a Wildfire Hazard Development Permit for work within 100 metres of undisturbed forest. Check both early on every hillside lot.
The growth is all above the subdivision,: The growth is all above the subdivision, on purpose: the Official Community Plan directs growth to Ambleside, Park Royal, Dundarave, Caulfeild and Horseshoe Bay, and treats the British Properties as an "established existing neighbourhood", while Rodgers Creek Areas 5–6 above are capped at 974 homes under CD3 zoning. Both the scarcity of lots in the original subdivision and the new homes in the Uplands come from the plan.
Park Royal's tenure split is at the area: Part of Park Royal, at the foot of the area, is leasehold: it's on Capilano Indian Reserve No. 5 under the 1974 Park Royal Lease, separate from District of West Vancouver land. Don't assume fee-simple ownership if you look east across Taylor Way.
One building: Hawksley, 3963 Uplands Way: One building: Hawksley, 3963 Uplands Way, a new freehold strata condo building by British Pacific Properties with Beedie Living. It's on the Uplands and Rodgers Creek lands above the original subdivision (listings give the subdivision as Cypress Park Estates). I don't know of any condos in the original subdivision itself.
Yes, in two pockets only: Whitby Estates: Yes, in two places only: Whitby Estates in Chartwell (Aerie II at Garden Court, 8 homes built in 2010; Highgrove, 18 townhouses finished in December 2013) and the base of Hawksley in the Uplands (7 townhouses). I don't know of any townhouses in the original subdivision itself.

The corridor stock is detached houses un: The homes are detached houses in the District's R1 and R2 zones, on streets beside the canyon off Capilano Road and on the higher streets toward Montroyal Boulevard.

Caulfeild Cove predates the heritage-era: Caulfeild Cove is a 1970s complex in a much older neighbourhood. Fee-simple homes (the surrounding stock): Fee-simple homes (the homes around it): Caulfeild is in the District of West Vancouver, and the District's bylaws apply.

Three permit areas stack at the west end: Three permit areas overlap at the west end of the District: the foreshore at the water, wildfire near the forest toward Lighthouse Park, and watercourse setbacks inland. Caulfeild is the one area where all three of the District's permit areas can apply to ordinary house lots.
Where the condo stock concentrates: nowh: Where the condos are: there are none. The homes are detached houses on RS-zone lots on Burley Drive, Kings Avenue and Mathers Avenue. It's a small, purely residential area with its own elementary school and two District parks, at the District's east edge.

Hazard diligence: check the Environmenta: Hazards: on east-edge lots near the Capilano River, check the Environmental Development Permit Area (watercourses and streamside land) and the Wildfire Hazard Development Permit Area before you price a build or a lot split.

Outside the neighbourhood. The aggregato: Outside the neighbourhood. The City states these are City lands pla: The City says these are City lands planned for housing in high-rises and ground-level homes, with Lonsdale Square and a seniors' residence already built on part of them and more land to be made available by the City. On and one block off Lonsdale Avenue bet: On and one block off Lonsdale Avenue between 13th and 23rd Streets. The nine buildings I know of range from Georgian Manor (1971) and The Grande (1999) through Anderson Walk (2012) and Centreview (2017) to the 2025–2026 Polygon and Millennium buildings (Lennox, Elle, Millennium Central Lonsdale). Different strata, different diligence, d: It's a different strata, with different documents to review and different comparable sales.
Fee-simple homes (the stock that does ex: Fee-simple homes (what Chelsea Park has): Chelsea Park is in the District of West Vancouver, so the District's bylaws apply and the Vancouver Empty Homes Tax doesn't.
Chairlift Park is a park, not housing: t: Chairlift Park is a park, not housing: the "Park" in the area's name is a District park on the Chelsea Close streets, zoned RS7 and dedicated as park. It isn't a housing complex and there are no lots in it.
Ground-oriented density / SSMUH, as the: How many homes per lot, under the zoning bylaw: a maximum of 4 homes per lot, or 6 if any part of the site is within 400 metres of a designated bus stop. Check the current zoning for a property before marketing it for a multiplex.
The bylaw's ground-oriented rules allow: The zoning bylaw allows 4 homes per lot, or 6 within 400 metres of a designated bus stop. But the area is in the RS single-family zones, the zone for a specific lot must be confirmed on the District Zoning Map, and I don't know of any strata project here.
District sources call the existing resid: District sources call the existing residential area Cypress Park, Rodgers Creek and the Uplands, and call the planned future neighbourhoods Cypress Village and Cypress West. It's also a different place from Cypress Provincial Park and Cypress Mountain Resort, which are up the same road (Cypress Bowl Road) and aren't residential.
Where the condo stock actually concentra: Where the condos are: in one building, Hawksley, on Uplands Way in Rodgers Creek (CD3 zoning). Everything else in the area is detached houses on RS2, RS3 and RS5 streets, semi-detached strata homes, or the future Cypress Village land west of Cypress Bowl Road, where nothing is built yet.
Where the stock sits: detached houses on: Where the homes are: detached houses on RS2, RS3 and RS5 streets, semi-detached strata homes on Chippendale Road, and one new project with condos and townhouses, Hawksley, on Uplands Way in Rodgers Creek (CD3 zoning). Nothing is built yet on the future Cypress Village land west of Cypress Bowl Road.
Condo stock actually concentrates on the: The condos are on the village's two main streets: Gallant Avenue, the main street (with the shops and two of the three apartment addresses), and Panorama Drive, the waterfront loop around Panorama Park. The surrounding streets are detached houses in the District's R1 and R2 zones.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates:: Where the townhouses are: in one small spot at most, the corner of Caledonia Avenue and Panorama Drive above the village, where the Cove Gardens townhouse listing is. Everything else in the village is detached houses and three small apartment buildings.
The Livable Deep Cove project (lower Gal: The Livable Deep Cove project (a pedestrian area on lower Gallant Avenue) is work on the village centre under the Official Community Plan, not a housing project. In the District's September 2022 engagement, 818 online surveys were completed and 82% of respondents strongly or somewhat strongly supported change on lower Gallant. It creates no lots for sale.
Only a 55-or-older bylaw is valid under: Only a 55+ bylaw is legal, and the directory doesn't give the age or the terms of the bylaw. Exemptions cover existing residents, live-in caregivers and, since May 1, 2023, younger spouses or partners and some children.
That is the complex's core diligence ite: That's the main thing to check for the complex: get the title and, if it's a strata, the Form B and strata plan before you price it. Don't rely on a line in a directory.
District zoning (Bylaw 3210, s. 525): R1: District zoning (Bylaw 3210): the R1 minimum lot is 4,000 m², 30 m wide and 34 m deep; the R2 minimum lot is 660 m², 18 m wide and 34 m deep, with variations of 335 m² (R2(S1)), 1,100 m² (R2(S2)) and 4,000 m² (R2(S3)). Since June 2024, a main house plus a secondary suite plus a coach house (3 homes) is allowed on single-family lots inside the Urban Containment Boundary, and small-scale multi-unit housing allows up to 6 homes on lots over 280 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop.
It is documented in the District's own r: It's in the District's own records, not just listings: a March 24, 2004 council report names Queensbrook as the one project built on the three sites the 1995 North Lonsdale–Delbrook plan designated for 55+ housing. As with any strata, the registered bylaws and Form B apply to a specific purchase.
Since June 2024 the District permits a p: Since June 2024, the District has allowed a main house plus a secondary suite plus a coach house (3 homes) on single-family lots inside the Urban Containment Boundary, and up to 6 homes on lots over 280 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop. The base zoning is R1 (minimum 4,000 m²) or R2 (minimum 660 m²) under Bylaw 3210.
Where the condo stock actually concentra: Where the condos are: in two small places only. Queensbrook is on West Queens Road at the south-west edge of the area near Westview, and Delbrook Plaza is on Delbrook Avenue itself, at the Evergreen Place end.
The District report states the site is b: A District report says the site is being redeveloped with a new neighbourhood park on the north part and, on the south part, a four-storey building with rental housing for low to moderate incomes and a seniors' care facility, at the corner of West Queens Road and Stanley Avenue, with Mission Creek to the west. It's a District rental, care and park project on District land: no lots are offered for sale.
Hazards — landslide diligence: the Distr: Landslide hazards: the District's landslide work is based on its Landslide Risk Assessment, commissioned after the Berkley landslide of January 19, 2005 in the District's east end. Check slope lots anywhere in the District, including Delbrook's upper streets, against the District's hazard reports; don't assume they're clear.
It is marketed as a 55+ community and th: It's marketed as a 55+ community, and a building directory shows age restrictions, pets allowed and rentals allowed. A 55+ bylaw is the only legal age bylaw, and the exemptions cover existing residents, live-in caregivers and, since May 1, 2023, younger spouses or partners and some children. So a younger spouse isn't automatically excluded, but the registered bylaw's wording decides, and you should read it with the Form B before writing an offer.
No — the area's only 55+ ownership compl: No. The area's only 55+ complex you can buy into is Queensbrook, an apartment strata. A 55+ bylaw is the only legal age bylaw, and you should still read Queensbrook's registered bylaw with the Form B before writing an offer.
A 4-storey waterfront complex by Polygon: A 4-storey waterfront complex by Polygon, designed by Keith Hemphill of Rositch Hemphill Architects, finished in 2017. Current listings describe freehold strata, wood frame, and amenities including a fitness room, guest suite, bike room, kayak storage, dog wash, meeting rooms and an on-site building manager. A building directory says pets are allowed with restrictions.
The sub-area's only strata complex is fi: The area's only strata complex is listed in a different area (checked Nov 1, 2026).
Hazard Development Permits (District fra: Hazard development permits, which matter in Dollarton: the Official Community Plan's permit areas cover protection of the natural environment, streamside land, wildfire, creeks and slopes. On the shoreline: the port authority reports that erosion at Cates Park is getting worse as sea level rises, the District models flood levels to the year 2100 plus 0.6 m, and main buildings on waterfront lots must be set back 7.6 m from the natural boundary of the ocean. On a waterfront lot, get the flood construction level from GeoWeb and an insurance quote before you remove subjects.
Connaught, the Grosvenor project at the: Connaught, the Grosvenor project at Edgemont Boulevard and Ridgewood Drive, is 82 concrete condos and townhouses over ground-floor shops including Thrifty Foods. Construction started in 2016 and finished in 2019. It's open to all ages; the developer states no age restriction.
Mount Currie is the main community of th: Mount Currie is the main community of the Líl̓wat Nation, on federal reserve land. There's no open-market housing here: no condos, no strata and no fee-simple sales. Housing is allocated by the Nation to its citizens. The off-reserve land around it (Squamish-Lillooet Regional District Electoral Area C) is described here only for context.
Where condo stock concentrates: nowhere: Where the condos are: there are none. The community's housing is single detached family homes in the village neighbourhoods, including newer subdivision homes and modular or manufactured homes, allocated by the Nation.
Surrounding-area frame — SLRD Electoral: The surrounding area (for context only; it doesn't govern reserve land): off reserve, the Pemberton Valley around Mount Currie is Squamish-Lillooet Regional District Electoral Area C, a separate jurisdiction with its own bylaws. The Village of Pemberton is the neighbouring municipality, with regular municipal taxes, zoning and MLS® sales.
GST and buyer programs — off-reserve ins: GST and buyer programs: programs such as the Home Buyers' Plan ($60,000), the First Home Savings Account ($40,000 lifetime, $8,000 a year) and CMHC mortgage insurance (premiums of 0.60%–4.50%) apply to off-reserve purchases. None of them is a way into Mount Currie housing: there are no developer sales, presales or MLS® purchases here. Financing for citizens goes through the Band Council Resolution and Ministerial Loan Guarantee process described above.
Land use: there is no municipal zoning b: Land use: there's no municipal zoning bylaw for the reserve lands. Land is allocated through the Nation's Lands Department and Band Council. The surrounding off-reserve valley is Squamish-Lillooet Regional District Electoral Area C, and the Village of Pemberton's rules apply to Pemberton land only; neither applies to the reserve lands.
Property taxes / levies: For that reason: Property taxes: I don't give a property transfer tax calculation, tax due date or penalty schedule for Mount Currie itself. The standard BC figures below are for comparison with off-reserve land only.
Different municipality, manufactured-hom: It's in a different municipality, it's a manufactured home, and it's on a rented pad: three reasons it isn't Mount Currie land. A manufactured home on a rented pad isn't land ownership in any case.
Subdivision — the provincial subdivision: Subdivision: the provincial subdivision rules and other municipalities' bylaws don't apply on reserve land.
Because the Band Council acts as guarant: Because the Band Council acts as guarantor and a Ministerial Loan Guarantee backs the loan, mortgages and foreclosure don't work the way they do off reserve. The lender's security runs through the Nation's process, not against fee-simple title, and the court foreclosure process used off reserve doesn't apply here.
GST on vacant land — CRA GI-003 level on: GST on vacant land (off reserve): sales by developers or businesses and newly subdivided lots are generally taxable; land an individual held for personal use is generally exempt.
Where the 55+ housing actually concentra: Where the 55+ housing is: in one block only, the 100 block of West Queens Road and West 29th Street at Chesterfield Avenue, at Queensdale. All of the area's 55+ and seniors' housing that I know of (Somerset Green, Vista 29, Chartwell Churchill House) is in that block, which the District's planning records designated for seniors' housing. The rest of Upper Lonsdale is mostly single detached houses climbing the slope, with no other 55+ complex that I know of.
The seawalk is the flat route between th: The seawalk is the flat route between the two villages. The Centennial Seawalk runs about 1.7 km east from Dundarave Park to Ambleside. It's the level, paved waterfront path that links Dundarave on foot to Ambleside's shops, library and seniors' centre, which is why buyers value the Bellevue Avenue buildings for walkability and not just for the village shops.

ALR block (applies only where a parcel i: ALR: I don't know of any ALR land in Dundarave. Recreation and hazards frame: Murdo Fraz: Recreation and hazards: Murdo Frazer Park is the District park in the Edgemont area (6 tennis courts and 6 pickleball courts in the District's Outdoor Sports Courts Optimization Strategy, approved July 21, 2025), and the Delbrook Community Recreation Centre, 851 West Queens Road, is the nearest full-service recreation centre. The Grosvenor Edgemont project redeveloped the main grocery site at Edgemont and Ridgewood with a larger grocery store (Thrifty Foods), ground-floor shops and 82 condos and townhouses. The ordinary form: Edgemont's stock is p: The usual home: Edgemont is mostly single detached homes on sloped lots, many with views, on the plateau between the Mackay Creek and Mosquito Creek ravines. District plans and zoning — District of: District of North Vancouver plans and zoning: the Official Community Plan is Bylaw 7900. The apartment buildings in the sales sto: The apartment buildings you may hear about don't exist yet. The covenant room is far larger than the: The covenants allow far more than has been built. The built strata stock is Oliver's Landi: The strata homes that are built are Oliver's Landing (56 townhouses) and Ocean's Crest (12 single-family strata homes). Apartment buildings exist only in a rezoning proposal for the unbuilt Lot 2 waterfront lands.
A 27-storey concrete freehold-strata tow: A 27-storey concrete freehold strata tower by Intergulf Development Group at Hunter Street and Mountain Highway. Lynnmour sits on the flat-to-gently-slop: Lynnmour is on flat to gently sloping land between Lynn Creek (west) and the Seymour River (east), from the mountain slopes down to Highway 1 and the Second Narrows crossing at its south end. Nearby areas: Maplewood (east, across the Seymour River), Lynn Valley (north), Lower Lynn and Lynn Creek Town Centre (south-west), and the City of North Vancouver (west, across Lynn Creek).
The recreation centre is brand new and w: The recreation centre is brand new and was built by a developer. The neighbourhood's main indoor facility is newer than most of its condos.
Do not confuse this complex with Lynmour: Don't confuse this complex with Lynmour Village Apartments, 1923 Purcell Way, a separate purpose-built rental building beside Capilano University (described below).

Norgate is a planned post-war subdivisio: Norgate is a planned post-war subdivision ("Norgate Park", from the late 1940s and 1950s) of small detached ranchers and bungalows on flat lots and crescents, many since renovated, extended or replaced.
