The two can be streets apart, so confirm ownership on the individual title; don't assume it from the area name.
No. There is no strata lot and no Form B: No. A leasehold interest has no strata lot and no Form B. You review the head lease itself, and lenders look at leasehold on reserve land case by case, so tell your mortgage broker about it when you make an offer.
Where condo stock concentrates: the Mari: Where the condos are: along Marine Drive (The Drive, 1330 Marine Drive) and in the Lions Gate Village towers (Park West, at Capilano Road and Lions Gate Lane).
Hazard diligence: creek, slope, wildfire: Hazards: Development Permit Areas for creeks, slopes, wildfire and streamside land can add geotechnical costs to an addition, a rebuild or a lot split. The District's GeoWeb flood construction levels are modelled to the year 2100 plus 0.6 m. Get the GeoWeb report for the property before you price any lot beside the river or a ravine.
Three counted strata complexes, all in L: Three strata complexes, all in Lions Gate Village at the south-west edge of the area: Belle Isle by Citimark (2060 Curling Road, 88 townhouses in 11 three-storey buildings, built in 2022), Mason by Cressey (2070 Curling Road, 40 townhouses in six three-storey buildings, built in 2021) and Ebb & Flow (2035 Glenaire Drive, built in 2023, strata plan EPS7673, according to listings). Pemberton Heights itself has no townhouse complexes; it's detached houses.
That is the District's documented permis: That's what the District allows: since June 2024, a main home, a secondary suite and a coach house (three homes in total) have been allowed on single-family lots within the Urban Containment Boundary, with the suite up to 49% of the house. Confirm the specific lot on GeoWeb.
Where condo stock concentrates: in one b: Where the condos are: in one block only, the 100 block of West Queens Road and West 29th Street at Chesterfield Avenue, at Queensdale, plus the older low-rise buildings on West Kings Road. The rest of the area is mostly single detached houses climbing the slope.
Where townhouse stock concentrates: ther: Where the townhouses are: in effect, one block.
Upper Lonsdale is the GVR board sub-area: Upper Lonsdale is the real estate board area running up Lonsdale Avenue from about 24th or 25th Street to Rockland Avenue, where Lonsdale ends. The first blocks (roughly 25th to 29th Street) are in the City of North Vancouver, and the blocks from 29th Street to Rockland are in the District of North Vancouver. TransLink's North Shore Area Transit Plan supports that split: it puts the Lonsdale Avenue bus layover at 29th Street in the City and the Upper Lonsdale layovers at Osborne Avenue and at Prospect and Rockland in the District. Confirm a specific address on the municipal maps.
The usual duplex form: Predominantly sin: The usual home: mostly single detached houses climbing the Lonsdale slope (post-war houses, renovations and rebuilds designed for views, with lot values rising with elevation and view). Most are freehold. There are strata homes near the shops, and a few older low-rise apartments and condos near Queensdale and on the lower (City) blocks.
West Vancouver had 351 detached sales be: West Vancouver had 351 detached houses sell between November 1, 2025 and October 31, 2026, and 128 of them (36%) had "golf course" ticked on MLS®. Those 128 sold for a median of $3,062,500, 8% above the $2,845,000 median for all 351.
The balance of the sub-area is freehold: The rest of the area is freehold detached estate homes on large lots; attached homes are the minority.
The townhouses are estate-scale, not ent: The townhouses are very large, not entry-level. Highgrove's 18 terrace homes are roughly 3,282–3,569 sq ft, built in concrete with private garages and private elevators, and were finished in December 2013. They're strata homes the size of detached houses, so their fees and reserve fund look more like a small luxury building's than a row of townhouses'.
No. Detached estates dominate, but the s: No. Most homes are detached estates, but the area also has the Garden Court strata homes (Aerie II, 8 homes, 2010) and the 18 Highgrove townhouses (finished in 2013). Neither is duplexes.
Strata plan NWS518 (recorded on a unit's: Strata plan NWS518 (from the property record for a home at 8720 No. 1 Road). A low-rise wood-frame complex of several buildings at No. 1 Road and Francis Road, across from Seafair Shopping Centre. Current listings describe freehold strata, wood frame, and amenities including a clubhouse, indoor and outdoor pools, hot tub, sauna, exercise centre, guest suite and library, with heat, hot water and city utilities included in strata fees at some addresses.
Where the condo stock concentrates: exac: Where the condos are: in one place, the south side of Francis Road at No. 1 Road, where the Apple Greene low-rise complex (8720–8880 No. 1 Road) is across from Seafair Shopping Centre and a short walk south of the park.
The amenity set is a 1970s resort packag: The amenities are a 1970s resort-style package, and they still drive the fees. With indoor and outdoor pools, a hot tub, sauna, gym, clubhouse, guest suite and library in a low-rise wood-frame complex, the depreciation report (now required every five years) covers pools and building systems that newer low-rises don't have.
Depreciation reports / CRF minimum: sinc: Depreciation reports and the reserve fund: since July 1, 2024, stratas with five or more lots must get a depreciation report every five years, and can't vote to defer it. Apple Greene (strata plan NWS518, several buildings from 1973–1975) is well over that size. Since November 1, 2023, at least 10% of the annual operating budget must go to the contingency reserve fund. In a complex this old, the depreciation report and the record of major repairs are the main things to review.
One complex, six addresses, two build ye: One complex, six addresses, two build years. Apple Greene homes are at 8720, 8740, 8760, 8840, 8860 and 8880 No. 1 Road, with buildings from 1973 and 1975. Search all six addresses, and check the year for the specific building.
Apple Greene's levy history is the real: At Apple Greene, look at the history of special levies. In a 1973–1975 complex of this size, the record of major repairs matters more than any restriction. What listings say about it should be confirmed against the strata documents.
Flood / dike diligence — Bylaw 8204: flo: Flooding and dikes: flood construction levels and dike setbacks under the Flood Plain Designation and Protection Bylaw 8204 apply to new construction. The area is in the Fraser River floodplain, behind dikes designed for a 1-in-500-year flood, which are being raised. Find out what applies to the specific property before you price a rebuild.
One complex, six addresses, two build ye: One complex, six addresses, two build years: Apple Greene homes are at 8720, 8740, 8760, 8840, 8860 and 8880 No. 1 Road, with buildings from 1973 and 1975. Search all six addresses, and check the year for the specific building.
Any page or listing that states a Boyd P: I haven't confirmed a school catchment for Boyd Park, so check the exact address in the school locator.
One complex: Apple Greene (8720–8880 No. 1 Road, strata plan NWS518), a low-rise wood-frame complex at No. 1 Road and Francis Road across from Seafair Shopping Centre. Everything else in the area is detached houses.
A buyer who wants its location and ameni: If you want its location and amenities, you're buying an apartment in a strata, not a townhouse, so review it like an apartment (depreciation report, history of special levies).
Transit anchors: Bridgeport Station is t: Transit: Bridgeport Station is where the Canada Line splits. One branch runs south along No. 3 Road to Richmond–Brighouse, one runs west to the airport on Sea Island, and the line to Vancouver runs north to Waterfront. It's also a regional bus exchange (routes 403, 430 Express, 601, 352 and 604, among others). TransLink's SkyTrain timetable (effective September 7, 2026) gives 26 minutes from Richmond–Brighouse Station to Waterfront Station. River Rock Casino Resort is at the station, on the Great Canadian Way and River Road side.
The station core and the condo strip ans: The station area and the condos come under two different plans. The plan for Bridgeport Village doesn't allow homes where the casino, hotels and warehouses are. The homes the real estate board lists in "Bridgeport RI" are to the west on River Drive, built under the Parc Riviera approvals; council approved a development permit for the first phase in 2012, with Dava Development Ltd. as applicant. A listing that says a River Drive home is "steps to Bridgeport Station" is describing about a kilometre, going by the listings themselves.
The townhouse component of the Parc Rivi: The townhouses in the Parc Riviera riverfront master plan: listings at both addresses describe Parc Riviera Mews townhouses by Dava Developments, built in 2020 (one listing at 10199 River Drive says 2021, so the year varies by home), with strata fees. A building directory lists 90 homes for the building at 10233 River Drive, with pets not allowed and rentals allowed.
Transit: Bridgeport Station is the Canad: Transit: Bridgeport Station is where the Canada Line splits. One branch runs south along No. 3 Road to Richmond–Brighouse, one runs west to the airport on Sea Island, and the line to Vancouver runs north to Waterfront. It's also a regional bus exchange (routes 403, 430 Express, 601, 352 and 604). River Rock Casino Resort is at the station, on the Great Canadian Way and River Road side.
Established-street house lots (Bridgepor: House lots on established streets (along Bridgeport Road): single detached houses in the Single Detached (RS1/F) zone south of the village. These are the homes closest to the village.
Bridgeport Road / Shell Road townhouse r: Townhouse rezoning at Bridgeport Road and Shell Road: a rezoning from Single Detached (RS1/F) to Low Density Townhouses (RTM3) at 10760 and 10780 Bridgeport Road and 3033, 3091 and 3111 Shell Road. It's the residential change under way here.
Transit — the area's defining feature: B: Transit is the area's main feature: Bridgeport Station is where the Canada Line's Richmond–Brighouse branch, airport branch and line to Waterfront all meet, and it's a regional bus exchange (routes 403, 430 Express, 601, 352 and 604). TransLink's timetable (effective September 7, 2026) gives 26 minutes from Richmond–Brighouse Station to Waterfront Station.
Flood Control — Flood Plain Designation: Flooding: new construction must meet the flood construction levels and dike setbacks in the Flood Plain Designation and Protection Bylaw 8204. Bridgeport Village sites are in Flood Construction Level Area A.
The station is a junction, not just a st: The station is a junction, not just a stop: Bridgeport Station is where the Canada Line's Richmond–Brighouse branch, airport branch and line to Vancouver meet, with a regional bus exchange. For homes nearby, that access is the main selling point.
The plan's own words cap the upside stor: The plan itself is frank about the area: the City Centre Area Plan calls Bridgeport an industrial area in transition, with an incomplete street grid and former rail lines. Expect truck traffic and gaps in the streets. The plan also says a Community Centre (North) and library lending services are to be located in Bridgeport, Aberdeen or Capstan Village, or within 400 m of a village centre.
No — the City Centre Area Plan prohibits: No. The City Centre Area Plan doesn't allow residential use in the designations that cover most of Bridgeport Village, so the buildings around the station are industrial, commercial, hotel and entertainment. The apartment condos in this real estate board area are on River Drive to the west: Parc Riviera – Monaco (10177 River Drive, 2018) and Parc Riviera (10033 River Drive, 2014).
Strata, in every known case: all four co: Strata, in every case I know of: all four complexes are strata, with strata fees (Parc Portofino's listing says freehold strata).
King George / Cambie Community Park is t: King George / Cambie Community Park is the main park in the plan. At 4100 No. 5 Road, with heritage trees, courts, playgrounds, tennis and a waterpark, it's what the Area Plan calls the principal community park, to be kept and expanded where it is. The townhouses on Thorpe Road and No. 5 Road are beside it.
Two civic addresses, one complex — count: Two street addresses, one complex. A building directory shows pets allowed with restrictions and rentals allowed with restrictions.

Two street addresses, one complex. Listings at both addresses show Francisco Village townhouses, built in 1993, with strata fees. Confirm the number of homes and the rental and pet rules with the Form B.
Two civic addresses, one gated complex —: Two street addresses, one gated complex. A building directory shows pets allowed with restrictions and rentals allowed with restrictions.
Richmond zoning and plans: Zoning Bylaw: Richmond zoning and plans: Zoning Bylaw 8500 applies. The area's base zone is Single Detached (RS1/RS2), and the RS1/E subzone on Cambie Road sets a minimum lot area of 550 m², minimum width of 18 m and minimum depth of 24 m, with one main home per lot and a secondary suite allowed. Townhouse sites are developed under low-density townhouse zones (such as RTL4), and multiple-family sites are Development Permit Areas under the Area Plan. The East Cambie Area Plan (adopted October 21, 2002) is part of the city-wide 2041 Official Community Plan, Bylaw 9000.
Established-street house lots: single de: House lots on established streets: single detached houses are the usual home here.
Heritage note for lot diligence near the: Heritage near Cambie Road and No. 5 Road: the Area Plan asks the School Board to conserve the Mitchell School buildings as heritage structures, and Mitchell Elementary is the longest continuously operating school in Richmond's public system. That's background for redevelopment nearby, not a rule for lots.
Flood — the Richmond-specific diligence: Flooding, which matters everywhere in Richmond: all land in Richmond is designated floodplain under Flood Plain Designation and Protection Bylaw No. 8204. It sets flood construction levels that habitable floors must meet unless an exemption applies. The city is protected by 49 km of dikes designed for a 1-in-500-year flood, which are being raised to 4.7 m.
North Arm is the GVR board sub-area name: North Arm is the real estate board area named after the North Arm of the Fraser River: the riverfront along the south side of mainland New Westminster, below Marine Way and Stewardson Way, with the Waterfront Esplanade (North Arm) trail along the water.
Where the condo stock concentrates: nowh: Where the condos are: there are none. This is riverfront land that's largely non-residential, not a residential neighbourhood where homes sell.
The same name means three different geog: The name is used for more than one place. As a real estate board area, "North Arm" is the mainland New Westminster riverfront, which had no homes for sale in September 2026. Any "North Arm average price" a search site shows comes from somewhere else.
The river is the amenity and the paperwo: The river is both the attraction and the thing to check. The area's public asset is the Waterfront Esplanade (North Arm), the trail along the water. The same riverfront means floodplain, ownership and insurance checks come first on any river-side purchase.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates:: Where the townhouses are: there are none. This is riverfront land that's largely non-residential, not a residential neighbourhood where homes sell. The zoning for the slope above the river is single detached housing.
The OCP Green Zone includes the Esplanad: The Official Community Plan's Green Zone includes the Esplanade (North Arm) and the Annacis Channel shoreline. That's trail and shoreline, not lots.
Serviced position: New Westminster opera: Services: New Westminster runs its own electrical utility and City water and sewer. Servicing for a specific property is confirmed through the City's subdivision process.
Zoning — Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001: sl: Zoning (Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001): houses on the slope are in the Single Detached Residential Districts (the RS zones). In RS-1, the minimum site is 557.40 sq. m. (6,000 sq. ft.) and the floor space ratio can't be over 0.5.
Foreshore + flood diligence: the City fl: Riverfront and flooding: the City's floodplain study puts west-end Fraser River land in Floodplain Zone 2, and the North Arm is Fraser River riverfront. Before removing subjects, confirm the property's floodplain zone, any foreshore or water lot lease, and insurance. The City publishes flood management information for its low-lying areas.
The zero is the fact: a full month with: A full month with no homes for sale and none sold, of either type, tells you what this market is like. (SnapStats, September 2026)
The usual duplex form: A specific proper: Duplexes: if a property is marketed under the North Arm name, check its address, zone and title first, starting with whether it's on the New Westminster side of the river at all.
The foreshore diligence on any river-sid: On any river-side property: confirm its floodplain zone, any foreshore or water lot lease, and insurance before removing subjects.
Nothing was listed or sold in either pro: Nothing was for sale or sold, of either type, so there's no sales ratio or median for the area. The New Westminster figures (a detached median of $1,365,000 and a combined condo and townhome median of $560,000) describe the neighbouring areas, not North Arm (SnapStats, September 2026)
No. Mercer Village (388 Duncan Street) i: No. Mercer Village (388 Duncan Street) is a Queensborough townhouse community by Plat:form and Domus, with 146 townhouses according to its presale material and move-in-ready freehold strata homes now for sale. It happens to be on the bank of the North Arm of the Fraser River, but it isn't in the North Arm real estate board area.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates:: Where the townhouses are: there are no finished ones in the area. The homes here are detached houses in the Single Detached RS1 and RS2 zones. The one townhouse project, Quilchena West at 3888 Moresby Drive, is a presale. The nearest rapid transit is outside the area: Richmond-Brighouse Station (Canada Line) on No. 3 Road to the east, which the City has identified as a Transit-Oriented Area.
Fee-simple homes (the pocket's actual st: Fee-simple homes (what the area has): a secondary suite is allowed in the RS1 and RS2 zones.
Presales (REDMA) — Quilchena West: a pre: Presale rules, which apply to Quilchena West: a presale buyer must get the developer's disclosure statement and has seven days to cancel, from the later of signing or acknowledging it. Deposits are held in trust.
Lot character from the zone ladder, as s: Lot sizes by zone: the minimum lot sizes for subdivision in the RS1 and RS2 subzones include 360 m² for RS1/B and RS2/B, 550 m² for RS1/E, 828 m² for RS1/F and 2,000 m² for RS1/G. These are zone minimums, not the size of any existing lot. Confirm the subzone for a specific lot with the City.
A listing marketed as a \"Quilchena cond: If a listing is marketed as a "Quilchena condo", check where it actually is. The name is shared with homes in Terra Nova, such as Quilchena Green.
What is verified: the pocket itself is h: What I've confirmed: the area itself is houses; the City Centre to the east (Brighouse, a Transit-Oriented Area around Richmond-Brighouse Station) is Richmond's designated high-density core; and Terra Nova to the north-west has strata homes, including the 55+ Quilchena Green.
Flood position (Richmond): All of Richmo: Flooding in Richmond: all of Richmond is designated floodplain under the Flood Plain Designation and Protection Bylaw 8204, which sets dike setbacks and flood construction levels. On any Richmond duplex, check the flood construction level and insurance first.
What flood diligence applies to a Richmo: What should I check about flooding for a Richmond duplex?
All of Richmond is designated flood plai: All of Richmond is designated floodplain under Bylaw 8204. Early on, get the property's flood construction level, find out whether a dike setback applies, and get insurance terms. The city's dikes are designed for a 1-in-500-year flood.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates:: Where the townhouses are: on the east and south-east edges of the area. Oval Gardens and a nine-home community without a name are on No. 2 Road at the east edge, and Tiffany Estate II is on Tiffany Boulevard and Lynas Lane to the south-east. The interior streets (Riverdale Drive, Larkspur Avenue) are detached houses.
Fee-simple homes (the pocket's main stoc: Fee-simple homes (most of the area, including the Tiffany Estates houses). A co-op home (Granville Gardens) is neither strata nor fee-simple: there's no Form B and no individual title. You review the co-op's own membership, housing charge and occupancy documents.
The newest building at the pocket's corn: The newest building at the corner of the area is a rental, and it isn't seniors' housing. Rio Vista (5491 No. 2 Road, opened March 2026) is sometimes taken for seniors' housing because seniors are among its residents; the City describes its 80 homes as for "single people, families and seniors" at low and moderate rents. It adds rental homes at the corner, not townhouses.
Aircraft-noise diligence: the pocket sit: Aircraft noise: the area is on the Sea Island (airport) side of Richmond. The City's aircraft noise policy is set out in Bulletin DEVAPPS-05 and the Aircraft Noise Sensitive Development Policy Area. Check where a property falls under that policy before you commit.
The pocket's stock is detached houses, p: The homes here are detached houses, plus two townhouse communities on No. 2 Road at the east edge (Oval Gardens, 6511 No. 2 Road, and a nine-home community without a name at 6675 No. 2 Road).
Two townhouse communities, both on No. 2: Two townhouse communities, both on No. 2 Road: Oval Gardens (6511 No. 2 Road; one end unit listed is a 2-storey, 3-bedroom townhouse with a 2-car garage, built in 2015) and the nine-home community at 6675 No. 2 Road (built in 1990, freehold strata according to listings; the home listed there is 1,574 sq. ft. with a two-car garage). Both are townhouses, not apartment condos.
Both, under one enclave name. The 6100 T: Both, under one name. The townhouses at 6100 Tiffany Boulevard (Tiffany Estate II) are strata, while houses on Lynas Lane and the Tiffany streets that use the Tiffany Estates name are fee-simple single-family homes: no strata, no Form B and no strata fees. The title for the specific home tells you which applies.
No SD38 school by that name in Richmond: I don't know of a Richmond school by that name; Riverdale Elementary is in Surrey. Richmond families should check the School District 38 locator for their exact address.
Seafair is the west Richmond planning ar: Seafair is a west Richmond planning area on Lulu Island (planning area 6 in the City's Official Community Plan), and the City's name and the real estate board's name match. Rough boundaries from the City's map: Granville Avenue to the north, Railway Avenue and the No. 2 Road side to the east, Williams Road to the south, and the West Dyke Trail and dike along the Strait of Georgia to the west. Francis Road and No. 1 Road cross the area.
The \"apartments\" on Francis Road are a: The "apartments" on Francis Road are a 1969 rental building. Wall Seafair at 3851 Francis Road (78 units, 3 storeys, built in 1969 according to a rental directory) is run as renovated rental apartments by Wall Financial Corporation. A search for "Seafair apartments" brings up rental marketing, not strata homes.
Edgewater Park has already done one big: Edgewater Park has already had major building envelope work, according to a listing. A current listing reports new siding with a rainscreen, new windows and new patio doors for the complex, at a substantial cost per home that has already been paid. For a 1975 wood-frame complex, that matters a great deal for value, so confirm it in the depreciation report and strata minutes.
Serviced position, as the City states it: Services: Seafair homes are on City water and sewer. Confirm servicing for any vacant or assembled property with the City.
Flood position: Richmond is a low-lying: Flooding: Richmond is a low-lying island city in the Fraser River floodplain, protected by a ring of dikes (49 km of dikes and 39 pump stations across the city) designed for a 1-in-500-year flood. The dikes are being raised from 3.5 metres to 4.7 metres for sea level rise, and the west dike runs beside Seafair. The Flood Plain Designation and Protection Bylaw 8204 sets dike setbacks and flood construction levels, so check both on every Seafair lot.
Seafair is the west Richmond planning ar: Seafair is a west Richmond planning area on Lulu Island (planning area 6 in the City's Official Community Plan), and the City's name and the real estate board's name match. Rough boundaries from the City's map: Granville Avenue to the north, Railway Avenue and the No. 2 Road side to the east, Williams Road to the south, and the West Dyke Trail and dike along the Strait of Georgia to the west. Francis Road and No. 1 Road cross the area.
Flood / dike diligence — Bylaw 8204: Get: Flooding and dikes (Bylaw 8204): get the property's flood construction level and find out about any dike right-of-way before you price a rebuild or a lot split.
The park pocket carries two labels for o: The area around the park has two names: Hugh Boyd Community Park at 9200 No. 1 Road is in Seafair (planning area 6), and homes near it are also sold as "Boyd Park". Search under both names. Either way, the lots are fee-simple, in the RS1 and RS2 zones.
The \"apartments\" on Francis Road are a: The "apartments" on Francis Road are a 1969 rental building: Wall Seafair at 3851 Francis Road (78 units, 3 storeys, built in 1969 according to a rental directory) is run as renovated rental apartments. A search for "Seafair apartments" brings up rental marketing, not homes or land for sale. It's a short walk from the Seafair West strata townhouses on the same street.
The strata plan (NWS438) and the Form B: The strata plan (NWS438) and the Form B settle the number of lots, which decides each owner's share of any special levy. Sources disagree on the number.
Steveston North is the residential distr: Steveston North is the residential area in Richmond's south-west, north of the historic Steveston village and south of Blundell Road. "Steveston North" is a Greater Vancouver REALTORS® area name; the City doesn't use it for planning. The area covers the northern part of the Steveston planning area (Steveston Area Plan, part of Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 9000) and a little of the Seafair planning area to the north.
BC Housing groups Richmond differently f: BC Housing divides Richmond differently from the real estate board. Its directory's "Richmond — West" and "Richmond — South" groups cut across the board's Steveston areas: Ukrainian Village is under "Richmond — West" but is on a Steveston street. So a search for subsidized housing by the board's area name will miss buildings a Steveston North senior can apply for.
The district's newest strata stock is to: The area's newest strata homes are townhouses, and both named complexes show a rental rule that no longer applies. Heron (2022) and Innova30 (2023) show "rentals allowed with restrictions", but restrictions on long-term rentals have been void since November 24, 2022.
A strata complex built 2005, per the bui: A strata complex built in 2005, according to a building directory and current MLS® listings, which show apartment condos, freehold strata, wood frame and 4 storeys for homes at 4280 Moncton Street in Steveston South. A strata directory shows pets allowed with restrictions and rentals allowed. No age restriction is published. Listings market the homes to downsizers, but that isn't a 55+ bylaw.
Steveston South is the south-west corner: Steveston South is the south-west corner of the City of Richmond, on the South Arm of the Fraser River. "Steveston South" is a Greater Vancouver REALTORS® area name; the City doesn't use it for planning. The area is inside the Steveston planning area, under the Steveston Area Plan (part of Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 9000).
Steveston Village is the historic villag: Steveston Village is the historic village centre within the Steveston planning area of the City of Richmond, under the Steveston Area Plan (part of Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 9000). The City designates it as the Steveston Village Heritage Conservation Area. "Steveston Village" is also the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® area name for the village centre.
Where the condo stock concentrates: it d: Where the condos are: there are no apartment condo buildings as such. Homes in the village centre are detached houses on side streets plus low-rise mixed-use strata buildings over the shops on Moncton and Chatham Streets, and the one strata building named after the village is townhouses with a retail unit.
A 30-home freehold strata townhouse comp: A 30-home freehold strata townhouse complex on No. 1 Road: a current listing shows townhouses, freehold strata, strata plan EPP97342, wood frame, with the year built given as 2024 in one place and 2023 in another.
The north/south line runs through the co: The line between north and south runs past the front of the complex. Heron faces Steveston Highway, which listings treat as the line between Steveston North and Steveston South. A search limited to "Steveston South" can miss the area's only townhouse complex here, and the reverse is true too.
The waterfront the condos front was a ca: The waterfront where the condos are was a cannery. Imperial Landing Waterfront Park is on the historic BC Packers cannery site (the development is 6.5 acres of waterfront on that site, according to the City). That history is the setting for the strata homes on Bayview Street, and the Britannia Shipyards National Heritage Site is to the west along the same waterfront route.
Where the housing stock concentrates: de: Where the homes are: detached houses on the village side streets (RS1 and RS2 zones), with the village centre itself mixed-use. The strata homes in the centre are in low-rise mixed-use buildings over the shops on Moncton and Chatham Streets.
The village's strata stock hides inside: The village's strata homes are on its shopping streets. The centre is zoned for low-rise mixed use over the shops on Moncton and Chatham. If you search only residential streets, you'll miss them, and the one named townhouse-style building has a retail unit in the same strata.
ALR vs non-ALR: no ALR parcel in Stevest: ALR: I don't know of any ALR land in Steveston North. Check a specific property on the Agricultural Land Commission's map.
Heron was developer-marketed as a presal: Heron was marketed as a presale before it was finished in spring 2022. It's a finished complex now, not a presale.
Steveston North is the City of Richmond': Steveston North is the City of Richmond's residential area in the city's south-west, north of the historic Steveston village and south of Blundell Road. "Steveston North" is the real estate board's name; the City doesn't use it for planning. The area covers the northern part of the Steveston planning area and a little of the Seafair planning area to the north. Nearby areas: Steveston South and Steveston Village (south), Seafair and Boyd Park in West Richmond (north), and London/Steveston (east).
ALR vs non-ALR: no ALR parcel in Stevest: ALR: I don't know of any ALR land in Steveston South. Check a specific property on the Agricultural Land Commission's map.
Imperial Landing — Bayview Street at the: Imperial Landing, Bayview Street at the south end of No. 1 Road: former cannery land redeveloped as strata homes. It's fully built; there are no bare lots.
Steveston South is the City of Richmond': Steveston South is the City of Richmond's south-west corner, on the South Arm of the Fraser River. "Steveston South" is the real estate board's name; the City doesn't use it for planning. The area is inside the Steveston planning area, under the Steveston Area Plan. Nearby areas: Steveston Village (the historic centre, in the south-west of this area), Steveston North (across Steveston Highway), London/Steveston and South Arm (to the east), and Seafair (to the north-east).
Steveston Village is the historic villag: Steveston Village is the historic village centre inside the wider Steveston planning area in the City of Richmond, BC, under the Steveston Area Plan; the City designates the centre as the Steveston Village Heritage Conservation Area. "Steveston Village" is also the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® area name for the centre.
The dike is being re-thought around the: The dike around the village is being redesigned: the Steveston Island Dike project proposes a dike around Steveston Island from London Farm to Garry Point Park, with a navigation gate for Steveston Harbour. Flood protection here is a current City project, so check its status.
The usual duplex form: The documented ho: Duplexes: homes here are single detached houses in the RS1 and RS2 zones on residential streets, with secondary suites allowed, plus strata homes in the village centre's mixed-use zones. Check a specific pair's title to see whether it's one lot, a strata or a subdivided pair. Minimum lot sizes in the RS1 and RS2 zones vary by subzone: RS1/B 360 m², RS1/E 550 m², RS1/F 828 m² and RS1/K 315 m², with a 24 m minimum depth in most subzones.
The board sub-area name is \"Terra Nova\: The real estate board's name is "Terra Nova". The City plans the same area as part of the Thompson planning area: the plan is listed as Thompson (Terra Nova) in the Richmond Official Community Plan, and the City's Heritage Inventory gives the planning area as Thompson.
Where multi-family stock actually concen: Where the multi-family homes are: along Westminster Highway at the south edge of the area (Mayflower at 3880 Westminster Highway, Sonoma at 3555 Westminster Highway) and on Cornwall Drive inside it (Quilchena Green at 5531 Cornwall Drive). All three complexes are townhouses. The rest of the area is detached houses, with ALR farmland (zoned AG1) to the west and south.
Age bylaws — SPA ss. 123.1 / 123.2: only: Age bylaws: only a 55+ bylaw is legal in BC; a lower age (for example "45+") can't be enforced as an age bylaw. Exemptions cover existing residents, live-in caregivers and, since May 1, 2023, younger spouses or partners and some children.
Quilchena Green is Terra Nova stock, wha: Quilchena Green is in Terra Nova, whatever the name suggests.
Two of the four complexes share one buil: Two of the four complexes have the same builder and the same kind of amenities. Mayflower and Sonoma are both Polygon townhouse communities on Westminster Highway (from 1995–1997) with a clubhouse, outdoor pool, hot tub and gym. If you're choosing between them, you're really comparing floor plans, yards and how well each strata is run, not amenities.
Established house lots: single-detached: House lots: single detached houses in the residential area east of the rural park, alongside the ALR farm properties.
Quilchena Green — 5531 Cornwall Drive: P: Quilchena Green, 5531 Cornwall Drive: built strata homes, not lots. Sources give its age restriction as 45+ or 55+; confirm with the Form B.
Flood / dike diligence — Bylaw 8204: dik: Flooding and dikes (Bylaw 8204): dike setbacks and flood construction levels apply. The area is behind the ring of dikes designed for a 1-in-500-year flood, which are being raised. On purchases at the west and north edges, find out early what applies to the property.
Heritage diligence: the Terra Nova Herit: Heritage: the Terra Nova Heritage Area is on the City's Heritage Inventory. Check heritage status for properties in or beside that area.
Price the corner as it stands today, not: Price the corner as it is today, not as the proposal would make it.
Shopping: Terra Nova Village, 3671 Westm: Shopping: Terra Nova Village, 3671 Westminster Highway, is an open-air centre with Save-On-Foods, according to the centre's owner, First Capital.
Terra Nova's strata stock is three townh: Terra Nova's strata homes are in three townhouse complexes: Quilchena Green (5531 Cornwall Drive, 91 homes, built in 1992), Mayflower (3880 Westminster Highway, Polygon) and Sonoma (3555 Westminster Highway, Polygon, built in 1995).
Four strata complexes: Quilchena Green (: Four strata complexes: Quilchena Green (5531 Cornwall Drive, 91 homes, strata plan LMS423, built in 1992, with an age restriction to confirm), Mayflower (3880 Westminster Highway, Polygon, built in 1996–1997 depending on the home), Sonoma (3555 Westminster Highway, Polygon, built in 1995) and London Mews (6333 No. 1 Road, 66 homes, strata plan LMS2933, built in 1998). I don't know of any fee-simple townhouse complexes or apartment condos in the area.
By Polygon. Built 2019 per current listi: By Polygon. Built in 2019, according to current listings, which show wood frame with a mixed exterior, air conditioning, and the 5,000 sq. ft. Trafalgar Club (lounge, billiards, games area, fitness studio, ping pong, landscaped courtyard, children's play area and guest suite).
Where the condo stock concentrates: one: Where the condos are: in one area, Alexandra (Alexandra Gardens), along Alexandra Road, Odlin Road, Tomicki Avenue and McKim Way, where Polygon and Concord Pacific built a series of low-rise strata buildings between 2011 and 2019 (Mayfair Place, Alexandra Court, Omega, Cambridge Park, Trafalgar Square). Outside that area, West Cambie is houses.
District energy — the Alexandra pocket's: District energy, an extra utility in Alexandra: the City's Alexandra District Energy Utility serves apartment buildings on Alexandra Road, Odlin Road and Tomicki Avenue, and their listings describe geothermal heating and cooling. If you buy a strata home in Alexandra, expect a district energy bill as part of your monthly costs, charged separately from the strata fee.
A Cambie Road apartment application is i: An apartment application on Cambie Road has been made but not approved. Application RZ 23-015980 at 9720 Cambie Road proposes an apartment building on a site zoned Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing (RSM/XL) in the Alexandra neighbourhood. It's a rezoning application only.
West Cambie's own counted townhouse stoc: West Cambie's townhouses are all in Alexandra, on Alexandra Road.
The official record is a City of Richmon: A City of Richmond Planning Committee report (May 20, 2014) records that Polygon Jayden Mews Homes Ltd. rezoned the assembled site (application RZ 13-649641) to a site-specific townhouse zone, ZT71, to build about 64 three-storey townhouses. A current listing for a home in the complex shows a 3-storey townhouse built in 2015, with a clubhouse, management, grounds maintenance and snow removal. It's a managed strata complex.
Listing records give a 3-storey townhous: Listings show 3-storey townhouses built in 2018, in a strata.
A listing record gives Sub-Type Townhous: A listing shows a 3-storey townhouse, freehold strata, with a maintenance fee and a clubhouse. Listings at the address give both 2016 and 2017 as the year built.
How old is the condo stock, and who buil: How old are the condos, and who built them?
What flood and noise matters are documen: What should I know about flooding and noise in West Cambie?
Brighouse is the City of Richmond's down: Brighouse is the City of Richmond's downtown (the City's planning name for it is Brighouse Village). Quilchena Green is in Terra Nova, not Brighouse.
The condos home counts 6 apartment condo: There are 6 apartment condo buildings covered here, and I don't know of any 55+ stratas. They're built strata homes, not lots for sale.
How old is the townhouse stock here, and: How old are the townhouses here, and what should I check?
Ascott Wynde was built in 1977 — the dep: Ascott Wynde was built in 1977. In a complex that old, the depreciation report (required every five years for stratas with 5 or more lots), the contingency reserve fund balance and the minutes matter more than the finishes. The same goes for the oldest condos in the downtown, Regency Park Towers (1971–1974).
60 of the 1,218 Richmond condo sales car: 60 of the 1,218 Richmond condos that sold had "Penthouse" entered as the style, most of them in Brighouse (15). The listing agent enters that, so some top-floor homes aren't marked and a marked one isn't always on the very top floor.
Where the housing stock concentrates: si: Where the homes are: single detached houses in the RS1 and RS2 zones around South Arm Community Park and the schools beside it. Homes here are freehold detached houses, not condos.
The park cluster is the district's docum: The park and the facilities around it are the centre of the area. South Arm Community Park has 57.3 acres and 10 sports fields, with the community centre, an outdoor pool and two schools beside it, all according to the City. The playground was officially opened in July 2023 with funding support from the South Arm Community Association.
The newest townhome complex is filed und: The newest townhouse complex is listed under a different neighbourhood name. Kingz Court listings at 8233 Williams Road show Saunders, with South Arm named only as a nearby neighbourhood. A search limited to "South Arm" misses the area's newest attached homes.
A brand-new townhouse complex on the Wil: A brand-new townhouse complex on Williams Road by South Arm Community Park. It's a strata, according to MLS®. A building directory lists Kingz Court at 8233 Williams Road as built in 2026 with 22 homes, and shows completed sales there in October 2026, so it's finished, not a presale. Confirm the strata plan number with the Form B.
The counted complex wears two sub-area n: The complex is listed under two area names. If you're adding up Richmond townhouses from a Saunders list and a South Arm list, check the address so you don't count it twice.
The park cluster was reinvested in recen: The park and schools have had recent investment. Richmond City Council officially opened the rebuilt South Arm Community Park playground in July 2023, with funding support from the South Arm Community Association, and James Whiteside Elementary's full seismic upgrade (3,107 m², occupied in fall 2023) was a Province project. Both back up the area's reputation as a place for families.
Leasehold ground, stated as a tenure rec: Leasehold land (a note on ownership; it isn't land for sale)
Where the housing is: single-detached ho: Where the homes are: single detached houses in the RS1 and RS2 zones around South Arm Community Park and the schools beside it. Homes here are freehold detached houses.
City plans and zoning: Richmond Zoning B: City plans and zoning: Richmond Zoning Bylaw 8500 applies, and the Official Community Plan is Bylaw 9000. I don't know of a separate South Arm area plan, so the city-wide plan applies.
The park cluster was reinvested in recen: The park and schools have had recent investment: Richmond City Council officially opened the rebuilt South Arm Community Park playground in July 2023, with funding support from the South Arm Community Association, and James Whiteside Elementary's full seismic upgrade (3,107 m², occupied in fall 2023) was a Province project. Both back up the area's reputation as a place for families, for the lots around the park.
The usual duplex form: The documented ba: Duplexes: homes here are single detached houses in the RS1 and RS2 zones around the park and schools, with secondary suites allowed. They're freehold. Minimum lot areas by subzone include RS1/B 360 m², RS1/E 550 m², RS1/F 828 m² and RS1/K 315 m², with a 24 m minimum depth in most subzones.
Both are documented in as townhomes, not: Both are townhouses, not apartment condos.
Yes — one, documented: Kingz Court (8233: Yes, one: Kingz Court (8233 Williams Road), a 22-home strata complex. Listings describe its homes as two-storey, half-duplex-style homes with strata fees.
Transit-Oriented Development Areas: prov: Transit-Oriented Development Areas: the Province's Transit Oriented Development Areas, introduced in 2024, allow more density within 800 metres of the City's five SkyTrain stations, including 22nd Street, and the City is amending its Official Community Plan to extend them. A February 17, 2026 City report covers extending the "Residential – Limited Mid Rise" designation to properties at the outer edges of the provincial areas. That's what will eventually bring condos here. For now, it affects land values; nothing has been built.
Zoning Bylaw No. 6680's townhouse distri: The townhouse districts in Zoning Bylaw No. 6680 are RT-2 through RT-2C and RT-3, RT-3A and RT-3B. The RT-2 Townhouse Districts allow row houses and townhouses.
Nearby areas: the West End and Moody Par: Nearby areas: the West End and Moody Park to the east, Burnaby across the city's west boundary, and Queensborough across the Queensborough Bridge to the south-east. On MLS®, North Arm is a separate New Westminster area from Connaught Heights.
Depreciation reports / CRF (provincial s: Depreciation reports and reserve funds (the provincial rules, if you're also looking at stratas): since July 1, 2024, stratas with five or more lots must get a depreciation report every five years, and can't vote to defer it. Since November 1, 2023, at least 10% of the annual operating budget must go to the contingency reserve fund.
Density bragging rights belong to other: New Westminster's density is in other neighbourhoods: the 2021 Census counted 78,916 people in the city, at 5,052 people per square kilometre, but that density is in Downtown, the Quay and Uptown. Connaught Heights is detached houses beside an Expo Line station.
Flood position: the City's floodplain st: Flooding: the City's floodplain study covers only the city's low-lying edges: Zone 1 Queensborough, Zone 2 the industrial land on the Fraser River at the west end, Zone 3 the Quay waterfront and Zone 4 the Brunette River industrial area. I don't know of a floodplain zone for Connaught Heights' residential streets.
The city's condo stock is in Downtown, U: The city's condos are in Downtown, Uptown and the Quay, east of the neighbourhood. The median price for condos and townhomes across New Westminster was $560,000 in September 2026 (SnapStats).
RT-A (s.405) and RT-B (s.406) are the ne: RT-A and RT-B are the newer townhouse districts in Zoning Bylaw No. 6680. A site needs at least 836.1 m² (9,000 sq. ft.), at least 20 m of frontage and lane access. The older townhouse districts are RT-2 to RT-2C, and RT-3, RT-3A and RT-3B in Queensborough.
A completed wood-frame mid-rise by Areva: A finished wood-frame mid-rise by Areva Living at First Street and Royal Avenue: 189 homes in an eight-storey development with both condos and townhouse-style homes, designed around the restored 1890 E.M.N. Woods House on the site. Current listings say cats are allowed.
A rezoning-stage proposal for six to eig: A proposal at the rezoning stage for six to eight towers and about 2,400 homes (including purpose-built and affordable rental as well as strata condos) on the existing shopping centre site. It's a proposal only; nothing is built.
Where the condo stock concentrates: two: Where the condos are: in two groups. One is the Plaza 88 and Carnarvon Street towers around New Westminster Station (Azure 1, Azure 2, Marinus, Ovation, 618 Carnarvon). The other is the older buildings on Columbia, Carnarvon and Agnes Streets west and east of the stations (Westminster Towers, Carnarvon Place, Carnarvon Towers, C2C Lofts, News North, Argyle House, First & Royal).
The newest Downtown building carries an: The newest building downtown has an 1890 house in its plaza. First & Royal's developer restored the E.M.N. Woods House (built in 1890, designed by Samuel Maclure), moved it 65 feet south on the same street, and made it the centre of the project's plaza. It's a heritage house inside a brand-new wood-frame strata.
Downtown has two stations and a provinci: Downtown has two stations, and the Province allows extra density around them. New Westminster and Columbia stations are both downtown, and the Province's Transit Oriented Development Areas allow more density within 800 metres of the stations. That's behind both the 811 Carnarvon proposal and the Columbia Square redevelopment application. Neither is built.
Strata vs freehold: A buyer \"buying lan: Strata or freehold: "buying land" downtown really means buying a strata unit, or taking a comprehensive development site through the City's process. There are no vacant fee-simple lots to buy.
Serviced position: New Westminster opera: Services: New Westminster runs its own electrical utility and City water and sewer. Servicing for a specific property is confirmed through the City's subdivision and development process.
A rezoning-stage proposal for six to eig: A proposal at the rezoning stage for six to eight towers and about 2,400 homes (including purpose-built and affordable rental as well as strata condos) on the existing shopping centre site. It's a proposal only; there are no strata homes or lots here yet.
Flood diligence — Floodplain Zone 3: con: Flooding (Floodplain Zone 3): before removing subjects, confirm that the specific building or property meets the flood construction level, and check the insurance and its deductible. The City publishes flood management information for its low-lying areas, including the downtown waterfront.
A developer-era project profile (Onni, p: A profile of the project from when it was being sold (Onni, in the Vancouver Sun, November 2, 2013) describes The Lookout at Victoria Hill as 115 homes in two four-storey wood-frame buildings at 22 East Royal Avenue, New Westminster, with a sales centre at 295 Francis Way. The Francis Way address was the sales centre, not the building.
\"Fraserview\" is the GVR sub-area name: "Fraserview" is a Greater Vancouver REALTORS® area name. The City doesn't have a separate Historic Neighbourhood Context Statement for it, and plans it under the mainland parts of the Official Community Plan.
New Westminster's townhouse program adde: New Westminster's townhouse program added two districts to Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001: RT-A and RT-B. A townhouse site in either needs at least 836.1 m² (9,000 sq. ft.), at least 20 m of frontage and lane access (the City's Townhouses How-to Guide, February 2026, notes that this usually means combining two standard lots). The older townhouse districts are RT-2, RT-2A, RT-2B and RT-2C on the mainland, and RT-3, RT-3A and RT-3B in Queensborough.
North Arm is a New Westminster board sub: North Arm is a New Westminster real estate board area, not a Richmond one. The esplanade below this slope is in New Westminster, and comparable sales from Richmond's North Arm will misprice a Fraserview home.
Slope-street house lots (RS districts, Z: House lots on the slope (RS districts, Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001): houses are in the Single Detached Residential Districts. RS-1 sets a minimum site area of 557.40 m² (6,000 sq. ft.) and a floor space ratio of 0.5. The RS districts allow secondary suites, and laneway and carriage houses are regulated under the same bylaw. The RS-1 minimum is the smallest lot a subdivision can create, not the size of any existing lot.
Zoning: Zoning Bylaw No. 6680 (2001). Th: Zoning: Zoning Bylaw No. 6680 (2001). The RS districts cover detached lots (RS-1: minimum site area 557.40 m², or 6,000 sq. ft.). Townhouse sites in the newer RT-A and RT-B districts need at least 836.1 m² (9,000 sq. ft.), at least 20 m of frontage and lane access.
Floodplain diligence: the City states th: Floodplain: the City says both Queensborough and parts of the mainland are in the provincial floodplain, and that five of the city's twelve square kilometres are inside the flood boundaries on the Ministry of Environment's Floodplain Map. Zone 2 in the City's floodplain study covers the historically commercial and industrial land on the Fraser River at the west end of the city.
The building is published as a 55+ build: The building is published as 55+ (55 Blackberry Drive, built in 1994). A 55+ bylaw is the only legal age bylaw in BC, and its exemptions cover existing residents, live-in caregivers and, since May 1, 2023, younger spouses or partners and some children of a 55+ resident. Read the Form B and the registered bylaw to see whether you qualify before writing an offer.
No. Some listings carry Sub-Type Townhou: No. Some listings call it a townhouse and others an apartment. The building is a 4-storey elevator building with underground parking, so it's an apartment strata with townhouse-style homes at ground level. Review it as an apartment building (elevator, parkade, building envelope), whatever the listing says.
No named bare-land development, assembly: I don't know of any bare-land development, land assembly, development site or rezoning proposal in Glenbrooke North.
No named presale project in Glenbrooke N: I don't know of any presale project in Glenbrooke North.
Ravine / streamside diligence: Glenbrook: Ravine: Glenbrook Ravine is a watercourse in the City's Green Zone.
The stock is single-detached houses on q: The homes are single detached houses on quiet residential streets, and the City's historical work on Glenbrooke North and Queen's Park records some of the oldest houses in the city here. Older homes are the norm here.
Glenbrook Ravine is a watercourse corrid: Glenbrook Ravine is a watercourse in the City's Green Zone, so lots beside the ravine can have streamside setbacks that reduce how much you can build on. Confirm the setback for a specific lot with the City.
The area is documented in the City's His: The area is covered in the City's Historic Neighbourhood Context Statements. That's a historical record, not Heritage Conservation Area protection, and on its own it doesn't restrict a renovation.
Ravine-edge lots are the due-diligence i: Check lots beside the ravine carefully: Glenbrook Ravine is a watercourse, streamside setbacks differ by lot, and the City doesn't publish a setback for individual lots. Get the lot's setback and slope conditions from the City before you price an addition or a rebuild.
No known one — no named bare-land subdiv: None that I know of: no named bare-land subdivision, bare-land strata or presale lots. The homes are established RS-zoned house lots and built strata buildings.
Park-street house lots: single-detached: House lots near the park: single detached houses in the Single Detached Residential Districts (RS) of Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001, on the residential streets around the park, with apartment buildings on the 6th Street and 8th Avenue edges in multiple-unit residential districts.
Flood position: the City's floodplain st: Flooding: the City's floodplain study covers only the city's low-lying edges: Zone 1 Queensborough, Zone 2 the industrial land on the Fraser River at the west end, Zone 3 the Quay waterfront and Zone 4 the Brunette River industrial area. I don't know of a floodplain zone for the higher ground at Moody Park.
The stock is freehold houses on the resi: The homes are freehold houses on the residential streets around the park, with strata apartment buildings on the 6th Street, 6th Avenue and 8th Avenue edges. The blocks facing the park are houses; the blocks on the main streets are apartments.
One edge building is confirmed on its pr: One building at the edge is confirmed by its property manager: The Diplomat, 707 Eighth Street, strata plan NW920, managed by Quay Pacific Property Management, on the Eighth Street edge of the park.
Check the flood layer anyway: the City's: Check for flood risk anyway: the City's floodplain study names zones only at the city's low-lying edges, but it's a city-wide study and doesn't clear any individual Moody Park lot. Confirm with the City.
RS-1 sets a minimum site area of 557.40: RS-1 sets a minimum site area of 557.40 m² (6,000 sq. ft.) with a maximum floor space ratio of 0.5. A subdivision application is measured against that and goes through the City's Approving Officer.
No floodplain zone for the plateau was c: I don't know of a floodplain zone for this higher ground in the City's floodplain study. Its zones are Queensborough, the west-end industrial land, the Quay (Zone 3) and the Brunette River industrial area.
Not without clearing two City steps firs: Not without two City steps first: for any building more than 50 years old, the City reviews heritage value before it accepts a demolition permit application, and a tree permit application must go in with every demolition application. Older homes here are recorded in the neighbourhood's Historic Neighbourhood Context Statement, so start a teardown plan with the City's heritage and tree staff, not with a builder's quote.
Serviced position: the waterfront is ful: Services: the waterfront is all strata buildings, served by City water and sewer and the City's own electrical utility.
Flood position — the defining fact: the: Flooding is the main thing to check: the City's floodplain study puts the Quay in Floodplain Zone 3, the Fraser River waterfront zone. Many newer buildings there have their floor space above the Flood Construction Level, but their exits and the waterfront path are below it. Check this on every Quay purchase.
Non-market co-operative land tenure — ex: Co-ops aren't covered here: Westminster Landing (13 K de K Court, 84 units) and Riverbend (1050 Quayside Drive, 72 units) are co-operative, non-market complexes in the City's non-market housing inventory, with homes for seniors, singles, people with disabilities and families. They're membership housing, not strata lots or land you can buy.
The Quay is the City of New Westminster': The Quay is the City of New Westminster's downtown waterfront neighbourhood along Quayside Drive on the Fraser River. "Quay" is the real estate board's name; the City calls the same waterfront "Quayside" in its Historic Neighbourhood Context Statements.
Floodplain Zone 3 is the defining dilige: Floodplain Zone 3 is the main thing to check at the Quay: the City's floodplain study puts the Quay in Floodplain Zone 3, the Fraser River waterfront zone, where many newer buildings have their floor space above the Flood Construction Level but their exits and the waterfront path are below it. The City publishes flood management information for its low-lying areas, including the Quay. Before removing subjects, confirm that the specific building meets the flood construction level, and check the strata's insurance and deductible.
The apostrophe is a filing system. \"Que: Watch the apostrophe. The real estate board writes "Queens Park" and the City writes "Queen's Park". City documents, permits and the Heritage Conservation Area use the City's spelling, and listings use the board's, so search both.
Three \"Queens\" buildings belong to oth: Three buildings with "Queens" in the name are in other areas. Queen's Park Estate is a Queensborough townhouse project (240 Jardine Street), and Queens Terrace and Amara Terrace are Uptown buildings on Queens Avenue. None of them is in Queens Park.
Care anchor at the east edge: Queen's Pa: Care home at the east edge: Queen's Park Care Centre, 315 McBride Boulevard (148 publicly subsidized long-term care beds, rehabilitation and adult day programs). It's a care facility, not housing.
The care centre is at the edge, not in t: The care centre is at the edge of the area: Queen's Park Care Centre (315 McBride Boulevard, 148 publicly subsidized long-term care beds) is on McBride. It comes up in searches for seniors' housing under this name, but nothing there can be bought.
No named bare-land development, assembly: I don't know of any bare-land development, land assembly, development site or rezoning proposal in Queens Park.
No named presale project in Queens Park: I don't know of any presale project in Queens Park.
Island house lots and the s.190.36 rule:: House lots on the island, and the sewer rule: under the Zoning Bylaw, no subdivision in Queensborough (Lulu Island, District Lots 757 and 758) can create a lot smaller than half an acre (0.20 ha) or with less than 66 feet (20.12 m) of frontage unless the land can connect to the City's sanitary sewer.
Compact-lot form under the current plan: Compact lots under the current plan: the Residential – Low Rise designation in the Official Community Plan amendment (Bylaw No. 8574, 2026) allows single detached houses on compact lots, low-rise buildings up to six storeys, and stacked and side-by-side townhouses, under the Queensborough Community Plan and the Queensborough Eastern Neighbourhood Node Master Plan. A designation is what the plan allows; it isn't a subdivision approval, and no lots are being offered.
Serviced position: New Westminster opera: Services: New Westminster runs its own electrical utility and City water and sewer, and Queensborough's drainage is pumped as part of the diking and drainage system it shares with Richmond. Whether a property can connect to the sewer (the rule above) decides whether it can be subdivided.
Queensborough is the City of New Westmin: Queensborough is the City of New Westminster's island neighbourhood on the eastern tip of Lulu Island, bordered by the main arm of the Fraser River to the south and east and the North Arm to the north. It shares Lulu Island with the City of Richmond. "Queensborough" is the real estate board's name too, and the City plans the area through the Queensborough Community Plan, part of the Official Community Plan.
Only through two gates: Zoning Bylaw s.1: Only if it passes two tests. The Zoning Bylaw doesn't allow a new lot smaller than half an acre (0.20 ha) or with less than 66 feet (20.12 m) of frontage unless the land can connect to the City's sanitary sewer. And the subdivision itself needs approval under Subdivision and Development Control Bylaw No. 7142, 2007 (approval by the Approving Officer, full works and services, the Zoning Bylaw's minimums, and consistency with the Official Community Plan). Whether the specific lot can connect to the sewer decides it.
The new East Columbia supply is rental,: The new homes on East Columbia are rentals, by design. Premiere (72 homes, 408 East Columbia Street) is purpose-built rental, and East Columbia + Strand (209 East Columbia Street) adds 99 market rental homes beside Royal Columbian Hospital and the Brewery District, with occupancy expected in early 2027. New homes are coming to this street, but none of them can be bought.
The Brunette River/Creek corridor and Br: The Brunette River and Brunette Avenue run north across the city boundary into Coquitlam (the Maillardville side, at the Brunette Interchange on Highway 1). North of the boundary is Coquitlam and School District 43, not New Westminster and School District 40, and the one "Brunette" townhouse complex a name search brings up (Brunette Villas) is on the Coquitlam side. New Westminster's townhouse districts are RT-2 through RT-2C, plus RT-3, RT-3A and RT-3B in Queensborough.
Presales (REDMA), if any are ever market: Presale rules, if a presale is ever marketed here: a disclosure statement, seven days to cancel, and deposits held in trust.
Established house lots: single-detached: Established house lots: single detached homes in the Single Detached Residential Districts (RS) of Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001. In RS-1, the minimum site is 557.40 sq. m. (6,000 sq. ft.) and the floor space ratio can't be over 0.5. These are zoning figures, not the size of any existing lot.
No named presale project in Brunette was: I don't know of any presale project in Brunette.
Flood diligence — Floodplain Zone 4 (Bru: Flooding (Floodplain Zone 4, the main thing to check in Brunette): the City's floodplain study puts the industrial land along the Brunette River in Floodplain Zone 4, below the Flood Construction Level, with the river running through it. Zone 4 is Brunette only; Queensborough is Zone 1, the Quay and Downtown are Zone 3, and North Arm is Zone 2.
The two named East Columbia projects che: The two East Columbia projects I checked are rentals, not condos: Premiere (408 East Columbia Street) is a purpose-built rental complex of 72 homes, and East Columbia + Strand (209 East Columbia Street, Sapperton) offers 99 market rental homes with occupancy expected in early 2027. Neither is strata.
Connaught Heights is the City of New Wes: Connaught Heights is the City of New Westminster's west-end mainland neighbourhood, around 22nd Street Station, London Street and Marine Way. The City's name and the real estate board's name match, and the City covers Connaught Heights in its Historic Neighbourhood Context Statements.
Connaught Heights houses also sit in a d: Connaught Heights houses are also part of the City's heritage record: the neighbourhood is in Volume 3 of the City's Heritage Resource Inventory (Sapperton, Victory Heights, Queensborough, Connaught Heights, West End, Kelvin and Glenbrooke).
Yes, under the same bylaw that zones the: Yes, under the same bylaw that zones the lot. The downtown stock is towers and low-ris: Downtown's condos are towers and low-rise stratas along Carnarvon Street and Agnes Street: 618 Carnarvon at 618 Carnarvon Street, Azure 1 and 2 at 898 and 892 Carnarvon Street, Marinus at Plaza 88 at 888 Carnarvon Street, Ovation at 823 Carnarvon Street and Westminster Towers at 828 and 838 Agnes Street. Confirm addresses on title.
Fraserview is the south slope above the: Fraserview is the south slope above the North Arm of the Fraser River. It's a real estate board area name, not one of the ten neighbourhoods on the City's Official Community Plan map of residential neighbourhoods.
The slope runs along Stewardson Way and: Stewardson Way and the Waterfront Esplanade (North Arm) run along the bottom of the slope, and the strata homes are above them on Jamieson Court, Ross Drive and Francis Way.
The waterfront edge holds the low-rise s: The low-rises are at the waterfront edge: Palace Quay at 69 and 71 Jamieson Court is the largest building on the court, with the Jamieson Place townhouses at 72 Jamieson Court beside it.
Two index entries sit off the hill — Que: Two buildings are off the hill (Queen's Park Place at 55 Blackberry Drive and Fraserview Park at 74 Miner Street), and there are few townhouses (245 Francis Way and 72 Jamieson Court), because most Fraserview stratas are apartment buildings.
Fraser Mews at 340, 365 and 385 Ginger D: Fraser Mews at 340, 365 and 385 Ginger Drive is called a townhouse in some listings, but it's a four-storey elevator apartment building.
Apartment side: at least one unit at the: Apartments: at least one home at the same address is listed as an apartment (built in 2003, garden level). A listing that calls a garden apartment "townhome-like" doesn't make it a townhouse; it's an apartment.
What condo stock actually exists in Glen: What condos are there in Glenbrooke North?
The condo stock hides on the park's edge: The condos are on the edges of the park area, not in the middle. The residential streets between 6th and 10th are RS-zoned houses (RS-1: minimum site of 557.40 m², floor space ratio of 0.5). Every apartment building I know of is on Eighth Street, Eighth Avenue or the edges of the avenues, in the multiple-unit RM districts. If a "Moody Park condo" search shows a home on an interior street, it's something else.
Moody Park is a documented heritage neig: Moody Park is one of the City's recorded historic neighbourhoods. The City includes it in its Historic Neighbourhood Context Statements. Heritage status is checked property by property, and work on a listed property can need heritage approval, which matters when an older low-rise strata plans exterior work.
Heritage is a live check, not a footnote: Check heritage status: Moody Park is one of the neighbourhoods in the City's Historic Neighbourhood Context Statements, and heritage status must be checked property by property before you plan renovations to an older home.
How old is this stock, and what does tha: How old are these buildings, and what does that mean for special levies?
Houses here are early stock: residential: The houses here are early ones: building along Sixth Avenue began shortly after the park was cleared in 1889, and the neighbourhood was largely built and served by streetcar by the First World War.
New Westminster's condo stock is organiz: New Westminster's condos are grouped around its five SkyTrain stations, because Transit Oriented Development Areas allow more density within 800 metres of each station. Downtown, the Quay, Sapperton and Uptown are each near one of the mainland stations, while Queensborough is planned under its own community plan.
Downtown holds the city's tower stock ar: Downtown has the city's towers, around its two stations: transit-oriented development in New Westminster is mainly around New Westminster Station and Columbia Station, with Plaza 88, built around New Westminster Station, as the best-known example. Tower condos elsewhere in the city are the exception.
Sapperton's stock is a single master-pla: Sapperton's condos are mostly in one master-planned district. Wesgroup says the Brewery District is a finished community of residential high-rises, shops and office buildings on the former brewery site, and that The Keary is the last chance to buy new in that district. So a Sapperton condo search is largely a search of one developer's district on Keary Street.
Queensborough's multi-family stock is go: Queensborough's multi-family buildings come under named development permit areas. The City's residential Development Permit Areas for Queensborough include Ewen Avenue Multi-Family, Compact Lot, East Queensborough, Port Royal and Queensborough Eastern Node. Which permit area a property is in sets the form a Queensborough condo or multi-family building can take.
New multi-unit buildings must include in: New multi-unit buildings must include storage. In May 2025, Council approved a requirement that every new home have at least 3.7 square metres (39.8 square feet) of residential storage, in the unit or in a common storage room, for applications received on or after May 5, 2025. So a new condo includes storage that many existing ones don't.
Since June 2026 the infill frame is city: Since June 2026, infill rules have applied city-wide: the RGO-A zone (up to four homes) and the RGO-B zone (up to six homes) allow infill housing on single detached and duplex properties across most of the city without a site-specific rezoning.
Queensborough runs on a different clock:: Queensborough is on a different schedule: the Province extended Queensborough's deadline to comply with the small-scale multi-unit housing rules to May 4, 2029, so the mainland and Queensborough don't have the same rules at the same time.
53 of the 624 New Westminster condo sale: 53 of the 624 New Westminster condos that sold had "Penthouse" entered as the style, most of them in Queensborough (13). The listing agent enters that, so some top-floor homes aren't marked and a marked one isn't always on the very top floor.
New Westminster's townhome stock cluster: New Westminster's townhouses are mostly in Queensborough, the island neighbourhood on the eastern tip of Lulu Island reached by the Queensborough Bridge, where strata complexes line Ewen Avenue. Smaller groups are at Victoria Hill, Queen's Park and on Royal Avenue downtown.
Ewen Avenue in Queensborough holds the c: Ewen Avenue in Queensborough has most of them: Portside at 488 Furness Street in Port Royal, Coopers Landing at 935 Ewen Avenue, English Mews at 1111 and 1135 Ewen Avenue, Ewen at 843 Ewen Avenue, Alexander Walk at 1211 Ewen Avenue and Oxford Townhomes at 728 Ewen Avenue.
Brickstone Walk at 828 Royal Avenue look: Brickstone Walk at 828 Royal Avenue looks like a townhouse complex but is an apartment building, while Brickstone Walk II at 838 Royal Avenue is a townhouse strata.
Clinton Place at 114 Park Row dates to 1: Clinton Place at 114 Park Row dates from 1974, decades older than the Queensborough townhouses. Its strata plan is NWS262.
The Quay has two names and both are offi: The Quay has two names, and both are official in different places. The real estate board calls the area "Quay"; the City's heritage name for the same neighbourhood is "Quayside", and the street, park and bus route all use Quayside. Search under both names.
Where the stock sits: high-rise and mid-: Where the homes are: high-rise and mid-rise apartment buildings along Quayside Drive and its side courts (Renaissance Square, Rialto Court, Reliance Court, K de K Court, Laguna Court).
Floodplain Zone 3 is the defining dilige: Floodplain Zone 3 is the main thing to check at the Quay, including for townhouses: the City's floodplain study puts the Quay in Floodplain Zone 3, the Fraser River waterfront zone, where many newer buildings have their floor space above the Flood Construction Level but their exits and the waterfront path are below it. For a townhouse at the base of a tower, compare the home's own floor level with the Flood Construction Level, and check the strata's insurance and deductible, before removing subjects.
Mostly towers, but not all: Quay West (3: Mostly towers, but not all: Quay West (31 Reliance Court) is a 4-storey, 60-home wood-frame low-rise built in 1986, Quayside Terrace (5 K de K Court) is a 4-storey building, and Murano Lofts (7 Rialto Court) is a 7-storey concrete mid-rise of 237 homes built in 2005. Wood frame and concrete differ on insurance, depreciation reports and special levies, so check which the specific building is.
Is there any low-rise or wood-frame stoc: Are there any low-rise or wood-frame buildings, or is it all towers?
No standalone one — the count is 0 strat: No stand-alone complex, strata or fee-simple. The waterfront is apartment stratas. The closest thing to a townhouse is the TH-series homes at the base of RiverSky 2, which are strata lots in that tower's strata plan (EPS5412).
Queen's Park itself, the park, occupies: Queen's Park itself, the park, takes up the eastern part of the neighbourhood, nearly 30 hectares. The City's Statement of Significance treats the park separately from the residential streets, so the park edge on McBride Boulevard is a boundary of the housing area.
Queen's Park's stock is valued as a coll: Queen's Park's houses are valued as a group, not one by one: the Statement of Significance says the neighbourhood is valued in particular for its large collection of grand houses and their gardens. That's why heritage rules apply to the whole area, not only to listed houses.
The park's bandshell is mid-renovation,: The park's bandshell is partway through a renovation, not simply closed: the City says the Queen's Park Bandshell, a wood-frame structure built in 1969, was found to be at the end of its service life. Its roof and stage-level storage were removed in Phase 1, and the Phase 2 restoration is being designed.
Geography note: Queensborough is New Wes: Geography: Queensborough is New Westminster's island neighbourhood on the east tip of Lulu Island, bordered by the main arm of the Fraser River and the North Arm, and joined to mainland New Westminster only by Highway 91A, over the Queensborough Bridge. Queensborough's condos are the low-rise strata buildings at Port Royal, the newer development area at the north end of the island, plus one older low-rise on Star Crescent and one mixed-use building on Hampton Street at Ewen Avenue.
The island's older waterfront low-rise,: The island's older waterfront low-rise, at the north-east tip of Lulu Island. A building directory says it was built in 1998, with a bike room, garden, in-suite laundry, playground and storage; current listings give 1997 for some homes and 1998 for others. Listings describe a 2.1-acre site steps from a sandy beach, a community garden, a dog park and a 1.3 km riverwalk, wood frame with brick and wood siding.
Where the condo stock concentrates: Port: Where the condos are: at Port Royal, at the north end. A series of Aragon low-rise strata buildings runs along Salter Street (Paddler's Landing, Regatta, Glasshouse Lofts, Portage, Light House, Timber House), ending at the community's only high-rise, The Peninsula at 210 Salter Street. Residences by the River (83 Star Crescent, 1998) is the older waterfront building at the north-east tip of the island, and Via (288 Hampton Street) is on the Ewen Avenue side.
Flood rules — the defining Queensborough: Flooding is the main thing to check in Queensborough: the whole neighbourhood is Floodplain Zone 1, behind a 1960s ring dike protecting about 350 hectares, with pumped drainage shared with Richmond. The City's Flood Hazard Development Permit Area sets minimum construction levels of 3.53 metres above GSC datum in Area A and 4.20 metres in Area B. The City received $800,000 from the provincial Community Emergency Preparedness Fund to repair the dike's shoreline protection at two places on the north-east side of Lulu Island (behind 345 Gifford Street and behind 805 Boyd Street). Get the lot's flood construction level and an insurance quote before you remove subjects.
A Queensborough lot can be unsubdividabl: A Queensborough lot can be impossible to subdivide because of the sewer, not its size. Under the Zoning Bylaw, no subdivision in Queensborough can create a lot smaller than half an acre (0.20 ha) or with less than 66 feet (20.12 m) of frontage unless the land can connect to the City's sanitary sewer. Most lots are connected, but check the specific lot.

Only within the island's sewer rule. The: Only within the island's sewer rule. Whether the specific lot can connect to the sewer decides whether it can be subdivided. Confirm that with the City; don't assume it from the lot's size.

\"Sapperton\" is both the board (GVR) su: "Sapperton" is both the real estate board's name for the area and a City neighbourhood name (also written McBride-Sapperton).
Where the condo stock concentrates: two: Where the condos are: in two places. One is the Brewery District towers on Nelson's Court, Nelson's Crescent and Keary Street, across from Sapperton Station; the other is the older low-rise walk-ups on Cedar Street above East Columbia Street.
Schools: SD40, address-based. Skwo:wech: Schools: School District 40, by address. Skwo:wech Elementary (331 Richmond St) opened on June 6, 2022.

A 9-lot strata is over the depreciation: A 9-lot strata is just over the size that requires a depreciation report. McBride Boulevard is the west-side route: McBride Boulevard is the route off the slope on the west side, and Brunette Creek and the Brunette-Fraser Greenway are on the east side.
Character: the residential streets above: Character: the residential streets above East Columbia Street are single detached homes in the RS districts of Zoning Bylaw No. 6680 (2001), including some of the city's oldest houses around the 1891 Knox Presbyterian Church and the historic centre. Secondary suites and laneway and carriage houses are regulated in the same bylaw. Most homes on the older residential streets are freehold.
Flood position — Sapperton's own, never: Flooding in Sapperton: the City's floodplain study puts the industrial land along the Brunette River in Floodplain Zone 4, below the Flood Construction Level. The risk in Sapperton is on the low land by the Brunette River and Braid, not on the residential slope. Confirm a specific lot against the City's flood maps.
