Heritage: Sapperton is one of the neighb: Heritage: Sapperton is one of the neighbourhoods in the City's Historic Neighbourhood Context Statements, with landmarks such as the 1891 Knox Presbyterian Church on Knox Street. Confirm whether a property is on the City's heritage register before planning exterior work or a teardown.
One masterplan, two tenures, no lots. No: One master plan, with both strata and rental homes, and no lots for sale.
Most single detached dwellings and some: Most single detached houses and some duplexes in New Westminster are zoned to allow a secondary suite, which must meet the Zoning Bylaw and the Building Code. There's a limit of one suite per house, and a property can have both a suite and a laneway or carriage house.
The City's suite guide position is that: The City's suite guide says some duplexes are zoned to allow a secondary suite that meets the Zoning Bylaw and the Building Code. There's a limit of one suite per house, and a property can have both a suite and a laneway or carriage house. Confirm the zone for the specific property.
The stock is post-war houses built for r: The houses are post-war homes built for returning veterans: the City opened the sale of Victory Heights lots on October 1, 1945, for 30 days exclusively to returning veterans, at 30 percent of the assessed land value, on condition that the land be used right away to build new homes.
One Heights-specific cost follows from i: One cost to know about in The Heights: a house with a secondary suite pays the higher utility rate for suites. The City's 2026 net utility subtotal for a single-family home with a secondary suite is $4,143.46, against $2,753.73 without one.
A 14-storey, 97-unit concrete strata hig: A 14-storey, 97-home concrete strata high-rise at Queens and Eleventh, with a gym, pool, shared laundry and underground parking, according to the property manager.
A small Uptown NW strata low-rise built: A small strata low-rise in Uptown built in 1994. Current listings call the complex "Penny Lane".
The stock is detached houses on the plat: The homes are detached houses on the streets at the top of the hill, in the RS districts of Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001. The RS-1 district requires a minimum site area of 557.40 square metres (6,000 square feet), with a floor space ratio of 0.5.
RS districts allow secondary suites, and: The RS districts allow secondary suites, and laneway and carriage houses are regulated under the same bylaw, so houses here can have a suite or a laneway house under their zoning.
Uptown's Frequent Transit Development Ar: Uptown is designated a Frequent Transit Development Area in the Official Community Plan (Our City 2041), which is the basis for added density around Sixth Street.
School District No. 40 (SD40) runs a sin: School District No. 40 has one secondary school, New Westminster Secondary at 820 Sixth Street. Its replacement building opened on January 11, 2021, at a cost of $106.5 million, with 1,900 seats. As examples, the school locator gives Lord Kelvin Elementary, Fraser River Middle and New Westminster Secondary for 835 Eighth Street, and École Lord Tweedsmuir Elementary, Fraser River Middle and New Westminster Secondary for 1714 Eighth Avenue.
Added-homes potential is part of the lot: The option to add homes is part of a lot's value: the RS districts allow secondary suites, and laneway and carriage houses are regulated under the same bylaw. Check this on any Uptown house purchase. Suite space built with permits is a selling point when you resell.
Heritage: Uptown's side streets hold som: Heritage: Uptown's side streets have some of the city's older houses.
Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001 governs. The: Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001 applies. The townhouse districts are the older RT-2, RT-2A, RT-2B, RT-2C and RT-3, RT-3A and RT-3B, plus the newer RT-A and RT-B (at least 836.1 m², or 9,000 sq. ft., of site area, at least 20 m of frontage and lane access). The side streets are in the Single Detached Residential Districts (RS), where RS-1 sets a minimum site area of 557.40 sq. m. (6,000 sq. ft.) and a floor space ratio of 0.5.
The RS districts allow secondary suites,: The RS districts allow secondary suites, and laneway and carriage houses are regulated under Zoning Bylaw No. 6680. Get the City permits and confirm what's allowed on the specific lot before you put a value on a second home. Suite space built with permits is a selling point when you resell.
A strata unit there is bought as a strat: A strata unit there is bought as a strata lot, with a Form B to review. It isn't half of a duplex.
40's (SD40) only secondary school, servi: New Westminster Secondary is School District 40's only secondary school and serves the whole city. For 835 Eighth Street, on the area's east side, the school locator gives Lord Kelvin Elementary, Fraser River Middle and New Westminster Secondary.
The Twelfth Street corridor stock is old: Some buildings on Twelfth Street are older still: the City's heritage inventory records the street's older buildings, including the Boughen-designed houses in the 400 block of Twelfth Street.
It is the West End's commercial street a: It's the West End's commercial street, and the City has recorded its heritage. The City prepared a Twelfth Street Heritage Inventory to add to its heritage records and guide planning for the street ahead of expected commercial and residential development. According to the inventory, the street's commercial district stayed active through the 1950s and 1960s.
Under the Strata Property Act, ss. 123.1: A strata can restrict residents to age 55 or older. Any age bylaw set below 55 (19+, 40+, 45+) has been void since November 24, 2022, when Bill 44 took effect.
the Real Estate Development Marketing Ac: a presale buyer has seven days to cancel, from the later of signing and acknowledging the disclosure statement, and deposits are held in trust.
5% GST applies to new construction, not: 5% GST applies to new construction, not resales. Moody on the Hill was built in 2024, so whether GST is payable depends on the specific home's sale history (a first sale from the developer or a resale). The First-Time Home Buyers' GST/HST Rebate rebates 100% of the GST on a price up to $1 million (maximum $50,000), phasing out by $1.5 million, for agreements signed on or after March 20, 2025 and before 2031. The legislation (Bill C-4) received Royal Assent on March 13, 2026, according to the Canada Revenue Agency. The older GST New Housing Rebate (36%, maximum $6,300, phasing out between $350,000 and $450,000) still exists.
Strata Property Act ss. 123.1/123.2 — on: Only a 55+ age bylaw is legal, with exemptions for a younger spouse or partner, a live-in caregiver, existing residents and some children (expanded May 1, 2023).
5% GST applies to new construction, not: 5% GST applies to new construction, not resales. A never-occupied home in a tower finished in 2025 (Plaza One, Plaza Two, The Grand on King George, Park George) can still be a sale by the developer, so find out for each home whether it's a developer sale or a resale. The First-Time Home Buyers' GST/HST Rebate (Bill C-4, Royal Assent March 13, 2026, according to the Canada Revenue Agency) rebates 100% of the GST up to $1 million, to a maximum of $50,000, phasing out by $1.5 million, for agreements signed from March 20, 2025 and before 2031. The GST New Housing Rebate is 36%, to a maximum of $6,300, phasing out between $350,000 and $450,000.
Strata Property Act ss. 123.1/123.2 and: Only a 55+ age bylaw is legal, with exemptions for existing residents, live-in caregivers and, since May 1, 2023, younger spouses or partners and some children. That works two ways in this city: the Fraserview Village buildings are published as 55+ (confirm the registered bylaw with the Form B), while Canuck Plaza's "25+" label is void, because no age other than 55+ can be a legal strata age bylaw. Haney Pioneer Village is a 60+ co-op, and its age rule is a co-op rule, not a strata bylaw.
only 55+ residency bylaws are lawful (St: only 55+ age bylaws are legal (with exemptions, expanded May 1, 2023, for a younger spouse or partner, live-in caregivers, existing residents and some children).
Bill C-4, Royal Assent March 13, 2026 pe: Bill C-4 received Royal Assent on March 13, 2026, according to the Canada Revenue Agency. Together with the GST/HST new housing rebate, it rebates 100% of the GST (or the federal part of the HST) on a newly built or substantially renovated home worth up to $1,000,000, is gradually reduced between $1,000,000 and $1,500,000, and isn't available at $1,500,000 or more. The maximum is $50,000. To qualify, the agreement with the builder must be entered into on or after March 20, 2025 and before 2031 (or, for an owner-built home, construction must begin in that period), construction must begin before 2031 and be substantially finished before 2036, and the buyer must be at least 18, a Canadian citizen or permanent resident, and a first-time buyer (not having owned a home in the last four calendar years).
The farm stock here is quota plus barns,: A broiler farm is quota plus barns, not land alone. The Board's General Orders cover barn space and require a grower to have an allotment form before producing in a quota production period, with an 8-week cycle allotted at 1.929 kilograms per quota unit.
Mainstream and specialty quota are diffe: Mainstream and specialty quota are different. The Board's specialty pilot allocates specialty quota on a 48-week, 6-cycle annual basis starting with Period A-198 (September 21, 2025), and from that period lets specialty quota holders use leasehold agreements on the same terms as mainstream growers.
One secondary source states Greater Vanc: One source says Greater Vancouver REALTORS® published no Calverhall condo or townhome benchmark for September 2026, which fits with there being no condos here.
The density arrived by bylaw, not by bui: The extra density came from a bylaw, not from new buildings. Calverhall's future attached homes will be small strata multiplexes on today's house lots, and lot values now depend on the Official Community Plan designation. There's no apartment zoning here.
Fee-simple homes (the stock that actuall: Fee-simple homes (what Calverhall has): a house with a legal suite is still one fee-simple title.

No named bare-land development, assembly: I don't know of any bare-land development, land assembly, development site or rezoning proposal in Calverhall. Both operation types must be certified,: Both kinds of operation must be certified, and a buyer takes that on.
Quota is counted in layers: a BC Farm In: Quota is counted in layers (laying hens): a BC Farm Industry Review Board decision records a national allocation increase distributed as 44,475 layers to licensed producers in good standing.
The farm stock for tax purposes splits l: For tax purposes, a farm's land and buildings are classed separately. BC Assessment says land can be Class 9, Farm, where it produces a set amount of qualifying primary agricultural products for sale, while farm buildings are in Class 1, Residential.
The ALC states the same frame in plain t: The Agricultural Land Commission puts the same rules in plain terms for buyers. Land in the ALR can generally have no more than one home per parcel unless it qualifies for an additional home; a main house must be 500 square metres or less, with no more than 1,000 square metres of fill placed to build it; a secondary suite is allowed only inside the main house; and local governments can be stricter but not more lenient.
Confirm residence plans against both the: Check plans for a house against both the Agricultural Land Commission's rules and local zoning. The Commission says local or First Nation governments can set stricter total floor area limits and can't be more lenient than the Commission, so a plan that meets the Commission's rules can still be refused locally.

Abbotsford frame (Abbotsford parcels onl: In Abbotsford (for comparison only): the current Official Community Plan is Abbotsforward 2050. It doesn't apply to properties in the Township of Langley, Surrey, Mission or the Fraser Valley Regional District's rural areas.
Tax schedules are local: whether a speci: Property tax dates depend on where the farm is. Sea Island is a separate island in the F: Sea Island is a separate island in the Fraser River in the City of Richmond, BC, with Lulu Island (the main part of Richmond) to the south and east and the City of Vancouver across the North Arm to the north. Why this section still exists on a zero-: Why this section is here when there are no strata homes on the island: BC's strata rules below apply to any strata purchase in the province, and would apply if a strata unit were ever offered on Sea Island. The city and federal rules after them are the ones that affect Burkeville purchases.
Aircraft noise and height: federal Airpo: Aircraft noise and height: federal Airport Zoning Regulations, administered by Transport Canada, set zoning around the airport, including maximum building heights. Aircraft noise is managed through the YVR 2025–2029 Noise Management Plan, and the City's Aircraft Noise Sensitive Development Policy Area (City Bulletin DEVAPPS-05) applies to noise-sensitive development near the airport. Check both when buying in Burkeville: they affect additions, rebuilds and tree height, as well as daily life.
Three Canada Line stations, no condo at: Three Canada Line stations, and no condos at any of them. Templeton, Sea Island Centre and YVR-Airport stations serve the island, but the land around them is airport and commercial. Sea Island is a rare area with SkyTrain service and no strata homes.
\"Sea Island\" is both the board sub-are: "Sea Island" is both the real estate board's name and one of the City of Richmond's own planning areas (planning area 12 in the Official Community Plan), so the City's name and the board's name match.
Aircraft noise and height — the island-s: Aircraft noise and height, which are particular to the island: federal Airport Zoning Regulations, administered by Transport Canada, set zoning around the airport so aircraft can operate safely, including maximum building heights. Aircraft noise is managed through the YVR 2025–2029 Noise Management Plan, YVR publishes annual noise reports with monitoring data, and the City's Aircraft Noise Sensitive Development Policy Area (City Bulletin DEVAPPS-05) applies to noise-sensitive development near the airport. Check both before you price an addition or a rebuild on a Burkeville lot.
Sea Island is planning area 12 in the Ci: Sea Island is planning area 12 in the City of Richmond's 2041 Official Community Plan (Bylaw 9000), which applies to Burkeville. Senior governments aren't bound by the City's plan, so changes on the airport side follow the federal and airport process under the YVR 2037 Master Plan. On this island, first find out which rules apply to the property.
Flood / dike diligence — Bylaw 8204: the: Flooding and dikes (Bylaw 8204): the Flood Plain Designation and Protection Bylaw 8204 sets flood construction levels and dike setbacks. The island is in the Fraser River floodplain, behind the City's dikes. Confirm the lot's requirements before planning a rebuild.
The usual duplex form: A specific proper: Duplexes: if a property in Burkeville is marketed as a duplex, check its title to see whether it's one lot, a strata or a subdivided pair.
Richmond's own s.5.4 rule: 33.0 m² minim: Richmond's own rule for secondary suites: a minimum of 33 m², and a maximum of 40% of the home or 110 m², whichever is less.
